<a id="memory-project_3dgs_1080p_perf_and_reference_blocker"></a>
## project_3dgs_1080p_perf_and_reference_blocker

---
name: project_3dgs_1080p_perf_and_reference_blocker
description: B19 3DGS rasteriser hits real-time millions@1080p (435fps 1M / 248fps 4M render on RTX 4070 Ti SUPER); the Inria reference could NOT be run locally (CPU-only torch)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

**B19 3DGS is performance-real: the shared-mem tiled rasteriser (`build_gsplat_block_render_smem_kernel`) renders
1920×1080 at 2.30 ms / 435 fps for 1M splats and 4.04 ms / 248 fps for 4M** on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, GPU-timestamped
(`[.gsplat-bench]` in `test_vulkan_gsplat.cpp`). Full-frame (+ measured sort/bin) ≈ 385 fps @ 1M / 210 fps @ 4M. Board:
`docs/bench/2026-07-21-3dgs-1080p-rasterizer.md`.

**Two perf levers that mattered (both non-obvious):**
1. The shared-mem composite inner loop MUST be bounded by the chunk's actual splat count `min(BS, re−cbase)`, NOT a fixed
   BS=256 — otherwise low-overdraw tiles waste the whole 256-wide loop on padding and shared-mem is a 0.92× LOSS. With the
   variable bound it's a 3.5× win.
2. **Early termination** (config `early_terminate`): a shared active-pixel count + `stmt_for_break_if` stops a tile once
   every pixel's transmittance T<1e-4. Turns 3.5×→4.9× @ 1M and 2.4×→**10.5×** @ 4M (high overdraw). NOT bit-exact (drops
   the saturated tail, ~1e-13 error here) ⇒ it's a config flag; the no-early-out smem variant is bit-exact vs the direct
   render, gated 0.0.

**⛔ THE REFERENCE PEER (Inria `diff-gaussian-rasterization`) COULD NOT BE RUN in this environment:** PyTorch here is
CPU-only (`torch 2.12.0+cpu`, `cuda.is_available()==False`) and CUDA-torch wheels for Python 3.14 don't exist yet, so the
CUDA extension can't compile. The host DOES have CUDA 13.3 + nvcc + an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. To close the head-to-head, a
future session needs a Python env with a CUDA-enabled torch (or an nvcc-only reimplementation of the reference kernel).
Our numbers are in the same class as the reference's published ~130–240 fps @ 1080p, portable (5 backends) + bit-exact,
but a DIRECT win is unproven and honestly documented as env-blocked — not declined. See
[feedback_bench_all_peers_never_cherry_pick](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_all_peers_never_cherry_pick), [feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards).


<!-- end-memory:project_3dgs_1080p_perf_and_reference_blocker -->

<a id="memory-project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction"></a>
## project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction

---
name: project-agent-native-engine-strategic-direction
description: Strategic direction locked 2026-05-19 — Cerid is being built agent-native. Every engine operation reachable via CLI/RPC; AI agents are peer users.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8cb26449-c85d-4ed3-82cc-cc0ed35ddca1
---

User locked a major strategic direction 2026-05-19 (during Phase 3.1.6
hesap planning conversation):

> "I want this hesap module to be a true elite level engineering and
> maths module and then we will build a cli and an interactive
> notebook on this (notebook might come later when we do ui ux stuff
> but cli must be ready) and also not specific to hesap module, I
> also want everything in the engine absolutely controllable by cli
> commands. The reason I want that is to integrate AI agents like
> you to our workflows for robotics, aerospace design, cinematics
> design, game design by writing scripts, shaders and stuff and all
> the creative tasks can be easily done by the ai agents in the
> future."

**Why:** Cerid's multi-domain mandate is converging on a future where
AI agents (Claude, GPT, Gemini class) are peer collaborators across
robotics + aerospace + cinematic + game + medical + scientific
workflows. Every domain is heading toward agent-driven authoring.
Engines that ship GUI-first with CLI as afterthought lose. Cerid bets
on agent-native from the substrate up.

**How to apply:**

- **CLI is the source of truth.** GUI is a visualization layer that
  emits CLI commands. Every engine op reachable from CLI / JSON-RPC /
  Anthropic MCP.
- **Per-slice DoD from 2026-05-19 forward:** ship CLI commands
  alongside the C++ API. Existing modules back-fill as they ship new
  slices.
- **Hesap (Phase 3.1.6) is the FIRST concrete consumer** — ships
  with CLI surface from v0. Matrix construction, BLAS, solvers, etc.
  all CLI-driveable.
- **Phase 4.0 = `crd-cli` + `crd-rpc` substrate** (~12 wk; replaces
  the original Phase 4.0 = C++ scripting/DLL hot-reload, which folds
  in as a sub-aspect).
- **MCP compatibility from day 1** — Claude Code / OpenAI Function
  Calling / Gemini Function Calling agents drive Cerid out of the
  box.
- **Determinism + replay** (ADR-0063 + ADR-0078) make agent sessions
  bit-exactly reproducible across machines + time.
- **Capability-based security** + transactional sessions + sandbox
  isolation = safe agent execution. Agents can't `system:shell`
  unless explicitly granted.

**Consolidated phase doc (2026-05-22):** `docs/phases/phase-4.0-platform.md` — "Cerid Platform Layer (Reflection · Command Interface · Scripting · Agents)" is now the canonical umbrella. Architecture-deep / slices-provisional. Folds ADR-0081 in as Pillar 2 (command interface) and adds three NEW pillars beyond it: **(1) reflection/codegen substrate `crd-reflect`** — annotation + clang-tooling parse exposed/marshalled functions+structs → generate CLI/RPC/MCP/serialization/inspector bindings (validated by regenerating hesap's hand-written commands and diffing); **(4) ECS-integrated scripting** — scripts as systems/components; **(6) app packaging** — dev hot-reload DLLs → shipped baked-in app. Executes AFTER hesap (full) + eylem (full) for consumer-driven design. New ADR-0084 (reflection-codegen) to mint at Pillar-1 execution. Old `phase-4-extensibility.md` §4.0/§4.1 superseded (4.1 math → hesap); §4.2 networking stays separate. Resolved: NO new CLI scripting language (C++ + RPC + thin declarative batch). See also [project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal](project-history.md#memory-project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal) (command interface is browser-native; C++ hot-reload is the WASM-hard part).

**Key docs (created 2026-05-19):**

- `docs/research/cerid-agent-native-engine.md` — vision dossier.
- `docs/research/cerid-hesap-2026-update.md` — hesap CLI-from-day-1 +
  matrix types + complex + 2024-2026 SOTA.
- `docs/decisions/0081-agent-native-engine-cli.md` — ADR (Proposed;
  Accepted when `crd-cli` v0 ships); supersedes ADR-0034.
- PRINCIPLES.md cornerstone added.

**Sequencing:** This vision INFORMS Phase 3.1.6 v0 (immediate next
slice — ship hesap with CLI from day 1) but the FULL `crd-cli` +
`crd-rpc` substrate is a new Phase 4.0 (~12 wk; sized when v0 hesap
proves the CLI pattern).

Memory entry name pinned so future sessions know this is a load-bearing
strategic decision, not a side feature.

<a id="memory-project_amd_port_cs_amd_faithfully"></a>
## project_amd_port_cs_amd_faithfully

---
name: project_amd_port_cs_amd_faithfully
description: "v2b AMD must match Eigen/cs_amd fill (~1.0x), not settle for faithful-min-degree 1.08x"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 74c7eabe-7e9b-4444-ace0-9618068f9bbf
---

2026-05-21 user decision (hesap v2b-2 rung 3): close the AMD fill gap by porting **CSparse `cs_amd` selection faithfully** — the "reference is the floor" path ([feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor)).

**Context:** my from-principles approximate-min-degree (approx degree + supervariables + aggressive absorption + current element sizes) is valid, deterministic, fast (3-16 ms), beats natural ~1.5x, but lands at **1.08x/1.08x/1.11x** vs Eigen-AMD fill on bcsstk13/24/25. Eigen uses CSparse `cs_amd`.

**Key diagnostic finding:** comparing my raw elimination order to Eigen's `permutationP()` step-by-step is apples-to-oranges — `cs_amd` POSTORDERS the assembly (elimination) tree, so its permutation's "first" node is a postorder leaf, NOT first-eliminated. Postordering does NOT change nnz(L), so the 8-11% fill gap is real elimination-quality, independent of postorder. My degree FORMULA already matches cs_amd (verified algebraically: external degree + dk - nvi, clamped by min(old+dk-nvi, n-nel-nvi)).

**The missing cs_amd pieces (in priority order):**
1. **Mass elimination** — when a node i in Lk has external degree d_ext==0 (connects only to Lk), absorb it into pivot k: `dk-=nvi; nv[k]+=nvi; nel+=nvi; nv[i]=0`. Changes nv[k] → changes other nodes' degrees → indirect fill effect. Output: i's members fold into k's member chain (so move perm-output to AFTER mass-elim).
2. **Dense node handling** — nodes with degree > `dense=min(n-2, max(16, 10*sqrt(n)))` get nv=0/elen=-1 and ordered LAST. Real fill effect (eliminate sparse structure first).
3. cs_amd phase order: A=degree-update+mass-elim+hash → B=supernode merge → C=finalize bucket-insert with final dk. (I had supervar AFTER bucket-insert; reorder.)

**Determinism:** re-pins D(ord)-1 from "lowest-index tiebreak" to cs_amd's deterministic tiebreak (still deterministic — cs_amd is a fixed algorithm). Update [project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision)-adjacent docs/systems/hesap-ordering.md D(ord) pins when closed.

Reference: CSparse `cs_amd.c` (Davis, "Direct Methods for Sparse Linear Systems"). Validate against `bench_hesap_ordering_vs_reference` targets 258179/285671/1443995, gate <=1.05x (aim ~1.0x).


<!-- end-memory:project_amd_port_cs_amd_faithfully -->

<a id="memory-project_atmosphere_gold_sky_ckir"></a>
## project_atmosphere_gold_sky_ckir

---
name: project_atmosphere_gold_sky_ckir
description: "D-007 B15-a: gold-standard physically-based atmosphere (Hillaire 2020 / UE5 Sky-Atmosphere) in CKIR (ckir_atmosphere.hpp) — transmittance + multiple-scattering + sky-view LUTs, CPU-physics + Vulkan verified. Two reusable scars: relative-error metric divides by near-zero on [0,1] LUTs (use ABSOLUTE); the CPU oracle has NO memoization so deep shared DAGs blow up — stmt_materialize + reduced-res tests fix it."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**D-007 B15-a — physically-based ATMOSPHERE (Hillaire 2020, the UE5 Sky-Atmosphere method), in CKIR (2026-07-15).** The next
visual-frontier slice after B14 GI. `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_atmosphere.hpp` (namespace `crd::kir::atmos`), statement-tier
COMPUTE, SCALARIZED RGB. Pure analytic scattering integrals — NO ray-tracing leaf, so the whole thing is buildable +
bit-exact-verifiable now. Three medium: Rayleigh (∝exp(−h/8km), wavelength-dep β_R, no absorption), Mie (∝exp(−h/1.2km), grey,
Cornette-Shanks g=0.8), ozone (tent absorber @25km). Earth-reference constants in 1/km. Tests `tests/kir/test_ckir_atmosphere.cpp`
+ `tests/gpu-context-vulkan`.

- **[✅ B15-a-1] `build_atmos_transmittance`** — T(r,μ)=exp(−τ), the extinction integral ray-marched (40 steps) over the Bruneton
  (r,μ) LUT parameterisation. CPU physics: T∈(0,1], Rayleigh **blue>green>red** (T_r≈0.94, T_b≈0.76 straight up — why the sky is
  blue / sunsets red), horizon far darker, T→1 at altitude. Vulkan maxabs **6.25e-5**.
- **[✅ B15-a-2] `build_atmos_multiscatter`** — Hillaire's isotropic 2nd-order fill: per texel (μ_sun,alt), integrate single
  scatter over a Fibonacci sphere (each ray bilinear-samples the transmittance LUT), form L₂ + transfer f_ms, sum the closed
  series **Ψ = L₂/(1−f_ms)**. CPU physics: Ψ≥0/finite, grows toward the ground, bluish, brighter sun-up. Vulkan **1.46e-5**.
- **[✅ B15-a-3] `build_atmos_skyview`** — the renderable per-direction sky: march the view ray adding single scatter
  (Rayleigh + Cornette-Shanks Mie phase, sun-transmittance-weighted) + isotropic multiple scatter (from the multiscatter LUT),
  attenuated by view transmittance. CPU physics: blue zenith, sun-side Mie glow, bright horizon. Vulkan **1.43e-5**.
- **[✅ B15-a-4] `build_atmos_aerial`** — the 3D camera-frustum froxel volume: one thread per (x,y) column marches the depth
  slices, writing each cell's running (RGB inscatter + mean transmittance) via the same single+multi-scatter integrand →
  composites into B12-d fog as `surface·T + inscatter`. CPU physics: T falls with depth, inscatter accumulates, bluish; Vulkan
  **1.79e-5**. **▶ B15-a COMPLETE — the full Hillaire atmosphere.** NEXT: **B15-b** volumetric clouds (Nubis, reuse B6
  `ckir_noise.hpp`).

**⛔ SCAR 1 — a RELATIVE error metric divides by a near-zero reference; for a LUT that spans down to ~0, use ABSOLUTE error.**
The transmittance Vulkan test first used `|got−ref|/(|ref|+1e-3)` (the DDGI/ReSTIR metric) and "failed" at 9e-4 — but T→0 at the
horizon, so that was really 9e-7/1e-3, i.e. a **9e-7 ABSOLUTE** error (the hardware-transcendental floor), not a bug. DDGI/ReSTIR
never hit this because their refs were O(0.1–1). For a [0,1]/small-radiance LUT, assert on max ABSOLUTE error. Note: only
exp/sqrt/pow diverge (GPU-hardware vs CPU-libm, ~3 ULP); add/sub/mul/div/max/min are bit-exact ⇒ ~1e-5 floor is expected + fine.

**⛔ SCAR 2 — `eval_cpu_kernel` is a RECURSIVE tree-walker with NO memoization; deep shared DAGs blow up exponentially.** A
nested bilinear LUT sample (r_x → μ_sun_x → forward-map → 4 taps × 3 channels) re-evaluates every shared subtree per reference,
so the sky-view oracle hung (multi-minute). Two fixes, both applied: (1) **`g.stmt_materialize(node)`** freezes a node into a
per-thread snapshot — the oracle then returns the snapshot instead of re-walking (line ~106 of ckir_kernel_eval.hpp), AND it's a
register reuse on the GPU (strictly good codegen). Materialize the hot shared nodes (r_x, μ_sun_x, the bilinear x0/y0/x1/y1/frac).
(2) Even fully memo'd, the oracle is O(texels·steps·nodes) at ~0.5µs/node — a 256×64×40 LUT is ~20s. **LUT unit tests must run at
REDUCED resolution** (e.g. tlut 64×16, skyview 32×16); physics + portability are per-texel identical at any size, production uses
the full defaults. A proper memo cache in the oracle (per-eval-root, tid-aware around subgroup ops) is a worthwhile future
engine win. See also [feedback_oracle_must_round_every_elementary_op](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_oracle_must_round_every_elementary_op) (the oracle rounds every op to the node dtype).


<!-- end-memory:project_atmosphere_gold_sky_ckir -->

<a id="memory-project_b11_subgroup_op_class"></a>
## project_b11_subgroup_op_class

---
name: project_b11_subgroup_op_class
description: B11 — the CKIR wave/subgroup op class (reduce/scan/broadcast/shuffle) landed bit-exact on both backends; work graphs are env-blocked on NVIDIA Vulkan
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

**B11 SUBGROUP OP CLASS landed (2026-07-22), bit-exact both backends.** The full wave op class in CKIR (appended at END of `KOp`,
cook-stable, joining the existing `SubgroupBallot/ExclCount/Match`): reduce `SubgroupAdd/Min/Max/And/Or/Xor` · prefix scan
`SubgroupInclusiveAdd/ExclusiveAdd` · data movement `SubgroupBroadcastFirst`/`SubgroupShuffle`. Builders `g.subgroup_add/…/shuffle`
(result carries the operand type). Wired **GLSL** (`subgroupAdd`/`subgroupInclusiveAdd`/`subgroupShuffle` + the
`GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_arithmetic`/`_shuffle` extensions — added to ALL THREE emit paths: fused-elementwise `ta`, kernel `self`,
kernel `pv`) + **HLSL** SM6.0 (`WaveActiveSum/Min/Max/BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor`; `WavePrefixSum` is EXCLUSIVE ⇒ inclusive =
`WavePrefixSum+self`; `WaveReadLaneFirst`/`WaveReadLaneAt` — the pv kernel path + the fused elementwise path; registered in the
shared `is_fusable`). CPU oracle extended (32-lane sim). **INTEGER reductions/scans are order-independent ⇒ BIT-EXACT/portable**
(sums accumulate in f64 (32·u32 < 2^53) then `round_dtype` wraps mod-2^32 — modular add is associative ⇒ == the GPU's per-step
wrap); FLOAT reductions are NOT bit-exact (HW reduction order) — use integer forms or a fixed-tree.

Gate `[subgroup]` (shared kernel `tests/gpu-shared/ckir_subgroup_test.hpp` — 64-thread wg = 2×32-lane, 7 results/thread): GPU ==
CPU oracle **BIT-EXACT on Vulkan (0/448) AND DX12 (== Vulkan)**. Full kir regression green (52400/229). Session
`docs/sessions/2026-07-22-b11-subgroup-ops.md`.

**Perf role:** subgroup ops are THE fast cross-lane primitive — a workgroup reduction/scan via `subgroupShuffle`/`subgroupInclusiveAdd`
is far cheaper than a shared-mem log-tree with `barrier()`s (no shared memory, no barriers). Fast path for workgroup reductions,
stream compaction, histogram binning, the radix-sort rank (already uses `SubgroupBallot`). See [feedback_compute_kernel_emitter_lacked_exp_pow](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_compute_kernel_emitter_lacked_exp_pow)
(the "wire ALL emit paths, all backends" scar — reinforced: 3 GLSL paths + 2 HLSL paths per op).

**✅ QUAD OPS (2026-07-22):** `QuadBroadcast`(value, quad-lane 0..3) + `QuadSwapX/Y/Diagonal` (local id ^1/^2/^3) — GLSL
`subgroupQuadBroadcast`/`subgroupQuadSwap{Horizontal,Vertical,Diagonal}` (+ `GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_quad`; device
`subgroupQuadOperationsInAllStages=true`) + HLSL `QuadReadLaneAt`/`QuadReadAcross{X,Y,Diagonal}` + oracle (4-lane sim). The
`[subgroup]` gate now covers 11 ops — **0/704 mismatches Vulkan AND DX12**. **B11 FUNCTIONALLY COMPLETE** (only env-blocked
work-graph node shaders remain).

**✅ C5 GPU-DRIVEN DISPATCH (2026-07-22, DEV — row 32):** `ComputeRecorder::dispatch_indirect` (appended at END, non-pure virtual) —
the workgroup count comes from a compute-written INDIRECT-args buffer (`compute_usage::indirect`): **Vulkan `vkCmdDispatchIndirect`
+ DX12 `ExecuteIndirect` with a cached DISPATCH command signature.** New `ComputeAccess::IndirectRead` (→ `INDIRECT_COMMAND_READ`/
`DRAW_INDIRECT` · `D3D12_RESOURCE_STATE_INDIRECT_ARGUMENT`) for the ShaderWrite→IndirectRead barrier. `[indirect]` gate: a compute
pass counts even inputs (128/256) → `dispatch_indirect` launches exactly 128 groups == CPU ref, **both backends**. The GPU decides
its own workload (compute analogue of B4 `draw_mesh_indirect`). Session `docs/sessions/2026-07-22-c5-gpu-driven-dispatch.md`.

**⏭ WORK GRAPHS ENV-BLOCKED:** NVIDIA Vulkan does NOT expose `VK_AMDX_shader_enqueue` (an AMD ext), and D3D12 Work Graphs need the
Agility SDK (not vendored) — so the work-graph NODE-shader halves of B11 + C5 are env-blocked (documented like the coopvec-DX12
block). **✅ C5 DEVICE-GENERATED COMMANDS — the full multi-token DGC (2026-07-22).** `VK_NV_device_generated_commands`(+`_compute`)
enabled (gated; needs buffer-device-address, chained for `m_ray_query || m_dgc`; accessor `device_generated_commands()`). Two `[dgc]`
raw-Vulkan gates: (1) `[PUSH_CONSTANT, DISPATCH]` tokens → a stream where each of 4 sequences carries its OWN push constant + dispatch,
one `vkCmdExecuteGeneratedCommandsNV` runs all (4/4); (2) `[PIPELINE, PUSH_CONSTANT, DISPATCH]` + **indirect-bindable** pipelines
(`VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_2_INDIRECT_BINDABLE_BIT_NV` + `VkComputePipelineIndirectBufferInfoNV` metadata buf → `vkCmdUpdatePipelineIndirectBufferNV`
→ `vkGetPipelineIndirectDeviceAddressNV`) → the GPU-authored stream **switches PIPELINE per sequence** (4/4). The GPU authors its own
command buffer (Nanite-class). Token layout: `VkDeviceAddress` (PIPELINE) needs 8B align ⇒ stride 32. No regression (1418/44). **C5
FULLY CLOSED** (dispatch_indirect + DGC; only work graphs env-blocked).

<a id="memory-project_b17_oit_two_tiers_and_rtt_blend_capability"></a>
## project_b17_oit_two_tiers_and_rtt_blend_capability

---
name: project_b17_oit_two_tiers_and_rtt_blend_capability
description: B17 OIT COMPLETE — all 5 tiers (WBOIT/MBOIT/A-buffer static+atomic/stochastic) both backends; MBOIT 6-moment 18x win; value-returning atomics + stochastic transparency + GPU perf board shipped
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

**B17 (order-independent transparency) — ALL THREE tiers shipped + device-verified both backends (2026-07-19).**
Session log: `docs/sessions/2026-07-19-b17-oit.md`; accuracy board `docs/bench/2026-07-19-oit-tier-scoreboard.md`.

- **[✅ B17-a WBOIT]** (McGuire-Bavoil 2013, the cheap tier). Landed a NEW, broadly reusable gpu-context capability:
  **render-to-texture float MRT + per-attachment blend equations** (`IRasterContext::draw_wboit`). Vulkan =
  `vkCmdSetColorBlendEquationEXT` dynamic state; DX12 = `IndependentBlendEnable` static PSOs (`build_wboit_accum_pso` /
  `build_wboit_composite_pso`). accum RGBA16F additive + reveal R16F multiplicative → composite. This is the piece the
  whole post-processing / deferred / composite frontier needs (every prior draw forced blend OFF). Shaders +
  f16-aware oracle in `tests/gpu-shared/ckir_oit_test.hpp`. **To-ULP tier** (≤2 LSB: f16 accum + non-CR f32 divide).
- **[✅ B17-c A-buffer exact reference]** (Carpenter 1984). Two portable CKIR **compute** kernels in
  `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_oit.hpp` (`build_abuffer_store` + `build_abuffer_resolve`): deferred per-fragment
  store (static slot = fragment id) + per-pixel depth **sort network** + exact front-to-back `over` composite. Pure f32
  mul/add/sub, deterministic order, NO divide ⇒ **BIT-EXACT** vs `eval_cpu_kernel` and VK==DX12. The GROUND TRUTH the
  approximate tiers score against. Harness `tests/gpu-shared/ckir_abuffer_test.hpp`. Scoreboard: WBOIT is 14 LSB off exact.
- **[✅ B17-b MBOIT]** (Münstermann 2018, the hero tier): absorbance-weighted power-moment generation + the Peters-Klein
  Hamburger reconstruction (SCALAR transcription, because the compute-kernel emitter is scalar-only) → per-fragment
  `T=exp(-b₀·G(w))` → composite, over the shared deferred store. To-ULP. **Validated via the exact A-buffer gate** (why it
  was built first — see [feedback_bit_exact_blind_to_symmetric_bugs_energy_comp](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_bit_exact_blind_to_symmetric_bugs_energy_comp)).
  - **4-moment** (`oit::msm_hamburger_scalar`): resolves 2 depth masses EXACTLY ⇒ bit-exact at 2-layer (glass); beats WBOIT (30 LSB).
  - **6-moment** (`oit::msm_hamburger6_scalar`): the LIFT to high depth complexity — the Hamburger solve generalized to a
    4×4 Hankel Cholesky + a CUBIC root-solve (3 real roots via trig `acos`/`cos`) + a Gauss-Radau/Lagrange-weight form
    factor. Resolves 3 masses ⇒ **~1 LSB from exact at 3 layers where WBOIT is 18 off — an 18× win**, both backends.
  - **Exact-capacity = ⌊moments/2⌋ masses** — MBOIT BEATS WBOIT within its moment budget (6-moment 18× at 3 layers).
  - ⛔ **PRACTICAL CEILING MAPPED (both routes past 6-moment explored + REMOVED):** (1) **8-moment power = compile WALL** —
    full 5×5 Cholesky + Ferrari quartic + 5-node Gauss-Radau (math correct), but unrolled OR looped it's too big; the driver
    re-unrolls the constant-bound loop → never finishes compiling → MEASURED test hang. (2) **Trig moments = quality WALL** —
    the compact Fourier/Fejér reconstruction (depth→angle, integrated truncated Fourier series) compiles fast (no root-solve,
    scales to 12+ moments) but is too blurry: raw Fourier = Gibbs garbage (200 LSB), Fejér = bounded but plateaus ~80 LSB,
    LOSES to WBOIT (14). The exact-recovery Szegő trig needs root-finding → back on the compile wall. **6-moment power (3
    masses) is the ceiling of per-fragment moment OIT; beyond that use the EXACT A-buffer (shipped, bit-exact).** Untried
    lever for >3 power masses: per-pixel-hoisted reconstruction (Cholesky out of the loop + runtime layer-count) — an
    architecture change, not a formula change. **TRIED IT** — the runtime-loop + config-buffer architecture WORKS (diagnostic:
    a trivial reconstruction body runs instantly), but the 8-moment quartic body is too complex for the shader compiler EVEN
    EMITTED ONCE ⇒ the wall is reconstruction complexity, not unrolling. **6-moment (3 masses) is the DEFINITIVE ceiling; the
    exact A-buffer is the tool for arbitrary complexity.** (The runtime loop does scale FRAGMENT count/overdraw freely — a
    separate axis from masses-resolved.) **B17 = DONE, WBOIT beaten across the board.**
  - ⚠ CONDITIONING: at exactly N masses the (N+1)×(N+1) Hankel is rank-deficient → the regularizing `moment_bias` is
    CRITICAL. For 6-moment, bias `1e-2` is the sweet spot (both tames the cubic's GPU/CPU transcendental amplification AND
    improves accuracy 7→1 LSB). A speculative self-inclusion "fix" made it WORSE → reverted.

**[✅ B17-c SCALABLE — the three carry-forwards ALL SHIPPED (2026-07-19, both backends):**
- **Atomic linked-list A-buffer** — NEW **value-returning atomics** in CKIR (`atomic_add_fetch` node allocator +
  `atomic_exchange` list push; `AtomicResult` impure leaf materialized once). Race-built per-pixel lists, sort-resolved ⇒
  matches the static-slot exact reference **BIT-FOR-BIT** (worst |Δ|=0), VK==DX12. Gold node layout: one interleaved stride-5
  pool + parallel u32 `next` (≤8 bindings — see [feedback_ckir_gpu_dispatch_binding_cap_and_sort_unroll_explosion](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_ckir_gpu_dispatch_binding_cap_and_sort_unroll_explosion)).
- **Stochastic transparency** (Enderton 2010) — one kernel, S sub-samples, nearest hash-covered fragment, mean = the UNBIASED
  `over` estimate (E[stochastic]==exact A-buffer; converges ~1/√S; per-frame TAA = 1 sample/frame). DETERMINISTIC triple32
  hash ⇒ GPU==oracle **bit-exact** both backends (portable TAA history). Required fixing the oracle's u32 arithmetic →
  [feedback_ckir_oracle_u32_arithmetic_must_wrap_mod32](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_ckir_oracle_u32_arithmetic_must_wrap_mod32).
- **GPU perf board** `docs/bench/2026-07-19-oit-tier-perf.md` (`[.oit-bench]`, `last_gpu_ms` min-of-30, 1024²×4-layer): static
  store-based tiers cheapest (~0.28 ms) and **MBOIT's accuracy is FREE** (memory-bound hides the reconstruction); atomic list
  ~10× (3.0 ms, unbounded-depth price); stochastic cheapest unbounded tier per-frame (~0.061 ms @ S=1).

**B17 fully complete — 5 tiers, both backends, accuracy + perf boards, no loss recorded.** Next: B18 hair/fur. Related:
[feedback_ckir_binary_vec_scalar_shape_mismatch_gpu_broadcasts_oracle_oob](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_ckir_binary_vec_scalar_shape_mismatch_gpu_broadcasts_oracle_oob), [project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope](project-history.md#memory-project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope).

<a id="memory-project_b18e_dual_scatter_combination_unfinished"></a>
## project_b18e_dual_scatter_combination_unfinished

---
name: project_b18e_dual_scatter_combination_unfinished
description: "RESOLVED 2026-07-20 — Zinke Psi^G = T_f * S_f, and S_f is a DISTRIBUTION over incoming directions (a delta at n=0), so only the scalar T_f may multiply the direct lobe; fusing them renders the groom black"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

**RESOLVED 2026-07-20.** Kept because the failure mode is subtle, general, and easy to repeat.

**The bug.** `build_dual_scatter_kernel` returns `psi_g` and `f_back`, and the header comment says the caller combines
them as `Psi * f_s = Psi^G * (f_s + d_b * f_back)`. Read literally off that signature I wrote
`psi_g * (f_s + 0.7 * f_back)` — and every frame came out **black**.

**Why.** Zinke Eq 4: `Psi^G = T_f * S_f`. `T_f` (Eq 5) is a scalar transmittance `d_f * a_f^n`. But `S_f` (Eq 7) is a
**spread function — a distribution over incoming directions**, and the paper states outright that for a single
directional light at `n = 0` it "becomes a delta function `delta(w_d - w_i)`". `Psi^G` must therefore be **integrated
against f_s over w_i**. Evaluating it at the one light direction and using it as a scalar multiplier evaluates a delta
at its own centre and zeroes everything off the specular cone.

**The fix.** Only `T_f` multiplies the direct lobe. Compute it host-side from the moment LUT using the same nearest-bin
mapping the kernel uses — `bin = clamp((theta_d + pi/2)/pi * bins, 0, bins-1)`, `a_f = lut[bin*kLutStride + 0]`,
`T_f = 0.7 * pow(a_f, n)`. `f_back` IS pointwise (a local backscattering BCSDF, Eq 10-15) and is correct to add.
`T_f` already carries the shadow-path attenuation, so it REPLACES the raw DOM transmittance — using both double-counts.

**How to know it works** — do not trust the picture, check the ordering: light hair must scatter MORE than dark, which
is the entire reason the model exists. Platinum went from *darkest* (mean 0.144) to *brightest at the lowest exposure*
(0.255 at exposure 0.72, vs black 0.246 at 1.70).

**General lesson:** a kernel's signature tells you the shapes, not the measure. Before combining terms from a paper,
check which are scalars and which are **distributions requiring integration** — read the paper, not the interface.
Related: [feedback_hair_deferred_one_strand_per_pixel_is_line_art](rendering.md#memory-feedback_hair_deferred_one_strand_per_pixel_is_line_art), [feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor).


<!-- end-memory:project_b18e_dual_scatter_combination_unfinished -->

<a id="memory-project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal"></a>
## project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal

---
name: project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal
description: user wants to run Cerid modules (esp. hesap + numerical) in the browser via WASM/WebGPU with the right module integration
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 021fa904-7b98-4a07-9c4e-4f1cb715ea28
---

User aspiration (2026-05-22, reflective chat): **be able to run "all these stuff through the browser with the right modules to integrate"** — Cerid modules, especially the hesap numerical substrate, deployable to the browser, not just native.

This is a directional goal, not a scheduled phase yet. It should inform architecture choices NOW so the path stays open:

- **hesap core is a strong WASM candidate** — pure compute, no OS deps in the kernels; the custom TLSF allocator fits WASM's linear-memory model well.
- **Multi-width SIMD design pays off**: WASM SIMD is 128-bit only (`wasm-simd128` ≈ SSE/NEON, NOT AVX2/AVX-512). The existing scalar + SSE2/`Vec4f` fallbacks (already exercised in the full sweep) are the WASM path; AVX2 `Vec8f` microkernels won't translate. Keep those fallbacks healthy.
- **Biggest WASM hazard = `crd-jobs`**: the fiber job system uses a hand-rolled **asm context switch** that does NOT work in WASM. A browser target needs either a WASM-threads (SharedArrayBuffer + Web Workers, requires COOP/COEP headers) job backend or a single-threaded fallback. Flag this before any WASM commitment.
- **Browser GPU = WebGPU backend on `crd-rhi`**: the backend-agnostic RHI ("Vulkan first, multiple backends possible") is set up for a WebGPU backend; v17 GPU compute kernels could target it. This is the natural payoff of the RHI abstraction.
- **The agent-native CLI/RPC bet ([project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction](project-history.md#memory-project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction), Phase 4.0 `crd-cli` + `crd-rpc`) makes "browser as peer client" natural** — two deployment flavors, choose per module: (a) compile module to WASM, run in-tab (good for hesap/geometry/pure-compute); (b) thin browser client drives a native engine over RPC (good for heavy GPU/physics). The v18 notebook (`.cnb` `'CNBK'`) is the natural in-browser UI.


<!-- end-memory:project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal -->

<a id="memory-project_c6_cooperative_vector_device_enabled"></a>
## project_c6_cooperative_vector_device_enabled

---
name: project_c6_cooperative_vector_device_enabled
description: C6 DONE — VK_NV_cooperative_vector is enabled + GPU-verified on the RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (per-invocation matvec inference, the device half of the B10 neural-shading moat); the fp16 matmul supports ONLY an fp16-result combo
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

**C6 (cooperative-vector device enable) is DONE + GPU-verified (2026-07-22).** `VK_NV_cooperative_vector` (rev 4) is enabled on
the converged Vulkan device (`vulkan_context.cpp`, gated exactly like coopmat2 — a non-coopvec device is byte-identical). The
RTX 4070 Ti SUPER reports **coopvec=YES, training=YES, max_components=1024, all 14 stages (fragment incl. ⇒ per-pixel neural
shading), 16 matmul type-combinations**. Accessors on `IVulkanGpuContext`: `cooperative_vector()` / `cooperative_vector_training()`
/ `coopvec_max_components()` / `coopvec_supported_stages()`. Gate `[coopvec]` in `test_vulkan_context.cpp`: a real per-invocation
`coopVecMatMulNV` kernel (`GL_NV_cooperative_vector`, shaderc-compiled) dispatches == a CPU fp16 oracle to worst **0.00391**.

**coopvec vs coopmat (the architectural split):** coopmat (`VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2`, shipped — the NRC fused MLP + GEMM tier,
`emit_contract_coopmat2_glsl` / `ckir_mlp.hpp`) = WORKGROUP-cooperative M×N×K GEMM, emitted as whole-kernel templates because it
does NOT fit CKIR's per-invocation statement tier. **coopvec = PER-INVOCATION matrix×vector** (each pixel/thread runs its own small
MLP) ⇒ it DOES map onto the statement tier ⇒ B10 can be a real CKIR op class, not a template. This is the neural-shading path
(RTX Neural Shading / DLSS-style neural textures/materials). See [project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas](project-history.md#memory-project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas), [project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct](project-history.md#memory-project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct), [project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope](project-history.md#memory-project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope).

**⛔ SCARS (both cost real debug time):**
1. **fp16 matmul supports ONLY the {input f16, matrix f16, RESULT f16} combo.** The natural "fp16 weights, fp32 accumulate" model
   gives GARBAGE (worst 6551) — fp32 result is NOT a supported combo for fp16 input; the other 15 combos are int8/fp8 quantized
   (→ SINT32/fp16 results). ALWAYS enumerate `vkGetPhysicalDeviceCooperativeVectorPropertiesNV` (the `VkCooperativeVectorPropertiesNV[]`
   of {inputType, inputInterp, matrixInterp, biasInterp, resultType, transpose}) and pick a supported combo BEFORE writing the shader.
2. **Load/store/stride offsets are BYTES** (spec: load/store offset a multiple of 16, `matrixStride` a multiple of 16B, `matrixOffset`
   64B-aligned). RowMajor tightly-packed fp16 weights multiply correctly with byte offsets — **no optimal-layout conversion needed
   for CORRECTNESS**; `gl_CooperativeVectorMatrixLayoutInferencingOptimalNV` + `vkConvertCooperativeVectorMatrixNV` is a PERF lever
   for B10, not a requirement. GLSL API: `coopvecNV<T,N>`, `coopVecLoadNV(v,buf,byteOff)`, `coopVecMatMulNV(r,v,inInterp,matBuf,
   matByteOff,matInterp,M,K,layout,transpose,strideBytes)`, `coopVecStoreNV(r,buf,byteOff)`; enums Float16=0, RowMajor=0.

The toolchain (shaderc/glslang in VulkanSDK 1.4.341.1) compiles `GL_NV_cooperative_vector` cleanly (no offline compile).

**⭐⭐ B10 CORE + PERF CRUSH LANDED (2026-07-22).** `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_neural.hpp` (`crd::kir::neural`):
`emit_coopvec_mlp_glsl` = a config-keyed (`CoopVecMlpConfig`) PER-INVOCATION MLP (per layer `coopVecMatMulAddNV` matmul+bias +
component-wise ReLU, linear output, all fp16) + `emit_scalar_mlp_glsl` (the honest scalar-FMA baseline) + `eval_coopvec_mlp_cpu`
(matched-fp16 reference). Gate `[coopvec][neural]`: a 16→16×2→16 MLP == reference to worst 0.00027. **THE CRUSH (`[.coopvec-bench]`,
RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, GPU-timed min-of-6): a per-pixel MLP 16→32×3→16 over 1080p (2.07M invocations) runs in 0.204 ms (4893 fps,
31 TMAC/s) on the tensor units vs 2.547 ms hand-written scalar-FMA = 12.46× speedup**, outputs bit-identical fp16 (self-verifying).
Board `docs/bench/2026-07-22-coopvec-neural-shading-crush.md`. This is the per-invocation counterpart to the coopmat WORKGROUP GEMM
([project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas](project-history.md#memory-project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas)) — coopvec is what per-pixel neural materials need.

**✅ VISUAL NEURAL-MATERIAL CONSUMER (2026-07-22).** `emit_neural_material_render_glsl` + `neural_uv_encode`: a 2-D NEURAL FIELD
(16-D frequency-encoded uv → 32→32→3 MLP) CPU-trained with **Adam** to reproduce a target, then rendered per pixel in ONE fused
coopvec pass (input vector built by component assignment `a0[i]=float16_t(...)`, no memory round-trip) → `neural_material.bmp`.
**PSNR 38.9 dB; the fp16 tensor render tracks the fp32 net to 0.08 dB** (`[.neural-material]`). Recipe
`docs/recipes/2026-07-22-neural-material-coopvec-field.md`. ⛔ **SCAR: a neural field that under-fits reads as "correct STRUCTURE,
washed/wrong COLOURS" — it's TRAINING, not a render/layout bug.** Isolate with a CPU-fp32 forward PSNR (matched the bad GPU PSNR ⇒
training). Plain full-batch GD stalled at ~11 dB; **Adam (lr 0.01), same net/epochs → ~39 dB.** Also: frequency-encode the input or
spectral bias can't fit texture detail; fp16 render is NOT the accuracy bottleneck, convergence is.

**⏭ DX12 coopvec is ENV-BLOCKED (honest, not declined):** DirectX Cooperative Vectors needs HLSL `dx/linalg.h` (SM6.9 linalg lib) +
the D3D12 Cooperative-Vector tier (Agility SDK) + runtime — none present (DXC 1.9 compiles `cs_6_9` but no linalg header; no
`CooperativeVector` D3D12 feature in the Windows SDK; no Agility SDK). Documented like the WGSL-raster block. CUDA/Metal have no
per-invocation coopvec primitive (batched neural path there = the coopmat/WMMA fused MLP, `ckir_mlp.hpp`).

**✅ ON-DEVICE DIFFERENTIABLE TRAINING (2026-07-22) — the moat's defining claim, GPU-verified.** `emit_coopvec_linear_train_glsl`:
forward + loss-grad δ=2(y−t) + WEIGHT-grad outer product (`coopVecOuterProductAccumulateNV` → a **TrainingOptimal**-layout matrix,
MANDATORY layout) + BIAS grad (`coopVecReduceSumAccumulateNV`) ALL on the tensor path; host converts TrainingOptimal→RowMajor
(`vkConvertCooperativeVectorMatrixNV`, the HOST fn — takes host pointers, no cmd plumbing; query the TrainingOptimal byte size by
calling it with dstData=null) + applies SGD. Gate `[coopvec][neural][train]`: (a) on-device gradient == CPU ref (worst dW err
0.106 over ~256-batch accumulation — accumulates race-free across workgroups), (b) a 16×16 linear layer from W=0 → **loss
0.261→0.00004 (100% down, 150 steps) — it LEARNS.** ⛔ scar: **lr=0.8 → nan** (fp16 weight overflow on overshoot); a nan loss with
a PASSING step-0 gradient check = the optimizer, not the gradient (lr=0.1 converges). Multi-layer MLP composes this per layer with
transposed-matmul deltas. **B10 REMAINING (documented, not gaps):** inferencing-OPTIMAL weight layout (a forward perf lever) ·
multi-layer on-device backprop · NTC/neural-BRDF consumers (the neural material IS one). **B10 is GPU-complete on Vulkan** —
inference + 12.46× perf + visual material (38.9 dB) + on-device training.

CEIR-33 (the D7E "universal program editor") is **not** a UI framework to build. Per **ADR-0107 §D8**
it decomposes into TWO halves:

- **33a — the domain CONTRACTS the editors satisfy** (frame-graph / material / CKIR / CEIR-CHIR-graph
  authoring + round-trip/cook gates + hot-reload). This is substrate-side, autonomously drivable, and
  **largely already delivered** by the CEIR bands (`.frame.toml` ×23, `.crdm` ×6, `.ckir` ×42,
  `.chirgraph`/`.ceir` ×17, CEIR-10a hot-reload). The user's "D7E rides the finished substrate" model
  maps HERE. Geometry-graph + capture/profiling contracts are GAP-**until-consumed** — defining them
  before the I2D-9 widget exists is speculative invention.
- **33b — the editor WIDGETS themselves = the I2D programme's I2D-9** on the CR-D007 shell (I2D-4).
  NOT autonomously drivable: ADR-0107 is **"Proposed"** (pending user review) and I2D-1…4 (Canvas →
  Text → UiWorld → CR-D007) have **zero code** in the tree.

**Why:** the one non-obvious cross-cut — **CEIR-33's UI half, the §174-manifest L6 bar, and I2D-9 are
the SAME blocker.** `docs/capabilities/gpu-platform-capabilities.toml` header: *"L6 requires a CR-D007
inspection/authoring schema (band D7E, unstarted)."* So no feature reaches maturity L6, the §174 Q10
schema=2 migration cannot claim L6, and D7E cannot ship widgets — all until CR-D007 (I2D-4) lands. One
review (ADR-0107 acceptance) unlocks all three.

**How to apply:** if asked to "finish CEIR-33 / build the D7E editor," do NOT build a UI framework —
drive 33a (the contract inventory) and surface **Decision C** (C1 accept ADR-0107 → I2D-9; C2 scope
CEIR-33 to contracts + the L6 bar, lean C2 = D8's own text). Full orientation:
`docs/design/ceir-33-d7e-orientation-census.md`. Related: the CEIR-32b graph schema
([project_ceir_master_spine_locked](project-history.md#memory-project_ceir_master_spine_locked)) already delivers the CR-D007 program-graph contract. See also
[project_ceir_autonomous_loop_grant](project-history.md#memory-project_ceir_autonomous_loop_grant).

<a id="memory-project_ceir_band9_universality_validation_method"></a>
## project_ceir_band9_universality_validation_method

---
name: project_ceir_band9_universality_validation_method
description: How CEIR-9 proved universality — the reusable template for any substrate validation band
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: fade8ea4-87ca-470f-83e0-cdfe82a44e7f
  modified: 2026-08-09T21:44:54.296Z
---

CEIR-9 (BAND 9, closed 2026-08-10) validated the CEIR substrate's universality with a repeatable METHOD, not
a feature push: **one proof SLICE per domain, each slice a COMPOSITION of already-shipped foundation pieces
(never a new runtime), and one falsifiable question asked every single slice** — U-§97: *did this domain need
a second scheduler / compiler / runtime / depsgraph / transaction-manager / capability-system?* Eight slices
(9a notebook · 9b DAW · 9c DCC · 9d CAD · 9e EDA · 9f ECS · 9g agent · 9h a MANDATORY foreign external plugin),
U-§97 = **NO ×8**, with **zero engine-line changes** across the whole band — that zero is the band's falsifiable
claim (the only deltas were one stale-comment fix and one standing invariant gate ADDED, the U-§116 enum-pin).
The gate slice (9z) was DOC-SYNTHESIS only — no code, no gate test, no ADR — because each slice is already a
composition, so the existing test-suite × 4 configs IS the gate's executable half (contrast the 3z/4z/5z/8z
composition gates, which earned a test because their guarantees lived in separate tests that never met).

**Why:** a universal substrate is *defined* by "a new domain composes existing mechanisms + adds its own
types/attrs/locations/interfaces/caps/providers through open-world doors, reusing the one runtime" — so the
proof is N independent compositions each answering "no second engine", and the honest metric is engine-lines-
changed (target 0). Overclaiming ("proven") a domain you only argued is the failure mode; the mandate is to
name boundaries and never inherit a stale mid-band claim into the gate answer (the 8z re-verify discipline —
9z caught two stale rows against code).

**How to apply (future validation bands, and the CEIR consumer bands 10→35):** (1) one slice per domain, each a
~100-line test DRIVER through the substrate, not a bespoke runtime; (2) ask U-§97 at every slice and record the
verdict with its NAMED boundary (op-local vs module-wide, structural vs semantic, per-op vs per-location); (3)
tier every UNPROVEN domain by evidence, never as a result — ✅ proven (a driver ran) · ◧ foundation-validated
(mechanisms proven, no driver) · ◑ analogous-proven (shape proven by a sibling slice) · ○ future (space validated,
domain unbuilt); (4) the gate is synthesis (fill the matrix from evidence, re-verify rows vs code, tally the
verdicts, answer the final question) + confirm the existing suite green across all configs — not a new mega-test;
(5) state the SCALE boundary plainly (proof/mock scale here; production-scale accrues as the real domains get
built). Related: [project_ceir_master_spine_locked](project-history.md#memory-project_ceir_master_spine_locked) · [project_ceir_autonomous_loop_grant](project-history.md#memory-project_ceir_autonomous_loop_grant) ·
[feedback_solve_losses_never_document_and_accept](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_solve_losses_never_document_and_accept).

<a id="memory-project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor"></a>
## project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor

---
name: project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor
description: "The unified shader-representation vision — CKIR as the shared core, domain profiles, the node editor, and the capability ladder to author geometry kernels once."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 934ee96e-34fa-4239-87ad-44921a7d5a19
---

**THE VISION (user, 2026-07-08): one node-editable shader representation → all backends, for BOTH compute techniques AND
materials/VFX.** The honest architecture is LAYERED, not one flat language:

- **Shared CORE = the "shader representation language":** a typed expression DAG + control flow + the multi-backend
  EMITTERS (GLSL/HLSL/WGSL/MSL/CUDA), written ONCE. **This is CKIR (`crd-kir`)** — it already emits all 5 languages.
- **Domain PROFILES on top** (reuse the core + emitters):
  - **Compute profile (CKIR today):** standalone kernels over buffers — radix, morton, BVH build, software ray traversal,
    particle sim, physics → lower to COMPUTE shaders.
  - **Material/surface profile (NOT built):** dataflow producing surface props (albedo/normal/rough), plugged INTO the
    rendering pipeline's lighting model, run per-fragment with interpolants+samplers → lower to FRAGMENT/vertex shaders.
  - VFX = compute sim + material render; post-fx = fullscreen compute/fragment; hardware-RT = its own pipeline profile.
- **Node editor = a visual front-end that builds graphs in this representation**, with different PALETTES per profile
  (compute nodes for engineers, material nodes for artists). Same IR + same emitters underneath ⇒ "write OR node-edit →
  all backends" holds for every profile. Why compute vs material can't be ONE flat language: material needs rasterizer
  semantics (interpolants/samplers/lighting hooks) that a compute IR shouldn't carry — hence profiles over a shared core.

**WHY grow CKIR now = correct:** every capability added to express geometry kernels lands in the SHARED CORE, so the
material profile + node editor inherit it. Foundation, not throwaway; the multi-backend lowering is written once.

**⭐⭐ FORMALIZED as ADR-0101 (2026-07-09): "the IR is the single source of truth for EVERY shader; backend languages
are OUTPUTS only."** User mandate: fix the inconsistency where geometry `.comp` + rendering shaders are hand-written GLSL/
HLSL (backend-locked) — GLSL/HLSL/SPIR-V/DXIL must be EMITTED/cooked, never authored or stored. Deep look at frontier
engines grounded it: **Slang** (NVIDIA→Khronos: a language + IR → SPIR-V/DXIL/HLSL/GLSL/MSL/CUDA/WebGPU for compute AND
graphics — the exact vision, proven; THE prior art / north star), **MaterialX** (ASWF material-graph standard → ShaderGen
GLSL/OSL/MDL/MSL + a PBR surface node set; one generator/language, target-specialized), **Unreal** (material graph→HLSL
codegen, HLSL is a read-only view, permutations = the pain), **Unity ShaderGraph** (graph+Master-Stack→HLSL, variant/
keyword limit, Custom-Function inline-HLSL escape hatch DISABLES the SRP batcher = the portability tax). Lessons: IR is
the pivot; graph→codegen one-snippet-per-node; materials need a defined SURFACE model + shading models + domains; variants
are a real cost (minimize + spec-constants); an escape hatch must be explicitly non-portable ("opaque import"). **Phased
plan (ADR-0101): A** harden CKIR CORE (value types vecN/matN + structured control flow = RUNG 3 + full intrinsic library)
**· B** material profile (surface model + samplers + derivatives + vertex/fragment I/O) **· C** front-ends (node editor
↔IR + our text shader language → IR) **· D** storage/cook (IR-graph-as-crdr + emit+compile per backend → 'SHDR' chunks +
variants). ⭐ **RUNG 3 (control flow) = Phase A step 1** — it advances BOTH the compute LBVH goal AND the unified-shader-IR
fix (same shared core). Shader asset pipeline: IR graph in crdr (editable, source of truth) → cook → per-backend bytecode
in crdr → load → pipeline; GLSL never stored. See docs/decisions/0101-ir-is-source-of-truth-for-all-shaders.md.

**PROGRESS — Phase A step 1 DONE (intrinsic library, 2026-07-09).** Within Phase A the order is LOWEST-STRUCTURAL-RISK
FIRST (sanity): (1) intrinsics [done], (2) value types vecN/matN, (3) structured control flow. Added `KOp::{Pow, Step,
Fract, Clamp, Mix}` + the **ternary-node machinery** (`ternary()` builder, `apply_ternary`, `is_ternary` + eval branch —
reusable for Smoothstep + vec intrinsics). Emitters: explicit formulas for the EXACT ops (Fract=x-floor(x), Step,
Clamp=min(max), Mix=a*(1-c)+b*c) so GLSL/HLSL match the CPU bit-for-bit; `pow` = builtin (ULP transcendental, like
exp/log/sin). Validated: CPU F64 bit-exact (`tests/kir` `[intrinsics]`) + Vulkan F32 bit-exact for the algebraic 4 + pow
ULP (`tests/kir-vulkan` `[intrinsics]`). Suites: kir 118, kir-vulkan 32940, zero regression.

**A2 corpus + batch DONE (2026-07-09).** Deep-researched the FULL intrinsic corpus + stage model (CUDA compute primitives,
Unreal material nodes, GLSL/HLSL/MSL builtins, mesh-vs-geometry) → captured as `docs/systems/shader-ir-corpus-and-stages.md`
(living build reference: intrinsics by category × profile [C]core/[K]compute/[M]material + the stage model). ⭐ STAGE MODEL =
mesh-first, geometry-LEGACY (industry abandoned geometry shaders — low occupancy; mesh+task/amplification is the modern
path, DX12 2019 / VK `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` 2022). Implemented A2 batch: `Rsqrt/Exp2/Log2/Tan/Radians/Degrees` (unary),
`Atan2` (binary), `Smoothstep` (ternary) — backed by `crd::math::*`; emitters use builtins (transcendentals ULP) + explicit
radians/degrees. Vulkan ULP-tested; kir-vulkan 32948, zero regression. ⚠ run() n_inputs must match the graph's REACHABLE
inputs (smoothstep-of-y needs n_inputs=1 even if the KGraph declared 2). **A2 COMPLETE (2026-07-09):** added the tail `Asin/Acos/Atan/Sinh/Cosh` (unary,
ULP), `Mod` (binary, ULP — C-fmod: HLSL `fmod`, GLSL `a-b*trunc(a/b)`; ⚠ standard float-mod boundary sensitivity near
integer a/b, test with well-separated inputs), `Fma` (ternary, **BIT-EXACT** — GPU `fma()` = IEEE single-round = std::fma;
distinct from Mul+Add which is 2 roundings under `precise`). kir-vulkan 32966, zero regression. `cbrt` deferred (no
GLSL/HLSL builtin — needs sign·pow(abs,1/3) composition). ⭐ The full SCALAR intrinsic corpus is now DONE.
**A3 CPU/IR FOUNDATION DONE (2026-07-09):** vector value types. Added `KNode.comps` (1=scalar / 2/3/4=vecN; default 1 ⇒
fully backward-compat) + builders `vec2/vec3/vec_comp(extract)/dot/cross/normalize/vlength` + `unary/binary/ternary/select/
cast` propagate comps. Component storage = INTERLEAVED (`buf[e*comps+k]`); eval offset `numel*comps`; componentwise ops
loop flat over `nc=ne*comps`; Select is per-component (scalar cond); new eval branches for Vec2/Vec3/VecComp/Dot/Cross/
Normalize/VecLen. Bit-exact on the CPU oracle (`tests/kir` `[vec]`: vec3 construct/add/dot/cross/normalize/length); kir 119,
ZERO regression (comps=1 default). Also finished A2's `cbrt` (unary, emitted `sign·pow(abs,1/3)` — no GPU builtin). ⬜ A3
REMAINING: the GPU vecN EMITTER — make the elementwise emitter comps-aware (typed `vecN` temps + interleaved buffer I/O
`in[gid*comps+k]` + the vec-op emits: dot/cross/normalize/length builtins) + backend buffer sizing `numel*comps`. That's an
emitter rewrite (the structural GPU half of A3), a next slice.
**VECTOR corpus COMPLETE on CPU/IR (2026-07-09):** added `VecConcat` (concat two vecs → wider; the primitive) + `vec4` =
concat(vec3, w) [avoids needing a 4th KNode operand] + general `Swizzle` (arbitrary reorder/subset — `.x`/`.xy`/`.yzx`/
`.wzyx`, pattern stored in `perm[]`, comps=width). Bit-exact on the oracle (`tests/kir` `[vec]`: vec4 + v.yzx + v.xy).
kir 119, zero regression. So vec2/vec3/vec4 + construct + component-extract + arbitrary swizzle + dot/cross/normalize/
length + componentwise = the full VECTOR corpus in the IR. **MATRICES DONE on CPU/IR (2026-07-09):** mat3/mat4
built column-major via `VecConcat` of columns (so NO 4th KNode operand needed — mat3=9 comps, mat4=16); ops `mat_mul_vec`
(mat·vec), `mat_mul` (mat·mat), `mat_transpose` — NOT componentwise, dimension inferred from comps (9→3, 16→4). Bit-exact
on the oracle (`tests/kir` `[mat]`: mat3 mat·vec + transpose + mat·mat). kir 120, zero regression.
⭐⭐ **The FULL VALUE-TYPE CORPUS is now complete in the IR + oracle:** scalars (full intrinsic corpus) + vec2/vec3/vec4 +
construct + component-extract + arbitrary swizzle (.x/.xy/.yzx/.wzyx) + dot/cross/normalize/length + componentwise +
mat3/mat4 + mat·vec/mat·mat/transpose. "Whatever shaders can do" (value side) is expressible. ⬜ REMAINING A3: (1) the
**GPU vecN/matN EMITTER** — the whole vec/mat corpus is CPU/oracle-only so far; needs the comps-aware elementwise emitter
(vecN temps + interleaved I/O + vec/mat op builtins + backend buffer sizing) — the structural GPU slice; (2) nice-to-haves
reflect/refract, determinant/inverse, vec-relational (any/all/lessThan) — additive later. THEN **A4 control flow**
(if/for/while). Then Phase B (material profile: derivatives/texture/stages/PBR), C (node editor + text lang), D (cook).

**GAP-FILL batch DONE (2026-07-09):** audited IR vs the corpus doc + filled scalar/bit gaps — comparisons now COMPLETE
(added `CmpGt/CmpGe/CmpNe` alongside Lt/Le/Eq) + bit-op corpus filled (`BitNot`=~ · `BitCount`=popcount · `FindLSB`/
`FindMSB`=bit-scan · `BitfieldExtract`=(v>>off)&mask). All bit-exact on the CPU oracle (`tests/kir` `[bitops]`, ≤31-bit
positive so i64/i32 agree); GLSL builtins (bitCount/findLSB/findMSB) + HLSL (countbits/firstbitlow/firstbithigh); emitters
compile, kir 121 / kir-vulkan 32968, zero regression. ⚠ added to the MAIN elementwise switch only (the fused-GEMM-epilogue
switch falls back safely). REMAINING GAPS (audit): bit — `bitfieldInsert` (4 operands→needs KNode `d`), `bitfieldReverse`
(result-sign), reinterpret casts `floatBitsToInt`/`asfloat` (subtle in the f64-eval model), pack/unpack; common —
frexp/ldexp/modf (multi-output); geometric — distance/reflect/refract/faceforward (need vec, additive); vec-relational —
any/all; matrix — determinant/inverse/outerProduct. Plus the two STRUCTURAL pieces: the **GPU vecN/matN emitter** and
**A4 control flow**. SCALAR IR is now essentially complete; vec/mat IR complete on CPU (GPU emitter pending).

**FULL VALUE/MATH CORPUS COMPLETE on CPU/IR (2026-07-09) — GLM-class.** Researched GLM (the de-facto reference) + filled
all additive gaps in 3 batches, each bit-exact / consistency-validated on the oracle (kir 124, zero regression):
• **geometric**: reflect/refract/faceforward/distance + `Splat` (scalar→vecN, the scalar*vec enabler);
• **relational**: vany/vall (lessThan etc. = componentwise Cmp);
• **matrix**: outerProduct/determinant/inverse (general cofactor d≤4, column-major; det=25 exact, M·M⁻¹≈I);
• **interpolation + QUATERNIONS** (quat = vec4 (x,y,z,w), w=scalar): slerp (shortest-path + nlerp fallback near-parallel),
  nlerp=normalize(mix), quat_mul (Hamilton), quat_conj, quat_rotate (t=2·cross), quat_axis_angle, quat_to_mat3 — validated
  by CONSISTENCY (rotate≡mat·v, q·conj(q)≡identity, slerp(q,q)≡q; all pass ⇒ the formulas are mutually correct).
So the IR value/math vocabulary = GLM: scalars + vec2/3/4 + swizzle + geometric + relational + mat3/4 (+det/inv/outer) +
interp + quats.
**MINOR GAPS CLOSED (2026-07-09, oracle-validated, kir 126 / kir-vulkan 32968 zero-regression):** `bitfieldInsert`
(composed from Shl/Sub/BitAnd/BitNot/BitOr — no 4th operand needed), `BitReverse`, `Ldexp` (m·2^e exact), reinterpret
casts `FloatBitsToInt`/`IntBitsToFloat` (via memcpy; f32-roundtrip since inputs are F32-rounded — roundtrip=identity
verified), `Modf`→vec2(int,frac); + transform builders `translate`/`scale` (pure mat4/vec4 composition). ⬜ HONESTLY
DEFERRED (niche/low-value/consumer-level, NOT IR-capability gaps): `frexp` (exponent-extraction edge cases), pack/unpack
half (IEEE f16 encoding rabbit hole), `noise` (GLSL noise is deprecated — engines use texture-based), transforms
`rotate`/`perspective`/`ortho`/`lookAt` (SAME compose-pattern as translate/scale — trivial consumer sugar, add on demand).
⭐⭐ The IR value/math corpus is now COMPLETE. The 2 STRUCTURAL pieces are THE remaining critical path: the **GPU vecN/matN
EMITTER** (the whole vec/mat/quat corpus is CPU-oracle-only — nothing runs on GPU yet) + **A4 control flow** (if/for/while).

**GPU VEC EMITTER — STARTED, vec2/3/4 PROVEN on Vulkan (2026-07-09).** Added `emit_vec_glsl` (comps-aware: vecN/matN temps
via `vtype(comps)`, INTERLEAVED buffer I/O `in[gid*comps+k]`, GLSL builtins for vec/mat ops) + `GlslKernel.in_comps[]/
out_comps` + `is_vec_fusable` + `graph_uses_vec` routing in kir-vulkan run() (reuses dispatch_glsl with numel*comps byte
counts; element count = shape.numel(), comps separate). PROVEN: vec3 construct+cross+add+normalize on Vulkan, ULP vs float
ref (`tests/kir-vulkan` `[vec]`). kir-vulkan 32970, zero regression (isolated from the scalar emitter). ⛔ FINDING: mat
construction via VecConcat BREAKS on GPU — mat3=concat(concat(c0,c1),c2) makes a comps=6 intermediate with NO GLSL type
(vec6 doesn't exist); vec4=concat(vec3,float) is fine (valid GLSL). ⬜ MAT-GPU NEEDS a native `MatFromCols` op (emit
`mat3(c0,c1,c2)` directly; rebuild mat3/mat4 on it) + a vec/mat-INPUT declaration (`g.input` is comps=1 only). Then
mat*vec/mat*mat/det/inv (already in emit_vec, GLSL builtins) run on GPU. THEN quats/slerp GPU (helper funcs — no builtins),
HLSL/DX12 vec emitter, then **A4 control flow**.

**MATRICES ON GPU — DONE (2026-07-09).** Added `KOp::MatFromCols` (mat3 from 3 vec3 columns → emits `mat3(c0,c1,c2)`
directly, no comps-6 intermediate; rebuilt `mat3()` on it — CPU eval + tests still green) + `input_vec(sh,dt,comps)` (vec/
mat inputs, comps>1, interleaved). PROVEN on Vulkan: mat3 construct + `mat_mul_vec` + `mat_mul` + `mat_inverse` (M·M⁻¹·v≈v)
via `[mat]` test; CPU 126, kir-vulkan 32973, zero regression. ⭐ GPU vec/mat emitter now covers vec2/3/4 + all vec ops
(dot/cross/normalize/geometric) + mat3 (construct/mat·vec/mat·mat/transpose/det/inverse).

**GPU VEC/MAT/QUAT EMITTER COMPLETE on Vulkan (2026-07-09).** Added: (a) 4th KNode operand `d` (threaded through ALL
reachability walks — emit_vec/emit_elementwise/graph_uses_vec/run_graph/build_mini + optimize reach/hash/CSE; hash+CSE also
now include `comps` [was a latent CSE bug]; const-fold skips comps>1); `MatFromCols` extended to mat4 (4 cols via d) →
mat4 in-shader construct on GPU. (b) quats/slerp GPU via EMITTED HELPER FUNCTIONS (`crd_qmul/qconj/qrot/qaa/qmat/slerp`,
emitted once in a prelude when the graph uses them — no GLSL builtins exist). (c) VecAny/VecAll → `any/all(notEqual(v,0))`.
PROVEN on Vulkan (`[vec]`/`[mat]`): mat4·vec4, quat rotate≡mat3·v, slerp compiles+runs, any/all; CPU 126, kir-vulkan 32979,
zero regression. ⭐⭐ The ENTIRE vec/mat/quat/interp corpus now RUNS on Vulkan (author-once from the IR).

**FAN-OUT TO DX12 — vec corpus DONE (2026-07-09).** Added `emit_vec_hlsl` (comps-aware HLSL: float2/3/4 temps, interleaved
`RWStructuredBuffer<float>` I/O, HLSL builtins [rsqrt/frac/lerp], emitted quat helpers [crd_qmul/qconj/qrot/qaa/slerp]) +
`graph_uses_vec` + routing in kir-dx12 run(). vec2/3/4 + all vec ops + quats/slerp/any-all run on DX12; PROVEN vec3

**CAPABILITY LADDER to author geometry kernels in CKIR (grounded in the actual IR 2026-07-08):** CKIR already has
I32/I64 + Cast + ScanSum/Scatter/Gather/Contract, but lacked bit ops, atomics, control flow.
- **Rung 1 — bit ops: ✅ DONE + RUNS ON GPU (2026-07-08).** Added `KOp::{Shl,Shr,BitAnd,BitOr,BitXor}` (integer bitwise,

  the backends copy raw bytes with a 4-byte UAV stride — no dispatch change; the readback lands the i32 bits in the f32
  slot, the test `memcpy`s them back to u32. Suites green: kir-vulkan 32930, kir-dx12 30793, kir 115. NEXT: the WGSL/MSL/
  CUDA emitters (mechanical, same edits — NOT validatable on this machine); then rung 2 (atomics → radix).
- **Rung 2 — atomics: ✅ 2a DONE + RUNS ON GPU (2026-07-08).** Added `KOp::ScatterAdd` (atomic scatter-add / histogram:
  `out[M]=0` then `out[idx[i]] += updates[i]`) — IR + builder + CPU interpreter + GLSL (`atomicAdd`) + HLSL
  (`InterlockedAdd`) emitters + kir-vulkan/kir-dx12 routing. ⭐ INTEGER atomics are order-independent ⇒ bit-exact +
  run-to-run deterministic, so the determinism moat SURVIVES (float atomics would not). Zero-init: Vulkan pre-zeros the
  host-visible output (map+memset); DX12 gets it free (committed resources are zero-initialized by spec). Proven bit-exact
  on CPU + Vulkan + DX12 (`tests/kir/test_ckir_bitops.cpp` + kir-vulkan/kir-dx12 `[atomics]`). idx/updates are Input leaves
  (a computed digit is a prior elementwise kernel). Integer GPU inputs are bit-reinterpreted into the f32 upload slots.
  Suites green: kir 116, kir-vulkan 32932, kir-dx12 30795.
- **Rung 2b — radix SORT COMPOSES from the CKIR op set: ✅ PROVEN (CPU oracle, 2026-07-08).** Used the classic scan-based
  STABLE SPLIT (1 bit/pass, deterministic — NO atomic position allocation): biti=(k>>bit)&1; f=1-biti; e=exclusive_scan(f);
  tf=Σf; pos = biti ? tf+i-e : e; k=scatter(k,pos,k). 20 passes → output matches `std::sort` (`tests/kir` `[radix]`). So the
  op set {bit ops, ScanSum, ReduceSum, Broadcast, Iota, Select, Scatter} is SUFFICIENT for a full sort. ⛔⛔ ARCHITECTURAL
  FINDING (the real blocker): radix sort is inherently MULTI-KERNEL (histogram/scan/scatter phases with global barriers,
  repeated per digit), but CKIR's `run()` executes ONE kernel per call — the emit fns require Input leaves, so
  `Scatter(scan(...),...)` can't be one GPU dispatch. **The gating GPU enabler is now the MULTI-KERNEL SCHEDULER (v17-e):
  lower a multi-op graph → a SEQUENCE of kernels with on-GPU intermediate buffers (no CPU round-trips). This unblocks radix
  sort AND LBVH on GPU — bigger than rung 3.** Atomic histogram (2a) is still the fast-radix building block once the
  scheduler exists.
- **★ MULTI-KERNEL SCHEDULER (v17-e) — CORE BUILT + PROVEN on GPU (2026-07-08).** `KirBackendVulkan::run_graph()` executes
  an arbitrary multi-op graph as a SEQUENCE of kernels in ONE command buffer with on-GPU intermediate buffers (no CPU
  round-trips). Design: (1) reachability from output; (2) MATERIALIZE graph Inputs + non-fusable ops + operands-of-non-
  fusable (elementwise cones fuse between the boundaries); (3) ascending node-id == topo order (operands precede
  consumers); (4) per materialized node, `build_mini` clones its kernel cone into a fresh KGraph with boundaries as Input
  leaves (added `KGraph::clone`) → reuse EVERY existing emitter unchanged; (5) buffers: Input=CpuToGpu upload,
  output=GpuToCpu readback, else GpuOnly intermediate; (6) record dispatch+barrier per kernel, one submit, readback. PROVEN:
  `ScanSum(Mul(x,y))` runs as a 2-kernel GPU pipeline, Mul result stays on-GPU, BIT-EXACT vs the f32 reference
  (`tests/kir-vulkan` `[scheduler]`). kir-vulkan suite 32934 green. Op coverage: elementwise + ScanSum + ScatterAdd
  + ReduceSum + Broadcast + Iota + Scatter (added emit_broadcast_glsl + emit_iota_glsl; scheduler branches for each).
- **★★ FULL RADIX SORT RUNS ON GPU as ONE multi-kernel pipeline (2026-07-08) — the payoff.** The entire 16-pass scan-based
  stable-split radix sort, authored as ONE CKIR graph (~272 nodes → ~112 kernels), runs through `run_graph` in a SINGLE
  command buffer with ALL intermediates on-GPU, BIT-EXACT vs `std::sort` (`tests/kir-vulkan` `[radix][scheduler]`).
  KEY TRICK: keys are F32 holding EXACT integer values (16-bit ≤ 2^24 exact), casting to I32 only for the transient
  bit-extraction — so scan/reduce/broadcast/scatter all use the FLOAT emitters (no int-dtype surgery needed); the
  elementwise emitter's dtype-awareness handles the Cast(F32↔I32)+bit-ops cone. A real, complete multi-kernel algorithm
  authored once in CKIR → GPU pipeline. kir-vulkan 32936 green. ⚠ scatter is O(N²) output-centric (fine ≤ small N; a fast
  input-centric permutation-scatter is a perf follow-up); ~112 kernels recompiled per call (a GLSL-hash pipeline cache is
  a follow-up). NEXT: fan run_graph to DX12 (same design, HLSL emit); then rung 3 (control-flow → build_tree) → full LBVH.
- **Rung 3 — control flow (loop/if)** → build_tree, ray traversal.

**Second dispatch backend already shipped:** D3D12 `IComputeContext` (see [project_compute_rendering_separation](project-history.md#memory-project_compute_rendering_separation)).

<a id="memory-project_cholesky_smalln_rowmajor_limit"></a>
## project_cholesky_smalln_rowmajor_limit

---
name: cholesky-smalln-rowmajor-limit
description: "WHY Cerid's small-N (≤256) dense Cholesky trails Eigen ~1.4× — it's a row-major-vs-column-major data-layout fit, proven by 3 controlled experiments. Not a kernel-quality gap."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8232c613-08b5-412f-9d51-73f8c05a65d9
---

Small-N dense Cholesky (N≤256, f64) sits at ~0.50–0.94× of Eigen-MT and
that is **near the practical ceiling for our row-major layout**. This was
investigated deeply (2026-05-20, v0e-perf-attack) by reading Eigen's
source + running 3 controlled experiments.

**Why (causal, evidence-backed):**

Eigen's unblocked Cholesky (`Eigen/src/Cholesky/LLT.h:332`) updates each
column as `A21 -= A20·A10ᵀ` — a **column-major gemv**. Eigen's gemv
(`GeneralMatrixVector.h:156`) tiles the output into 8-packet register
chunks, sweeps all columns inside, writes the accumulator ONCE, no
horizontal sums, contiguous column-major loads. Cholesky's natural access
is **column-oriented**, so Eigen's column-major-native layout makes the
matrix operand contiguous *for free*.

Cerid is **row-major** (pinned by ADR/D21 — the whole matrix catalog,
solve, BLAS surface assume it). The same column update in row-major is
either rs row-dots (one `horizontal_sum` each) or strided column access.

Three experiments (all REGRESSED vs the simple per-row dot):
1. **Per-row SIMD dot** (row-major, register-accumulated): 0.94/0.70/0.55
   at N=64/128/256 — the BEST. MSVC compiles it extremely tightly;
   contiguous-row access is cache/prefetch-perfect.
2. **Naive column-major axpy** (copy to col-major scratch, 1 column at a
   time): 0.75/0.45/0.39 — WORSE. The accumulator column is written k
   times (RMW per prefix column).
3. **Register-tiled column-major gemv** (Eigen's exact structure —
   accumulator hoisted to registers, written once, no hsum): 0.78/0.43/0.40
   — STILL WORSE. At small N the per-tile column-sweep touches k columns
   spanning k×n stride (cache-unfriendly), plus the O(n²) copy-in/out
   overhead, and MSVC's tight codegen on the simple dot wins.

**Conclusion:** the gap is the row-major-vs-column-major *layout fit* for
Cholesky's column-oriented access, NOT a kernel-quality deficiency.
Closing it would require either (a) storing Cholesky factors column-major
(violates the row-major architecture, ripples through solve + catalog), or
(b) hand-tuned asm (ADR-0082 rules out for general substrate). Both are
out of scope. **Per-row dot is the right answer for row-major small-N.**

Where we DO win: Cholesky N≥512 (packed parallel syrk: 0.84× at 512,
1.41× at 1024), and LDLT/QR/LU broadly. The bench is fair — both Cerid
and Eigen allocate per iter (Eigen's LLT ctor allocates too).

Related: [feedback_register_tiling_needs_packing](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_register_tiling_needs_packing),
[project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision).


<!-- end-memory:project_cholesky_smalln_rowmajor_limit -->

<a id="memory-project_cholmod_factor_gap"></a>
## project_cholmod_factor_gap

---
name: cholmod-factor-gap
description: "hesap sparse-direct supernodal Cholesky LOSES to SuiteSparse CHOLMOD ~2-4x on factor at scale; gap is per-thread BLAS-3 kernel efficiency, not parallelism. The Eigen-SimplicialLLT crush was a WEAK peer."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a9e2b042-249d-4290-abf9-3c707236fa70
---

Measured 2026-05-29 (v5a CHOLMOD oracle, fair bench — both timed full symbolic+numeric, matched threads, both on OpenBLAS, Linux Release): Cerid's tree-parallel supernodal Cholesky **loses to CHOLMOD** on factor at scale.

- FACTOR cerid/cholmod @8thr→@1thr: bcsstk25 1.25→1.04 WIN · hood 0.66→0.55 · ldoor 0.45→0.45 · bmwcra_1 0.24→0.38. SOLVE x16 loses everywhere (0.36–0.72×). We WIN only the cache-resident bcsstk25.
- **The gap is PRIMARILY per-thread efficiency**: at 1 thread we're 0.38–0.61× (2–2.6× slower/thread) EVEN THOUGH CHOLMOD carries MORE fill (115M vs our 96M on bmwcra) ⇒ its flop-rate is ~2.5–3× ours. Parallel scaling is a SECONDARY, matrix-specific lever (only bmwcra scales worse 0.38→0.24 — few huge supernodes; CHOLMOD BLAS-threads INSIDE a supernode, we only tree-parallelize).

**Why:** Eigen `SimplicialLLT` (what v5a-1b/v5a-3 benched against, where we showed 1.5–6× "crush") is a SCALAR SIMPLICIAL solver — a weak peer for a supernodal lib. CHOLMOD is the real gold standard (Davis et al., 20 yrs of BLAS-3 tuning; the engine behind MATLAB chol / Eigen CholmodSupernodalLLT / scikit-sparse).

**Why:** the whole hesap premise (user mandate) is "beat and crush ALL frontier libraries"; reference impls are the FLOOR not the ceiling ([reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor)). So v5a is NOT closed as a crush — it's a known loss to be crushed (no shortcuts).

**How to apply:** when claiming a hesap "crush", bench against the CORRECT-CLASS peer ([bench_against_the_correct_peer](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_against_the_correct_peer)) — for supernodal direct that's CHOLMOD, not Eigen-simplicial. The planned crush is v5a-4 (phase doc), measured levers in containment order: (1) `cmod` uses a full `gemm` where the symmetric diagonal block wants `syrk` (2× the diagonal flops); (2) panel BLAS-3 microkernel vs OpenBLAS `dgemm` at supernode-panel sizes; (3) within-supernode (BLAS-thread the big panels) parallelism for bmwcra-type; (4) maybe more aggressive amalgamation (CHOLMOD trades +fill for bigger panels). RE-MEASURE vs the CHOLMOD oracle after each lever. Oracle setup: [cholmod-oracle-and-wsl-build](build-and-verification.md#memory-reference_cholmod_oracle_and_wsl_build).

**Bench-fairness lesson:** when racing a one-shot factor against a lib that splits analyze/factorize (CHOLMOD), time the SAME phases on both — the advisor caught `cholmod_analyze` hoisted OUT of the timing loop while Cerid timed symbolic+numeric (unfair to Cerid). Fixed by timing analyze+factorize together. (The realistic factor-once-solve-many comparison is numeric-only-both, which needs a Cerid analyze/numeric split — not yet built.)

<a id="memory-project_ckir_material_lowering"></a>
## project_ckir_material_lowering

---
name: project_ckir_material_lowering
description: "D-007 B7 COMPLETE — the material LOWERING compiler lives in engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_lower.hpp (namespace crd::kir::lower): frequency classification (Constant/Uniform/Vertex/Fragment cheapest-correct-stage), lower/lower_entry (wraps the semantics-preserving KGraph::optimize = const-fold+DCE+CSE), uniform_boundary (hoist analysis), and specialize (static switch → ShaderOption variant via KGraph::pin_const/alias). Every transform is round-trip BIT-STABLE."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 40e3ad67-a505-447d-89df-272b48c237f6
---

**B7 (the material lowering compiler) is COMPLETE (2026-07-12).** `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_lower.hpp`, namespace
`crd::kir::lower`. It turns an authored material graph into a stage-classified, optimized, variant-ready program — every
transform ROUND-TRIP BIT-STABLE (the lowered material evaluates identically; proven on the CPU oracle AND pixel-identical
both backends: a lowered B6 overlay renders 57,36,14 / 244,227,210 == un-lowered).

**What it provides:**
- `Frequency`{Constant·Uniform·Vertex·Fragment} + `classify(g, entry, out[])` — each node's CHEAPEST CORRECT STAGE. Leaf
  rules: `Const`→Constant; `UniformBlock`/`Texture`/`Sampler`→Uniform; a `Builtin` by its `builtin_info().stages`
  (VertexIndex→Vertex, FragCoord→Fragment); `StageIn`→Vertex in a VS / Fragment in an FS; interior = MAX of inputs, pinned
  to Fragment by `is_fragment_forcing` (the derivatives + implicit-LOD `TexSample` + `StorageLoad`). `entry_frequency` folds
  the entry sinks. (Frequency IS ADR-0102's variability axis — the `UniformBlock.dset` is the frame/pass/material/object slot.)
- `lower(g, roots, n)` — wraps the pre-existing semantics-preserving `KGraph::optimize` (const-fold → DCE → CSE hash-cons).
  `lower_entry(g, e)` gathers an entry's live roots (position/frag_depth/discard/shading_rate/storage/colour outputs), lowers,
  writes the renumbered ids back — the ONE call a cook/renderer makes before `create_program(g, e)`.
- `uniform_boundary(g, e, freq, seen, out, cap)` — the maximal Uniform-frequency subexpressions consumed on the per-fragment
  path (the value-neutral HOIST sites). B7 owns this classification; the physical VS-flat-varying / uniform-buffer
  materialization lands with B8's cook + renderer plumbing.
- `specialize(g, option, value, roots, n)` — pin a `ShaderOption` selector to a compile-time constant (new
  `KGraph::pin_const`), const-fold it into the switch conditions, then `fold_static_branches` collapses each static-cond
  `Select` to its chosen branch (new `KGraph::alias` — copy the branch node into the select slot; CSE merges, DCE reclaims
  the dead branch). Yields a smaller VARIANT bit-identical to the runtime switch. The full permutation matrix + dedup is **D3**.

**Two new KGraph primitives (ckir.hpp):** `pin_const(node, value)` (overwrite a node to a `Const` in place — specialization)
and `alias(node, target)` (copy target's KNode into node — branch elimination; target is always an operand so no forward
ref). Both are the same in-place node rewrite `optimize()` already does internally; compute byte-exact HELD (33010/30821).

Consumers: **B8** lowers a CKIR material via `lower_entry` into the `MaterialTemplate`/cook path + the shared lighting
library (GGX + clustered + shadow/CSM). See [project_ckir_materialx_node_library](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_materialx_node_library), [project_ckir_material_surface_contract](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_material_surface_contract),
[project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor](project-history.md#memory-project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor), [project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu](project-history.md#memory-project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu).


<!-- end-memory:project_ckir_material_lowering -->

<a id="memory-project_ckir_material_surface_contract"></a>
## project_ckir_material_surface_contract

---
name: project_ckir_material_surface_contract
description: "B5 fixed the CKIR material contract — a material outputs an OpenPBR SURFACE STRUCT and does NOT light (lighting is B8); the deferred G-buffer packing lives in engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_material.hpp, and the surface struct is APPEND-ONLY (reconcile with the shipped renderer SurfaceData)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 40e3ad67-a505-447d-89df-272b48c237f6
---

**The material contract (D-007 B5, ADR-0102 D3), fixed 2026-07-12.** A CKIR **material** is a fragment graph that outputs
an **OpenPBR surface-parameter struct** and does **NOT** compute lighting — "material = surface response; render path =
lighting technique." The shared lighting library (GGX BRDF + clustered light loop + shadow/CSM) that CONSUMES the surface
is **B8**, NOT B5; the full Forward+/Deferred pipelines + light-culling are the post-hesap rendering phase. Do not add
BRDF/light-loop code to a material — it only emits surface params.

**Where it lives:** `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_material.hpp` (namespace `crd::kir::material`) — the material-profile
layer on top of core CKIR. It owns:
- The canonical **OpenPBR 1.1 slab** `enum SurfaceField` (~37 fields: base · specular · transmission · subsurface · coat ·
  fuzz/sheen · thin-film · geometry · emission) + `define_surface` / `surface_defaults` (spec defaults) / `build_surface_full`.
- `ShadingModel`{Standard·Unlit·Toon·Cel·Gooch·Outline·Hatching} + `AlphaMode`{Opaque·Masked·Translucent·Additive} tags.
- The **deferred G-buffer packing**: `pack_gbuffer` (compact 4 MRT: base+metallic · enc_normal+roughness · emissive+occlusion
  · opacity+shading_model+alpha_mode) and `pack_gbuffer_ext` (8 MRT, carries every slab layer). Normal is encoded n*0.5+0.5
  for the UNORM attachment. `set_masked` does the alpha-test discard (via the B1-b `KEntry::discard_cond`).

**⛔ APPEND-ONLY.** `SurfaceField` order IS the on-wire G-buffer layout every material + the future lighting pass agree on
(and it must stay reconciled with the shipped renderer `SurfaceData` in `engine/renderer/include/crd/renderer/surface_data.glsl.inc`,
whose stability rule is "never remove/reorder; new fields default 0"). Append new OpenPBR fields at the END only.

**Device substrate B5 added: MRT (multiple render targets)** — `IGBufferTarget` / `create_gbuffer_target(w,h,N)` /
`draw_gbuffer` in the gpu-context (Vulkan: dynamic-rendering N colour attachments + N-attachment blend/write dynamic state;
DX12: N RTVs in one heap + a PSO with `NumRenderTargets=N`, RT-count baked into the pso_for cache key). This is the deferred
substrate B8's lighting pass reads.

**Taxonomy reconciliation (from ADR-0046/0048/0102):** `MaterialDomain`{Surface·PostProcess·Compute·Decal·UI} is FROZEN and
is the OWNING-system axis, NOT opaque/masked. The opaque/masked/transparent axis is the renderer's `AlphaMode`
(pass_type.hpp, frozen at 3 values; "additive" is a new/append value). The CKIR `ShadingModel` enum is fresh (none existed).
The arc: **B5 (surface) → B6 (MaterialX node library) → B7 (graph→IR lowering + stage split) → B8 (renderer integration +
lighting library)**. See [project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu](project-history.md#memory-project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu), [project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor](project-history.md#memory-project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor),
[project_compute_rendering_separation](project-history.md#memory-project_compute_rendering_separation).


<!-- end-memory:project_ckir_material_surface_contract -->
