## project_ckir_materialx_node_library

---
name: project_ckir_materialx_node_library
description: "D-007 B6 COMPLETE — the MaterialX-parity CKIR node library (~90 nodes) lives in engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_nodes.hpp (operators/shapes/geometric/UV/NPR) + ckir_noise.hpp (perlin/cell/worley/fractal); each a value-graph builder faithfully transcribed from MaterialX genglsl/nodegraph source, bit-exact on the CPU oracle + observable pixel-identical both backends"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 40e3ad67-a505-447d-89df-272b48c237f6
---

**B6 (the MaterialX-parity node library) is COMPLETE (2026-07-12).** Two headers, one namespace `crd::kir::nodes`:

- **`engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_nodes.hpp`** — OPERATOR (math · logical `logical_and/or/not/xor` · conditional
  `ifgreater/ifgreatereq/ifequal/switch5` · channel `combine/extract/convert` · adjustment `remap/smoothstep/luminance
  (ACEScg)/rgbtohsv/hsvtorgb/contrast/range/saturate/hsvadjust` · compositing `mix/plus/minus/difference/burn/dodge/screen/
  overlay/disjointover` + Porter-Duff `over/comp_in/comp_out/mask/matte` + `inside/outside/premult/unpremult` · convolution
  `heighttonormal`), SHAPES (`ramplr/ramptb/splitlr/splittb/checkerboard`), GEOMETRIC (`position/normal/tangent/bitangent/
  texcoord/geomcolor` — thin `stage_in` wrappers), UV (`rotate2d/rotate3d/place2d`(SRT+TRS)/`triplanar_weights`+`triplanar`),
  NPR (`viewdirection/facingratio/gooch_shade`).
- **`ckir_noise.hpp`** (`crd::kir::nodes::noise`) — `perlin2/perlin3 · cell2/cell3 · fractal2/fractal3 · worley2/worley3`
  (all 4 metrics + both styles), a faithful port of MaterialX `mx_noise.glsl` (the OSL oslnoise subset).

**Each node is a value-graph BUILDER** `int node(KGraph& g, int a, …)` composing core KOps (the style of
[project_ckir_material_surface_contract](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_material_surface_contract)'s surface builders). **NO new KOps were needed** — the op set was already complete.

**Conformance methodology (how "bit-exact vs MaterialX" is met):** B6 is a CONFORMANCE library, not a perf crush —
MaterialX's published genglsl/nodegraph reference IS the definition. Each node is a faithful transcription of that reference's
exact op sequence (constants fetched from MaterialX source via curl — floor-`mod`, ACEScg luma, overlay bg-pivot,
`M_FLOAT_EPS=1e-8`, the OSL Bob-Jenkins hash), verified **bit-exact on CKIR's own F64 CPU oracle** (`tests/kir/test_ckir_nodes
.cpp` + `test_ckir_noise.cpp`, C++ ports of the reference) AND **observable pixel-identical on both GPU backends**
(`tests/gpu-context-{vulkan,dx12}`). Key transcription facts: per-channel-branched blends (burn/dodge/overlay) decompose to
scalar-per-channel because core `Select` takes a SCALAR condition (not a `bvecN`); the 32-bit hash runs on the f64/i64 IR via
split-rotl + `&0xFFFFFFFF` wraparound with U32-typed nodes. **B6 adds NO device features** (pure value-graph logic on the
already-clean raster path) so validation is inherited.

**Surfaced [feedback_raster_emitters_lag_compute_wire_both_and_uint_suffix](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_raster_emitters_lag_compute_wire_both_and_uint_suffix)** (2 emitter bugs the GPU caught, CPU oracle
couldn't). Consumers: **B7** lowers a material graph → IR (per-vertex/fragment stage split, const-fold/DCE, static
switch→variant); **B8** feeds it the shared lighting library + renderer. See [project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor](project-history.md#memory-project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor),
[project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu](project-history.md#memory-project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu), [project_ckir_material_surface_contract](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_material_surface_contract).

<a id="memory-project_clouds_and_oracle_memo_ckir"></a>
## project_clouds_and_oracle_memo_ckir

---
name: project_clouds_and_oracle_memo_ckir
description: "D-007 B15-b: volumetric clouds (Nubis/Schneider) in CKIR (ckir_clouds.hpp) — the GOLD industry-standard PERLIN-WORLEY density, fully procedural + portable across ALL 5 backends + Vulkan bit-exact (NO baked-texture crutch). SIX general CKIR wins: (1) recursive CPU oracle now MEMOIZES; (2) BitOr/And/Xor of BOOL operands emit ||/&&/!= not bitwise; (3) UNROLLED 27-cell Worley is GPU-un-compilable → worley3_loop emits a RUNTIME LOOP (bit-exact, order-independent min); (4) the compute-kernel GLSL emitter's statement path is SCALAR-ONLY (vec3/dot/swizzle are raster-only) → scalarize; (5) a value shared across sibling For-bodies must be stmt_materialize'd at top level; (6) the CUDA/MSL/WGSL compute emitters lacked CSE (inline-expand) → deep DAGs OOM → gave them the GLSL decl/matd pass."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**D-007 B15-b — VOLUMETRIC CLOUDS (Nubis, Schneider 2015/2023), in CKIR (2026-07-15).** Closes B15 (atmosphere + clouds).
`engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_clouds.hpp` (namespace `crd::kir::clouds`), statement-tier compute, both Vulkan bit-exact.
- **`build_cloud_density`** — the industry-standard **PERLIN-WORLEY** base (a Perlin-FBM DILATED by an inverted Worley-FBM ⇒
  Schneider's billowy cauliflower cumulus; `pw = sat(remap(perlin01, worley_fbm−1, 1, 0, 1))`) × cumulus HEIGHT gradient ×
  weather COVERAGE carve × high-freq **WORLEY** EROSION. **Fully procedural + portable — NO baked-texture crutch for the shape.**
  Verified: density∈[0,1], vanishes at the slab floor/ceiling, grows with coverage, deterministic; Vulkan **1.51e-7** (`optimize=true`).
- **`build_cloud_march`** — the Nubis pipeline: BAKE the density into a 3D VOLUME then the march SAMPLES it TRILINEARLY per step
  (sampling a baked volume per march step is the standard Nubis PERF tier — legitimate, not a portability fallback). Accumulates
  BEER-POWDER transmittance + a short LIGHT-MARCH toward the sun + Cornette-Shanks phase + Schneider's MULTI-OCTAVE MS series.
  Verified: T∈(0,1], denser→more opaque; Vulkan **4.77e-7**.

**⭐⭐ WIN #1 — the CPU oracle (`eval_cpu_kernel`) now MEMOIZES.** Generation-keyed per-node cache (bump a counter on each
TOP-LEVEL eval; cache node→value under that gen so contexts self-invalidate). **DISABLED when the graph has subgroup ops** (they
change `tid` mid-eval). Full kir suite 200s→29s, all 30544 assertions unchanged. Makes ALL deep-graph kernels tractable on the
oracle. See [feedback_oracle_must_round_every_elementary_op](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_oracle_must_round_every_elementary_op).

**⛔ SCAR #2 — `BitOr/BitAnd/BitXor` of BOOL operands must emit LOGICAL `||`/`&&`/`!=`, not bitwise.** Perlin `gradient3` does
`(h==12) | (h==14)`; the compute GLSL emitter emitted `bool | bool` → a type error. Fix in `ckir_glsl.hpp` pv: `binbit(opi, opb)`
picks the logical operator when `g.node(nd.a).dtype()==DType::Bool`. Companion to the u32-const scar in [project_nrc_functional_core_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_nrc_functional_core_ckir).

**⛔⛔ SCAR #3 — UNROLLED 27-cell Worley is GPU-un-compilable → make it a RUNTIME LOOP (this was the born-scar of
[feedback_always_pick_gold_standard_never_disguise_failure](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_always_pick_gold_standard_never_disguise_failure)).** `nz::worley3` fully unrolls its 27 neighbour cells (~1350 nodes);
stack 6 (a 3-octave FBM × base+detail for Perlin-Worley) ≈ 8000 nodes and shaderc's spirv-opt AND the driver's pipeline compile
blow up SUPER-LINEARLY (killed at 500–800 CPU-s; `optimize=false` didn't help). **SOLVE, don't retreat:** `clouds::worley3_loop`
emits a `stmt_for_begin` LOOP over the 27 cells (decode `j∈[0,26] → (dz,dy,dx)` by float floor/div), so each Worley is ~30 nodes ⇒
the full gold Perlin-Worley compiles `optimize=true` in seconds. **BIT-EXACT with the unrolled worley3: the running-min is
ORDER-INDEPENDENT** (min/select-min is associative + exact over the same 27 cell distances, whose hashes depend on cell COORDS not
visit order), so looping in a different order yields the identical minimum. Loop-carried min lives in a per-thread SHARED slot
(the compute for-loop has no loop-phi register — the ReSTIR accumulator pattern, [project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir)). Earlier I
mistook the 500–800 CPU-s for a driver-compile wall and shipped Perlin-only — it was actually the *CPU oracle bake* (runs BEFORE
emit); the true GPU blocker was scars #4/#5 below.

**⛔ SCAR #4 — the compute-kernel GLSL emitter's statement/decl path is SCALAR-ONLY.** `emit_compute_kernel_glsl`'s `pv`/`rhs`
handle NO `Vec3`/`Vec2`/`Dot`/`Swizzle`/`Splat` (those live only in the RASTER `emit_value_stmt`); a vector node reaches the `rhs`
default → `ok=false` → `emit_compute_kernel_glsl` returns false. So **compute-path noise must be SCALARIZED** (compute noise was
never needed pre-clouds — ReSTIR/atmosphere/NRC are all scalar). `worley3_loop` computes localpos/offset/diff/dist as scalars
(reuse `nz::detail::cell_vec3_from3` → 3 scalar hash channels, `floorfrac`). Bit-exactness is SELF-CONSISTENT: oracle + all
backends evaluate the SAME scalar graph, so it need not match the vec worley3's `dot`. Diagnose by DUMPING the emitted GLSL +
running `glslangValidator -S comp -V` on it.

**⛔ SCAR #5 — a value shared across sibling For-bodies (or a top-level value stranded inside a loop) → `stmt_materialize` at top
level.** The emitter declares each temp at its FIRST encounter and the `temped[]` set is GLOBAL, so an arithmetic temp used by
several sibling loop bodies gets declared inside the FIRST loop's `{}` and is OUT OF SCOPE in the rest → GLSL "undeclared
identifier `tN`". The emitter's own assumption ("sibling loops never share an arithmetic node") is violated by the position loads
(`px/py/pz` and their `p*3+k` index temps) feeding all 6 worley loops, and by `h01` (top-level) stranding inside a loop. Fix:
`g.stmt_materialize(x/y/z)` and `g.stmt_materialize(h01)` BEFORE the loops (safe — this kernel has no barriers), forcing them into
`main()` scope. General rule: any value consumed by several sibling loop bodies, or a top-level value pulled into a loop, must be
materialized at top level.

**⭐ WIN #6 — the CUDA/MSL/WGSL compute emitters now CSE like GLSL/HLSL (found via a cross-backend emit gate; debt
`ckir-offhost-emitter-cse`, FIXED same session).** GLSL/HLSL materialize every non-inline arithmetic node ONCE as a `t<node>` temp
keyed by node id (`temped[]`); the three off-host emitters (`emit_compute_kernel_cuda`/`_msl`/`_wgsl`) instead INLINE-EXPANDED each
value recursively (`ev(self, nd.a)`) with no cache, so a node referenced M times re-emits its subtree M-fold. Shallow kernels
(reverse, FFT-per-statement) were fine — but the DEEP cloud density DAG (perlin FBM + hash) exploded EXPONENTIALLY (128 MB TLSF
OOM). Fix: gave each off-host emitter an `is_inline_op` predicate + a `decl` pass that emits every non-inline node once (children
first) as a `t<node>` temp (keyed by the emitters' existing `matd[]`), and wired `decl(...)` before each statement's value/index in
`emit_body`. Leaves + cast/select/compare/bitops stay inline. Determinism unaffected (CUDA compiles `--fmad=false`). Add a
5-backend structural emit gate for any NEW deep compute kernel (`tests/kir/test_ckir_kernel_emit.cpp`) — CUDA/Metal/WebGPU have no
host compiler (real run = ADR-0098 Part C), so "the emit accepts it" is the portability proof there.


<!-- end-memory:project_clouds_and_oracle_memo_ckir -->

<a id="memory-project_command_layer_unified_action_interface"></a>
## project_command_layer_unified_action_interface

---
name: project_command_layer_unified_action_interface
description: "The command layer is Cerid's single action interface — for UI emitters, dev-time agents, AND runtime NPC agents; editor/game/DAW are owner-scoped apps on the spine"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 021fa904-7b98-4a07-9c4e-4f1cb715ea28
---

Architecture model crystallized 2026-05-22 (brainstorm; written into `docs/phases/phase-4.0-platform.md`). The command registry is the **one action interface** that three very different consumers share, and that unification is the load-bearing idea:

1. **UI emitters** — a button = three separable things: a UI **entity** (Godot scene-tree node, ADR-0020) + a command **verb** (Blender operator, in the registry) + a click→command-**name** binding (glue). The button emits the verb *by name*; it never holds the logic. **Invariant: every UI action is a standalone callable verb** reachable headlessly. GUI emits *committed* commands (continuous drags commit one command on release). Undo/redo = the command log (reversible commands) — no separate undo system. Precedents: Godot (editor-as-app), Blender (`bpy.ops` operators).
2. **Authoring-time agents** (external/cloud Claude/GPT via MCP/RPC) — drive the editor, generate content (ADR-0081 Scope 1).
3. **Runtime agents bound to entities (NPCs / companions / helpers)** — THE forward bet (extends ADR-0081 → amendment candidate). NPC-agent **perceives** via scene/ECS queries (MCP resources) → **reasons** (local micro-LLM via [project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate)'s downstream `crd-ml-inference`/v14/v17, or cloud) → **acts** via a constrained command set that IS its capability/action space (`npc.move`/`npc.speak`, never `scene.delete_entity`). Full circle: hesap ML/tensor powers the model, the registry is the action API, the scene is perception. Caveats: LLM nondeterminism → log *chosen commands* not model internals (replay preserved); latency → decide on events/intervals not per-frame (micro/local models for fast paths); capability = gameplay design knob.

**Cerid-as-spine app model:** engine registers domain verbs (ECS/scene/physics/geometry/hesap, always present); each **app** (editor/game/DAW) registers its own verbs as an **owner-scoped command set** that loads on launch and `unregister_owner`s on teardown.

**Registry consequence (real design finding):** the current hesap registry is *register-only* (no `unregister`) — fine for static-init, BROKEN for hot-reload scripts + per-app sets (a `CommandImpl` is a raw fn-ptr into a DLL/app module; dispatching after unload = call into freed code). Requires: `OwnerId` per record (`kEngine` sentinel never torn down), removal-stable storage (slot-map w/ generation indices like the ECS, or hashmap-keyed — NOT position-indexed Array), `unregister_owner` via RAII `ScriptCommandScope`, and a hot-reload protocol that quiesces jobs + deregisters BEFORE the DLL unloads. This requirement only surfaced once the *script consumer* was considered — validates the consumer-driven "build the platform layer after hesap+eylem" sequencing.

See also [project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction](project-history.md#memory-project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction), [project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal](project-history.md#memory-project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal), [feedback_hesap_clean_structure_over_calendar](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_hesap_clean_structure_over_calendar).


<!-- end-memory:project_command_layer_unified_action_interface -->

<a id="memory-project_compute_rendering_separation"></a>
## project_compute_rendering_separation

---
name: project_compute_rendering_separation
description: "ACCEPTED architecture (user decision 2026-07-08, ADR-0099): crd-gpu-context = a deep GPU CONTEXT MANAGER owns/configures backend contexts; compute (CKIR, geometry-bvh-gpu) and rendering are INDEPENDENT consumers that draw contexts from it; share a context (Vulkan render+compute, zero-copy) or not (CUDA headless) BY CONFIG. NOT a separate device baked in. Do the v17-i refactor BEFORE more GPU-compute features."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 934ee96e-34fa-4239-87ad-44921a7d5a19
---

**Decision (user, 2026-07-08 — ADR-0099, Accepted):** separate compute + rendering CONCERNS fully; own the devices in a
deep manager; compose by choice.

**Audit that settled it (2026-07-08):** every CKIR backend already self-creates its context (kir-cuda `cuInit`, kir-metal
`MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice`, kir-dx12 `D3D12CreateDevice`, kir-webgpu adapter, kir-hip, **kir-vulkan** via
`crd::rhi::create_vulkan_instance` — the ONLY one coupled to the rendering module, gets a rendering-flavored device:
forced swapchain + graphics queue). geometry-bvh-gpu takes a rendering `crd::rhi::Device&`. NO deeper context module;
kir-vulkan + a renderer make SEPARATE VkDevices today ⇒ "shared-device interop" wasn't even happening (paid the cost,
got no benefit). So the "render loop / interop" defense of a shared device was WRONG — corrected: timing (compute runs
before rendering) is not the issue; device-locality of the compute→render buffer handoff is, and the manager decides it.

**Target architecture:**
- **`crd-gpu-context`** (deep module): backend-agnostic `IGpuContext` (instance/device/queues/allocator — NO compute/
  render semantics) + per-backend lean impls (`gpu-context-{vulkan,cuda,metal,dx12,webgpu,hip}`, so Vulkan-only builds
  don't pull CUDA/Metal headers) + a `GpuContextManager` that holds the configured set (which backends, headless vs
  windowed, shared vs separate), reconfigurable at runtime (engine options).
- **`ComputeDevice`** (compute pipeline/buffer/dispatch/compute-queue) and **`RenderDevice`** (swapchain/graphics/render
  pass) are independent interfaces OVER a context; neither depends on the other; manager can give both the SAME context
  (shared, zero-copy) or separate.
- Consumers take from the manager: CKIR backends → ComputeDevice (kir-vulkan drops `create_vulkan_instance`); geometry-
  bvh-gpu → ComputeDevice; renderer → RenderDevice; CUDA/HIP = headless.
- Lands WITH it: **pipeline cache** (compile-once per kernel, key=source hash) + **remove bench_contract/bench_tensor
  timing** from the backend (the `bench_ms` smell — it only existed because run() recompiled every call). Shaders:
  crd-shader = shared compiler for BOTH authored (.comp, geometry LBVH) + generated (CKIR) compute shaders → ComputeDevice.

**Plan = v17-i (incremental, before more GPU-compute features):** i-a crd-gpu-context+Vulkan ctx; i-b ComputeDevice +
kir-vulkan on it + headless/compute-queue + pipeline cache + bench removal (re-verify 70.9 TF); i-c RenderDevice + geometry-
bvh-gpu → ComputeDevice; i-d other kir backends → manager; i-e shader-org note. See [project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct](project-history.md#memory-project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct).

**PROGRESS — i-a DONE (2026-07-08):** NEW modules `engine/gpu-context` (IGpuContext + GpuContextManager, header-only
interface, deps=crd-core) + `engine/gpu-context-vulkan` (VulkanGpuContext + `create_vulkan_gpu_context(config)` — raw
Vulkan headless device: instance 1.3, discrete GPU, DEDICATED compute queue [prefers COMPUTE-without-GRAPHICS family],
coopmat+coopmat2+fp16+16bit+memory-model feature chain guarded by `dev_has`). Registered in top CMakeLists (after
rhi-vulkan) + tests/CMakeLists. Test `crd-gpu-context-vulkan-tests` PASSES: 4070 Ti Super, coopmat2=YES, compute_family=2
(a dedicated compute queue — NOT the graphics queue the old rhi-coupled kir-vulkan borrowed). Zero consumer changes.
GOTCHA: /WX rejects `strncpy` (C4996) — use a bounded manual copy.

**PROGRESS — i-b DONE (2026-07-08):** NEW `VulkanComputeDevice` in crd-gpu-context-vulkan (raw Vulkan over a
VulkanGpuContext: command pool + descriptor pool + PIPELINE CACHE keyed by FNV-1a of the SPIR-V; two ops — `dispatch()`

## project_crd_math_transcendental

---
name: project_crd_math_transcendental
description: "crd-math deterministic transcendental cluster (the Cerid Math Mandate) — COMPLETE: 6 real families + complex layer + double-double pow, ROUTE 100% (all engine modules), guard ON; crush libm+std::complex, moat gcc↔MSVC"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d5b177a9-0034-4430-b88d-14a6ad594f07
---

# crd-math transcendental cluster — ✅✅ COMPLETE (2026-06-26, UNCOMMITTED)

**FINAL: kernel + complex layer + ROUTE 100% + guard ON.** Real kernel (6 families ≤1-2 ulp, crush libm) + **`complex.hpp`** (exp/log/sqrt/pow/sin/cos/tan/sinh/cosh/tanh/abs/arg/polar/norm/conj on std::complex<T>, built on the REAL cores ⇒ deterministic; **CRUSH std::complex: exp 1.58× · log 2.40× · sqrt 1.93×**, pow parity) + **double-double pow** (`2^{y·log2 a}`, exponent carried hi/lo ⇒ ≤2 ulp, was ≤7 — FIXED the lone tight-gate break, special `zeta(-3)=1/120` @1e-12). **ROUTE 100%: every engine module on crd::math::*; `crd-no-std-transcendental-check` REGISTERED in ctest + PASSES (gcc+MSVC).** ALL 20 modules re-gated GREEN (special 402081 · dense 359508 · stats 317845 · …). units routed via INCLUDE-only (crd-math headers are header-only, deps=crd-core, never pull scalar.hpp ⇒ no link ⇒ no cycle). crd-math 3050/161 gcc+MSVC, checksums bit-identical = moat. ⭐ **Why select-tier wraps std:: (the user's Q):** sqrt/fma/floor/ceil/round/trunc/copysign/fmod are IEEE-754-MANDATED exact + single hardware instructions + ALREADY bit-identical on every platform ⇒ nothing to implement better; we IMPLEMENT the transcendentals (which VARY across libm) and WRAP what IEEE perfected.

## (historical) kernel COMPLETE, route IN PROGRESS (superseded by the FINAL above)

Plan: `docs/phases/crd-math-transcendental.md`. Premise (tx-a finding): Cerid ALREADY had deterministic transcendentals in 3 partial homes but they were UNEVEN (log core good; exp Taylor ~30ulp + denormal-broken; legacy `deterministic::sin` 2.5× SLOWER than libm) ⇒ this is UPGRADE+UNIFY+complete-gaps+route, not build-from-scratch. The engine was paying a trig tax for the moat; this removes it.

## ✅ KERNEL COMPLETE — 6 families, all in `engine/math/include/crd/math/`
- `transcendental.hpp` (+`simd/transcendental.hpp` cores `crd_exp1`/`crd_log1`/`crd_log_reduce`): exp·exp2·exp10·expm1·log·log2·log10·log1p — **all ≤1 ulp**.
- `trig.hpp`: sin·cos·sincos·tan (≤1, tan ≤2) + atan·asin·acos·atan2 (atan ≤2, asin/acos ≤3, atan2 ≤1 vs std). **Double-double π/2 reduction with a 4th part** (≤1 ulp at sin's zeros; a naive 3-part collapses to 7 ulp there).
- `hyperbolic.hpp`: sinh·cosh·tanh·asinh·acosh ≤2, atanh ≤3 (compose expm1/log1p anti-cancellation forms; large-x sinh/cosh via 0.5·exp).
- `power.hpp`: cbrt ≤2 (bit-trick seed + Halley) · rsqrt ≤1 · hypot ≤2 · **pow ≤7 ulp** (2^{y·log2 x}, ed-exact; ⚠ ≤1 ulp needs a double-double exponent — DOCUMENTED FOLLOW-ON).
- `select.hpp`: min/max/clamp/abs/fabs/floor/ceil/round/trunc/nearbyint/lround/fmod/sqrt/copysign/sign/lerp/fma — EXACT.
- `cmath.hpp` = **the unify**: ONE include (the deterministic `<cmath>` replacement) pulling all the above.

**Gated** `tests/math/test_transcendental.cpp` (≤ulp vs mpmath via `gen_transcendental_refs.py`→`transcendental_refs.inc` + golden cross-platform determinism checksums). **gcc + MSVC both 3048/161 green; checksums bit-identical gcc↔MSVC = the moat proven under normal CI** (`-ffp-contract=off` + explicit fma). ⭐ CRUSH vs libm: exp 1.05× · log 1.6× · sin 1.26× · cos 1.34× · atan 1.27× · cbrt 1.71×.

## ▶ ROUTE (tx-route) — 15 MODULES DONE + re-gated GREEN; 209 sites blocked (complex + cycle)
Tool: **`scripts/route-to-crd-math.sh <module-dir>`** (sed std::fn→crd::math::fn + `<cmath>`→`<crd/math/cmath.hpp>`, scope = include/+src/ ONLY, NEVER tests/ [gold oracles] or runtime/examples [bench peers]). Guard: **`scripts/check_no_std_transcendental.sh`**.
**ROUTED + RE-GATED GREEN (15):** comms 39663 · wavelet 14951 · dsp 27069 · opt 3782 · ode 577 · **stats 317845** · ordering 7771 · quadrature 130 · meshgen 17265 · draw 167 · geometry-spatial 7382 · -delaunay 1163 · -curves 3010 · -mesh 503 · -decomposition 89. ⭐ **The trajectory-EXACT gates (opt/ode vs scipy/CVODE step counts) + the tight stats gates TOLERATED the ~ulp shift — my fear they'd break was WRONG.** kernel itself still 3048/161.
**BLOCKED — 209 sites, two ARCHITECTURAL exceptions (NOT unfinished):**
1. **Complex math (192): hesap-special 135 · hesap-fft 50 · hesap-dense 5 · hesap-eigen 2.** They call `std::exp/pow/sqrt/...` on `std::complex`; crd::math is REAL-only ⇒ the route broke them (no matching fn). REVERTED them (reverse-sed crd::math::fn→std::fn). FIX = a `crd/math/complex.hpp` with complex overloads (`exp(z)=exp(re)·(cos(im)+i·sin(im))` etc., deterministic via the real cores), then re-route + re-gate (⚠ hesap-special gated <1e-12 — watch the tight Bessel/Airy gates).
2. **units (17): the crd-math→crd-units CYCLE** (crd-math/scalar.hpp uses Vec3<Quantity>) ⇒ units can't depend on crd-math. FIX = split the transcendentals into a lower module (below units), or keep units' nonlinear (dB) conversions on std:: as a documented exception.
⚠ route gotchas hit: sed too broad (caught complex-arg calls) ⇒ revert complex modules; CMake link `crd-math` must go UNDER `target_link_libraries(...) PUBLIC`, not after the target name (or after `target_include_directories` PUBLIC); recompiling routed files surfaces pre-existing -Werror (e.g. opt dead `inf_nrm` lambda → `[[maybe_unused]]`).

## Follow-ons (documented, not lost)
1. **pow ≤1 ulp** via double-double exponent (currently ≤7). 2. **Payne–Hanek** for |x|≫1e6 trig (currently Cody-Waite to ~1e6; beyond degrades — rare). 3. **win-tidy pass**: `kPio2_1..4` underscore-digit naming + `select.hpp` clamp nested-ternary. 4. **Flip the guard ON** (register in `tests/math/CMakeLists.txt`) once all modules routed. 5. **legacy `deterministic::`** (eylem/hesap-sparse use it): either forward it to the facade or route those consumers to bare crd::math:: + retire it.

## DoD so far
crd-math suite gcc+MSVC 3048/161; comms/wavelet/dsp re-gated gcc. NOT committed. NOT yet: win-asan/shipping/tidy on the routed modules, the full route, the guard flip. <a id="memory-project_d1_d5_ir_as_crdr_deploy"></a>
## project_d1_d5_ir_as_crdr_deploy

---
name: project_d1_d5_ir_as_crdr_deploy
description: D1-D12 ALL LANDED (2026-07-22) — the CKIR shader deploy pipeline is COMPLETE: IR-as-crdr → cook (SPIR-V/DXIL/PTX real bytecode + MSL/WGSL src) → variants (dedup) → zero-compile load + persistent pipeline cache → hot-reload → joint VS+FS specialize → full raster reflection → multi-variant container → neural completeness → parallel cook (crd-jobs) → async warmup → spec constants. CKIR is a full shipping pipeline.
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

**D1–D5 = the deploy system that turns CKIR from "compiles in tests" into a SHIPPING content pipeline** (ADR-0104, extends ADR-0101
"the IR is the source of truth for all shaders"). Today every shader is built in C++ → emit GLSL/HLSL → shaderc/DXC compile AT
RUNTIME. D1–D5 makes a shader a `crdr` resource cooked offline to bytecode, loaded with zero runtime compile. Plan:
- **D1 IR-as-crdr + reflection** ✅ (below) · **D2 cook** (standalone `crd-shader-cook` CLI: IR→SPIR-V/DXIL/MSL/WGSL/PTX at build
  time, cook-time validation, content-hash cache, parallel cook, writes the `.crdr` bundle) · **D3 variants** (feature toggles →
  specialization matrix, variant key → specialized graph, content-hash dedup, on-demand) · **D4 runtime load + pipeline cache**
  (zero runtime shader compile; `VkPipelineCache`/D3D12 PSO cache; async warmup) · **D5 hot-reload** (IR edit → recook affected
  variants → atomic pipeline swap). User decisions: standalone cook CLI; all 5 backends targeted (real bytecode where the toolchain
  exists — SPIR-V/DXIL/PTX on the dev box; MSL/WGSL final bytecode platform-gated like other blocks); D1 first, then sequence.

**✅ D1 LANDED (2026-07-22).** `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_serialize.hpp` (`crd::kir`): `serialize_graph(KGraph,KEntry)→bytes`
+ `deserialize_graph(bytes)→{KGraph,KEntry}` — a versioned LE container: `FourCC 'KGPH'` + version + a **`sizeof` layout manifest**
(KNode·KStmt·KType·KEntry) + `n_inputs` + the five POD pools (nodes·ext·struct-fields·struct-begins·stmts) + `KEntry` bytes. Added
`KGraph::serial_{nodes,ext,sfields,sbegin,stmts}()` + `serial_restore()`. `reflect()→ShaderReflection` = descriptor bindings +
vertex attrs + workgroup size, **derived from the IR (no SPIRV-Cross)**. **KEY DESIGN:** a cook artifact is regenerable, so a
POD-pool container guarded by version+`sizeof` is the correct+fast format (layout drift → clean reject → recook, never mis-read) —
this is what the whole append-at-END/cook-stable enum discipline was FOR. Gate `[kir][serialize][d1]`: serialize→deserialize→re-emit
is **BYTE-IDENTICAL GLSL AND HLSL** (the ADR-0101 proof) + reflection correct + bad blobs rejected; kir regression green. ⛔ note:
`ckir.hpp` brings `Array` but NOT `ConstSpan` (span.hpp) — `serial_restore` takes raw ptrs+counts; `ckir_serialize.hpp` includes
`span.hpp`. Session `docs/sessions/2026-07-22-d1-ir-as-crdr.md`.

**✅ D2 LANDED (2026-07-22) — the cook ships bytecode; both production backends RUN it zero-runtime-compile.** New module
`engine/shader-cook/` (`crd-shader-cook`, lib+CLI like `asset_cooker`; a BUILD-TIME tool linking both backends' compilers).
`cook_compute_shader(KGraph,KEntry,name,opts)→CookResult`: serialize IR (D1) → content-hash key (`ResourceId::from_content`) ·
reflect (D1) → POD blob · emit+compile **SPIR-V** (GLSL→shaderc) + **DXIL** (HLSL→dxc) + **real PTX** (CUDA→NVRTC, guarded on
CUDAToolkit, `--fmad=false`/prec-div/prec-sqrt @ virtual `compute_75` — portable + matches the kir-cuda runtime) = 3 REAL bytecode
targets · emit **MSL/WGSL** source (final AIR/WGSL = target toolchain, Metal/naga not on Windows) · pack a **CRDR container**

the first non-test TU to pull the CUDA/MSL/WGSL emitters together → surfaced a latent `-Wswitch` gap (RT `KStmtKind`s

`default:`, so a future non-RT kind still trips `-Wswitch`). tidy-clean. Session `docs/sessions/2026-07-22-d2-shader-cook.md`.

**✅ D3 LANDED (2026-07-22) — the variant/permutation matrix cooks on-demand with content-hash dedup.**
`engine/shader-cook/{variant.hpp,variant.cpp}`. A shader is an übershader with feature toggles; a VARIANT is a `key` bitmask.
`cook_variant_matrix(build_fn, keys[], opts) → VariantMatrixResult`: the caller's **`VariantBuildFn(g, key)`** constructs the
kernel per key emitting only the LIVE path (how real material compilers cook per-permutation — and the honest fit since
`KGraph::stmt(i)` is const-only + no graph copy ⇒ in-place kernel specialize needs kir surgery; the per-key builder sidesteps it
and a builder may still call B7 `specialize()`). Each specialized IR is content-hashed (`ResourceId::from_content`) and identical
hashes **DEDUP** (the cook's own content-hash cache ⇒ a deduped key is a cache hit, cooked once). Returns manifest (key→hash) +
**telemetry** (`requested` vs `unique`). `cook_one_variant(build,key)` = ON-DEMAND single. `[variant]` gate: 4 keys (bit0=scale,
higher DEAD) → `requested=4 unique=2` (50% reduction); dedup proven (key0==key2, key1==key3, key0≠key1); each variant's cooked
SPIR-V runs GPU-correct. **✅ ÜBERGRAPH STYLE (2026-07-22) — both authoring styles unified through the SAME `cook_variant_matrix`:**
per-key builder OR one übergraph with `ShaderOption` selectors + option-gated `Select`s. Added `KGraph::specialize_kernel(entry,
options, values, n)` (compute analogue of `lower_entry`: pin selectors + gather body statement node-refs as roots + `optimize()`

GPU-correct ×1/×2. **⛔⛔ SCAR: `optimize()` const-folded operand-less RESOURCE decls** (BufferDecl/SharedDecl/Texture/Sampler/
AccelStructDecl/RayPayloadDecl) into garbage `Const` — no operands + not in the skip list. SILENT until a kernel was specialized
(übergraph emit collapsed both buffers to `buf0`, ninputs=0, empty decls → shaderc fails → spirv_bytes=0, cook still ok via
IR+REFL chunks). Fixed: `is_resource_leaf()` in the const-fold skip (next to `is_stage_leaf`). kir 52420/230 (materials
unaffected — they use UniformBlock/StageIn, already skipped). Lesson: `optimize()` folds any operand-less non-Const node; every
NEW leaf op must join a skip list.

**✅ MATERIALS THROUGH THE VARIANT MATRIX (2026-07-22).** Made the cook **STAGE-AWARE**: `cook_compute_shader` dispatches on
`e.is_kernel()` → `emit_compute_kernel_glsl`@Compute (kernel) vs `emit_stage_glsl`/`_hlsl`@Fragment (material); CUDA/MSL/WGSL stay

**(1) Load:** read a cooked `.crdr` from disk → pipeline straight from the cooked bytecode + IR-reflection (`n_bindings`), NO

<a id="memory-project_ddgi_gold_gi_ckir"></a>
## project_ddgi_gold_gi_ckir

---
name: project_ddgi_gold_gi_ckir
description: "D-007 B14-b: gold-standard DDGI (Majercik 2019 dynamic diffuse GI, visibility-moment irradiance probes) in CKIR (ckir_ddgi.hpp) — octahedral encode/decode + Chebyshev visibility + probe sample (leak-free indirect diffuse) + probe update (integrate rays + moments + hysteresis). CPU+Vulkan verified. The no-RT-HW GI source; pairs the SVGF denoiser."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**D-007 B14-b — DDGI (Dynamic Diffuse Global Illumination, Majercik et al. 2019), GOLD-STANDARD, in CKIR (2026-07-15).** The
no-RT-HARDWARE GI tier of B14: a grid of light probes, each an OCTAHEDRAL irradiance map + an octahedral DEPTH-MOMENT map that
drives a Chebyshev occlusion test so GI does NOT leak through walls. Same approach as SVGF — the per-probe RAY GENERATION
(dir+radiance+dist) is the deferred B9 ray-tracing leaf; the ANALYTIC CORE is built + verified now. All in
`engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_ddgi.hpp` (namespace `crd::kir::ddgi`), statement-tier COMPUTE, SCALARIZED (dir.x/y/z as
separate F32 nodes — the compute emitters are scalar; vec ops live on the fragment path). Tests `tests/kir/test_ckir_ddgi.cpp`
+ `tests/gpu-context-vulkan`.

**[✅ B14-b-1] octahedral + Chebyshev.** `oct_encode`/`oct_decode` (Cigolle 2014): project a unit dir onto the octahedron by
the L1 norm, fold the −Z hemisphere out to the square corners ⇒ the WHOLE sphere maps to [−1,1]² with no singularity.
Round-trip `decode(encode(d))` recovers every dir (min dot > 1−1e-5; only ULP is the normalize sqrt, IEEE-exact). `chebyshev`:
`select(dist ≤ mean, 1, σ²/(σ²+Δ²))` with σ²=E[d²]−E[d]², Δ=dist−mean — soft visibility, monotone, →0 when far past the mean.

**[✅ B14-b-2] probe SAMPLE `build_ddgi_sample`** (Majercik §4) — the shading-time indirect-diffuse lookup: blend the 8 corner
probes of a 2×2×2 cell by trilinear weight × normal-wrap `((n·d̂_probe+1)/2)²` × Chebyshev visibility (from the depth moments,
toward the probe) × irradiance sampled octahedrally in the NORMAL direction; out = Σw·E/Σw. Verified: uniform field → exactly C
(the whole trilinear+weight+oct pipeline normalizes); a bright probe behind a "wall" (depth mean ≪ dist) leaks ≥4× less red.
**✅ POLISHED (2026-07-15): BILINEAR octahedral sampling** (`sample_oct_bilinear`, 4-tap, `probe_base` is a runtime NODE) +
**full ARBITRARY probe GRID** — `build_ddgi_sample` computes the cell = `floor((pos−origin)/spacing)` clamped to [0,grid−2] and
addresses the 8 corner probes by flat index `((cz+dz)·grid_y+(cy+dy))·grid_x+(cx+dx)`; `DdgiConfig` gained `grid_x/y/z`,
`origin_x/y/z`, `spacing`, `probe_count()`. Verified on a 4×4×4 grid: a single bright probe lights ONLY its own cell.

**[✅ B14-b-3] probe UPDATE `build_ddgi_probe_update`** (Majercik §3.2) — one thread per (probe, texel): texel center →
oct_decode → direction d; integrate the probe's rays — irradiance = Σ max(0,d·rd)·radiance / Σcos; depth moments = Σ
cos^depth_sharpness·{dist, dist²} / Σ (sharper ⇒ crisp occlusion); then `out = lerp(prev, new, hysteresis)`. Verified over 40
frames: aligned rays accumulate irradiance in the matching texel + the depth mean converges to the hit distance, back-facing
texels stay dark.

Verified: CPU oracle 57 asserts; **Vulkan sample 1.31e-7, update 1.82e-6** (all arithmetic bit-exact; sqrt/pow ULP ⇒
effectively exact). tidy-clean. Config `DdgiConfig{oct_res=8, num_rays=64, hysteresis=0.03, depth_sharpness=50, grid_x/y/z=2,
origin=0, spacing=1}`.

**DONE:** B14-b complete + polished (bilinear oct + full grid). ⭐ B14 GI now has an indirect-light SOURCE (this, DDGI), a
SAMPLER ([project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir) — ReSTIR RIS/reuse estimator), AND a DENOISER
([project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir)) — three halves of a real-time GI stack, all no-RT-HW analytic cores, all gold, all in
CKIR (each with the RT ray-gen as the deferred B9 leaf).

<a id="memory-project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid"></a>
## project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid

---
name: project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid
description: "The end goal Cerid serves — AI-leveraged, episodic, story-driven cinematic games (The Last of Us-class) made by a solo/tiny team"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7b0bb65d-6788-4a80-96e7-82e1072ab242
---

Cerid is ultimately a means to an end: the user wants to **make games**, specifically
**story-driven cinematic games in the vein of The Last of Us** — strong narrative, heavy
cinematics, decent gameplay — shipped **episodically** (Family-Guy-style cadence) by a
solo / very small team. The whole **agent-driven / CLI-RPC-first** architecture (see
[project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction](project-history.md#memory-project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction), [project_command_layer_unified_action_interface](project-history.md#memory-project_command_layer_unified_action_interface))
is the deliberate force-multiplier for this: AI accelerates content production while the
user consumes Cerid as the engine. Plan: finish hesap (Phase 3.1.6), then return to
game-facing "fun stuff" and actually USE hesap/Cerid to build games.

**Why this matters for prioritisation + advice:**
- The bottleneck for these games is **content + writing + pacing + performance/taste**, not
  engine features — engine tech is necessary but not sufficient.
- The user's "elite, no shortcuts" bar is an asset for the engine but a SHIPPING RISK for
  games (engine-itis; perfect-vs-done). When game work starts, the right counsel shifts to
  "good-enough tech + great content + iteration; ship the episode."
- The differentiated edge is the **runtime-agent-operable engine** (NPCs perceiving via
  scene queries, acting through a constrained command set) — believable characters as a
  first-class capability, enabled by building the command layer first.

**Distribution vision (far-future, 2026-05-28):** platform-INDEPENDENT (not bound to Steam) —
a "Netflix-for-games" model: a **free base game (Cerid runtime/launcher) + paid, signed,
downloadable content/mission packs loaded into the base game's lore monthly** (proven shape:
Warframe/Destiny/Fortnite free-base + content drops). NOT per-episode separate exes (user
self-corrected). This maps 1:1 onto Cerid's existing tech (CRDR pack format + resource
manager/streaming + scene cooker + command layer) — a mission = a data pack the runtime
loads. So the "platform" is THIN (content CDN + auth + payment), not a full storefront. ⇒
ARCHITECTURE IMPLICATION: invest in the content-pack / signed-DLC / live-content-loading
pipeline; LINEAR cinematic missions (not open-world — user knows open-world fights both AI
automation and the model). Honest caveats to keep raising: the real moat platforms provide
is trust/discovery/payment (audience problem is separate + brutal — consider Steam as an
early discovery on-ramp); full "story-in-game-out" automation is north star not schedule
(near-term = AI ~70% grind + human direction of the 30% soul).

**User context (2026-05-28):** the user is a **TaleWorlds employee** (Mount&Blade: Bannerlord)
and has lived the slow-development / mid-air-scope-churn failure mode firsthand. Their explicit
directorial philosophy: ENGINEERING (Cerid) must be perfect; GAMES must NOT chase ultimate
perfection — no constant mid-production changes, no unnecessary scope churn. When advising on
the game phase, REINFORCE scope discipline (lock episode scope, park new ideas for "next
episode", ship at ~80% of the dream) and act as the accountability voice asking "this episode
or next?" Do NOT encourage perfectionism on the game side (only on the engine side).

<a id="memory-project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism"></a>
## project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism

---
name: project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism
description: "eylem MUST crush PhysX AND Jolt on raw performance AND keep cross-thread bit-determinism + solver quality — elite/world-class on EVERY domain; the fast-vs-deterministic tradeoff is FALSE (Jolt disproves it); no 'deliberate trade' accepted"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f039483d-cb60-446b-af8b-a75467157c25
---

2026-05-30 — EMPHATIC user directive. eylem's bar is NOT "competitive but deterministic." It is: **crush PhysX AND Jolt on raw performance/throughput AND keep the determinism + solver quality.** Every domain must be **world-class / elite** at the target the user wants held at EXTREME-HIGH confidence: rigid bodies, co-rotational FEM soft-body, implicit cloth, particles/SPH-FLIP fluids, offline/cinematic, GPU. The user explicitly REJECTED my sentence "eylem will not be the fastest physics engine, and that's a deliberate trade, not a failure" — I RETRACT it as defeatist AND technically wrong.

**Why (the tradeoff is FALSE):**
- **Jolt is BOTH fast AND deterministic** (same-platform) — existence proof that fast ≠ non-deterministic. I had conflated them.
- **Jolt/PhysX are elite SIMD C++, NOT hand-asm** (unlike OpenBLAS/MKL) ⇒ the ADR-0082 no-asm ceiling barely bites physics (it bit hesap's dense GEMM; physics is broadphase/narrowphase/solver/integration, not dense GEMM). Matchable + beatable by equally-elite SIMD C++ over ECS SoA + the fiber job system.
- **Cerid's edges over BOTH:** (1) the **hesap sparse-direct/iterative backbone** = world-class stiff-system solving — Jolt/PhysX use PGS/sequential-impulse (cheap, poorly convergent on stiffness, which is WHY they fake soft-body); a real solver converges in fewer iterations ⇒ FASTER *and* more accurate on FEM/cloth/soft-body (beating them on their weak axis). (2) **cross-thread-count BIT-determinism** (stronger than Jolt's same-config; PhysX has none). (3) **fiber jobs + GPU extension** force-multipliers. (4) determinism ENABLES speed (safe sleeping/warm-start/caching/sub-step decisions a non-det engine can't trust). The cross-thread determinism cost (fixed-topology parallel reductions + fixed-lane SIMD horizontal sums) is an ENGINEERING problem to drive toward ~zero (single-digit %), NOT a tax to accept.

**How to apply:**
- HARD per-slice gate (reference-is-the-floor applied to physics, [feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor) + [feedback_benchmarks_mandatory_at_slice_close](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_benchmarks_mandatory_at_slice_close)): every eylem slice ships a **head-to-head bench vs Jolt AND PhysX** on its domain and must **WIN** — or it is NOT closed — AND holds the determinism moat (bit-identical {1,2,4,8} threads).
- NO "deliberate trade" framing survives: a fast-but-nondeterministic OR deterministic-but-slow path is an unsolved engineering problem to CRUSH, not a tradeoff to accept.
- Confidence is EARNED to extreme-high PER-SLICE via the head-to-head wins (exactly how we earned the CHOLMOD crush — measured, not assumed; the symbolic breakthrough came from profiling, not faith). HIGH confidence today that it is ACHIEVABLE; certainty is locked slice by slice.
- Thread this bar into `docs/phases/phase-3.1-eylem.md` + `docs/research/cerid-eylem.md` (perf posture + per-slice gate) when eylem resumes (currently paused for geometry + hesap).
- Honest risks to MANAGE (not accept as excuses): sustained elite execution across ~30 slices/multi-year; GPU bit-determinism is genuinely hard (deterministic-GPU-reduction work, not "relax determinism on GPU").

Links: [project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision) (ADR-0082 no-asm — barely bites physics), [project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid](project-history.md#memory-project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid) (the games this serves), [feedback_full_honest_evaluations_crush_every_metric](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_full_honest_evaluations_crush_every_metric), [feedback_quality_bar](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_quality_bar).

REN-38-F16 (2026-07-27) opened the geometry-pull seam for every amplification stage:

- **Emitters**: `emit_task_glsl/hlsl`, `emit_mesh_glsl/hlsl`, `emit_tese_glsl/hlsl` declare the `sbuf` storage
  binding whenever a reachable `KOp::StorageLoad` exists (set 0 binding 0 / `register(u0)` — same seam as the
  pulling VS). The VK descriptor-set layout's binding 0 stage flags grew TESC|TESE (+TASK|MESH when the device
  has mesh shaders); DX12 root param 0 was already ALL-visible.
- **Verbs** (vtable END, both backends): `draw_tess_storage(_load)`, `draw_mesh_storage(_load)` — frame-recording
  only; the frame executor routes a draw item carrying a storage buffer to them for BOTH amplification kinds.
- **Vocabulary** (`vertex-cook`): `[mesh] fetch = true` pulls the SAME scene contract as the pulling VS
  (indices → vertex records → visible slot → instance matrix → view_proj; workgroup `wgi` covers `max_vertices`
  consecutive index slots, thread `tid` fetches one indexed vertex — the reason fetch keeps V == 3·P). Morph/skin
  under fetch → BadMesh (refused loudly, the deformers belong to the pulling VS). `[mesh] payload = true` declares
  the task pairing ([feedback_as_ms_payload_contract_dx12_pso](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_as_ms_payload_contract_dx12_pso)). `[task] emit_header = N` reads the
  amplification count from buffer word N at dispatch (GPU-driven meshlets; > 1023 refused). `hdr:`/`hdru:` node
  inputs are legal in tess_eval + fetch-mesh graphs (the heightfield/ocean seam) — the author who reads a header
  word takes on the storage-binding obligation.
- **Gates** (all pixel-dichotomy, VK + DX12): tess pull (buffer corners drive the patch; a `hdr:22`-scaled domain
  proves the tese lowering), mesh fetch (2 instances, extent tracks records), emit_header (word=1 lights one
  quad, word=2 both), vertex-cook probe (entry_valid + StorageLoad + no VertexIndex + round-trip + 3 refusals).

Found and fixed on the way: the PSIn register-packing scar
([feedback_dx12_hlsl_svposition_last_register_packing](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_dx12_hlsl_svposition_last_register_packing)) which had silently broken EVERY DX12 scene render
gate behind a `SKIP`, and the DX12 visbuffer probe orientation (D3D mirrors the fullscreen quad's diagonal vs
Vulkan — probes now sit on the horizontal midline where classification is orientation-invariant).

<a id="memory-project_frame_graph_is_a_recording_mode_of_raster_context"></a>
## project_frame_graph_is_a_recording_mode_of_raster_context

---
name: project_frame_graph_is_a_recording_mode_of_raster_context
description: REN-1 frame graph is a RECORDING MODE of the raster context (Vulkan+DX12) — reuse existing draws; the per-draw descriptor-pool/heap reset is the batching blocker
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

The REN-1 frame graph (`engine/gpu-context/include/crd/gpu/frame_graph.hpp`, Vulkan impl in
`vulkan_raster_context.cpp`, landed 2026-07-24) is NOT a new draw API. It is a **recording MODE** of the existing
raster context: while a graph executes, `draw_storage_depth` / `draw_storage_depth_load` / `draw_overlay` branch
on `frame_recording()` and RECORD into ONE shared command buffer instead of each doing begin→record→submit+wait→
readback. Zero new draw vocabulary — the same CKIR draws the sandbox already issues compose into one submission.

**Why:** the synchronous submit+wait+readback-PER-DRAW substrate is what capped the sandbox at ~58 fps; batching
N draws into one `vkQueueSubmit` is the whole point. Don't reinvent the draws — gate them behind a recording flag.

**How to apply (the two load-bearing gotchas for REN-2..REN-8 and the DX12 port):**
- **The batching blocker is the per-draw descriptor-pool reset.** Each standalone draw did `vkResetDescriptorPool`,
  which would free the previous draw's still-live sets mid-recording. The graph owns a FRAME descriptor pool (256
  sets) reset ONCE per `execute()`, so all N draws' sets coexist. It MUST be sized for every set-0 type
  (STORAGE_BUFFER + SAMPLED_IMAGE×(kBindlessMax+1) + SAMPLER) or `vkAllocateDescriptorSets` warns.
- **DX12 has the identical problem, worse — and it's DONE (2026-07-24, `Dx12FrameGraph`).** DX12's single
  storage-UAV heap slot (slot 0, overwritten per draw) is read at EXECUTE time, not record time — so multi-draw
  recording needs a per-draw descriptor-heap RING (the DX12 analog of the Vulkan frame pool): each recorded draw
  bumps a cursor in a shared shader-visible heap and binds its table at that slot. Transient aliasing = one
  `ID3D12Heap` per interval-color slot + `CreatePlacedResource` (RT/DS vs BUFFER heap classes on Tier 1). The
  DX12 gate's ring proof is STRONGER than Vulkan's: two DIFFERENT per-pass buffers (a red field, a green tip) —
  if the ring were broken both draws would read the last buffer; the red field surviving off-centre proves each
  draw got its own slot.
- **Transient aliasing** = greedy interval-coloring on lifetimes `[first_pass,last_pass]`: disjoint transients
  share one `VkDeviceMemory` (`VK_IMAGE_CREATE_ALIAS_BIT`). `transient_memory_bytes() < transient_logical_bytes()`
  is the gate's aliasing proof.
- Handles are 1-field STRUCTS (`FgImage`/`FgBuffer`), never enums (dodges `performance-enum-size`).
- **The batching win scales with draws/frame** (`docs/bench/2026-07-24-ren1-frame-graph-batching.md`): collapsing
  N submit+fence-waits to one is **Vulkan 2.5×→6.14×, DX12 1.22×→38.76× (N=1→64, win-debug)**. DX12 wins MORE
  (its per-`ExecuteCommandLists`+fence cost is heavier) and its frame time is near-flat in N. Sandbox ~58→65 fps.

**REN-2 RTT (both backends, 2026-07-25):** a `sampled` transient is now DRAWN-THROUGH — one pass renders into it,
a later pass SAMPLES it. Reuses the proven `draw_wboit` sequence (create `COLOR_ATTACHMENT|SAMPLED` → render →
barrier `COLOR_ATTACHMENT→SHADER_READ_ONLY` → sample). The transient becomes a **BORROWED** render target +
texture over the graph-owned aliased image: Vulkan needs an explicit `m_borrowed` flag on `VulkanRasterTarget`/
`VulkanTexture` (their dtors `destroy_image_bundle` — skip it when borrowed, else double-free with `free_transients`);
DX12 needs NO flag (ComPtr refcounting — the borrowed target just holds a ref). New `record_offscreen` (color-only,
branch `draw_storage`) + `record_textured` (sample, branch `draw_sampled`) mirror `record_scene`. The graph inserts
the RTT barrier in `execute()` when a transient goes write-pass→read-pass. Spec:
`docs/design/ren-2-rtt-and-material-textures.md`; gates `[ren2]` in `test_{vulkan,dx12}_frame_graph.cpp`.

Related: [project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context](project-history.md#memory-project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context) (gpu-context IS graphics),
[project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program](project-history.md#memory-project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program), [feedback_raster_emitters_lag_compute_wire_both_and_uint_suffix](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_raster_emitters_lag_compute_wire_both_and_uint_suffix).


<!-- end-memory:project_frame_graph_is_a_recording_mode_of_raster_context -->

<a id="memory-project_full_ckir_after_detour_legacy_path_deleted"></a>
## project_full_ckir_after_detour_legacy_path_deleted

---
name: project_full_ckir_after_detour_legacy_path_deleted
description: "After the D-007 detour, the engine goes 100% CKIR — the legacy rhi+GLSL-Effect render path is DELETED, not kept"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 40e3ad67-a505-447d-89df-272b48c237f6
---

⭐⭐ Architectural intent (user 2026-07-12, flagged "very important"). The engine is MID-MIGRATION with two shader/render paths
coexisting on purpose — this is a temporary BRIDGE, not the destination.

**Where we are now (transitional):**
- **Device seam: already unified** (C2/D-008). The runtime bootstraps `create_vulkan_gpu_context(...)` and rhi ADOPTS its
  `VkDevice` — ONE device, gpu-context-owned (`create_vulkan_device_adopting`). rhi creates no device. See
  [project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context](project-history.md#memory-project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context).
- **LEGACY render path (still what the shipped runtime + `runtime/examples/smoke_*.cpp` use):** rhi pipelines + the
  HAND-AUTHORED GLSL Effect system — `.vert`/`.frag` source → `crd::shader::EffectDesc` → `runtime->create_effect` →
  `device->create_program(cooked SPIR-V)`. GLSL is written by hand here. (This is why the smokes show GLSL/Vulkan.)
- **CKIR render path (this detour, built in `tests/gpu-context-*` first):** authored in backend-neutral CKIR
  (`KGraph`+`KEntry`) → `create_program(KGraph,KEntry)` → `IRasterContext`/`IComputeContext`. GLSL/HLSL/WGSL/MSL/PTX appear ONLY
  as emitter output inside a gpu-context backend, never hand-written. See [project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program](project-history.md#memory-project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program).

**Three different "cook"s (don't conflate):** B8-k "cook seam" (`ckir_cook.hpp`) = in-memory material→per-pass-program VARIANT
assembly + B7 lowering, feeds `create_program`; touches NO `.crdr`. D1 = serialize the CKIR/material graph into the versioned
`.crdr` resource (replaces stored GLSL/HLSL). D2 = offline cook, IR → SPIR-V/DXIL/MSL/WGSL/PTX bytecode, content-hash cached.
D1/D2 are the CRDR cook; B8-k is not.

**⛔ THE ENDGAME (non-negotiable):** once the D-007 detour is FULLY over, the engine is 100% CKIR. The runtime renderer migrates
ENTIRELY onto CKIR → gpu-context + the `.crdr` cook (D1–D5). The legacy GLSL Effect system (`EffectDesc`, `create_effect`, the
hand-authored `.vert`/`.frag`, the SPIR-V-source path) is **DELETED** — no dual path survives. GLSL/HLSL/etc. remain ONLY as
machine-emitted backend outputs behind the I1/I2 gates. **Full CKIR, no exceptions.** Documented in
`docs/detours/D-007-gpu-program-system.md` §"Legacy path vs CKIR path".

**Why:** apply when reasoning about the smokes/runtime still using GLSL (it's the bridge, expected), and when planning the
post-detour rendering phase — the migration + legacy deletion is REQUIRED work, not optional. Do not "preserve" the Effect
system for compatibility; it goes away.


<!-- end-memory:project_full_ckir_after_detour_legacy_path_deleted -->

## project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu

---
name: project_full_visual_frontier_before_hesap_gpu
description: User direction 2026-07-11 — build the COMPLETE visual shader frontier (raster→materials→mesh→RT→neural→work-graphs→cook) before returning to the hesap-GPU branch
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 9b330af5-88bb-499e-a92a-1752e160e0ba
---

**User direction (2026-07-11), resolving the "when hesap" sequencing question:** build the ENTIRE visual shader
frontier to completion FIRST, then return to hesap-GPU. This is the comprehensive "gold-standard, everything"
vision the user stated this session ("compute to lightings to materials to ray tracings to mesh shaders to
everything"). hesap-GPU is the LAST stop of the CKIR/v17 arc, not an early return.

**The locked order (D-007 Phase B + D-008 frontier device contexts, interleaved):**
1. **B3-c** raster VS+FS emitters (the foundational non-compute stage — start HERE, not C3)
2. **B1/B2** materials + lighting (OpenPBR 1.1 / MaterialX surface-response; render-path = lighting)
2b. **B8** the FULL lighting+shadow system (a–e lighting library ✅: BRDF·OpenPBR lobes·punctual·area-LTC·IBL; f–i shadows; j skinning; k–m renderer)
2c. **B12 + B13** the SCREEN-SPACE + POST-PROCESSING frontier (user 2026-07-12, "every technique that looks beautiful, full feature complete"): **B12** = ambient occlusion (**GTAO** + bent normals + specular occlusion) · screen-space reflections (Hi-Z SSR) · screen-space GI · **volumetric lighting/fog + god-rays** · screen-space SSS. **B13** = **TAA** + velocity + TAAU · **bloom** (physically-based dual-filter pyramid → neon/LED/sci-fi glow) + lens flare/anamorphic/dirt · auto-exposure + tonemap (**AgX**/ACES/PBR-Neutral) + LUT grade · depth-of-field + motion blur · CA/vignette/grain/CAS/FSR-upscale. Slotted AFTER B8, BEFORE mesh/RT (the raster visual completion). RT counterparts (RTAO/RT-reflections/RT-GI/path-tracing) come with B9.
3. **B4** mesh + task shaders (meshlets, VRS, cluster emission)
4. **B9 + D-008 C3** ray tracing (RT shaders ↔ RT device context: pipelines/SBT/inline rayQuery/SER/opacity
   micromaps/cluster-AS / RTX Mega Geometry)
5. **B10** NEURAL shading (cooperative vectors + long vectors — the differentiable-shader moat, v15/v16 autodiff IR)
6. **B11 + D-008 C5** subgroup/wave + work-graph node shaders ↔ GPU-driven dispatch (device-generated commands → work graphs)
7. **D-007 Phase D** cook (serialize/cache compiled programs)
8. **THEN** hesap-GPU compute.

**⭐ REVISED sequencing (user 2026-07-12): build the hesap-GPU COMPUTE PRIMITIVES the frontier rendering needs DURING
this D-007 detour** (as part of the technique's slice), then finish the REST of crd-hesap AFTER the detour. Rationale:
CKIR/v17 IS the GPU compute compiler, so the compute kernels the frontier requires ARE hesap-GPU pieces — building them
now serves rendering + hesap-GPU from ONE bit-exact source. This SUPERSEDES the earlier "if you need crd-hesap's GPU part
tell me before going / hesap-GPU is a clean later return" stance for the specific primitives rendering depends on. Known
render→compute dependencies to fold into the gap slices: **FFT** (convolution/physically-accurate bloom + glare · FFT
ocean/Tessendorf) · GPU **sort** (radix/bitonic — Gaussian-splatting depth sort · OIT · light lists) · **scan/stream-
compaction** (clustered/tiled light-cull · Nanite cluster-cull · particle/visibility compaction) · **reduction** (auto-
exposure histogram · SDSM + Hi-Z depth min/max · luminance) · small **GEMM/MLP** (neural radiance caching · neural
materials — with B10 coop-vectors). Each = a CKIR compute kernel, bit-exact CPU oracle + both backends. The BROADER
hesap-GPU (dense/sparse linear algebra, eigensolvers, ODE, stats — the parts rendering never calls) stays post-detour.

**Why the visual frontier is first anyway:** the COMPUTE substrate hesap-GPU needs is ALREADY proven (GEMM at cuBLAS
parity, 6 backends, bit-exact) — so hesap-GPU is a dependency-light return whenever wanted. The user deliberately chose
to finish the whole visual frontier first. Do NOT propose returning to hesap early; that choice was made and rejected.
See [project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor](project-history.md#memory-project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor), [project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope](project-history.md#memory-project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope),
[project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program](project-history.md#memory-project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program), [feedback_mission_portable_gpu_compute_all_backends](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_mission_portable_gpu_compute_all_backends).

<a id="memory-project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program"></a>
## project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program

---
name: project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program
description: ADR-0103 / detour D-008 — crd-gpu-context owns every GPU program for all 14 shader stages; crd-shader must never know GLSL or HLSL.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9b330af5-88bb-499e-a92a-1752e160e0ba
---

⭐⭐ **`crd-gpu-context` handles ALL the shaders. `crd-shader` must not know any GLSL or HLSL.** User direction
2026-07-10; recorded as **ADR-0103**, executed as detour **D-008** (C0–C4), which **blocks D-007 from B3-c onward**.

Two invariants, meant to be **grep-gates in CI**, not prose:
- **I1** — no shading language (GLSL/HLSL/WGSL/MSL/CUDA-C) crosses a module boundary. Source exists only on the codegen
  path: `crd-kir`'s `ckir_<lang>.hpp` emitter → the owning `gpu-context-<backend>` → the vendor compiler.
- **I2** — no bytecode (SPIR-V/DXIL/PTX/metallib) appears in a public header. A consumer holds an opaque `IGpuProgram`.

Currency **in** = the IR (`KGraph` + `KEntry`); **out** = `IGpuProgram`. `IGpuContext` gains
`create_program(graph, entry)` + `create_program(cooked_name)` (ship path + ADR-0101 §4's explicitly non-portable escape
hatch) and the domains `compute()` / `raster()` / `raytracing()`. Edge `crd-gpu-context → crd-kir` is **acyclic**
(verified: crd-kir links only core/containers/memory/math).

**Three leaks it closes, measured:** `crd-shader` exports `compile_glsl`/`compile_hlsl` — 9 call sites ·
`crd::rhi::ShaderModuleDesc::code` is a `ConstSpan<u8>` of raw SPIR-V in a public header — 38 `create_shader_module`
sites / 9 files · `rhi::Device` and `gpu::IGpuContext` are two device layers over two `VkDevice`s.

**The stage model is COMPLETE, day one:** `KStage` = the 14 SPIR-V execution models (compute · vertex · tess-control ·
tess-eval · geometry(legacy, discouraged) · fragment · task · mesh · raygen · intersection · any-hit · closest-hit ·
miss · callable). A backend that cannot lower a stage **refuses loudly**; it never falls back to compute. Shipped in
D-007 B3-a′ with 32 builtins in one `builtin_info` table (type + legal-stage mask together) and `entry_valid()`, which
is what makes the table bite — a graph carries no stage, so only an entry can reject `gl_FragCoord` in a vertex shader.

**Why:** the mission is every kind of shader — compute, lighting passes, materials, mesh deformation, skinning, tensor/
CNN/AI kernels, ray tracing, mesh + task, geometry. A portable mid-level module owning two backend languages makes that
impossible and makes a node editor impossible (ADR-0101).

**Progress:** **C0 DONE (2026-07-10).** The standalone compilers moved `crd-shader` → `gpu-context-vulkan`
(`crd::gpu::compile_glsl_to_spirv` / `compile_hlsl_to_spirv`); `crd/shader/compile.hpp` deleted; `crd-kir-vulkan` no
longer links `crd-shader`; `crd/gpu/program.hpp` = `ShaderStage`(14) + `IGpuProgram`;
`IGpuContext::create_program(cooked SPIR-V) → IGpuProgram` implemented + tested. **I1 grep-gate = `crd-no-shader-language-leak`**
(ctest-registered). **⚠ Known remaining leak, allowlisted + tracked for C2:** `crd-shader/src/runtime.cpp` (the
Effect/Module RENDERING frontend) still compiles GLSL via shaderc — migrating it is the rendering convergence (dragging
Vulkan into crd-shader), so it's C2, not C0. C1 = `IRasterContext` + the `create_program(KGraph, KEntry)` overload (its
raster path needs D-007 B3-c). C0→C4 sequencing lives in `docs/detours/D-008-gpu-context-convergence.md`.

**Frontier commitment (2026-07-10, web-grounded — D-008 is now C0✅→C6, D-007 gained B10/B11):** the C-slices were first
a *correctness* convergence; a research audit pulled the 2024–26 state of the art into explicit slices (full extension
list + citations in the D-007/D-008 frontier tables). Load-bearing bits:
- **C1 must be designed on SHADER OBJECTS (`VK_EXT_shader_object`) + bindless (descriptor buffers/heaps) + dynamic
  rendering from the start** — retrofitting them onto monolithic PSOs is a rewrite, and shader objects are the frontier
  answer to the variant/permutation explosion ADR-0101 explicitly fears. This is a *design* constraint on C1, not a
  later feature.
- **C5 = GPU-driven** (device-generated commands `VK_EXT_device_generated_commands` → work graphs
  `VK_AMDX_shader_enqueue`); keep the dispatch recorder abstract enough that GPU-generated commands are an add-on.
- **C3 RT frontier** = SER (`VK_EXT_ray_tracing_invocation_reorder`, 20–100% path-tracing) + opacity micromaps
  (`VK_EXT_opacity_micromap`) + cluster AS / RTX Mega Geometry (`VK_NV_cluster_acceleration_structure`).
- **⭐ THE MOAT — C6 + D-007 B10: differentiable neural shaders.** Cooperative vectors (`VK_NV_cooperative_vector` / DX12
  coop-vectors SM 6.9) put small MLPs inline in a shader (neural materials/BRDF/NTC). Because CKIR *is* the autodiff graph
  (v15/v16), we can author a neural material AND get its gradient from ONE IR — no shipping engine does this. Treat as a
  first-class differentiator, gated bit-exact vs a CPU MLP ref + a gradient check.

**How to apply:** never add an API that takes shader *source* or *bytecode* outside a backend. Never gate a CKIR test on
`crd::shader::compile_*` (deleted) — gate through `crd::gpu::IGpuContext::create_program` or `crd::gpu::compile_*_to_spirv`.
A raster test that compiles emitted GLSL must NOT live in `crd-kir-tests` (its link-isolation smoke must stay GPU-free);
put it in `tests/gpu-context-vulkan`.

Related: [feedback_superseded_adr_clause_must_be_struck_in_place](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_superseded_adr_clause_must_be_struck_in_place) (ADR-0099 §6 said the opposite),
