<a id="memory-project_gpu_fft_crush_campaign"></a>
## project_gpu_fft_crush_campaign

---
name: project_gpu_fft_crush_campaign
description: B-compute GPU FFT crush campaign — the crush is FUSION (not raw cuFFT parity); build the COMPLETE CKIR shared-mem IR first; plan → gpu-fft-crush-plan.md
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 40e3ad67-a505-447d-89df-272b48c237f6
---

**B-compute GPU FFT** (D-007 B-cmp; feeds B13-b FFT-convolution bloom). Campaign started 2026-07-13.
Execute-ready plan → `docs/research/gpu-fft-crush-plan.md` (read it before any FFT work — full design,
IR ops, FFT algorithm, bench plan; like `fft-stockham-v2.md` did for the CPU FFT).

**⭐⭐ THE CRUSH IS FUSION, not raw throughput.** Per [feedback_frontier_must_be_2026_cutting_edge_research_the_gaps](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_frontier_must_be_2026_cutting_edge_research_the_gaps)
+ the GEMM gotchas (`docs/hints/v17-kir-gpu-gotchas.md`): cuFFT/cuBLAS run ~90% of hardware peak — you
CANNOT crush a 90%-of-peak flagship kernel; parity is the raw ceiling. The crown = the **fused 2D
FFT-convolution** (fwd 2D FFT → ×PSF spectrum → inv 2D FFT, on-chip, ONE dispatch) vs cuFFT's 3 global
round-trips. That fused convolution IS B13-b's bloom. 2026 SOTA confirms: TurboFNO (SC'25, fused
FFT-CGEMM-iFFT), kernel-fused single-dispatch FFT (arxiv 2604.03585, 8s→370ms), radix-8 Stockham
two-tier register↔shared (arxiv 2603.27569, 138 GFLOPS). Reference `engine/hesap-fft` (radix-4
Stockham, 0.71–0.95× MKL — [project_v10_fft_plan.md](project-history.md#memory-project_v10_fft_plan)).

**User decisions (2026-07-13):** (1) build the **COMPLETE general CKIR shared-memory IR FIRST** — NOT
minimal; it is the substrate every future on-chip compute kernel reuses (scan/sort/stencil/conv). (2)
Deliver **BOTH** general 1D/batched FFT AND 2D image FFT-convolution — full crush on both. (3) Always
research cutting-edge 2026 SOTA. (4) [feedback_benchmarks_mandatory_at_slice_close](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_benchmarks_mandatory_at_slice_close) the crd-hesap way:
bench ALL peers (cuFFT + VkFFT + CPU FFT + FFTW), min-of-N ≥3 clock-locked, matched accuracy, full board
→ docs/bench; [feedback_full_scoreboard_no_partial_victory](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_scoreboard_no_partial_victory); [feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat).

**Phase 0 FOUNDATION ✅ (2026-07-13):** the IR data model + CPU oracle are BUILT + GREEN. New KOps `BufferDecl`/
`SharedDecl`/`BufferLoad`/`SharedLoad` + `KernelLoopVar`; `KStmt`{BufferStore,SharedStore,Barrier,For,If} +
`KEntry.local_size`+statement body (in `ckir.hpp`); KGraph authoring API (`buffer_decl`/`shared_decl`/`buffer_load`/
`shared_load`/`stmt_*`); the CPU oracle `ckir_kernel_eval.hpp` (`eval_cpu_kernel` — single-workgroup sim, barrier-segment
semantics: cross-thread shared writes visible only after a barrier, same-thread immediately). `[kernel]` test
(`tests/kir/test_ckir_kernel.cpp`) bit-exact: shared REVERSE + workgroup REDUCTION. kir 544/85 green, tidy clean. ⛔ gotcha:
`select(cond,a,b)` → node **a=true, b=false, c=cond** (NOT a=cond); the Select oracle/emitter must read c as the condition.

**Phase 0 EMITTERS + BOTH-GPU DISPATCH ✅ (2026-07-13):** `emit_compute_kernel_glsl` (`ckir_glsl.hpp`) +
`emit_compute_kernel_hlsl` (`ckir_hlsl.hpp`), routed in BOTH `create_program`s. ⛔ HLSL uses **`RWByteAddressBuffer`** raw-UAV
byte-addressed `.Load(idx*4)`/`.Store(idx*4, asuint(v))` + asfloat/asint — NOT `RWStructuredBuffer` — because the DX12 compute
context binds every storage buffer as R32_TYPELESS `FLAG_RAW` ("no element type baked in", dx12_compute_context.cpp); a
structured decl would mismatch the descriptor. GLSL side is a normal `std430 buffer`+`shared`; both index element i at byte 4i
so the staged upload bytes match. THE "GREEN ON BOTH GPUs" GATE: shared harness `tests/gpu-shared/ckir_kernel_dispatch.hpp`
(portable **GpuOnly device buffer + Cpu/GpuToCpu staging** = the DX12-safe readback contract; push_size 0 — both backends omit
the root-const/push range when 0) dispatches the REVERSE kernel (1 wg) on Vulkan (SPIR-V) AND DX12 (DXIL) via the same
`IComputeContext`/`ComputeRecorder`, **bit-exact vs `eval_cpu_kernel` AND vs each other** (`[gpu][kernel]` Vulkan 7 / DX12 5,
live devices; dx12 527/54 · vulkan 636/61 no regressions; win-debug+win-tidy clean). F32 buffers (not F64 — no shaderFloat64).
**ALL 5 KERNEL EMITTERS ✅ (2026-07-13):** CUDA (`ckir_cuda.hpp` — typed pointer params, `__shared__`, `__syncthreads()`,
`threadIdx.x`), MSL (`ckir_msl.hpp` — `device [const] T* [[buffer(N)]]`, `threadgroup` arrays declared IN-BODY since Metal's
threadgroup space is function-local, `threadgroup_barrier`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`), WGSL (`ckir_wgsl.hpp` —
`var<storage,read[_write]>`, `var<workgroup>`, `workgroupBarrier()`, `@builtin(local_invocation_index)`). ⛔ WGSL `Select` =
`select(false_val, true_val, cond)` — operand order REVERSED vs the ternary (CUDA/MSL/GLSL/HLSL use `cond ? true : false`);
kernel comparisons are Bool predicates so the cond needs no `!= 0` wrapper. CUDA/Metal/WebGPU have no compiler off-host, so
these three are GOLDEN-STRING gated (`tests/kir/test_ckir_kernel_emit.cpp`, `[kernel]` — reverse kernel structural check per
backend + a Select-order case proving WGSL false-first vs CUDA/MSL cond-first; 6 cases/37 assert; kir 578/89, win-tidy clean).
Compile+run bit-exact on real CUDA/Apple/WebGPU = ADR-0098 Part C. Vulkan + DX12 already dispatch the kernel bit-exact.
**For/If + FFT PRIMITIVES ✅ (2026-07-13) — Phase-0 DoD complete.** Scoped-builder API `stmt_for_begin`/`stmt_for_end`/
`stmt_if_begin`/`stmt_if_end`/`kernel_loop_var` (ckir.hpp). ⛔ LAYOUT: a For/If body lives CONTIGUOUSLY after the statement;
the parent range spans both, and every consumer executes `body_begin`/`body_count` then SKIPS past it — this fixed a latent
DOUBLE-EMISSION in all 5 emitters (their `emit_body` for-loops re-emitted the body; now while-loops that advance past it).
Oracle (`ckir_kernel_eval.hpp`) rewritten to a RECURSIVE LOCKSTEP interpreter: For = uniform bound + per-iter body re-entry
(barrier inside a loop syncs each iteration) · If = reduces the active-thread set (a barrier under a divergent If is GPU UB) ·
a barrier commits the per-thread write overlay. ⛔⛔ `round_dtype` now TRUNCATES integer storage (I32/I64/U8/U32) toward zero
— GPU int/uint is never fractional and `uint/uint`+`(u)int(x)` truncate; the old no-op diverged the oracle on index math
(byte-exact canary HELD after). Primitives (`tests/kir/test_ckir_kernel.cpp` `[ctrlflow]`/`[fft]`): PREFIX-SCAN (Hillis-Steele,
For+If+inner-barrier, bit-exact) · TRANSPOSE (2 For loops + barrier + cross-thread, bit-exact oracle AND dispatches bit-exact
on Vulkan+DX12 via `build_transpose_kernel` in the shared harness) · radix-2 BUTTERFLY PASS (twiddled complex butterfly →
SEPARATE out buffer). ⛔ FFT GOTCHAS for Phase 1: (1) in-place multi-stage FFT needs PING-PONG — CKIR re-reads shared LAZILY,
so writing `sh[i0]` then re-reading it for the `sh[i1]` store returns the NEW value (RAW hazard); use ping-pong/Stockham. (2)
butterfly `a·w−b` FMA-contracts → oracle-bit-exact but GPU-ULP-tolerant until the KERNEL emitter emits `precise` temps (the
elementwise emitters already do — per-node `precise float tN=`; the kernel emitters use INLINE exprs, so add precise in Phase 1).
Green: kir 583/92 · vulkan 642/62 · dx12 531/55, win-tidy clean.
**PHASE 1 STARTED (2026-07-13).** ⭐ BENCH ENV: this host = **NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (Ada) + CUDA 13.3 (nvcc + nvidia-smi
present)** — cuFFT is the primary peer, the CUDA emitter can COMPILE+RUN bit-exact on real HW (not just golden-string), and
`nvidia-smi -lgc` clock-locking works. Vulkan+DX12 also run on it. **Radix-2 Stockham FFT authored in CKIR ✅** —
`engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_fft.hpp` `build_fft1d_radix2(g, n, inverse)`: the REUSABLE FFT authoring layer (engine, not
test). AUTOSORT (natural-order in→out, no bit-reversal) · OUT-OF-PLACE PING-PONG across two shared (re,im) pairs (fixes the
lazy-eval RAW hazard) · log2(N) stages UNROLLED at authoring time (N compile-time → the src/dst shared arrays alternate
DETERMINISTICALLY; CKIR cannot select a shared array by a runtime parity, so a For-loop over stages with ping-pong is
impossible — unroll) · verified DIT index map: r=2^s, L=2^(s+1), g=t/r, j=t%r → in0=g*r+j, in1=in0+N/2, out0=g*L+j,
out1=out0+r, twidx=j<<(p-1-s) into a precomputed W_N[N/2] table (butterfly = add/sub/mul only). Oracle-correct vs a direct
f64 DFT within f32 tol for N=2..64; impulse→all-ones + constant→DC=N BIT-EXACT (`tests/kir/test_ckir_fft.cpp` `[fft]`; kir
592/95). Uses Div/Mod (needs the round_dtype truncation fix).

**FFT BIT-EXACT ON BOTH GPUs ✅ (2026-07-13):** the radix-2 Stockham FFT DISPATCHES on Vulkan (GLSL→SPIR-V) AND DX12
(HLSL→DXIL), both **bit-exact vs the CPU oracle** (`tests/gpu-context-*` `[fft]`; Vulkan 64/64 bins maxdiff 0, DX12 bad==0) —
one CKIR graph, identical bits on 3 backends. TWO emitter fixes: (1) ⛔ **GLSL `mod()` is FLOAT-ONLY** — integer Mod must emit
`%` (the FFT's `t%r` is uint; the other 4 emitters already branched on dtype, GLSL didn't → the FFT GLSL failed to compile,
`spv.ok==false`). (2) ⭐ the GLSL+HLSL KERNEL emitters now materialize FLOAT arithmetic as `precise` temps (SPIR-V
NoContraction / HLSL `precise`): a node→temp table, LEAVES (loads/consts/builtins) + cast/select/cmp/bitops stay INLINE (so a
load re-reads across a barrier), arithmetic → `precise float t<node> = ...;` CSE'd by node id. ⛔ Without precise the butterfly
`wr*x1r - wi*x1i` FMA-fused → only 25/64 bins bit-exact (~1 ULP, maxdiff 7.6e-6); WITH it → 64/64 maxdiff 0. Invariant that
makes CSE-no-clear safe: every kernel authors FRESH load nodes after a barrier + sibling loops never share an arithmetic node
(so no load-derived temp crosses a barrier, no cross-scope temp). CUDA/MSL get determinism from a COMPILE flag (`--fmad=false`
/ Metal fast-math OFF) — NO source precise needed; WGSL is ULP-tolerant. vulkan 647/63 · dx12 534/56, reverse/transpose still
bit-exact.

**cuFFT GOLD BOARD + RADIX-4 ✅ (2026-07-13).** cuFFT peer measured: `bench/gpu-fft/cufft_bench.cu` (nvcc `-O3
-allow-unsupported-compiler ... -lcufft`, batched C2C fwd, min-of-30, CUDA-event GPU-timed) → board in
`docs/bench/2026-07-13-gpu-fft-cufft-gold.md`. cuFFT on the RTX 4070 Ti SUPER PEAKS **~2500-2664 GFLOP/s** (N=8K-16K),
memory-bound (~6% of 44 TFLOP/s FP32 peak — FFT is bandwidth-bound); DROPS to ~1530 at N≥65536 (goes multi-pass = global
round-trips = the seam the fused-conv crush attacks). ⚠ clocks NOT locked (`nvidia-smi -lgc` needs elevation) — min-of-30
mitigates; re-lock before a FINAL parity claim. **RADIX-4 Stockham** `build_fft1d_radix4(g, n, inverse)` (ckir_fft.hpp): half
the shared passes of radix-2 (log4 vs log2). The 4-point DIT DFT is EXACT — t0=a0+a2,t1=a0-a2,t2=a1+a3,t3=a1-a3; X0=t0+t2,
X2=t0-t2, X1=t1∓i·t3, X3=t1±i·t3 (i·(re,im)=(-im,re)); NO irrational twiddles inside, only the per-butterfly PRE-twiddles
multiply → bit-exact via precise. Uses the FULL W_N[N] table (radix-4 pre-twiddle idx = m·j·(N/L) reaches ~3N/4 > N/2, so
radix-2's N/2 table is too small). Oracle-correct vs DFT N=16..1024 + BIT-EXACT on Vulkan (N=256). kir 596/96 · vulkan 652/64.
**⭐⭐ HEAD-TO-HEAD — WE BEAT cuFFT ON RAW 1D FFT ✅ (2026-07-13).** Batching: NEW scalar builtin `KBuiltin::WorkgroupIndex`
(appended at enum END; `gl_WorkGroupID.x` / `SV_GroupID.x`—added `uint3 wgid3:SV_GroupID` to the HLSL cs_main / `blockIdx.x` /
MSL `threadgroup_position_in_grid` param / WGSL `@builtin(workgroup_id)` param — all 5 emitters). `build_fft1d_radix4(g,n,
inverse,batched=true)` offsets its IN/OUT buffers by `WorkgroupIndex*N` (twiddles stay shared) so one workgroup = one N-point
FFT over a grid of `batch` groups. Oracle `eval_cpu_kernel` gained `num_workgroups` (default 1): loops workgroups, zeroing
shared + resetting overlay each, `WorkgroupIndex`→wg. Batched-correctness test: each wg bit-exact vs the single-wg FFT of its
slice. BENCH (`tests/gpu-context-vulkan` `[.fft-bench]`, hidden): Vulkan, GPU-timed KERNEL-ONLY via
`VulkanComputeContext::last_gpu_ms()` (upload/readback excluded — apples-to-apples w/ cuFFT cudaEvent), min-of-30, ~16.7M
total elements, self-verifying (wg0 output BIT-EXACT vs oracle in-run — a fast wrong kernel fails). **RESULT (RTX 4070 Ti
SUPER, `docs/bench/2026-07-13-gpu-fft-cufft-gold.md`): N=256 ours 1749 vs cuFFT 1584 = 1.10× WIN; N=1024 ours 2037 vs cuFFT
1901 = 1.07× WIN — both bit-exact.** WHY: FFT is BANDWIDTH-bound; our single-wg Stockham = ONE global read + ONE write (all
log₄ stages ping-pong in shared) → N=256 ≈ 656 GB/s ≈ 98% of the 672 GB/s card; cuFFT ≈ 91%. A specialized single-pass kernel
edges the general vendor lib for sizes that fit one wg's shared (radix-4 = 16·N bytes ≤ 48KB ⇒ N≤3072). EXCEEDS the doctrine's
"parity" expectation for raw 1D. kir 597/97 · vulkan 652/64 · dx12 534/56, tidy clean. ⚠ scope: N=256/1024, power-of-4,
single-wg, NOT clock-locked (both unlocked min-of-30 — fair relative; re-lock for a headline).
**⭐⭐ WE BEAT cuFFT AND VkFFT — 3 sizes, all bit-exact (2026-07-13).** VkFFT peer: `bench/gpu-fft/vkfft_bench.cpp` (reuses
VkFFT's own `utils_VkFFT` for Vulkan setup + SDK glslang libs; `cl /MD /O2 /DVKFFT_BACKEND=0`, built FIRST TRY — link cmd in
the board). num_iter appends/submit amortized, min-of-20. RADIX-8: `build_fft1d_radix8(g,n,inverse,batched)` — 8-pt DFT = TWO
exact 4-pt DFTs (even/odd) + a radix-2 combine with W_8 (only W_8^1=(c,-c), W_8^3=(-c,-c) carry c=√2/2; W_8^0=1, W_8^2=(0,-1)
free); full W_N[N] table; covers N=512 (power of 8, which radix-4 can't). Oracle-correct vs DFT N=8/64/512 + bit-exact on
Vulkan. **★ HEADLINE BOARD — CLOCK-LOCKED (core 2100 / mem 10501, user's elevated `nvidia-smi -lgc 2100,2100`+`-lmc 10501`; back-to-back
min-of-N, reproducible, no boost variance) in `docs/bench/2026-07-13-gpu-fft-cufft-gold.md`, GFLOP/s: N=256(r4) ours 1704 /
cuFFT 1538 / VkFFT 1533 = 1.11×; N=512(r8) 1930 / 1711 / 1710 = 1.13×; N=1024(r4) 1941 / 1876 / 1915 = 1.01-1.03× — WIN vs BOTH
peers at ALL 3, bit-exact.** (Unlocked earlier reads were 1749/1825/2037 — boost-inflated at N=1024 past the 2100 lock; locked
is the honest reproducible board.) ⭐ ROBUST: FFT is bandwidth-bound (single global read+write ≈98% of 672 GB/s, near the
physical limit), peers ~91%. radix-8 is bandwidth-PARITY with radix-4 (both one global read+write → the radix helps compute-bound FFTs,
but we're already at the bandwidth wall — so radix-8 wins by parity+, not a leap; expected). kir 600/98 · vulkan 652/64, tidy
clean. ⛔ clock-lock BLOCKED (session lacks GPU-clock permission; user runs elevated `nvidia-smi -pm 1; -lgc 2100,2100 -lmc
10501`); ⚠ peers measured in separate unlocked runs (~3-5% spread < the win margin); a same-process ours+VkFFT run (both Vulkan,
via our `vk_device()`/`compute_queue()`) would make the margin airtight.
**⭐⭐⭐ THE CRUSH LANDED (1-D) — fused FFT-convolution ~2× cuFFT (2026-07-13).** `build_fft1d_convolution(g, n, batched)`
(ckir_fft.hpp): forward radix-4 Stockham → ×filter-spectrum (in-shared) → inverse radix-4 → 1/N, ALL in ONE dispatch (ping-pong
via a current/other pointer that FLIPS each stage). ⛔ the in-shared multiply must write the OTHER buffer then flip — writing
in-place re-hits the lazy-eval RAW hazard (the 2nd store's shared_load re-reads the 1st store's new value) — the SAME scar as
the butterfly; caught it as a failing conv test, fixed. Also finally VALIDATED the inverse FFT (wired via `inverse` but untested
until now — conj pre-twiddle + flipped 4-pt i-rotation; iFFT(FFT(x))=N·x). 1/N is EXACT in f32 for power-of-4 N ⇒ whole pipeline
bit-exact via precise. Bit-exact circular-conv on the oracle (N=16/64/256); correct on GPU (identity filter Filt=1 recovers the
input). **CRUSH BOARD: vs cuFFT's 3-pass conv (`bench/gpu-fft/cufft_conv_bench.cu` = cufftExec(fwd)+cmul kernel+cufftExec(inv)),
GPU-timed batched: N=256 ours 0.441 ms vs 0.879 = 1.99×; N=1024 0.586 vs 0.887 = 1.51×.** We pay ONE global round-trip, the
vendor ~two (fwd+inv each global + the multiply). This is the fusion win the raw-1D board CAN'T show (bandwidth-tied at parity+
there). kir 603/99 · vulkan 652/64, tidy clean.
**NEXT — Phase 3 PROPER = the 2D image FFT-convolution (BLOOM, B13-b's consumer):** extend the fused conv to 2D (row FFTs →
in-shared transpose → col FFTs → ×PSF spectrum → inv 2D), where the vendor's global round-trips cost even more. Also open: CPU-FFT
(engine/hesap-fft) + FFTW peers; same-process ours-vs-VkFFT; CUDA backend nvcc `--fmad=false`; larger N via multi-wg four-step
(single-wg caps N≤3072). Then Phase 2 (general 2D FFT).

**Phase 0 (original spec):** CKIR imperative compute-kernel IR — `SharedAlloc`/`SharedLoad`
/`SharedStore` (workgroup arrays + bank-conflict pad), `Barrier` (control+memory), `StorageAlloc`/
`StorageLoad`/`StorageStore` (generalize the B1-f binding-0 StorageLoad to multi-buffer indexed R/W),
`KEntry.local_size` + an imperative statement body, CPU-oracle workgroup model (serial invocations +
barrier = full-workgroup sync), all 5 emitters (GLSL/HLSL/CUDA/MSL/WGSL). DoD: workgroup-reduction +
shared-transpose primitives bit-exact + both backends, then a radix-2 butterfly pass. **Phases 1–3:**
1D/batched FFT (parity cuFFT) → 2D FFT → fused convolution (THE CRUSH). GPU f32 div is ~2 ULP on Vulkan
(bit-exact on CUDA --prec-div --fmad=false) — the v17-b/c determinism split; `precise` temps.

<a id="memory-project_hair_rt_renderer_works_offline_realtime_path"></a>
## project_hair_rt_renderer_works_offline_realtime_path

---
name: project_hair_rt_renderer_works_offline_realtime_path
description: "The B18-f path-traced hair renderer WORKS (real fibre size, real GI, all defects fixed) - it is an OFFLINE renderer at ~194ms/full-frame-sample; real-time needs the denoiser + DOM shadows the engine already has"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0138d6a-548b-428b-87b2-fe30c9f36f7c
---

As of 2026-07-20 the B18-f RT strand tier has a WORKING path-traced hair renderer (`ckir_hair_rt.hpp` +
`hair_swatch.hpp` + `test_vulkan_hair_swatch_rt.cpp`): realistic 68 µm fibres, 3-bounce GI with NEE, coloured
transmittance self-shadow, real contact shadow on a ground plane, five hair types via melanin σₐ + helix
grooming. Continuous smooth strands, sheen travelling along the fibre, no beading. All the shading/geometry
defects are fixed (see [feedback_hair_rt_shading_five_defects](rendering.md#memory-feedback_hair_rt_shading_five_defects) and
[feedback_lss_f32_cancellation_reorigin_ray_at_segment](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_lss_f32_cancellation_reorigin_ray_at_segment) — the last one was the big one).

**PERFORMANCE (measured, board: docs/bench/2026-07-20-hair-rt-swatch-perf.md):** on the RTX 4070 Ti SUPER,
1400×1000, 3 bounces, 3-light NEE, 8-step transmittance shadows, OPTIMISED SPIR-V —
`time ≈ 3350 ms fixed + 194 ms × spp`. **One full-frame sample = ~194 ms** (~139 ns/sample/pixel). A converged
~384 spp film frame ≈ 75 s of GPU. This is an **OFFLINE / film** renderer as configured.

**Can it be real-time?** Yes, but not with this path unchanged — and the engine already has every piece:
- **B14 ReSTIR / SVGF denoiser** (built + GPU-verified) → 1-4 spp instead of ~384: the ~50-100× that makes RT
  hair possible at all. This is how ALL real-time path tracing works.
- **B18-c deep opacity maps** (built) in place of the 8-step transmittance march: ~5-10×, the biggest per-sample
  lever (the shadow march dominates).
- 1 indirect bounce instead of 3 (~2-3×); reduced res + DLSS-class upscale (~2-4×).
- Product ≈ 1000-24000×, past the ~12× (1spp/60fps) to ~700× (converged/60fps) gap.

Also: the engine ships the **pure-raster hair tier** (B18-a…e: deferred raster + DOM + Lipp filter) — the
shipping-games real-time path, no RT. The RT path is the FILM reference that tier is measured against.

**Not yet done:** clang-tidy on the new files; a grazing-limit BCSDF gate (the white-furnace test integrates over
h and misses a narrow bad band — `test_ckir_hair_grazing.cpp` exists as a probe, not an assertion); a measured
real-time board (DOM + 1 bounce + SVGF at 1-4 spp). The renderer geometry lives in the TEST, not the engine — a
production groom system (strand meshes, distribution on a disc not a card, inter-lock scattering) is future work.

Related: [project_ckir_material_surface_contract](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_material_surface_contract), [project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir),
[project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir), [feedback_ckir_kernel_eval_is_scalar_vec3_evaluates_to_garbage](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_ckir_kernel_eval_is_scalar_vec3_evaluates_to_garbage).


<!-- end-memory:project_hair_rt_renderer_works_offline_realtime_path -->

<a id="memory-project_hesap_beats_eigen_mt_via_fma"></a>
## project_hesap_beats_eigen_mt_via_fma

---
name: hesap-beats-eigen-mt-via-fma
description: "2026-05-20 — `crd-hesap` GEMM beats Eigen-MT at every workhorse size (N >= 1024) on AVX2. Key win was switching the hesap microkernel from `mul_add` (two-rounded, ADR-0063 strict) to explicit `simd::fma(a,b,c)` (single-rounded IEEE 754) — ~2x FMA-port throughput."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8232c613-08b5-412f-9d51-73f8c05a65d9
---

**Fact:** Phase 3.1.6 `crd-hesap` v0d-parallelism-scaling closed the
Cerid-vs-Eigen-MT gap by switching the GEMM microkernel to explicit
hardware FMA. Final ratios (dev box i9-14900K, AVX2, P-core affinity,
16 P-threads, best-of-3): f32 N=4096 **1.21x** over Eigen-MT, f64 N=4096
**1.12x** over Eigen-MT. Cerid wins at every workhorse N (>= 1024) for
both f32 and f64.

**Why:** ADR-0063 (eylem determinism contract) bans hardware FMA
contraction for physics replay determinism. The hesap microkernel
inherited `mul_add(a, b, c) = (a*b) + c` (two-rounded) from crd-math.
This left ~50% of FMA-port throughput unused on AVX2-FMA hardware.

The fix added a SEPARATE `crd::math::simd::fma(a, b, c)` function on
Vec8f + Vec4d that uses `_mm256_fmadd_ps` / `_mm256_fmadd_pd` (single
rounding) with `std::fma` scalar fallback (IEEE 754-2008 mandated
bit-identical to hardware FMA). The hesap microkernel calls `fma()`;
crd-eylem keeps using `mul_add()`. Determinism is preserved within each
domain — bit-exact across SIMD widths within hesap (all paths use fma)
AND within eylem (all paths use mul_add) — but the two are NOT bit-
exact with each other. That's the right tradeoff: hesap is numerical
computing (perf-critical), eylem is physics replay (determinism-critical).

**How to apply:** when writing a new perf-critical inner kernel in
crd-hesap or future numerical modules:
- Use `simd::fma(a, b, c)` for the hot loop, NOT `mul_add()`.
- Document the choice — single-rounded FMA is more accurate than
  two-rounded mul_add and ~2x faster on FMA-equipped CPUs.
- The kernel remains bit-exact across SIMD widths WITHIN the module.

**Bench:** `runtime/examples/bench_hesap_gemm_vs_reference.cpp` is the
canonical comparison harness. Build with `-DCRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_REFERENCE=ON`
(off by default; fetches Eigen 3.4 + OpenBLAS into build/_deps/).

**Hybrid-CPU note (i9-14900K-specific):** the bench sets process
affinity to 16 P-thread logical IDs (`SetProcessAffinityMask(0xFFFF)`)
and matches `crd::jobs::Config::num_threads = 16` + `Eigen::setNbThreads(16)`
so both libraries get the same execution budget. Pass `--all-cores`
to use the full 32 hybrid threads (E-core static partition makes
this generally slower due to E-core bottleneck).

**Open follow-on:** `v0d-small-gemm-fastpath` — at N=256 f64 Eigen's
small-matrix specialized code path beats Cerid 2x because Cerid's full
Goto/BLIS packing pipeline has ~290 us fixed overhead per call. Add a
direct-vectorized GEMM for m*n*k below ~10M flops to close that gap.

**OpenBLAS-on-MSVC reality:** OpenBLAS v0.3.27 cannot produce an
asm-tuned reference under MSVC — upstream `prebuild.cmake:1346`
hardcodes `-DFORCE_GENERIC` AND its asm-tuned HASWELL kernels use
GAS syntax incompatible with ml64. The MSVC-buildable OpenBLAS runs
a 2x2 scalar-C kernel (10-70 GFLOPS) which is NOT a fair reference.
Real Cerid-vs-OpenBLAS-asm comparison requires Linux / MinGW / vcpkg
prebuilt — filed as future work.

Related: [hesap-microkernel-intrinsics-decision](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision) (ADR-0082; intrinsics
vs asm path; FMA-via-intrinsics is the spirit of the ADR).


<!-- end-memory:project_hesap_beats_eigen_mt_via_fma -->

<a id="memory-project_hesap_gemm_asm_reopen_and_bmwcra_kernel_ceiling"></a>
## project_hesap_gemm_asm_reopen_and_bmwcra_kernel_ceiling

---
name: project-hesap-gemm-asm-reopen-and-bmwcra-kernel-ceiling
description: "Hand-tuned GEMM asm REVERTED (intrinsics vindicated); v5a-7 within-front parallelism (3 sub-slices: cmod+cdiv row-slab) FLIPPED bmwcra 0.65→1.04-1.05x WIN — EVERY matrix now beats CHOLMOD w/ determinism moat; serial POTF2 floor ~0; fill ≠ flop"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3ec0583a-1bae-4ef2-ad8d-aa562b34cb2d
---

2026-05-30. **Hand-tuned GEMM asm was built end-to-end and REVERTED — DO NOT re-try it for Cerid's inlined-microkernel pattern.** ADR-0088 (Status: **Reverted**) re-opened ADR-0082's asm question: built a dual-syntax MASM/GAS f64 6×8 kernel + runtime CPUID dispatch + the build integration, all **bit-identical** to the intrinsic, green on MSVC/clang-cl/gcc. Then measured it. **Decisive same-process A/B (asm vs intrinsic timed µs apart, identical clock): asm ≈ 0.98× — ~1–2% SLOWER.** Structural, not tunable: the intrinsic **inlines** into `gemm_packed_inner` at ~98% peak; the asm is a hard call (per-call/prologue overhead). You can't inline hand-asm across TUs. (OpenBLAS/BLIS asm wins only because their whole framework is asm; Cerid competes against an inlined-98%-peak intrinsic.) Earlier "+10–16% IPC" was a turbo-clock artifact (%-of-peak normalization assumed startup-clock==GEMM-clock; false on a turboing 14900K — interleave or same-process to kill it). **ADR-0082 (intrinsics-first) STANDS, vindicated. The whole cluster (asm + the v0d-asm-0 direct-to-C framework change, which was ~3%-within-noise) was reverted to the committed v5a-5.** The ADR-0082 hot-swap point stays only for a genuine future asm-only-ISA need (AMX etc.), NOT a generic perf lever.

**bmwcra crush = the SCALING lever, NOT the kernel — and the scaling is FIXABLE, not a wall (DECISIVELY MEASURED 2026-05-30).** (1) **fill ≠ flop** — bmwcra Cerid flops == CHOLMOD's (1.286e11 ≈ 1.287e11); the "11–16% less fill ⇒ fewer flops ⇒ fill-margin wins" thesis in [project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap](project-history.md#memory-project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap) / [project_cholmod_factor_gap](project-history.md#memory-project_cholmod_factor_gap) is **FALSE**. (2) Clean same-build WSL measurement at HEAD: bmwcra FACTOR 1T 0.77× → 8T 0.65× — the gap **WIDENS** (CHOLMOD self-scales 1.87× vs Cerid 1.59×), so scaling IS a real lever (refutes the "lever-3 already fixed it / gap-narrows" guess). (3) Scale-profiler decomposition (8T): the loss is **concentrated ~70% in ~23 huge near-root fronts** (nc up to 2406), NOT spread out: huge-front cmod scales **1.86×**, cdiv only **1.20×** (the serial diagonal chain), setup ~9% / starved ~9%. (4) **ob_probe DECISIVE — NOT a bandwidth wall:** OpenBLAS-threaded dgemm on Cerid's EXACT cmod/cdiv shapes scales **4.5–6.8×** (cmod M2048/N512/K200=4.58×; cdiv dtrsm/dgemm 6.4–6.8×) where Cerid in-situ gets 1.86×/1.20×. ⇒ the shapes parallelize fine; Cerid's poor scaling is a **fork/join + scheduling deficiency** (the front fires MANY small per-descendant `gemm_parallel` calls, each paying fork/join; OpenBLAS does one efficient threaded call) — **FIXABLE**, not a wall. **Honest ceiling: parity-to-~1.1× on bmwcra** (per-thread gemm ~0.7× OpenBLAS = the ADR-0082 intrinsic ceiling caps the upside), but it flips bmwcra off the loss list AND is a **general within-front scaling lever for ALL large factors (hood/ldoor too) + the substrate strength eylem needs.**

**DECISION 2026-05-30: user chose GO on the multi-session within-front-parallelism rewrite** (cut per-descendant fork/join + batch front updates one-fork-per-front + parallelize the cdiv diagonal-chain front; PaStiX/MA87-class). The hard part PaStiX/MA87 DON'T carry: it must hold Cerid's **bit-identity cross-thread determinism moat** (row-slab partition ≡ serial accumulation order).

**v5a-7 SUB-SLICE 1 SHIPPED + VERIFIED 2026-05-31 (cmod ROW-slab parallelism):** node-parallel huge-front cmod now does ONE `parallel_for` over the front's ROWS (NOT per-descendant `gemm_parallel`); each lane does each descendant's sub-gemm over its contiguous pr-range (`lrm` is MONOTONIC — advisor corrected my wrong COLUMN-axis pick: row-split partitions the bigger operand am / shares am1 / IS OpenBLAS's M-partition that hit 4.58×; column would re-read am W×). Bit-identical by construction. cmod scaling 1.86→4.46× (matched OpenBLAS). **3 sub-slices, all bit-identical (moat GREEN 591348 asserts {1,2,4,8}): (1) cmod row-slab; (2) cdiv targeted serialization** — the cdiv "chain" INFLATED 223→375ms@8T (small per-block fork/join: A2/A3 ≤192×64 gemms + B1 apply ≤64 cols); forced those SERIAL (`par_workers=1`), → chain back to 225ms (bmwcra→~0.97×); **(3) cdiv B-block ROW-slab (refactor #2 — the WIN).** A1-floor probe proved the genuinely-serial POTF2 floor = **2.6ms (negligible)** ⇒ green-light; row-slabbed the B below-outer work over `below_o` rows (one fork per outer block, each lane walks jb-blocks SEQUENTIALLY B1→B2 = serial accumulation order ⇒ bit-identical; per-lane ub_w/linv_w, shared read-only L11, redundant 64×64 invert), `rest` 220→~100ms@8T (2.2×). **v5a-7 FINAL (clean WSL 8T, 2 clean runs): 🎉 bmwcra 0.65→1.04–1.05× WIN (both runs ≥1.04×) · hood 1.33→1.48× · ldoor 1.28→1.44–1.76× · bcsstk25 1.41→1.75× — EVERY matrix now BEATS CHOLMOD, with the determinism moat none of the peers carry; NO regression.** HONEST: bmwcra's win is MODEST ~4–5% (per-thread intrinsic-gemm ceiling keeps it modest; parallel scaling flipped it). Load-imbalance polish (`num_jobs=par_workers*4` over-decompose) TRIED + measured NULL on the real all-matrix workload (helped only the cold-start bmwcra-only corner = confound) ⇒ REVERTED — magic knob, no real-workload benefit; residual `rest` 2.2× (vs cmod 4.46×) = row-slab load imbalance whose genuine fix is guided/work-stealing chunking = CHARACTERIZED future lever, not chased (bounded-importance, already winning). The user's "I think we can crush" was RIGHT (probe-in read 1.00×; clean revealed the win). Owed before phase commit: clang-cl/asan/tidy/win-shipping (win-debug+gcc green; dormant CHOL_PROFILE `-Werror` landmine unfixed). Session log `docs/sessions/2026-05-31-hesap-v5a-7-within-front-cmod-rowslab.md`. [feedback_crush_mandate_bounded_by_importance](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_crush_mandate_bounded_by_importance)

**How to apply:** for Cerid the intrinsic GEMM (inlined, ~ceiling) is the per-thread elite path — don't propose hand-asm microkernels as a perf lever (measured slower). bmwcra's lever is WITHIN-FRONT PARALLELISM (fork/join + scheduling), proven fixable by ob_probe (`build/ob_probe_mt.cpp`, gitignored). Bench `bench_hesap_cholesky_vs_cholmod` (CRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_CHOLMOD, WSL). ⚠ dev landmine: `supernodal_cholesky.cpp` ~line 1337 has a dormant `-Werror=conversion` (`double / g_cholprof.cmod_calls`) that bites only when CHOL_PROFILE is enabled under gcc. [feedback_no_commit_recs_until_phase_done](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_no_commit_recs_until_phase_done) [project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism](project-history.md#memory-project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism)

## project_hesap_is_universal_foundation_zero_defect

---
name: project_hesap_is_universal_foundation_zero_defect
description: hesap is the universal computational substrate for ALL engine + external tools; v18 = agent-drivable MATLAB; zero-defect bar is non-negotiable
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d095b72d-cb68-40b1-aaa2-1147516ea4fd
---

⭐⭐ **hesap is the UNIVERSAL computational foundation.** Every system built on the Cerid engine — in-engine
(EYLEM physics, crd-ui, editor, …) AND every external tool made with the engine — calls into hesap for its math.
**v18 is "our own MATLAB": an environment agents must be able to drive FAITHFULLY and EASILY.** (Extends
[project_v14_v18_planning](project-history.md#memory-project_v14_v18_planning), [project_post_hesap_sequencing](project-history.md#memory-project_post_hesap_sequencing), [project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction](project-history.md#memory-project_agent_native_engine_strategic_direction).)

**Why the quality bar is ABSOLUTE (not aspirational):** a defect in hesap propagates to everything downstream. So
for EVERY hesap op / slice, ALL of these are required — none is optional:
- **Correct** — matched-accuracy vs the gold standards, self-verified (the all-peers-agree bench gate,
  [feedback_bench_gate_all_peers_agree](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_gate_all_peers_agree); the 3-oracle gradient gate; determinism moat).
- **Full crush** — beat every fastest peer at its best, all metrics, no cherry-pick, no losses
  ([feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards)).
- **No scars / no gaps** — no known-broken edge, no "documented loss", no config that fails, no silent perf break.
  A scar or gap is an OPEN BUG (SANITY #9). Cross-config green (6 configs) every slice.
- **Agent-drivable** — clean, discoverable, faithful API: a CLI command per op, typed two-layer architecture,
  documented, deterministic (same input → same bits), so an agent (and v18's MATLAB layer) can drive it without
  surprises. The CLI/system-doc/conformance work is the v15-z close, but design every op for it from the start.

**How to apply:** never trade any of correctness / crush / cleanliness / agent-ergonomics against another. If one is
at risk, solve it (research, persist) — do not ship a slice that sacrifices one. This is the standard for v15 and
every remaining hesap cluster.

<a id="memory-project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision"></a>
## project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision

---
name: hesap-microkernel-intrinsics-decision
description: "Hesap GEMM microkernels ship pure C++ intrinsics via crd-math::simd, NOT hand-rolled per-arch ASM. Locked 2026-05-19, ADR-0082. Hot-swap point preserved for future ASM via CRD_HESAP_MICROKERNEL_BACKEND switch + signature contract."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8232c613-08b5-412f-9d51-73f8c05a65d9
---

## Decision (ADR-0082, Accepted 2026-05-19)

Hesap BLAS L3 microkernels are pure C++ intrinsics via `crd-math::simd::Vec8f`
(AVX2) + `Vec16f` (AVX-512) + `Vec4f` (NEON) + scalar fallback. Hand-rolled
inline-asm per-µarch is **deferred indefinitely** behind a documented
compile-time switch.

## Why

User asked 2026-05-19: "do we really need hand-rolled inline asm per arch?"
Analysis:

- Asm buys 5-10% on Intel, 3-5% on AMD Zen 4, ~2% on modern compilers
  with PGO. Gap is shrinking over compiler generations.
- Asm costs: ~25 per-µarch files × 7 BLAS L3 ops = ~42 hand-maintained
  files; MSVC + clang-cl + GCC need three syntaxes (MASM / Intel-syntax
  .S / AT&T-syntax .S); typos cost a day to bisect; determinism
  contract audited per-variant.
- Cerid is a general-purpose engine substrate, NOT a BLAS library.
  Actual hesap consumers (eylem FEM GEMV, geometry small-N ops,
  iterative solvers spMV-dominated, future ML GPU not CPU) are not
  GEMM-FLOP-bound at scale where 5% peak matters.
- The `feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor` mandate is
  about workload measurement, not engineering class. Intrinsics
  microkernels matching Eigen / Faer / Highway / xtensor / Stan-math
  / Armadillo / mlpack at ~85% peak IS the elite reference floor for
  the intrinsics class. Asm-class is a different sport.

## Hot-swap architecture (open door)

Locked signature for future ASM swap:

```cpp
template <typename T>
void gemm_microkernel(crd::usize k,
                      const T* a_packed,
                      const T* b_packed,
                      T*       c_tile,
                      crd::usize ldc) noexcept;
```

Compile-time backend switch:

```cpp
#define CRD_HESAP_MICROKERNEL_BACKEND_INTRINSICS 1  // default
#define CRD_HESAP_MICROKERNEL_BACKEND_ASM        2  // reserved
```

`gemm_microkernel.hpp` `#if`-branches on this. Future ASM impl drops
into `engine/hesap-dense/src/asm/<arch>.S` files exporting symbols
that match the signature; the `_ASM` backend gates them in at link time.

## Revisit conditions (ADR-0082 §revisit)

Three must all hold to flip:

1. A measured Cerid workload sustains >50% of solve time on GEMM at N>1000
2. The intrinsics microkernel measures <70% of MKL/BLIS-asm peak on that workload's HW
3. No other optimization (GPU offload via rhi-compute, sparse algo switch, different solver) has a better cost-benefit ratio

Until all three: intrinsics is the path. No time-bounded review.

## How to apply

- When implementing new microkernels (today: AVX-512, NEON, scalar variants),
  always emit through crd-math::simd. Never write asm.
- When v0d-perf consumers measure GEMM perf, report intrinsics-class
  peak ratio (vs Eigen / Faer baseline), NOT asm-class (vs MKL/BLIS-asm).
- When a future architect considers ASM, route them to ADR-0082's
  three-condition revisit gate.
- The same engineering-economics argument applies to SIMD-tunable
  kernels in `crd-hesap-iterative` v4 (spMV, CG) and `crd-hesap-fft`
  v10 — default to intrinsics; ASM only after all three conditions hit.

## REAFFIRMED 2026-06-11 — with the strongest evidence yet + the WASM argument

User re-asked ("do we need hand tuned asm's?... we will use most of cerid functionality in browser...
I think intrinsics are enough") and the answer is now EMPIRICALLY settled, not just economically:

1. **ADR-0088 built the asm and MEASURED it at ≈0.98× of the inlined intrinsics — reverted.** The 6×8 f64
   intrinsics kernel runs ~98% of theoretical peak standalone. There is no inner-loop headroom.
2. **The entire 2026-06-11 CHOLMOD crush arc (solve 0.50×→WIN, factor 0.73→parity, x16 collapse→WIN) came
   from portable-C++ structure**: DRAM multi-stream parallelism (4-fused column streams, measured 22.7 vs
   36.9 GB/s), 4-way interleaved packing, r-blocking, fma-chain ILP, call-overhead removal. Zero asm.
   OpenBLAS's residual ~10% on big dense shapes = per-µarch memory tuning, mostly closed the same way.
3. **WASM makes asm strictly wrong**: no meaningful inline-asm path in the browser; the crd::math::simd
   backend abstraction maps onto WASM SIMD128 as just another backend — every kernel compiles unchanged.
   Asm = a per-ISA fork with a dead branch exactly where Cerid wants to ship
   ([project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal](project-history.md#memory-project_browser_wasm_deployment_goal)). ⚠ WASM determinism note for that future slice: relaxed-SIMD
   FMA is non-deterministic across engines — pin strict SIMD128 / emulated single-rounded fma; that's a
   dispatch decision only the portable layer can make.
4. The determinism moat's bit-identity audit (pinned fma + fixed reduction trees) lives ONCE in the
   intrinsics layer; per-µarch asm would multiply the audit surface.

The CRD_HESAP_MICROKERNEL_BACKEND seam stays (costs nothing); the three-condition revisit gate stands and
is NOWHERE near met (intrinsics ≈85–90% of OpenBLAS-asm on the shapes that matter). Standing answer:
**intrinsics, full stop — do not relitigate without new gate-passing measurements.**

Related: [feedback-reference-implementations-are-the-floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor),
[feedback-quality-bar](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_quality_bar), [feedback-ship-at-consumer-template-from-day-one](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_ship_at_consumer_template_from_day_one),
[feedback-elite-only-no-shortcuts](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_elite_only_no_shortcuts) (elite-only ≠ asm-only; the elite
choice for a substrate is the maintainable one).


<!-- end-memory:project_hesap_microkernel_intrinsics_decision -->

<a id="memory-project_hesap_simulation_target_and_gold_standards"></a>
## project_hesap_simulation_target_and_gold_standards

---
name: project_hesap_simulation_target_and_gold_standards
description: "hesap sparse-solver crush target = STRUCTURED simulation matrices (cloth/deformation SPD, CFD/Navier-Stokes); gold standards = CHOLMOD/UMFPACK/PARDISO/MUMPS, not just Eigen"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: de24be60-d214-48f5-94bf-4e8ca5e4673f
---

**2026-05-31 — user clarified the hesap sparse-solver CRUSH TARGET + the real gold standards.** The point of
the sparse solvers is FUTURE SIMULATIONS + GAMES: **cloth physics, deformations, CFD, Navier-Stokes.** This
reorients everything:

- **Cloth / deformation / structural FEM are SPD** (mass+stiffness, implicit integration) ⇒ **Cholesky**,
  gold standard **CHOLMOD** (+ PARDISO). Cerid's v5a supernodal Cholesky ALREADY CRUSHES CHOLMOD on the
  structural-mechanics matrices (hood 1.33×, ldoor 1.28×, bmwcra ~1.04×) WITH cross-thread bit-determinism
  CHOLMOD lacks. ⇒ **the most important sim workload (SPD deformation) is already a gold-standard crush.**
- **CFD / Navier-Stokes** split: pressure-Poisson SPD → Cholesky; advection unsymmetric → **LU**, gold
  standards **UMFPACK / PARDISO / SuperLU_DIST**. Cerid v5b LU beats Eigen on the structured CFD/PDE
  matrices (af23560 CFD 1.04×, wang3 semiconductor 3.53× crush, sherman3 1.02×).

**KEY STRATEGIC TRUTH:** the circuit/SPICE matrices I'd been grinding (memplus/add32/west2021/gemat11) are
NOT the target — they're EE benchmarks. Don't over-optimize them. The target is STRUCTURED. On structured
matrices Cerid already wins/crushes the RIGHT gold standards.

**For "PERFECT CRUSH" on LARGE structured matrices:** serial micro-opt won't 2-4× a mature Eigen. The lever
is the DETERMINISM MOAT's payoff = **parallel scaling**, and the fair same-class peer is NOT serial Eigen
but the **PARALLEL gold standards (PARDISO/MUMPS/SuperLU_DIST/parallel-CHOLMOD)** — which Cerid can beat on
speed AND offer bit-determinism none of them have. (parallel-Cerid-vs-serial-Eigen = the asterisked
category error [feedback_bench_against_the_correct_peer](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_against_the_correct_peer); vs parallel peers it's a legitimate crush.)

**CRITICAL FINDING (2026-05-31, from testing the ACTUAL NS targets — measure-first on real workload):**
the STATIC-PIVOT LU (the determinism-moat foundation) PRODUCES WRONG ANSWERS on SADDLE-POINT / indefinite
Navier-Stokes systems: garon2 (2D NS FEM) residual **1.9e+05**, raefsky3 (CFD) residual **1.4** — garbage
(should be ~1e-15). ns3Da (3D NS, definite-ish) is fine (6.7e-16, 0.72×). Root cause: incompressible NS
has indefinite velocity-pressure coupling ⇒ MC64 matches a near-zero diagonal ⇒ GESP perturbs ⇒ IR can't
recover. This is the TEXTBOOK static-pivot failure on indefinite systems. The bench `[ok]` was RESIDUAL-
BLIND (only `info()==0`) — it silently passed 1.9e5; FIXED to `cer_res<1e-6 ? ok : INACCURATE`.
⇒ **THE MOAT (static pivot) HAS A CORRECTNESS LIMIT: safe for SPD (Cholesky, unconditionally stable) and
DEFINITE unsym (LU), but UNSAFE for saddle-point/indefinite NS.** Implication: cloth/deformation/pressure-
Poisson (SPD→Cholesky) = the moat's solid majority; incompressible-NS saddle-point needs dynamic-pivot LU
(stable, serial, loses moat) OR a saddle-point method (Schur/Uzawa/aug-Lagrangian) — a real future gap, NOT
a speed issue. v5b-1 GP-LU (dynamic partial pivot, serial) IS stable for these — the correctness fallback.

**FIX LANDED (2026-05-31): `SupernodalLU::solve` now RETURNS FALSE on divergence** (honest contract — no
silent garbage). After IR, if a column didn't converge (`!converged`), it rechecks the FINAL y's true
residual; if > accept_tol=√ε (~1.5e-8) ⇒ `ok=false`. Converged solves (1e-11..1e-15) pass; saddle-point
garbage (garon2 1.9e5, raefsky3 1.4) ⇒ solve returns false. Common (definite) case pays nothing (only the
non-converged column rechecks). Full suite 591526 green (definite matrices still return true). FULL fix
(dynamic-pivot fallback to make saddle-point SOLVABLE) is a future completeness item — NOT needed for the
games path (projection-fluid → SPD → Cholesky). bench `[ok]→INACCURATE` (residual-gated) already shows it.

**REASSURING NUANCE (the practical sim/games path is FINE):** monolithic saddle-point LU (garon2) is a
RESEARCH-FEM formulation. PRODUCTION + GAMES incompressible fluid uses PROJECTION / fractional-step /
SIMPLE-PISO / pressure-correction ⇒ the heavy solve is the SPD **pressure-Poisson** (+ SPD/dom velocity)
⇒ **Cholesky** ⇒ moat-SAFE + crushing CHOLMOD. So the moat (via Cholesky) covers the PRACTICAL sim/games
workloads (cloth, deformation, projection-fluid pressure-Poisson). The static-pivot-LU saddle-point gap is
a research-FEM edge, addressable later (dynamic pivot / Schur / Uzawa), NOT a blocker for games fluid sim.

**PLAN (both paths, careful multi-session, user said "take your time"):**
0. (NEW, gating) DECIDE the saddle-point-NS strategy: dynamic-pivot fallback vs saddle-point solver. The
   SPD path (Cholesky, the bulk) is unaffected + already crushing.
1. Re-aim the LU bench corpus at TARGETS: Navier-Stokes/CFD matrices (garon2 [2D NS FEM], ns3Da [3D NS],
   venkat [CFD Euler], raefsky [CFD/struct], af23560) — replace circuit distractions.
2. UMFPACK comparison (unsym CFD gold standard; WSL, CRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_UMFPACK — see
   [reference_cholmod_oracle_and_wsl_build](build-and-verification.md#memory-reference_cholmod_oracle_and_wsl_build) for the WSL pattern) + push the v5a-Cholesky-vs-CHOLMOD
   margin on deformation/structural matrices.
3. The deterministic-parallel scaling (within-node + tree) benchmarked vs PARDISO/MUMPS — the real perf
   crush for large structured solves (+ the determinism edge). Within-node parallelism mirrors v5a-7.
4. iw-GC (clean serial AMD speedup, [project_lu_crush_two_kernel_plan](project-history.md#memory-project_lu_crush_two_kernel_plan)) along the way.

Related: [project_lu_crush_two_kernel_plan](project-history.md#memory-project_lu_crush_two_kernel_plan) (the v5b LU crush detail + Eigen-COLAMD fair result),
[project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism](project-history.md#memory-project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism) (the determinism-as-perf-weapon thesis),
[project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap](project-history.md#memory-project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap) (v5a Cholesky crushes CHOLMOD), [feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat).

<a id="memory-project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate"></a>
## project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate

---
name: project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate
description: hesap v3 (SVD + dense eig) is locked at maximum ambition — MRRR + AED HARD-GATE the cluster close
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 021fa904-7b98-4a07-9c4e-4f1cb715ea28
---

Phase 3.1.6 `crd-hesap` v3 (SVD + dense eigenvalue, in `crd-hesap-dense`) is locked at **maximum ambition** by user directive 2026-05-21. Two firm decisions:

1. **Algorithm tier = full LAPACK-elite.** Beat both Eigen AND LAPACK wherever possible. Deep-research the LAPACK reference (`dsytrd/dsteqr/dstedc/dstemr/dlasq/dlarrv/dgebrd/dbdsqr/dbdsdc/dgebal/dgehrd/dhseqr/dtrevc`), Eigen internals, and canonical papers (Demmel-Kahan, Gu-Eisenstat, Dhillon-Parlett MRRR, Braman-Byers-Mathias AED, Halko-Martinsson-Tropp randomized) before each sub-slice.
2. **MRRR + AED HARD-GATE the v3 close.** v3 does NOT close until MRRR (`dstemr`-class) beats LAPACK `stegr` AND Aggressive Early Deflation is in the non-symmetric eig path. NOT filed-in-cluster aspirational — they block close. Calendar risk (realistically 8–12+ weeks) explicitly accepted.

**Locked subdivision:** v3a sym-eig (a-1 blocked-WY-reduction-substrate + tridiag + QL/QR + Hermitian; a-2 D&C/Cuppen jobified; a-3 MRRR) → v3b SVD (b-1 bidiag + Demmel-Kahan + complex; b-2 D&C bidiag SVD; b-3 randomized Halko) → v3c LS family (lstsq + pinv + NNLS Lawson-Hanson + TLS) → v3d non-sym (d-1 balance + Hessenberg + Francis double-shift Schur + AED; d-2 eigenvectors `dtrevc` + 3-stage back-transform + complex Schur) → v3e CLI audit + vs-ref rollup + ADR-0065 §17 + 18-config sweep close.

**Why:** user values eigensolvers/SVD highly (masters/PhD background); the "beat the reference floor" mandate ([feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor)) applies in full here.

**STATUS (2026-05-22):** **v3a-1 CLOSED** — real symmetric eigensolver (`engine/hesap-dense/{include/crd/hesap/dense/eig_sym.hpp,src/eig_sym.cpp,src/cli_register_eig.cpp}` + `detail/householder.hpp`); blocked `dsytrd` + `steqr` QL/QR + column-major SIMD eigenvectors; **beats Eigen 1.2–1.5× and LAPACK 1.5–3.5×** at N=64–1024, accuracy ~1e-12; 5-config DoD PASS. `v3a-1-perf` re-scoped to a non-issue (flop recount: our parallel `P=V·Wᵀ` is already syr2k-flop-optimal). **v3a-1b (complex Hermitian) DEFERRED to after v3a-2.** **NOW: v3a-2 (Cuppen D&C), plan locked in phase doc; complex Hermitian folded in as v3a-2.5 (user directive 2026-05-22).** **v3a-2.1 DONE** — `detail/secular.hpp` `secular_root<R>` = bracket-confined Newton+bisection with anchor-shifted stable eval (**D(dense-eig)-8**, deliberate divergence from `dlaed4` BNS rational interpolation: advisor-approved since root-finding is O(n²logn) ≪ eigenvector O(n³), and bisection can't converge outside the bracket = strictly safer). Cross-checked vs `eig_sym(diag(d)+ρzzᵀ)`; `test_eig_dc.cpp` 6 cases green (clustered/small-ρ/n=1,2/determinism). **v3a-2.2 DONE** — `rank1_eigensolve` in `eig_sym.cpp` (decl in `eig_sym.hpp`): eigendecomp of `diag(d)+ρzzᵀ` = faithful `dlaed2` deflation (negligible-weight + equal-pole Givens; **bug found+fixed: Givens c=z_nj/τ, s=−z_pj/τ NOT swapped** — wrong order gives wrong eigenvectors though d-update/criterion unaffected for equal poles) + `secular_root` + Löwner/Gu-Eisenstat ŵ-reconstruction + `gemm_parallel` back-transform. `test_eig_dc.cpp` 11 cases/2863 assertions green (distinct/negligible-z/triple-equal-pole/unsorted/N=40, all vs `eig_sym` reconstruction + orthonormality). **v3a-2.3 DONE** — `dc_tridiag_eig` in `eig_sym.cpp`: Cuppen D&C on a symmetric tridiagonal (cut at n/2 + rank-1 correction `rho=e[m-1]`, recurse to `steqr` base case at n≤32, merge via `rank1_eigensolve` with **fused Q·V back-transform** — `rank1_eigensolve` gained a nullable `q_in` param + rho<0 negate-and-reverse handling). **Serial recursion + parallel merge gemm = deterministic + bit-identical across workers** (D(dense-eig)-6 satisfied without recursion-level parallelism, since the only parallelism is the deterministic gemm_parallel). `test_eig_dc.cpp` 14 cases/9822 assertions green (base-case-vs-steqr / recursion N=50,120,300 reconstruction+ortho / determinism N=80). Full hesap-dense suite 200 cases/78,085 assertions, no regression. **v3a-2.4 DONE — GATE MET.** `eig_sym` dispatches: QL/QR (steqr) for n≤`kEigDcThreshold`=256, D&C for n>256 (tuned crossover). vs Eigen `SelfAdjointEigenSolver` + LAPACK `dsyev`: **beats both at EVERY size — Eigen 1.21–1.94×, LAPACK 1.90–3.86×** (N=64..1024), accuracy ~1e-12. **Bug found+fixed: Löwner ŵ²=∏num/∏den overflowed at N=512 (separate K-factor products → NaN); fixed by interleaving (dlaed3 form)** → [feedback_lowner_product_overflow_interleave](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_lowner_product_overflow_interleave). Full suite 201 cases/78,599 assertions green. **5-config DoD PASS** (only win-tidy needed a test-only fix: `static_cast<usize>(n*n)`→widen-before-multiply, `bugprone-misplaced-widening-cast`; engine code tidy-clean). **v3a-2.5 complex Hermitian: CORRECT + TESTED + partial gate.** `eig_herm` in `eig_sym.cpp`: `tridiagonalize_hermitian` (zhetd2, complex reflector `make_householder_herm`, **phase-diagonal fix for the last subdiagonal** — m=1 step has no reflector so realize complex g as |g| with phase folded into Q) → real `dc_tridiag_eig` on (D,E) → **fused blocked back-transform `apply_q_to_z_complex`** (compact-WY zunmtr via complex `gemm_parallel`, replaced the 148ms scalar form_q). Tests `[herm]` 4 cases/20,110 assertions (N≤512, f32, determinism); matches Eigen to ~1e-12. **v3a-2.5 SHIPPED 2026-05-22 — SIMD complex reduction was the decisive fix.** Carry the working Hermitian as two REAL arrays `ar`/`ai` (lower tri) so the zhetd2 matvec + rank-2 update are contiguous-row real SIMD (`simd_dot`/`simd_axpy`), NO scalar complex; reflectors land in ar/ai and `apply_q_zsplit` reads them directly (dropped the complex `work` materialization). **Bench (c64) vs Eigen: N=64 1.00x (tie — floor, Eigen hand-inlined small `zhetrd`), N=128 1.11x (was 0.94x), N=256 1.56x, N=512 1.89x, N=1024 2.22x; beats LAPACK zheev everywhere 2.5–4.4x; accuracy ~1e-14.** User accepted N=64 tie ("we are pushing to the limits now"). CLI `hesap.dense.eig.herm.{c32,c64}` registered (A = interleaved `[re,im]`, lower tri) + CLI round-trip test `[[2,1+i],[1-i,3]]`→{1,4}. Dead scalar paths removed (`tridiagonalize_hermitian`, `form_q_hermitian`, `cgemm_split`, `apply_q_to_z_complex`). Full suite 206 cases/98,716 assertions green. (DoD 5-config in flight at close.) (Earlier NEXT was) v3a-2.5 complex Hermitian — FULLY RESEARCHED, ready to implement.** Recipe (refs read: `zhetd2.f`, complex `zlarfg.f`): (1) **complex reflector** = `zlarfg`: real `beta=-sign(alphr)·sqrt(alphr²+alphi²+xnorm²)`, `tau=Complex((beta-alphr)/beta, -alphi/beta)`, v-tail scaled by complex-div `x_k/(alpha-beta)`, + safmin loop. (2) **`tridiagonalize_hermitian`** = exact analog of my real `reduce_sub_unblocked` but complex: Hermitian matvec `x=tau·H·v` (H(r,c)=r≥c? a[r,c] : conj(a[c,r])), `alpha2=-0.5·tau·Σconj(x)v` (zdotc), `w=x+alpha2·v`, rank-2 `H(r,c) -= v_r·conj(w_c)+w_r·conj(v_c)` (lower only), **force diagonal real**; outputs real D,E + complex reflectors + complex tau. (3) reuse real `dc_tridiag_eig`/`steqr` on (D,E) → real eigvals + real Z. (4) **complex back-transform** V=Q·Z: form complex Q from reflectors (zungtr analog) then complex `gemm_parallel` Q·Z (gemm is templated on Complex — v0d shipped it). (5) `eig_herm(alloc, Hermitian<Complex<R>>) -> EigSym<Complex<R>>` (values real, vectors complex — interfaces already complex-aware). (6) CLI `hesap.dense.eig.herm.{c32,c64}` + anchor. Gate: vs Eigen complex SelfAdjointEigenSolver + LAPACK zheev. Test ≥512 (Löwner-overflow lesson). NOTE: only testable END-TO-END (no sub-piece test) → do in a fresh focused session. Then v3a-2 cluster DoD close. (deflation+merge, Löwner ŵ-reconstruction expressed as gemm, gate `‖VᵀV−I‖≤n·eps`) → 2.3 (recursion, flat-task-list-per-level parallel, fixed left-then-right join = bit-identical across workers) → 2.4 (dispatch+gate vs LAPACK `dsyevd`). Pins D(dense-eig)-6/-7.

**How to apply:** lift shared `detail::householder_block_reduction` (blocked WY) first so tridiag/bidiag/Hessenberg are bit-identical by construction. Fold complex into its real slice (Hermitian→v3a, complex Schur→v3d), not batched at close. Randomized SVD = v3b-3 (mid-cluster, Eigen has no path). Determinism pins (new D(dense-eig)-N for ADR-0065 §17): D&C recursion bit-identical across worker counts (deterministic merge + safeguarded fixed-iteration bisection/Newton secular root-finder); QR iteration fixed Wilkinson shift + capped max-iter; MRRR Gram-Schmidt re-orthogonalization fallback for clustered eigenvalues (commit, don't hope). Allocator propagation from input Matrix everywhere ([feedback_hesap_propagate_allocator](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_hesap_propagate_allocator)). <a id="memory-project_integer_lookback_is_bit_exact_sort_not_scan_walled"></a>
## project_integer_lookback_is_bit_exact_sort_not_scan_walled

---
name: integer-lookback-is-bit-exact-sort-not-scan-walled
description: Decoupled-lookback IS bit-exact for u32 radix-sort offsets (integer sums are order-independent) — the f32 scan wall does NOT apply to sort; onesweep is legal. Sort at 2.41 ms (0.437x CUB) with the remaining path fully quantified
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**AMENDS [bit-exact-scan-cannot-crush-decoupled-lookback](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bit_exact_scan_cannot_crush_decoupled_lookback):** that wall is about f32 ROUNDING order. For radix-sort
offsets everything is u32 COUNTS — integer addition is exactly associative/commutative, so decoupled-lookback's
timing-dependent arrival order yields IDENTICAL output bytes. **Onesweep is bit-exact-legal for sort.** Missing IR
for it: `stmt_for_break_if` (per-thread break out of kernel For; oracle = per-iteration active-set filtering like If)
— coherent publish + spin already exist from the chained scan.

**WARP-SYNCHRONOUS RANK SHIPPED (2026-07-14 later): CUDA B(epb4096) = 1.42 ms = 0.735x CUB; Vulkan 1.87 = 0.56x.** New IR
`SyncWarp`; rank = warp-contiguous chunks + per-warp counters (2 syncwarps/round, ZERO block barriers in rank; 33->6
barriers/scatter). Campaign 14.9 -> 1.42 = 10.5x. Remaining 1.36x itemized: ghist privatization/overlap (~0.12), reorder
bank-conflict padding, 384-thread config. Structure now matches CUB (onesweep+match_any+warp-rank), portable + bit-exact.

**CUDA BACKEND LANDED (2026-07-14): ONESWEEP via emit_compute_kernel_cuda = 1.77 ms = 0.59x CUB (best; Vulkan 2.20 = 0.48x).**
Pipeline: [.emit-cuda-sort] tool test generates bench/gpu-compute/ckir_onesweep_gen.cu (renamed kernels, hw __match_any_sync,
ticket forward-progress); driver ckir_onesweep_bench.cu runs A/B/C configs + CUB in one binary. epb 2048 best (8192 = 32
barrier-rounds, WORSE). REMAINING quantified lever to parity/crush: warp-synchronous rank (CUB-style per-warp counters +
ONE block scan = ~3 barriers/tile vs our 32) - needs a syncwarp-safe warp-accumulate pattern in CKIR.
**ONESWEEP BUILT + LANDED (2026-07-14): 2.20 ms = 0.48× CUB — the best portable bit-exact sort.** New IR: `ForBreakIf`
(oracle = per-iteration active-set filter; GLSL/WGSL conds need bool()) + `BufferAtomicAdd` (HLSL = byte-addressed
.InterlockedAdd). 7 dispatches/sort. ALSO: `SubgroupMatch`→subgroupPartitionNV was built and MEASURED SLOWER than the
8-ballot loop on Ada (0.43→0.59/pass — ballots pipeline, partition serializes) → op kept, hot path reverted. Crush >1×
not reached: the gap is rank machinery CUB hides in CUDA-only 99KB-shared 11K-key tiles; Vulkan caps 48KB. Next real
options: A/B paired-round rank (halve barriers) or bench the SAME IR on the CUDA backend (99KB tiles ⇒ near parity+).

Sort state (2026-07-13, 16.7M u32, RTX 4070 TiS): superseded — see above; earlier 4-kernel path 2.41 ms = 0.437×.
Winning structure (all bit-exact, oracle+Vulkan): bin-major privatized histogram (0.125/pass) → per-bin offset scan
(0.041) → 1-WG gbase totals-scan (0.001) → subgroup-ballot-rank scatter with LOCAL REORDER → coalesced run writes
(0.432 = 0.21 memory + 0.22 rank machinery). Quantified rest of the path: (1) `SubgroupMatch` IR op → NV
subgroupPartitionNV (hardware match_any; needs VK_NV_shader_subgroup_partitioned device ext; ballot-loop fallback
gives the SAME mask ⇒ bit-exact both lowerings) → ~0.55×; (2) onesweep (kills per-pass hist+offset ≈ −0.54 ms total)
→ ~0.7–0.8×; both + tile tuning ⇒ 0.9–1.0× parity band. >1× needs CUB-class scatter efficiency (their 0.236/pass
uses CUDA 99 KB-shared 11K-key tiles vs Vulkan's 48 KB cap). Board: docs/bench/2026-07-13-gpu-compute-primitives.md.

<a id="memory-project_loader_arena_concurrency_thread_safe_wrap"></a>
## project_loader_arena_concurrency_thread_safe_wrap

---
name: project_loader_arena_concurrency_thread_safe_wrap
description: Resource loaders own private per-type TLSF arenas called concurrently by async loads — wrap each in ThreadSafeAllocator; scratch/payload split rejected as over-engineering
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7b0bb65d-6788-4a80-96e7-82e1072ab242
---

Every `ILoader` (texture/mesh/material/shader/matrix + test loaders) owns a private
`crd::memory::GrowableTlsfAllocator` used for BOTH scratch (CrdrFile parse) AND the
persistent payload, and stores that allocator pointer in the payload so `unload()`
(which gets no LoadContext) can free cross-thread. There is ONE loader instance per
FourCC type. The async load path calls `loader->load()` on that shared instance from
multiple worker fibers concurrently → data race on the single-threaded TLSF heap,
surfacing as the `!block_is_free` assert. This was a real production race exposed (not
caused) by `win-debug-scalar` timing in the "four concurrent loads" test; the
no-malloc-sweep (which moved loaders from MallocAllocator → per-loader GrowableTlsf)
made it reachable.

**Elite fix (2026-05-27, advisor-endorsed):** wrap each loader's arena in
[project_no_malloc_sweep_before_v5](project-history.md#memory-project_no_malloc_sweep_before_v5)'s allocators —
```cpp
crd::memory::GrowableTlsfAllocator m_inner;
crd::memory::ThreadSafeAllocator   m_alloc{&m_inner}; // all existing &m_alloc refs now route through the wrapper
```
`ThreadSafeAllocator` (new in crd-memory, S8) is a mutex-guarded `IAllocator` wrapper.

**Why this over alternatives:**
- Keeps per-type pool locality (bulk eviction by type, hot-reload clears one heap,
  stable allocator ptr for cross-thread `unload()`) — don't abandon that for
  "loaders use ctx.allocator directly."
- Lock held only during `allocate()`/`deallocate()` (free-list manipulation, ~ns);
  decode/parse work runs lock-free between allocs. Uncontended in practice (16 textures
  × ~20 allocs = ~320 brief locks over tens of ms). This is what UE/Destiny typed pools do.
- **Scratch/payload split (per-thread lock-free scratch arena in LoadContext +
  thread-safe per-loader arena for payload only) was REJECTED as over-engineering** —
  it refactors LoadContext + every loader to save uncontended mutex acquisitions.
  Deferred-by-reasoning (NOT debt): revisit only on measured lock contention in a
  profiled streaming workload.

Also: `ResourceManager` wraps its caller-supplied allocator in `m_thread_safe` and
routes ALL bookkeeping containers + the loader-facing `m_alloc` through it (defensive —
container frees happen on job-completion paths). `StreamingAllocator` (S5) is already
internally thread-safe (mutex + atomic budgets). See [feedback_concurrent_tests_use_crd_jobs](build-and-verification.md#memory-feedback_concurrent_tests_use_crd_jobs).


<!-- end-memory:project_loader_arena_concurrency_thread_safe_wrap -->

<a id="memory-project_local_constexpr_naming_cleanup"></a>
## project_local_constexpr_naming_cleanup

---
name: project_local_constexpr_naming_cleanup
description: Local constexpr naming convention + win-tidy-local relaxed preset + the rename script that cleaned ~569 readability-identifier-naming warnings (2026-05-28)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7b0bb65d-6788-4a80-96e7-82e1072ab242
---

**Convention (settled 2026-05-28):** function-LOCAL `constexpr` constants are `lower_case`
snake (NO `k` prefix) — matches `CLAUDE.md` ("Constexpr var -> lower_case") and what
clang-tidy 20.1.8 enforces (it categorises a local `constexpr` as `LocalConstant` =
lower_case, NOT `LocalConstexprVariable`; the `.clang-tidy` `LocalConstexprVariableCase=k`
line is a dead letter on 20.1.8). The `k`-prefix is reserved for GLOBAL/namespace/static
constants only (`kLengthFactor` at file scope stays `kCamelCase` — those were left alone).

The codebase had ~569 violations (local `kFoo` constexprs); cleaned mechanically via
`scripts/rename_local_constexpr.py` (committed). It parses the VS Error List, then per file
word-bounded-renames: **drop-k -> snake** (`kMaxPrec`->`max_prec`); if that collides with an
existing same-named var in the file, **keep-k -> snake** fallback (`kN`->`k_n`); 1 needed a
manual unique name. Result: 229 drop-k + 118 keep-k + 1 manual, verified by a clean
`win-debug` build (exit 0) + clang-tidy spot checks (0 warnings). KEPT-K names (`k_n`,
`k_threads`) are valid lower_case and can be refined to pure drop-k later only by also
renaming the colliding local var.

**Gotcha (the script's one real risk):** a flagged local `kFoo` initialised from a class
member of the SAME name (`constexpr usize lane = BodyPool::kLane;`) — the word-bounded
file-wide replace also rewrites the `::kLane` member access (member isn't renamed) →
`BodyPool::lane` undefined. Hit `kLane` (BodyPool) + `kDegree` (BSpline3::k_degree). Catch
them: after running, grep changed files for `=\s*\w+(<...>)?::[a-z]` (member access with a
lowercase name; real static members are kCamel) and fix by restoring the member name. Also
note: the suspicious-call-argument + misc-redundant-expression checks may newly fire on the
snaked names / SIMD-backend macro check (false positives -> justified NOLINT). clang-tidy
won't run with only `clang-diagnostic-*`/`-*` enabled ("no checks enabled") -- enable one
real check to surface compile errors in a scan.

**`win-tidy-local` preset (committed in CMakePresets.json):** inherits `win-tidy` +
`CRD_CLANG_TIDY_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=OFF` — the local mirror of CI's win-tidy job
(`cmake --preset win-tidy -DCRD_CLANG_TIDY_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=OFF`, ci.yml line ~162). Use
THIS locally to get clang-tidy diagnostics WITHOUT the build failing (CI runs relaxed; bare
`win-tidy` is strict and fails on the version-skew warnings CI tolerates). Two benign
warnings remain and are expected: a dependency target's `/W4`->`/w` (D9025) and a
`misc-redundant-expression` false-positive on the SIMD-backend exactly-one compile check.
See [feedback_clang_tidy_must_be_llvm_20_not_22](build-and-verification.md#memory-feedback_clang_tidy_must_be_llvm_20_not_22).

## project_lu_crush_two_kernel_plan

---
name: project_lu_crush_two_kernel_plan
description: "v5b sparse-LU crush is a TWO-KERNEL effort (user-chosen): supernodal for structured + KLU-class scalar for circuit; amalgamation exhausted"
