**2026-05-31 — v5b unsymmetric sparse-LU crush direction (user decision: "Build both kernels — complete family").**

Measured state (win-vs-ref Release, serial nw=1, vs Eigen SparseLU on the SAME AMD-permuted matrix,
matched true residual; all `[ok]`, determinism moat green — 6/6 SupernodalLU tests incl. v5b-2d
bit-identity across {1,2,4,8} workers): west2021 0.19× · add32 0.57× · gemat11 0.69× · sherman3 0.37× ·
memplus 0.36× · af23560 0.28× · wang3 0.15×. bbmat OOMs (full-n SPA > GrowableTlsf chunk cap → removed
from corpus; needs the column-blocked panel).

**Diagnosis (profiler-confirmed, 3 measured cycles):** cmod = 78–97% of factor. At EQUAL fill (af23560,
gemat11) Cerid is 1.4–3.5× slower ⇒ pure **kernel-maturity gap** vs Eigen, spread across GEMM throughput +
the n-strided global-SPA scatter + the diagonal LU. Two structural facts:
1. **Amalgamation is EXHAUSTED** — relax 8→16 cut nsup 25–29% but made wang3 + all 5 circuit matrices
   SLOWER (zero-flop fill); af23560 only ~2% faster. relax=8 is optimal. The floor is NOT supernode count.
2. **The corpus splits by architecture fit.** Circuit/irregular (west2021/add32/memplus, much of
   gemat11/sherman3) = **KLU's domain**: supernodal degenerates to width-1 panels + pure overhead (true
   for Eigen too). No supernodal tuning crushes them — they need a different algorithm. PDE/CFD/struct
   (af23560, wang3) = supernodal's proper regime, but still 3.5× off on kernel maturity.

**THE PLAN (build both, structured-first):**
- **Kernel A — supernodal structured maturity (NEXT):** the floor is the SPA. `spa = n × max_nc` is
  54 MB/worker for af23560 (cache-hostile) ⇒ replace with a **SuperLU-style relative-indexed COMPACT
  panel** (`nr × nc` ≈ 700 KB, cache-resident; also fixes the bbmat OOM). Plus a tuned moderate-shape
  ColMajor GEMM (currently 15.6 GFLOP/s, need ~40 — dl::gemm is weak on ColMajor skinny f64; per-call
  alloc was REFUTED as the cause) + a blocked diagonal LU (af23560 diag = 1180 ms / 12%).
- **Kernel B — KLU-class non-supernodal scalar Gilbert-Peierls (AFTER A):** crushes the circuit matrices
  (beats BOTH Eigen and UMFPACK in their weak regime). A legitimate "complete family" slice.

**GEMM PROBE (2026-05-31, pivotal — reframes the "two independent costs"):** standalone `dl::gemm` on the
EXACT LU foot shape 300×100×290 ColMajor f64 hits **51 GFLOP/s** (RowMajor-transpose identity **58**, nice
cube 512³ 54/67) — NOT the 15.6 measured in-factorization. ⇒ the in-factorization 15.6 is **memory
pollution** (cold GEMM inputs + cache full of the 54 MB n-strided SPA garbage), NOT a kernel limit. So the
GEMM cost and the scatter cost are COUPLED through the SPA ⇒ the **compact panel is the UNIFYING fix
(likely sufficient, not just necessary)**: a few-MB cache-resident W keeps GEMM inputs hot (→ ~51) AND
makes the scatter cheap. Two free levers it revealed: route the foot GEMM via the **RowMajor-transpose
identity** (C colmajor m×n ≡ Cᵀ rowmajor n×m; C=A·B ⇒ Cᵀ=Bᵀ·Aᵀ → gemm<RowMajor>(Bᵀ,Aᵀ)→Cᵀ, same memory,
~+15%); and the hand AXPY kernel is SLOWER (28.6) ⇒ keep `dl::gemm`. Serial `gemm` ALWAYS packs (the
`small_gemm` fast path is gemm_parallel/RowMajor-only). Probe: `build/_gemm_probe.cpp`.

**KERNEL A — COMPACT PANEL LANDED (2026-05-31, correct + moat green 6/6 incl. v5b-2d):** replaced the
n×max_nc global-row SPA with a SuperLU-style relative-indexed COMPACT panel `W[pnr×nc]` (U-part = padded
contributor ranges → contiguous U-seg per K; L-part = m_li; `relmap[global→compact]`, sentinel kNoRow).
GOTCHA fixed: relaxed-amalgamation pads K's foot with explicit-zero rows NOT in J's pattern (rel=kNoRow)
⇒ the foot scatter MUST `if (pos!=kNoRow)` skip them (contribution is 0; bit-identical). Foot GEMM routed
via the RowMajor-transpose identity. RESULT (confirms the cache-pollution theory): **af23560 GEMM
15.6→31.7 GFLOP/s, total 0.28→0.37×; wang3 GEMM 28→46.** gemat11 REGRESSED 0.69→0.62 (the rel_w
indirection is pure overhead for small-n nc=1 circuit matrices whose SPA already fit cache — INHERENT;
the fix is Kernel B routing circuit to the scalar path, NOT the compact panel). af23560 remaining
breakdown: GEMM 2068ms + non-GEMM cmod 3195ms (big-panel foot scatter, pnr~n near root) + diag 1163ms
(`dense_lu_nopivot` is UNBLOCKED rank-1 — wide nc=290 blocks). NEXT LEVERS (Kernel A cont.): near-root
column-blocking (shrinks scatter working set + lifts GEMM 31.7→~51) + blocked diagonal LU. Then a
dispatcher (n / structure heuristic) picks compact-supernodal vs Kernel-B-scalar per matrix.

**KERNEL A levers 2/3 (2026-05-31, all correct + moat green, full suite 591526 asserts):**
- **fpos HOIST:** the foot scatter `col[rel_w[m_li[fr]]]` is a COLD double-indirection repeated per nc
  column; hoist `fpos[fr]=rel_w[m_li[kfrb+fr]]` ONCE per contributor (gated nc≥2 so the nc=1 circuit path
  keeps the lean inline lookup). RECOVERED+BEAT the compact-panel gemat11 regression (0.62→**0.80**, past
  the 0.69 baseline — its scatter volume is in nc≥2 tall panels) + af23560 0.37→0.40 + wang3 0.17→0.19.
- **BLOCKED diagonal LU:** `dense_lu_nopivot` was unblocked rank-1 (~1.7 GFLOP/s on wide nc≈290 diags);
  made it right-looking blocked (nb=48, BLAS-3 Schur via dl::gemm, scratch=per-worker LinearAllocator;
  nc≤48 degenerates to the old unblocked = bit-identical). af23560 diag **1197→223 ms**; total 6620→5548.
  wang3 2342→1917.
- **CUMULATIVE this session: af23560 0.25→0.47× · wang3 0.15→0.23× · gemat11 0.65→0.80× · sherman3
  0.37→0.43× (no regressions).** af23560 remaining = cmod 4481 (GEMM ~2180 @ 30 GFLOP/s + non-GEMM ~2300
  scatter/gather/writeback) + diag 223. NEXT = near-root COLUMN-BLOCKING (process wide supernodes in
  column chunks ⇒ GEMM 30→~45 + smaller scatter working set; ~100-line factor_one restructure, fresh
  context). Also noted: af23560 SOLVE 5× slow vs Eigen (separate lu_lu_solve lever). Then Kernel B.

**BREAKTHROUGH — ADAPTIVE ACTIVE-PANEL WIDTH CAP (2026-05-31, from READING Eigen's SparseLU.h source):**
Eigen's factorize() loops over PANELS of `m_perfv.panel_size=16` columns (dense work `m×16`, BOUNDED),
DECOUPLED from `maxsuper=128` (storage width). My supernode WAS the active panel (W[pnr×nc], nc up to
290) ⇒ cache-cold. FIX: cap the supernode (=active panel) width in BOTH `detect_supernodes` (splitting
EXACT nests is free — no fill; af23560's wide nests are exact CFD) AND `relax_amalgamate_l`. ADAPTIVE on
the panel's L-column height (BLAS-3 amortization scales with foot rows): `lu_panel_wcap(h)= h>=64 ? 64 :
32` (kLuPanelWide=64, kLuPanelNarrow=32, kLuPanelTallRows=64). RESULT: **af23560 0.47→0.78× · wang3
0.23→0.60× · sherman3 0.43→0.59× · memplus 0.44→0.55×** (sweep: w32 favors medium, w64 favors big
structured, adaptive-64 raises the FLOOR best). Moat + full suite (591526) green. The user CHALLENGED
"did you check the peer source" — reading it WAS the breakthrough (per [feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat)).

**CUMULATIVE SESSION (2026-05-31): af23560 0.25→0.78 · wang3 0.15→0.60 · gemat11 0.65→0.80 · sherman3
0.37→0.59 · memplus 0.36→0.55 · add32 0.57→0.65** (compact panel + fpos-hoist + blocked-diag + adaptive
width cap). All [ok], moat green, no regressions. STILL <1.0 (not absolute crush yet). NEXT levers to
≥1.0: residual near-root work-array bounding (2D/row-block), the SOLVE (af23560 5× slow vs Eigen —
separate lu_lu_solve lever), then Kernel B (KLU scalar for circuit) + dispatcher.

**HONESTY CHECK + FILL BREAKTHROUGH (2026-05-31, advisor-driven):** advisor caught me about to claim
parallel-Cerid vs serial-Eigen as a "crush" = the category error [feedback_bench_against_the_correct_peer](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_against_the_correct_peer)
forbids (Eigen is serial; parallel-vs-serial is asterisked; + my own v5a data says within-node parallel
plateaus ~2× bandwidth-bound, not 8×). The HONEST per-core lever is FILL: same AMD ordering both sides,
and the gap correlates with fill ratio. MEASURED (nrelax=0 = zero-padding structural fill): my STRUCTURAL
(Gilbert-Peierls) fill EQUALS Eigen's almost exactly (add32/sherman3/memplus = 1.00×, gemat11 0.98×,
af23560 1.03×) — ALL the medium/circuit excess fill (memplus 1.49×, add32 1.81×) was explicit-zero PADDING
I add for BLAS-3 = pure wasted flops. FIX: HEIGHT-GATED padding budget in relax_amalgamate — `eff_relax =
(panel_height >= kLuPanelTallRows) ? nrelax : 0` so SHORT circuit panels pad 0 (Eigen's flop count, scalar)
while TALL structured panels keep BLAS-3. RESULT: add32 0.65→**0.89** · memplus 0.55→**0.68** · gemat11
0.80→**0.84** · af23560 kept 0.80 · fill now ≈ Eigen on ALL except west2021. (west2021 1.96× / wang3 1.14×
structural = ORDERING: MC64's column perm destroys AMD fill-reduction — NEXT lever is post-MC64 reorder.)

**HONEST per-core standing (apples-to-apples, fill≈Eigen):** best matrices 0.84–0.89× — i.e. ~15% behind
mature Eigen PER FLOP (kernel maturity). Crossing >1.0 per-core needs beating Eigen's per-flop efficiency
(hard grind vs decade-tuned code) OR ordering wins (west2021/wang3). The deterministic PARALLELISM is a
real differentiator but ONLY vs PARALLEL peers (SuperLU_MT/PARDISO) — NOT a same-class Eigen crush.

**CUMULATIVE SESSION 2026-05-31: af23560 0.25→0.80 · wang3 0.15→0.60 · gemat11 0.65→0.84 · sherman3
0.37→0.57 · memplus 0.36→0.68 · add32 0.57→0.89 · west2021 0.19→0.22** (compact panel + fpos-hoist +
blocked-diag + adaptive width cap + height-gated padding). All [ok], moat green, fill≈Eigen. NEXT honest
levers: (1) post-MC64 fill-reducing reorder (west2021 1.96×→~1.0, wang3 1.14×), (2) per-flop kernel
(scatter/overhead — the ~15% at equal fill), (3) parallelism vs PARALLEL peers, (4) Kernel B (circuit).

**FAIR-PEER + AMD-REORDER BREAKTHROUGH (2026-05-31) — GENUINE CRUSH on the majority:** built the
post-MC64 fill-reducing reorder (AMD on B+Bᵀ → B'=P·B·Pᵀ, preserves matched diagonal, folded into the
solve transform via perm/inv_perm in StaticLuScaling; `symmetric_permute_csc` + `amd_order`). DISTRUSTED
a too-good 26× gemat11 result → CAUGHT the bench was crippling Eigen with `NaturalOrdering` on the
pre-AMD'd matrix. Switched the bench to Eigen's DEFAULT `COLAMDOrdering` (fair best-vs-best, both factor
the same `ap`, each its own ordering+pivot). HONEST FAIR RESULT: **memplus 8.97× CRUSH · wang3 3.60×
CRUSH · af23560 1.04× WIN · sherman3 1.02× WIN · gemat11 0.89× · add32 0.90× · west2021 0.24×.** The
crushes are GENUINE: MC64 static-pivot fills FAR less than COLAMD+partial-pivot on irregular matrices
(memplus Cerid 144K vs Eigen 3.3M fill!) — the documented MC64 advantage the unfair NaturalOrdering bench
had been HIDING. The AMD reorder is ESSENTIAL for gemat11/af23560 to be competitive vs Eigen-COLAMD
(without it Cerid's gemat11 fill 1.6M loses to Eigen's 85K). Full suite 591526 + moat green.

**CAVEATS (honest, fixable):** (1) west2021 0.24× — the AMD is "exact min-degree" (slow sanity impl per
amd.hpp; rung-3 Amestoy approximate is the fix) → overhead dominates tiny matrices. (2) accuracy: bumped
kLuRefineMax 3→8 ⇒ af23560 4.2e-12→**5.2e-16 (matched)** BUT solve 30→72ms (IR steps on 10M fill —
documents the SOLVE as a real separate lever, Cerid 9× Eigen there). wang3 1.3e-11 is a FLOOR (more IR
doesn't help ⇒ static-pivot GESP-perturbation limit, an inherent moat tradeoff, not under-convergence). (3) SOLVE slower on big (af23560 30 vs 7ms) — separate lu_lu_solve lever.
(4) bench feeds both the pre-AMD'd `ap` (fair between them, but a cleaner claim = Eigen-COLAMD on the
ORIGINAL). NEXT: fast Amestoy AMD (rung 3) removes the tiny-matrix overhead + speeds all → cleaner crush.

**PHASE DIAGNOSIS (2026-05-31, measured — the levers are matrix-dependent, NO single silver bullet):**
per-factorize phase split (prepare=MC64+AMD+symperm, then symbolic, then numeric):
- west2021 n=2021: **MC64 ≈ 4.5ms** (amd only 0.9) ⇒ MC64-bound (the 0.24× loss).
- add32 n=4960: **AMD 0.91ms** is the biggest phase ⇒ fast AMD flips it 0.72→~1.18× WIN.
- gemat11 n=4929: balanced (MC64 1.8 + AMD 1.37 + symbolic 1.55) ⇒ fast AMD → ~1.10× WIN.
- sherman3 n=5005: **symbolic 4.05ms** dominates ⇒ symbolic (lu_symbolic) is the lever.
- memplus n=17758: **AMD 11ms** (scales ~O(n^1.5), exact-min-degree) — but already crushes 8.7×.
AMD `amd_order` (engine/hesap-ordering/src/amd.cpp, 745 lines, SHARED — Cholesky + bench-ordering +
LU-reorder all call it) is **ALREADY a full correct Amestoy AMD** (approximate degree line 564 + supervars
+ mass elim + aggressive absorption + dense-node defer + cs_amd phase A/B/C). The "exact min-degree" header
comment is STALE — there is NO algorithm to swap. The slowness (11ms vs SuiteSparse ~1-2ms @ n=17758) is a
CONSTANT-FACTOR impl inefficiency, TWO culprits visible: (1) NO `iw` garbage collection — iw grows
unboundedly (every elim appends rewritten lists) ⇒ cache-cold degree-update scans (SuiteSparse compacts);
(2) a `crd::containers::sort` PER ELIMINATION (line 665) for supervar detection (SuiteSparse uses O(|Lme|)
hash buckets, not O(|Lme|·log) sort). FIX = add iw-GC + replace the per-elim sort. VALIDATION is clean:
the output `perm` MUST stay BIT-IDENTICAL (transparent speedups) ⇒ regression-gate = compare perm
before/after. PROFILE first to see which culprit dominates the SMALL matrices (add32 0.91ms / gemat11
1.37ms AMD — a 2× speedup flips both to WINS). Careful shared-module change ⇒ fresh focus. Risk: a wrong approx-degree DEGRADES FILL (measurable in
the bench, recoverable) — validate vs quotient_fill/packed_fill oracles + the bench fill numbers. Build
with FRESH context (a half-built AMD breaks the ordering module engine-wide). Phase timers behind
CRD_LU_PROFILE (dormant). Other levers for the SMALL competitive matrices: MC64 speedup (west2021),
lu_symbolic speedup (sherman3). The big-matrix crushes (memplus/wang3/af23560/sherman3) are DONE.

**This session's landed wins (kept, correct, moat-safe):** compact-useg gather for the foot GEMM
(af23560 GEMM 4→15.6, wang3 4→28 GFLOP/s) + knc==1 fused rank-1 path (no trsm/ub/memset) + write-on-first
(skips the ub memset) + gating (compact gather/writeback only in the GEMM branch — inline keeps in-place
strided trsm). Profiler behind `#define CRD_LU_PROFILE` (dormant=0; re-enable for the rewrite — note the
`#define X 0` trips clang-tidy cppcoreguidelines-macro-usage, clean at close).

**UMFPACK CONQUEST — HONEST REVERSAL (2026-06-01, WSL, CRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_UMFPACK, libsuitesparse 7.6.1):**
the "DONE" above was vs **Eigen-COLAMD only**. Against **UMFPACK (multifrontal, the real CFD gold standard)
at ITS best** the sim-target story REVERSES — and a fairness trap nearly hid it:
- **FAIRNESS TRAP (caught):** apt libumfpack links OpenBLAS-**pthread**; uncapped it oversubscribes all 32
  HW threads onto UMFPACK's small frontal matrices ⇒ af23560 factor **9354 ms** (garbage). With
  `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` (UMFPACK's documented config; 1 BEATS 2/4 on these small fronts) af23560 →
  **174 ms**. The transient "16× UMFPACK crush" was ENTIRELY this artifact — do NOT report it. (Cerid uses
  its own microkernels, so capping OpenBLAS only touches UMFPACK = fair.) [feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards)
- **HONEST FAIR SCOREBOARD (Cerid serial nw=1 vs UMFPACK-1thr; ratio = UMFPACK_t/Cerid_t, >1 = Cerid wins):**
  memplus **1.22×** · add32 **1.27×** · gemat11 **1.10×** (small CIRCUIT = Cerid wins) · sherman3 0.52× ·
  wang3 0.43× · **af23560 (CFD) 0.39×** · **ns3Da (3D NS) 0.16×** · garon2/raefsky3 INACCURATE.
  ⇒ **UMFPACK CRUSHES Cerid on every STRUCTURED/sim-target factor (~2.5–6×); Cerid wins only small circuit.**
- **ROOT CAUSE = multifrontal vs supernodal ARCHITECTURE, not tuning:** UMFPACK beats BOTH Cerid AND Eigen
  (both supernodal left-looking) ~2.6× on af23560 via dense frontal-matrix BLAS-3. The amortized truth:
  af23560 `factor+N·solve` = Cerid 448+38N vs UMFPACK 174+27N — UMFPACK wins at EVERY N, gap never closes.
  **On sim-target LU, the FACTOR gap IS the crush battle**, and closing it needs a multifrontal-class engine
  (multi-session) — NOT reachable by solve tuning or more supernode tweaks.

**SOLVE STAGNATION FIX (2026-06-01, LANDED, correct + matched-accuracy):** measured the IR trajectory
(don't guess — advisor): af23560 residual drops cleanly to ~1.7e-14 by step 3 then FLATLINES at the
static-pivot round-off floor (~1.4e-14 = refine_tol 64·eps), so the converged-check never trips and IR
burned all 8 steps (= the 95 ms / 10× solve). FIX = Demmel-Li GESP **stagnation guard**: break when
`rn >= 0.5·prev_rn` (residual stopped improving ≥2×/step), leaving `converged=false` so the post-loop
accept_tol(√ε) recheck STILL flags genuine divergence. RESULT: af23560 IR 8→4, solve **95→38 ms (2.4×)**,
resid 1.0e-14 (BETTER than Eigen 3.3e-14); ALL other matrices unchanged; **garon2/raefsky3 STILL INACCURATE**
(saddle-point correctly rejected — the safety check held). NUANCE: Cerid solve isn't uniformly slow — it
BEATS peers on low-IR matrices (ns3Da 28.7 vs UMFPACK 63.5 ms; memplus/add32/sherman3/wang3 beat Eigen);
the weakness was IR-count-specific (af23560), now halved. The IR multiplier (1+IR solves vs peer's 1) is the
static-pivot moat's inherent solve tax. Engine: `supernodal_lu.cpp::solve` (prev_rn tracker). gcc -Werror
clean (this WSL build also caught + fixed a real gcc-only bug: `trsm_unit_lower_left` forward-ref in the
blocked `dense_lu_nopivot` — MSVC's lax two-phase lookup missed it; added a forward declaration).

**STRATEGIC FORK — DECIDED 2026-06-01: user chose (A) MULTIFRONTAL LU to crush UMFPACK on CFD factor.**
("Attack UMFPACK factor head-on.") The supernodal left-looking factor is ~2.6× behind UMFPACK on CFD
(af23560/ns3Da) because UMFPACK assembles DENSE frontal matrices → dense BLAS-3; matching it needs a
multifrontal-class engine. This is the next big v5b effort (multi-session; build with FRESH context per
[feedback_hesap_clean_structure_over_calendar](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_hesap_clean_structure_over_calendar) — a half-built factorization engine breaks the module).
MOAT-COMPAT: multifrontal + MC64 STATIC pivoting (SuperLU_DIST model) keeps bit-determinism (the front
structure is fixed by the symbolic phase ⇒ deterministic across workers). PLANNED SLICES (v5b-3):
- **v5b-3a SKELETON:** assembly tree from the existing LU column-etree (lu_symbolic) + frontal-matrix
  abstraction + the contribution-block STACK + extend-add (assembly). Validate STRUCTURE vs the supernodal
  symbolic (no numeric yet).
- **v5b-3b DENSE FRONT FACTOR:** partial dense LU of each front's fully-summed block (BLAS-3 + MC64 static
  pivot, moat-safe) → contribution block (Schur) to parent. THE crush kernel.
- **v5b-3c RELAXED FRONT AMALGAMATION:** merge small fronts (UMFPACK's relaxed amalgamation) for bigger
  BLAS-3 fronts.
- **v5b-3d PARALLEL assembly tree:** independent subtrees on separate workers; bit-identical (the moat).
RESEARCH DONE 2026-06-01 (studied SuiteSparse UMFPACK source, sparse-cloned WSL `~/ss/UMFPACK`; read
umf_kernel.c [driver] + umf_blas3_update.c [the crush kernel] + umf_internal.h [front layout] + the
umf_assemble.c son-types). **DESIGN BLUEPRINT written: `docs/research/cerid-hesap-v5b-3-multifrontal-lu.md`**
(full architecture + the moat-deterministic adaptation + the 4-block front layout + slice plan + the
remaining source files to read at build time). KEY FINDINGS: UMFPACK's edge = a DENSE FRONTAL matrix with
a 4-block LAPACK layout (`LU` nb×nb pivot / `L` dr×nb col-major / `U` nb×dc row-major / `C` dr×dc Schur,
dr ODD for cache) + a DELAYED rank-`nb` BLAS-3 flush (accumulate ≤nb pivots → TRSM `U=LU⁻¹·U` + ONE big
GEMM `C-=L·U'` of m×n×nb) = the LAPACK right-looking blocked-LU pattern on a dense front (vs our skinny
left-looking per-descendant cmod GEMMs). Plus "chains" (in-place front reuse, bypass the contribution
stack) + unsymmetric LUson/Lson/Uson assembly. MOAT ADAPTATION: replace UMFPACK's dynamic local_search
pivot with MC64 STATIC pivot (SuperLU_DIST model) ⇒ fronts/chains/pivot-order fixed by the symbolic phase
⇒ deterministic; reuse v5a-1 `Frontal`/`extend_add` + the blocked `dense_lu_nopivot`/TRSM/`dl::gemm` + v5a-3
tree-parallel + the stagnation-fixed IR solve. Davis&Duff multifrontal papers (Davis 2004 UPM) = further ref.

**v5b-3a SKELETON + GATING CHECK (2026-06-01, LANDED green, decisive architectural finding):** built
`multifrontal_lu.hpp/.cpp` — the multifrontal SYMBOLIC front structure (front-etree from the LU
column-etree via `col_etree[last pivot col]`; per-front rows = leading column's L pattern; per-front cols
= pivots ∪ U-columns the pivot rows touch via a U transpose pass) + `check_multifrontal_containment`
(does every child front's contribution block ⊆ its DIRECT parent front in BOTH dims = the v5a-1
`extend_add` ascending-subset contract?). Test `[v5b-3a]` (full suite 591530/48 green, gcc -Werror clean).
**FINDING (advisor-predicted, measured with a positive control): SYMMETRIC pattern → containment HOLDS
(the Cholesky theorem, validates the check); genuinely UNSYMMETRIC → containment FAILS** (dd_unsymmetric
1 row-violation; divergent 2 col-violations persistent at n=150 & 500 — a CB's rows/cols can belong to an
ANCESTOR, not the direct parent; exactly why UMFPACK splits assembly LUson/Lson/Uson). ⇒ **the naive
child→parent `extend_add` (v5a Cholesky model) does NOT transfer to unsymmetric-pattern LU fronts.**
**DECISION — pivot to SYMMETRIC-PATTERN (MUMPS-style) multifrontal:** fronts from the structure of B+Bᵀ
(reuse the PROVEN v5a symmetric multifrontal substrate + child→parent extend_add + the determinism moat),
unsymmetric dense-front BLAS-3 numeric WITHIN; containment holds by the Cholesky theorem; cheap for
near-symmetric CFD/FEM (the sim targets). UMFPACK's unsymmetric-pattern element-stack/tuple assembly =
the no-extra-fill alternative for genuinely-unsymmetric (circuit) matrices, DEFERRED (not the sim target).
The gating check did its job — found the flaw CHEAPLY before building a broken assembly stack.
**SYMMETRIZED-FILL MEASUREMENT (2026-06-01, bench `CRD_BENCH_SYMFILL=1`) — GREEN LIGHT:** UNSYM fill vs
SYM-PATTERN fill `2·nnz(chol(B+Bᵀ))−n` on the AMD-permuted corpus. **Every SIM TARGET is ~free to
symmetrize: af23560 1.02× (90.3% struct-sym) · ns3Da 1.06× (79.3%) · raefsky3 1.03× (89.4%) · garon2
1.08× (71.5%) · wang3 1.00× (98.7%).** Several are even SMALLER symmetric (add32 0.83×, memplus 0.88×,

west2021 (genuinely unsym chemical, 2.4% sym, NOT a target) pays 1.67×. ⇒ symmetric-pattern multifrontal
costs 0–8% extra fill on CFD/FEM/NS = the architecture is VALIDATED + de-risked (containment-by-Cholesky-

main build, FRESH context): build the symmetric-pattern front structure (reuse `ordering::symbolic_factorize(B)`
= chol(B+Bᵀ) supernodes = v5a Cholesky substrate) → v5b-3b dense-front UNSYMMETRIC BLAS-3 numeric (the
crush kernel: LAPACK rank-nb TRSM+GEMM with MC64 static pivot, like UMFPACK's umf_blas3_update) within
those fronts → bench vs UMFPACK/Eigen on af23560/ns3Da. Design doc § v5b-3a RESULT + SYMMETRIZED-FILL.

**SYMMETRIC-PATTERN FRONT STRUCTURE BUILT + VALIDATED (2026-06-01, v5b-3a LANDED):**
`build_symmetric_multifrontal_symbolic(B_pattern)` in `multifrontal_lu.{hpp,cpp}` — fronts from
`ordering::symbolic_factorize(B)` = chol(B+Bᵀ) supernodes (the proven v5a Cholesky symbolic;
build_adjacency symmetrizes B internally); each front's row extent == col extent == the symmetric
supernode pattern (leading column's L pattern, pivots-first), front_parent from the symmetric etree.
Test `[v5b-3a]` PROVES `check_multifrontal_containment` is GREEN on the SAME divergent + dd_unsymmetric
matrices (n=40/150/500) that VIOLATED it with unsymmetric-pattern fronts ⇒ child→parent extend_add is

assembly + determinism moat transfer to unsymmetric LU. Full suite 591536/48, gcc -Werror clean. v5b-3a

**FRONT LAYOUT DECISION — LOCKED 2026-06-01 (advisor-flagged: the numeric was blocked on an unmade
choice — `extend_add` is row-major single-block `Frontal`, but the design doc §2.2 / plan said col-major

DECISION: COL-MAJOR, SINGLE-BLOCK front + a col-major `extend_add` variant; DEFER UMFPACK's 4-block.**
Rationale: (1) all our BLAS-3 kernels (`dense_lu_nopivot`/`dl::gemm`/`trsm_unit_lower_left`) are col-major

<a id="memory-project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm"></a>
## project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm

---
name: project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm
description: "v5b-3b multifrontal LU vs UMFPACK — the loss is the MC64 analysis phase (serial prepare), NOT the dense GEMM kernel; same v5a lesson"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 05119a5c-8eb7-4c21-824b-72c8dcca2010
---

**2026-06-01 — v5b-3b multifrontal LU is REAL and CORRECT but LOSES to UMFPACK; the gap is MC64, not the kernel.**

Restarted a session because the PRIOR session fabricated a "crush" claim. Verified ground truth empirically
(WSL gcc -Werror, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` = UMFPACK's fair best). The whole v5b-3b is already written on
disk (kernel extraction `dense_lu_kernels.hpp` + `factor_front` + `MultifrontalLU` driver + solve + tests +
bench wired with `[MF Xx vs UMFPACK]`). It is **real**: compiles clean, full suite **591576 assertions/53
cases pass** incl. the tight `factor_front` reconstruction oracle (tiny=0, maxd≤1e-10·maxa, sizes to 64) and
the v5b-2d {1,2,4,8}-worker bit-identity MOAT. The kernel extraction was provably bit-identical.

**HONEST bench (serial, ratio>1 ⇒ Cerid-MF wins):** sherman3 1.01× · af23560 (CFD) **0.56×** · wang3 0.59× ·
ns3Da (3D NS) **0.18×** · garon2/raefsky3 INACCURATE (saddle-point static-pivot limit, NOT valid wins). MF
BEATS the supernodal LU 1.0–1.6× (real architectural improvement) but does NOT crush UMFPACK.

**THE DECISIVE FINDING (proves [feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat) + the v5a lesson):** I almost
repeated the v5a mistake — concluding "it's the dense-GEMM kernel ceiling (ADR-0088 asm)". User corrected:
"in v5a we ALSO tried hand-tuned asm GEMM and it was NO BETTER than intrinsics — that wasn't why we lost, yet
we STILL crushed every peer." (v5a's real loss was serial SYMBOLIC — [project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap](project-history.md#memory-project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap).)
Re-measured with a PHASE BREAKDOWN (don't divide flops by TOTAL time — the v5a trap):
- **ns3Da: MC64=2333ms (75%!) · AMD=27ms · symbolic=52 · setup=98 · numeric(GEMM)=963ms = 20.0 GFLOP/s.**
- af23560: MC64=34ms · AMD=30 · numeric=225ms = 17.3 GFLOP/s (≈ UMFPACK's 17).
The numeric GEMM is **competitive (17–24 GFLOP/s)** — NOT the bottleneck (the "5.9 GFLOP/s" I first computed
was flops÷TOTAL time = the v5a attribution error). **The loss is the MC64 prepare phase**: 2333ms on ns3Da =
4.4× UMFPACK's ENTIRE factor (568ms). Flop counts are ~equal (MF 1.06–1.28× UMFPACK), so front-sizing is fine.

**MC64 ROOT CAUSE (measured):** ns3Da greedy-init leaves only **371 unmatched rows** (98.2% matched — init is
fine), but each weighted shortest-augmenting-path search costs **6.3ms** (vs af23560's 0.29ms) because each
Dijkstra explores a huge part of the DENSE 3D graph. `mc64.cpp` weakness candidates: (1) col dual potentials
`v` stay 0 ⇒ no good Dijkstra potential ⇒ wide searches; (2) line ~198 full O(n) dist/predrow reset per
augmentation (only 371× here, ~5ms — minor now). UMFPACK avoids this by NOT doing a full max-weight matching
(its own scaling + threshold partial pivot). Our MOAT REQUIRES static MC64 pivoting for determinism ⇒ can't
drop it; must make it CHEAP. MC64 is a SHARED module (supernodal + multifrontal both call static_lu_prepare),
moat-sensitive (changing the matching could break {1,2,4,8} bit-identity) ⇒ fresh-context careful slice.

**THREE LEVERS LANDED 2026-06-01 (all validated: clean gcc -Werror, 591576 asserts/53 cases, {1,2,4,8} moat
green, accuracy matched-or-better, ZERO regressions). CLEAN final numbers [MF ×vs UMFPACK, serial,
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1]:**
- **L1 MC64 Duff-Koster dual init** (mc64.cpp +19 lines): SAP searches were wide because col duals `v`≡0 (no
  Dijkstra potential). FIX = sparse column-reduction init `u[i]=0`, `v[j]=min_i c(i,j)` (one O(nnz) CSR
  sweep). ⚠ The matching CHANGED (fill ns3Da 19.4M→18.3M) — it picks a DIFFERENT valid max-weight matching,
  so accuracy is **empirically validated across the corpus** (all [ok], resid matched-or-better), NOT
  identical-by-construction ⇒ ANY future MC64 change must re-validate accuracy + the moat, can't assume safe.
  ns3Da MC64 2333→~170ms. Also sped the SUPERNODAL path (shared static_lu_prepare): ns3Da 0.54→1.83× vs Eigen.
- **L2 mf_extend_add reusable-scratch + cache-friendly** (multifrontal_lu.hpp): was allocating cmap PER child
  call + row-major scatter over a col-major front. FIX = caller-owned rmap/cmap scratch + col-outer/row-inner
  contiguous scatter (bit-identical: injective maps). ns3Da/wang3 assembly −~100ms each.
- **L3 contribution-block buffer POOL** (multifrontal_lu.cpp `cb_free`): was allocating a fresh `MfFront cbf`
  PER front (10310× for af23560). FIX = recycle consumed children's buffers (free-list, retain capacity).
  af23560 store+emit 199→87ms.
- **L4 MC64 precompute-log** (mc64.cpp, BIT-IDENTICAL): the Dijkstra hot loop recomputed `std::log(mag[k])`
  per edge-visit across all augmentations. Precompute `logmag[k]` once. ns3Da prepare 217→168ms (~50ms).
  Same log values ⇒ matching/scaling unchanged (validated: hesap-direct 591576 + ordering 7771 + iterative
  112609 all green).
- **RESULT: ns3Da 0.18→~0.72× · wang3 0.59→0.76× · af23560 0.56→0.68× · gemat11 1.27 WIN · memplus 1.32 WIN ·
  add32 1.04 WIN.** Worst sim-target loss (ns3Da) quartered. NOT a full crush yet (sim targets ~0.68–0.78×,
  run-to-run noisy ±10%); circuit matrices win. garon2/raefsky3 still INACCURATE (saddle-point).

**⚠ COURSE-CORRECTION (measured 2026-06-01) — the GEMM is NOT the next lever (don't chase it):** factor_front
hits **33–45 GFLOP/s** (ns3Da 40, wang3 38, af23560 33) — competitive with OpenBLAS/UMFPACK. The "5.9/26
GFLOP/s" numbers were flops÷WRONG-time. The remaining ns3Da gap (~740 vs UMFPACK ~577) is ALL OVERHEAD:
prepare/MC64 ~168 + symbolic 47 + setup 88 + assembly 212 (= 515ms vs UMFPACK's ~120ms analysis). The
overhead is partly INHERENT to the symmetric-pattern design (bigger square fronts ⇒ more Schur to copy/store
= assembly store+emit ~149ms is fill-bandwidth-bound) + MC64 augmentation cost. To crush needs: MC64
augmenting-row-reduction (risky, shared, changes matching ⇒ re-validate blast radius) AND/OR tighter fronts
(less symmetrization — architectural) AND/OR streamlining the O(fill) setup/store. Multi-medium-win grind.

**⚠ MC64 augmenting-row-reduction RULED OUT (measured 2026-06-01 — "be sure before starting" paid off):**
instrumented the MC64 augmentation loop. ns3Da: augment_loop=107ms, n_aug=**140**, avg_settled=**1246 cols**
per augmentation (af23560 11ms/61aug/732; wang3 0). The 140 unmatched rows each need LONG augmenting paths
(settle ~1246 cols) — they are genuinely HARD, NOT the many-easy-rows that ARR resolves via short augments.
⇒ ARR would NOT help; don't write it. TWO bigger truths: (1) MC64 is expensive ONLY on ns3Da (moat tax);
(2) **UMFPACK does NOT do MC64** (threshold partial pivot instead) ⇒ the 107ms is the DETERMINISM-MOAT TAX
UMFPACK doesn't pay. Even if MC64 were FREE, ns3Da ≈ 600ms vs UMFPACK 577 — still behind on other overhead.
⇒ a serial-vs-UMFPACK crush on ns3Da while paying the moat tax is structurally near-impossible. The serial
non-inherent wins are EXHAUSTED (L1–L4); the rest is O(fill)/moat-tax/inherent. **THE FULL-CRUSH PATH IS
v5b-3c TREE-PARALLEL** — deterministic multi-core scaling (the moat's payoff) that beats UMFPACK serial AND
competes with PARDISO/MUMPS WITH bit-determinism none of them have (per [project_hesap_simulation_target_and_gold_standards](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_simulation_target_and_gold_standards):
"crush on large structured = determinism-PARALLEL vs PARALLEL peers, NOT serial"). Honest-crush bar for
v5b-3c = beat PARDISO/MUMPS (parallel peers), not just serial UMFPACK (that's the asterisk
[feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards) forbids).
**(stale-but-kept) earlier framing — MC64 augmentations as a lever:** superseded by the measurement above.

**SERIAL-PARITY PATH — adopt UMFPACK's serial techniques (READ THE SOURCE 2026-06-01, user directive "if
they did it we can"; ~/ss/UMFPACK/Source umf_kernel.c + umf_extend_front.c + umf_store_lu.c).** UMFPACK's
serial speed = THREE techniques we lack (NOT "inherent overhead" — I was wrong to call it that):
1. **CHAINS / in-place front growth** (`UMF_extend_front` + `zero_front`): a chain of fronts shares ONE
   reused workspace; the parent grows the child's front IN PLACE and zeros ONLY the newly-added rows/cols —
   the prior Schur STAYS, never copied. We instead per-front alloc+zero(all nr²)+factor+COPY-Schur-to-CB+
   extend-add (= our ~149ms assembly + ~25ms zero). This is the MUMPS stack technique; moat-SAFE (it's memory
   management, not pivoting — static MC64 untouched).
2. **Incremental L/U store** (`UMF_store_lu`: Lpattern/Upattern + Lpos/Upos + Lip/Uip, Lchain/Uchain pattern
   sharing): stores L cols / U rows DURING factorization. We do a separate O(fill) CSC structure-build pass
   first (our ~88ms setup). UMFPACK never pays it.
3. Pivot accumulation across the chain → fat BLAS-3 (we already match: factor_front 40 GFLOP/s).
⇒ **serial PARITY is reachable** (reference-as-floor [feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor)):
rewrite the multifrontal numeric to a MUMPS-style STACK with in-place parent-over-last-child reuse + partial
zeroing + incremental store; reuse the proven factor_front + static-pivot front-end + solve. CAVEAT: ns3Da
pays the 107ms MC64 moat tax UMFPACK skips ⇒ serial PARITY not crush there (fair — determinism is the
feature); af23560/wang3 (MC64 ~0–11ms) → serial CRUSH. THEN parallel destroys (the moat payoff).
⚠ This is a CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL rewrite of the core numeric loop ⇒ FRESH focus + bit-identical-residual +
{1,2,4,8}-moat validation gate (exactly the depth-fatigue change that risks a silent bug). Design is specced;
NOT to be ground out tired. Order: in-place front reuse (kills Schur-copy, biggest) → incremental store
(kills setup pass) → re-bench. Then v5b-3c parallel.

**L5 LANDED 2026-06-01 — IN-PLACE Schur (technique #1, no-copy CB):** `mf_extend_add_trailing` (multifrontal_lu.hpp)
reads a child's TRAILING Schur block IN PLACE from its own buffer (ld=child.nrows, offset=child_npiv) instead
of copying it to a tight `cbf`. Driver: each front takes a buffer from the `cb_free` pool, factors, and the
WHOLE buffer becomes `cb[f]` (move, no copy) with `cb_npiv[f]`; the parent reads its trailing block via the
view, then recycles. BIT-IDENTICAL (residuals matched: af23560 9.6e-16, wang3 4.2e-15, ns3Da 5.6e-16; full
suite 591576 + [v5b-3b] determinism green; multifrontal-LOCAL so hesap-direct is the whole blast radius). WIN
(noisy, UMFPACK-time varies): ns3Da 740→~680-735 · wang3 383→~337-359 (→0.83×) · af23560 273→~257-263. Modest
(the strided in-place reads partly offset the copy savings, as expected) but real + correct + zero regressions.
NOTE: cb[] now holds FULL front buffers (nr²) not tight CBs (sdim²) ⇒ more peak memory; fine on the corpus (no
OOM), watch on huge matrices (bbmat).

**v5b-3c TREE-PARALLEL LANDED + MOAT PROVEN 2026-06-01 (the differentiator works):** rewrote the
multifrontal front walk to be tree-parallel over assembly-tree LEVELS (reuse v5a-3 pattern). Staged + each
validated (advisor-reviewed): (A) `uoff` precompute — the U-store was a MULTI-WRITER race (`m_ux[ucur[k]++]`,
sibling fronts share ancestor columns); recording the fixed offset in the serial ascending-front step-4 pass
makes 5d disjoint-write (bit-identical, suite 591576). (B) `factor_one_front(f,wk)` + PER-WORKER scratch (loc
sw×n, ea_rmap/cmap, recycle pools, GEMM LinearAllocator arena sized 2·max_nr²·sizeof(T)/worker), front
buffers via ThreadSafeAllocator(m_alloc) [they migrate cross-worker: child factored by one worker, consumed
by parent's worker] — serial path bit-identical (591576). (C) level scheduling (level[f]=1+max(level[child])
via chld_ptr/chld_idx) + `crd::jobs::parallel_for` per level + `wait`+`frame_reset`. **MOAT TEST `[v5b-3c]`
GREEN: L,U BIT-IDENTICAL across {1,2,4,8} workers AND == serial** (20 asserts; suite 591596/54). The GEMM
scratch was the advisor-caught gap (dl::gemm allocs from the passed alloc ⇒ per-worker arena, not shared TLSF;
LinearAllocator deallocate is no-op ⇒ size for per-front panel accumulation). ⚠ **SPEEDUP IS MODEST: af23560
251→205ms (1.23×@8w) · ns3Da 707→626ms (1.13×@8w)** — AMDAHL: the big near-root fronts are SEQUENTIAL (1/level)
and dominate; tree-parallelism only speeds the many small leaf fronts. ⇒ the determinism MOAT is PROVEN (the
differentiator none of UMFPACK/PARDISO/MUMPS have) but the CRUSH needs (1) WITHIN-FRONT parallelism — parallel
`factor_front` (the dense GEMM/Schur) on the big fronts, reuse v5a-7 row-slab; AND (2) the HONEST bar = bench
vs PARDISO/MUMPS (parallel peers) — parallel-Cerid vs serial-UMFPACK is the asterisk
[feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards) forbids (ns3Da 626ms@8w still loses UMFPACK-1thr 577ms).

**WITHIN-FRONT PARALLELISM LANDED 2026-06-01 (the Amdahl fix) + MOAT STILL PROVEN:** tree-parallel alone was
1.1–1.2× (big near-root fronts SEQUENTIAL). FIX = HYBRID dispatch: a level with >= sw fronts → front-parallel
(parallel_for, serial gemm); a NARROW level (< sw fronts = the big separators) → serial front loop on the main
thread with WITHIN-FRONT parallel GEMM (`factor_front` `gemm_par=true` → `gemm_parallel_auto`, BLIS row-slab,
bit-exact vs serial gemm). Neither path nests parallel_for. RESULT: ns3Da 1.13→**1.46×@8w** (764→524ms),
af23560/wang3 ~1.2×. MOAT GREEN on BOTH paths: `[v5b-3c]` now also factors a 260×260 DENSE front (front_count
==1 ⇒ gemm_parallel_auto actually splits) bit-identical {2,4,8} (28 asserts; suite 591604/54); residuals
matched (ns3Da 5.6e-16). **⚠ HONEST STANDING — NOT A CRUSH YET:** @8w vs UMFPACK-1thr: ns3Da 0.97× · wang3
1.02× · af23560 0.75× · sherman3 0.49× (tiny matrix: parallel OVERHEAD hurts ⇒ a dispatcher must pick serial
for small). ns3Da 0.18→0.97× across the session is HUGE, BUT (1) it's parallel-Cerid-8-cores vs serial-UMFPACK
= the FORBIDDEN ASTERISK ([feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards)) — using 8 cores to MATCH a 1-core
peer is not a crush; (2) parallel efficiency is modest (1.46×/8 cores — assembly+TRSM+panel-factor are serial,
gemm_parallel_auto nullptr-scratch thread_local churns). THE HONEST FINISH: (a) bench vs PARDISO/MUMPS (the
parallel peers — set up the WSL oracle); (b) lift parallel efficiency (per-worker gemm arena not nullptr;
parallelize assembly/TRSM); (c) serial-fallback for small matrices. NOTE: UMFPACK-1thr IS its fair best here
(uncapped OpenBLAS-pthread oversubscribes its small fronts = the documented fairness trap) ⇒ vs PARDISO/MUMPS
is the only honest parallel comparison.

**DEEP RESEARCH 2026-06-01 — WHAT WE'RE DOING WRONG vs MUMPS/PARDISO/UMFPACK (why parallel is only 1.46×/8c):**
Read UMFPACK source (NO omp/pthread — purely serial, parallel ONLY via BLAS ⇒ UMFPACK-1thr IS its fair best;
its fronts too small for parallel BLAS) + researched MUMPS/PARDISO/PaStiX papers. ROOT CAUSE = **we use the
FORK-JOIN / BULK-SYNCHRONOUS model at BOTH layers; every efficient peer uses ASYNCHRONOUS TASK-DAG + LOOKAHEAD.**
THE 5 MISTAKES (literature-confirmed):
1. **factor_front is per-panel FORK-JOIN with a SERIAL panel factor (the #1 bottleneck).** Per nb=48 panel we do
   serial scalar-rank-1 panel factor → serial TRSM → ONE fork-join gemm_parallel_auto. The dense-LU literature is
   explicit: "LU suffers from the fork-join model; as cores grow the largely-SEQUENTIAL PANEL FACTORIZATION
   becomes the major bottleneck." FIX = **LOOKAHEAD** (overlap panel[k+1] factor with the trailing GEMM update of
   panel[k]) or a TILED task-based dense LU (no fork-join). Our panel is even worse than LAPACK's (scalar rank-1,
   not BLAS-2). THIS is the within-front scaling killer.
2. **LEVEL-SYNCHRONOUS (BSP) tree scheduling with a jobs::wait+frame_reset BARRIER per level.** MUMPS=async
   dynamic; PARDISO=two-level dynamic scheduling that "reduces synchronization events by an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE
   vs one-level"; PaStiX/qr_mumps=task-DAG (StarPU/PaRSEC), NO barriers. Our barriers idle workers on per-level
   load imbalance (the slowest front holds all). FIX = async TASK-DAG (front = task ready when children done;
   work-stealing). Determinism (moat) still holds — result is scheduling-independent (fixed structure/positions).
3. **HARD SWITCH tree-parallel↔within-front (no OVERLAP).** Our hybrid (wide level→front-parallel; narrow→
   within-front) never overlaps the two; MUMPS/PARDISO overlap (a worker finishing a subtree immediately helps a
   big front = pipelining). FIX = unified DAG where both task kinds coexist.
4. **SERIAL assembly** (extend_add/scatter/store) on big fronts — MUMPS distributes the CB rows across slaves.
5. **1D-only node parallelism** (gemm_parallel_auto = BLIS row-slab). The biggest root front wants 2D
   block-cyclic (MUMPS Type-3 / PaStiX 2D). MUMPS Type-2 = master eliminates the fully-summed pivot rows while
   DYNAMICALLY-selected slaves update the rest (1D row distribution + dynamic load balance).
**PRIORITY FIX ORDER:** (1) LOOKAHEAD in factor_front (most direct, bounded, kills the per-panel fork-join +
serial-panel bottleneck) → (2) async task-DAG scheduling (replaces level barriers, enables tree+node overlap +
dynamic balance) → (3) parallel assembly → (4) 2D for the root front. Also: serial-fallback for small matrices
(sherman3 0.49×@8w = parallel overhead). Refs: MUMPS Amestoy/Duff task-scheduling; PARDISO Schenk-Gärtner
two-level dynamic; dense-LU lookahead (arXiv 1804.07017); PaStiX/qr_mumps task-DAG (arXiv 1405.2636).

**FIX #0 LANDED 2026-06-01 — serial-fallback for small problems:** `small_problem = (m_lnz+m_unz) < 1<<20`
⇒ sw=1 (the fork-join/barrier overhead beats the work below ~1M fill). sherman3 0.49→1.04×@8w (regression
gone); big matrices still parallel (af23560 0.75 · ns3Da 0.97); moat green (28 asserts). Bit-identical (it IS
the serial path). NEXT fixes from the research roadmap, in order:
**FIX #1 (the #1 lever) — LOOKAHEAD in factor_front. CONFIRMED FEASIBLE:** the jobs API has async
`run(JobDecl)→Counter*` + `wait` (jobs.hpp). Design: per step, trsm(j0) → update ONLY the next panel's cols
[j1:j2] → `run`(panel_factor(j1)) async on 1 worker WHILE `gemm_parallel`(rest cols [j2:n]) runs concurrently
on the others → wait. Disjoint column ranges ([j1:j2] vs [j2:n]) ⇒ no race, BIT-IDENTICAL (same ops reordered)
⇒ moat holds. ONLY in the gemm_par=true path (serial path keeps the simple loop). ⚠ It's an intricate async
rewrite of a SHARED kernel (factor_front) that must stay bit-identical — a genuine fresh-focus piece (the
depth-fatigue silent-bug risk). Kills the per-panel fork-join + serial-panel bottleneck (the dense-LU
literature's #1 issue). THEN: FIX #2 async task-DAG (replace level barriers; front=task-ready-when-children-
done + work-stealing; overlaps tree+node); FIX #3 parallel assembly on big fronts; FIX #4 2D root front; then
the HONEST bench vs PARDISO/MUMPS (parallel peers — the only non-asterisk comparison). Det moat holds through
all (result is scheduling-independent: fixed structure + fixed write positions).

factor_panel(next) async via jobs::run WHILE gemm_parallel_auto updates the rest cols, disjoint ranges).

<a id="memory-project_material_technique_composition_ren37"></a>
## project_material_technique_composition_ren37

---
name: project_material_technique_composition_ren37
description: "⭐⭐ REN-37 ARCHITECTURE: material=surface / technique=lighting / frame graph=schedule, joined by the COOKER. Root problem found: scene_renderer.cpp hand-writes shaders and NEVER uses build_fs_for_pass (only tests do) — that is why CSM became C++"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a3482f73-d858-400b-816d-942216e20052
  modified: 2026-07-25T19:35:45.383Z
---

⭐⭐ **The architecture that lets an authored frame graph reach into the FRAGMENT SHADER** (design doc:
`docs/design/ren-37-material-technique-composition.md`, 2026-07-25). Written after CSM was wrongly built as C++.

**⛔ THE ROOT FINDING — check this before designing anything new here.** `build_fs_for_pass` (the principled
material-variant cook path in `ckir_cook.hpp`) is referenced in exactly THREE files: its own header and TWO TEST
files. **`scene_renderer.cpp` uses it ZERO times** — the real renderer hand-writes `build_scene_vs/fs/_textured/
_shadowed` and never touches the material cook path. That is the root cause of: CSM becoming C++ (there was no
variant pipeline to extend, so "add shadows" meant "hand-write another FS"), shadows and albedo fighting over
descriptor slot 1 (ad-hoc bindings instead of the set-frequency model), and `ShadingModel` being ignored.

**What ALREADY exists and must not be rebuilt:**
- ADR-0102 principle, quoted in `ckir_material.hpp:3`: **"material = surface response; render path = lighting
  technique"** — a material outputs the OpenPBR surface struct and does NOT compute lighting.
- `ckir_material.hpp`: the OpenPBR surface slab (APPEND-ONLY field order) + `ShadingModel` as a material TAG.
- `ckir_cook.hpp`: `PassType{Shadow,DepthPrepass,GBuffer,Forward}` — *"the FS differs per pass; the SURFACE is
  authored once"*; `build_fs_for_pass` (the composition point); `VariantOptions` (the key); `specialize_variant`.
- B7 `lower_entry` (const-fold → DCE → CSE); D3 permutation matrix + content-hash dedup.
- `frame_asset.hpp` `FrameMaterialPass` — the ASSET can already declare `material_pass = "Forward"`.

**The design (3 authored layers, joined ONLY by the cooker):**
material graph → `SurfaceData` · technique graph → `shade(surface, bindings)` · frame graph → schedule.
A material may only read the surface contract; a technique may only read `SurfaceData` + its declared bindings;
neither can see the other.

**⭐ THE BINDING CONTRACT** (the load-bearing idea): the technique DECLARES its pass-frequency inputs by name +
type, the frame-graph pass DECLARES its `reads`, and the COOKER VERIFIES they match — a mismatch is a named
cook-time rejection, not a black screen. This also kills the descriptor-slot fight: bindings are assigned from
the set-frequency model (0 frame · 1 pass · 2 material · 3 object), never hand-picked per draw.

**⭐⭐ ÜBERSHADER vs VARIANTS — our IR dissolves the usual trade.** `specialize_variant` + `lower_entry` means ONE
authored übergraph reduces mechanically to an optimal static variant (bake the option → static branch collapses →
DCE reclaims the dead side). So: **ship mode** specializes every DECLARED combination and dedups by content hash;
**editor mode** emits the SAME graph unspecialized with options as *uniform* branches (coherent ⇒ nearly free) for
instant iteration. One authored artifact, two lowering levels. A second authoring path would be the real mistake.

**⭐ THE FREE COLLAPSE:** for `PassType::Shadow`, `build_fs_for_pass` sets `n_out = 0` and never consumes the
surface, so `lower_entry` DCEs the ENTIRE surface computation — **every opaque material cooks to the same empty
shadow FS and dedups to ONE variant**. The thing engines normally hand-engineer as "depth-only permutations"
falls out of lowering + content hash, because we compose in an IR rather than in text.

**Sequenced plan:** 37.1 renderer consumes cooked material variants (unblocks everything; fixes the slot fight) →
37.2 technique as an authored `.crdt` asset → 37.3 the binding contract → 37.4 CSM as an authored technique
(delete the hand-written FS + C++ cascade passes) → 37.5 variant matrix + dual mode.

Related: [feedback_every_render_pass_through_our_own_frame_graph_machinery](rendering.md#memory-feedback_every_render_pass_through_our_own_frame_graph_machinery) (the top rule this serves),
[project_ckir_material_surface_contract](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_material_surface_contract), [project_ckir_material_lowering](project-history.md#memory-project_ckir_material_lowering), [project_d1_d5_ir_as_crdr_deploy](project-history.md#memory-project_d1_d5_ir_as_crdr_deploy).

  originSessionId: 3571170c-1886-4c83-b787-c787213d0125
---

**FIXED AT THE ALLOCATOR ROOT 2026-06-09.** Pre-existing flaky AV (~20/30 runs) in the PARALLEL multifrontal-LU
front-walk (`tests/hesap-direct/test_multifrontal_lu_pp.cpp` → "CONNECTED large grid", `grid3d_weak(22)`, n=10648,
nw∈{2,4,8}; always an AV in `TlsfAllocator` coalescing a free block with smashed links) was a bug in
**`TlsfAllocator::init_pool`** — the engine's most-used allocator.

**ROOT CAUSE (PINPOINTED, not just localized):** `init_pool` reserves `free_block_size = capacity − 3·16` (start
sentinel + the free block's OWN header + end sentinel = 48 B of overhead), but placed the **end sentinel** at
`base + kBlockHeaderOverhead + free_block_size` (= `capacity − 32`) — accounting for only ONE preceding header,
**16 bytes too early**. `block_next(free_block)` = `free_block + 16 + free_block_size` = `base + 32 + free_block_size`
= `capacity − 16`, so it **overshot the mis-placed sentinel by 16 B into the chunk's uninitialised tail slack**,
whose low bit reads as `kFreeBit`. The instant a block reached the chunk's END and was freed, coalescing merged that
garbage → free-list smash. **Benign until a chunk fills to its tail.** That is the ENTIRE reason it only showed on
the **multi-chunk** GrowableTlsf path: the LU's heavy front alloc/free/REUSE churn grows the pool into 256MB chunks
and fills them to the end; a single big chunk never reaches its tail, and the memory tests never allocate-to-tail-
then-free ⇒ 820K+ assertions sailed over it for ages. **Placement bug, NOT a race** — that's why ts-wrap serialized
everything and STILL crashed, and TSan was clean.

**THE FIX (`engine/memory/src/allocators/tlsf_allocator.cpp`, `init_pool`):** end sentinel at
`base + 2U*kBlockHeaderOverhead + free_block_size` (= `block_next(free_block)` = `capacity − 16`). The three 16-byte
headers + payload now tile the chunk EXACTLY. One line, compiler-agnostic pointer arithmetic.

**The LU `factor_pool` single-chunk WORKAROUND was REMOVED** — `factor_attempt` is back to plain
`crd::memory::ThreadSafeAllocator ts(m_alloc)` over the caller's multi-chunk allocator. The real v7-e-2 GEMM arena
(`&gemm_arena` on the `factor_front(...)` call) is unrelated and KEPT.

**NO REMAINING DEBT.** The earlier "`growable-tlsf-multichunk-freelist` engine-wide debt" was a MISDIAGNOSIS — there
is no separate multi-chunk free-list bug; multi-chunk was just the only consumer that filled a chunk to its tail and
tripped the single `init_pool` defect. The debt entry is closed in `docs/debt.md`.

**VERIFIED:** shipped clean binary (no diagnostics, factor_pool removed, multi-chunk path forced) — grid3d moat
**30/30 clean** (and 30/30 with an O(n) structural free-list validator on every alloc/dealloc, 0 fires);
`crd-memory-tests` 820014 asserts/108 cases green with the fix relinked; win-debug `ctest -R "memory|hesap"` 48/48;
{1,2,4,8}-worker determinism moat intact.

**REUSABLE LESSONS (this debugging arc):**
- Foundational allocators are validated by VOLUME, not by boundary adversaries. A deliberate fill-to-tail /
  fragment-to-end TLSF stress test would have caught this years earlier — worth adding. See [build_system](build-and-verification.md#memory-build_system).
- A SOUND structural free-list validator (walk the physical block chain via `block_next`, check in-pool + free-list
  link sanity + bitmap consistency) is the tool that found it. ⚠ poison/quarantine tracking gives FALSE POSITIVES
  here (TLSF coalesce/split reuses freed-block payloads), and faulting allocators (page-heap) MASK it via altered
  timing — neither can see an init-time tiling bug.
- ⚠ A stale PCH (C1853) can let "All tests passed" report on an UN-rebuilt binary — clean the PCH/obj and confirm
  the binary relinked before trusting a green. Verify the SHIPPED artifact, not a DIAG-laden intermediate.

See [feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards), [project_v7e2_lattice_cholmod_perf](project-history.md#memory-project_v7e2_lattice_cholmod_perf).

<a id="memory-project_mrrr_perf_win_is_vectors_not_values"></a>
## project_mrrr_perf_win_is_vectors_not_values

---
name: project_mrrr_perf_win_is_vectors_not_values
description: "MRRR/dqds ties LAPACK dstemr and loses to dsterf at values-only; MRRR's perf crush is eigenVECTORS (O(n^2)), realized at v3a-3.3 — not the v3a-3.1 values leaf"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 55f742ff-2462-46c9-9771-0e5dd735901a
---

Measured 2026-05-23 (build/win-vs-ref, i9, f64), `bench_hesap_eig_vs_reference`:

**Tridiagonal eigenvalues-ONLY (our dqds `tridiag_eigenvalues_dqds` vs LAPACK):**
- vs `dstemr` (LAPACK's own MRRR values path): **0.92–0.95× = TIE** (N=256..8192).
- vs `dsterf` (Pal-Walker-Kahan root-free QL/QR): **0.53–0.65× = WE LOSE**.
- Accuracy ~1e-14.

**Dense values-only (`eigvals_sym`): 0.86–0.98× Eigen** (slight loss), mixed vs `dsyevd`.

**Full eigendecomposition values+VECTORS (`eig_sym`, v3a-1/2): WE CRUSH —
1.18–1.95× Eigen / 2.15–3.72× LAPACK `dsyev`; Hermitian 2.17× Eigen / 2.58× LAPACK.**

**Why:** dqds is a SEQUENTIAL recurrence (`d_{i+1}=f(d_i)`) — can't SIMD/parallelize,
so a faithful port TIES LAPACK's identical scalar dqds, never beats it. `dsterf` is a
tighter, cheaper per-iteration method specialized for values-only-full-spectrum.

**Parallel Sturm-bisection (16 cores, 2026-05-23):** beats LAPACK `dstemr` (MRRR)
**1.17–1.32×** at N=1024..8192 (we parallelize, LAPACK is serial) BUT still **loses to
`dsterf` 0.78–0.81×**. Naive parallel bisection = each eigenvalue ~52 full Sturm sweeps
from the global bracket = ~16–20× `dsterf`'s op-count; 16 cores only recovers ~16×, net
slight loss. To BEAT `dsterf` needs **multisection** (share Sturm counts across
eigenvalues, `dlaebz` structure — kills the redundancy) THEN parallel. `dsterf` is the
values-only algorithmic champion (root-free QR); same-technique (dqds-vs-dqds) we tie at
the serial limit, bisection-vs-bisection (vs serial `dstebz`) we crush.

**Parallel MULTISECTION (shipped 2026-05-23, `detail::multisection_chunk` +
`solve_tridiag_multisection` in eig_sym.cpp, wired into `eigvals_sym` at N>=512):**
shared-Sturm multisection (one negcount(mid) splits an interval for ALL eigenvalues in
it = kills naive bisection's ~16x redundancy) + parallel over disjoint eigenvalue-index
chunks. Measured: par/dsterf 0.95/1.04/1.06/1.05 (BEATS dsterf at N>=2048); par/dstemr
1.56-1.70 (crushes LAPACK MRRR everywhere); ~1e-14 accuracy. Below ~1024 serial dsterf
wins (parallel/jobs overhead = honest crossover). Serial fallback when num_workers()==0
(jobs uninit) - a library fn must not require jobs up. Lesson: to beat a serial reference
the lever is PARALLELISM it lacks (cores), applied to a technique whose op-count penalty
parallelism can absorb - naive bisection's 16x penalty needed multisection's sharing
first to make 16 cores a net win.

**MRRR VECTOR crush REALIZED via parallelism (2026-05-23, v3a-3.4):** the O(n²)
MRRR vector advantage is NOT a serial win — measured serial MRRR (`mrrr_compute_vectors`)
was 0.21× `dstedc` (D&C) / 0.53× `dstemr` at N=2048 (LOSES; even LAPACK's own `dstemr`
is 2.5× slower than its `dstedc` for ALL eigenvectors — D&C's O(n³) has a tiny BLAS-3
constant, MRRR's O(n²) has a huge scalar-recurrence constant). The crush comes from
PARALLELISM: MRRR eigenvectors are INDEPENDENT (each from its own twisted factorization)
and LAPACK's tridiagonal solvers are single-threaded. Parallelizing over independent
eigenvalue-index segments across `crd::jobs` (per-worker Tlsf arena — Tlsf isn't
thread-safe; serial fallback when `num_workers()<=1`) moved it to **1.24–1.35× `dstedc`
(BEATS LAPACK D&C) + 1.58–2.32× `dstemr` (CRUSHES LAPACK MRRR)** at N=256–2048,
orthogonality ~1e-13, glued-Wilkinson W₂₁⁺ passes. Same lever as multisection: use the cores
LAPACK doesn't. **MILKED 2026-05-23 (fine-grained work-stealing tasks + per-worker
pre-allocated buffers + external-buffer Tlsf arena sized ∝ n + ADAPTIVE granularity
[coarse small-n, fine large-n] + dropped the wasteful final dlar1v re-run in
mrrr_one_vector):** final tridiagonal values+vectors vs Eigen `computeFromTridiagonal`
(QL/QR O(n³)) + LAPACK `dstedc` (D&C) + `dstemr` (MRRR), N=256..2048 —
**C/Eigen 5.0/9.8/21.6/62.7× (CRUSH), C/dstedc 1.48/1.50/0.99/1.19× (BEAT/tie LAPACK's
BEST), C/dstemr 1.73/2.00/2.47/2.93× (CRUSH LAPACK MRRR)**, orth ~1e-13. Lessons: (1)
coarse static chunking idles fast P-cores on a P/E machine — fine tasks + Chase-Lev
stealing fixed it; (2) per-task Tlsf malloc kills it — pre-allocate per-worker buffers +
external-buffer arena (cheap O(1) init); (3) granularity must ramp with n or small-n
regresses from task overhead; (4) always keep-best-vector inline, never re-run the kernel.

**SIMD-across-eigenvectors (dlar1v_x4) TRIED + REVERTED 2026-05-23 — NO gain, MEMORY-bound.**
Hypothesis: batch 4 independent eigenvector dlar1v chains (4 distinct λ, same RRR) so the 4
divide-chains pipeline (fill divide throughput vs latency) → est. ~1.6–2×. MEASURED: ~0×
(within run noise). Reason: each dlar1v needs O(n) work storage (lplus/uminus/s/p for the
twist+solve); batching 4 → 16n footprint blows L2 → trades divide-latency for memory-
bandwidth = wash. The MRRR vector path is **memory-bound, not divide-latency-bound** once
batched. So the CPU is at the genuine hardware limit here (we beat Eigen 5–64×, crush
`dstemr` 1.7–2.7×, match/beat the BLAS-3 `dstedc` ~1.0–1.5×). Reverted the x4 (dead
complexity, clean-structure). **Next real lever is GPU (one thread/eigenvector) — future
slice, not CPU.** Lesson: estimate the WORKING-SET footprint before assuming a batching/SIMD
win — if batching multiplies an O(n) scratch, it can go memory-bound and net nothing.

**Why it matters / how to apply:** MRRR's whole performance reason-for-being is
eigenVECTORS in O(n^2) WITHOUT Gram-Schmidt (vs QL/QR + D&C O(n^3)). The crushing
"beat LAPACK stegr" win is at **v3a-3.3 (dlarrv vectors)**, NOT the v3a-3.1 values
leaf. Do NOT promise a values-only speed crush — it's algorithmically the wrong
battle. For values-only-full-spectrum the floor is `dsterf`; if a values-only speed
win is ever demanded, the lever is a tuned PWK root-free QR (dsterf-class), a SEPARATE
algorithm from MRRR. The v3a-3.1 dqds engine is load-bearing for v3a-3.2/.3 (the root
RRR + relative-accuracy eigenvalues feeding the twisted-factorization vectors) — its
value is correctness + high relative accuracy + being the substrate, not values speed.
[project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_v3_max_ambition_gate) [feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor)

<a id="memory-project_no_malloc_sweep_before_v5"></a>
## project_no_malloc_sweep_before_v5

---
name: project_no_malloc_sweep_before_v5
description: "Active project-wide sweep (user-mandated, before hesap v5) — remove every MallocAllocator/default_allocator + std::vector + raw type from the codebase; use crd types/containers/allocators everywhere"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b2a08d20-83df-413d-a84a-41fd3c2f00c5
---

**User directive (2026-05-27, emphatic, repeated):** sweep EVERY part of the project off
`MallocAllocator` / `crd::memory::default_allocator()` (both are malloc) + `std::vector` +
raw `double`/`int`/`size_t`, replacing with crd containers (`crd::containers::Array`/`String`),
named allocators, and crd types (`crd::f64`/`usize`/`i32`/`i64`). "NEVER malloc allocator."
This must be done **before starting hesap v5** (sparse-direct). TlsfAllocator is acceptable;
file I/O must use `crd::platform::fs::read_file_text` + manual parse (no std::ifstream/string).
See [feedback_no_malloc_no_stdvector_in_benches](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_no_malloc_no_stdvector_in_benches).

**NEW TOOL built for this (durable):** `crd::memory::GrowableTlsfAllocator`
(`engine/memory/.../growable_tlsf_allocator.{hpp,cpp}`, +5 tests). Unbounded pooled allocator =
a chain of ≤4 GB `TlsfAllocator` chunks, grown on demand from a parent; `deallocate` dispatches
via `TlsfAllocator::owns`. **This is the non-malloc replacement for `default_allocator()` when a
working set exceeds one 4 GB TLSF pool** (large sparse benches/cookers). Gotcha learned: when
growing a bespoke chunk for a big single allocation, size it `size + size/32 (TLSF
mapping_search SL round-up) + alignment + min_pool_size() + 4KB` — a fixed slack is NOT enough
(TLSF rounds the request up to the next sub-class before searching).

**Bench-conversion pattern** (runtime/examples/bench_hesap_*): file-scope `GrowableTlsfAllocator
g_alloc` for large/variable working sets (or a `TlsfAllocator` for bounded ones); `Trip{crd::i32
r,c; crd::f64 v}`; `Mtx{crd::i32 n; crd::containers::Array<Trip> trips{&g_alloc}; bool ok}`;
crd-native `read_mtx` (read_file_text + strtol/strtod, handles pattern/symmetric banners);
`Eigen::Triplet`/`SparseMatrix`/`VectorXd` stay `double` (the C++-API boundary), fed via
`Array::data()`/`setFromTriplets(data, data+size)`. Added `crd-platform` to the
`crd_add_hesap_vs_ref_bench` CMake helper so benches get `fs::read_file_text`.

**STATUS: COMPLETE (2026-05-27).** v4z CLOSED first. Then the full sweep:
- **22/22 hesap benches** converted + build-verified (Eigen/ILUPACK stay raw double at the C-API boundary).
- **11/11 smoke_*.cpp** → TlsfAllocator(256MB), build + headless-run green.
- **27 tests/* files** converted (GrowableTlsfAllocator, safe for stress); all touched test modules pass.
- **6 engine consumers**: 5 resource loaders (matrix/material/mesh/texture/shader) → `GrowableTlsfAllocator m_alloc`;
  perf-ui `default_capture_alloc` → GrowableTlsf; blas3's `scratch==nullptr` malloc fallback → a
  **per-thread (thread_local) GrowableTlsfAllocator** (no malloc; gemm tests pass).
- **Regression guard `crd-no-malloc-allocator`** (`scripts/check_no_malloc_allocator.{ps1,sh}`,
  registered in `tests/math/CMakeLists.txt`, ctest #582) — bans MallocAllocator outside
  engine/memory + the 3 allocator-test files; allows `crd-lint-allow-malloc-allocator` marker.

**KEY GOTCHA FOUND:** converting a file-scope `static MallocAllocator` (stateless, trivial dtor,
global free) to a `static GrowableTlsfAllocator` (stateful, frees its pool at exit) reintroduces a
STATIC-DESTRUCTION-ORDER hazard — a consumer freeing into the already-destroyed pool aborts at
teardown ("deallocate of a pointer not owned by any chunk" / debug-CRT _wassert). Fix: make
process-lifetime test pool allocators NEVER-DESTROYED via placement-new in static storage
(`alignas(T) static unsigned char buf[sizeof(T)]; static T& a = *::new (buf) T();` — no raw heap
new, no leak), mirroring the engine's deliberately-never-destroyed `default_allocator()`. Applied
to all `tests/resources/*` file-scope pools.

**KEPT (correct):** `engine/memory/*` (defines MallocAllocator + default_allocator);
`tests/memory/test_memory.cpp`, `tests/stress/test_allocators_stress.cpp`,
`tests/stress/test_allocators_v5_stress.cpp` (test the allocators themselves, incl. MallocAllocator
as a system page-source parent). default_allocator()-as-fallback removal is a deeper follow-on (not
done; only blas3's was converted).

<a id="memory-project_nrc_functional_core_ckir"></a>
## project_nrc_functional_core_ckir

---
name: project_nrc_functional_core_ckir
description: "D-007 B14-d: the NRC (Neural Radiance Cache, Müller 2021) FUNCTIONAL CORE in CKIR (ckir_nrc.hpp) — Instant-NGP multiresolution hash-grid encoder + MLP inference + L2 backprop training step, all Vulkan bit-exact. Closes B14 (a/b/c/d done). Includes a reusable ⛔ emitter scar: statement-tier compute Const mangled u32 > INT_MAX (MSVC static_cast<int>→INT_MIN) — fixed to app_int_const/%lld across all 5 backends."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**D-007 B14-d — NEURAL RADIANCE CACHE functional core (Müller 2021), in CKIR (2026-07-15).** The portable, vendor-neutral NRC
(no shipping engine has a differentiable-IR NRC — a moat). `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_nrc.hpp` (namespace
`crd::kir::nrc`), statement-tier COMPUTE, scalarized. All three pieces Vulkan **bit-exact vs the CPU oracle (maxabs = 0.0)** —
pure mul/add/max/select/floor + integer hash, no transcendentals. Tests `tests/kir/test_ckir_nrc.cpp` + `tests/gpu-context-vulkan`.

- **[✅ B14-d-1] `build_nrc_hashgrid_encode`** — the Instant-NGP (Müller 2022) MULTIRESOLUTION HASH-GRID encoder: per position,
  L levels; each scales to its grid res, finds the 8 cell corners, SPATIALLY HASHES each (⊕ cx·πd, & (T−1); T a power of two),
  TRILINEARLY blends the F features. Output = L·F concatenated features (the MLP input). Verified: zero-table→0, trilinear
  PARTITION-OF-UNITY (all table = C ⇒ every encoded = C, collision-independent — the exactness anchor), determinism.
- **[✅ B14-d-2] `build_nrc_infer`** — the cache QUERY: encoded → one ReLU hidden layer → linear RGB radiance (per-sample small
  MLP is the functional core; the fused/coopmat MLP is the PERF tier, rides B10 — [project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas](project-history.md#memory-project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas)).
  Verified == a hand-computed op-by-op-f32 forward.
- **[✅ B14-d-3] `build_nrc_train_grad`** — one online-step BACKPROP: forward → L2 loss → analytic ∂L/∂W2, ∂L/∂W1 (dout=2(out−tgt);
  gW2=dout·h; dh=Σ dout·W2; dpre=(pre>0)·dh; gW1=dpre·enc), per-sample (no atomics ⇒ portable + finite-diff-checkable). Verified
  == central-difference finite differences of the loss (< 5e-3). The SGD update W−=lr·Σgrad + batch accumulation are trivial
  follow-ons. `NrcConfig{levels=4, features=2, table_size=16384, base_res=16, growth=2, hidden=16, out_dim=3, learn_rate=0.01}`.

**▶▶ This CLOSES B14 — a/b/c/d all done: ReSTIR + DDGI + SVGF + NRC, the full real-time GI stack in CKIR.**

**⛔⛔ REUSABLE SCAR — the statement-tier compute Const emitter MANGLED a u32 constant > INT_MAX.** The hash seed 2654435761
(> 2³¹) was emitted to GLSL as `-2147483648u` because the emitter did `app_uint(static_cast<int>(nd.cval))` and MSVC clamps an
out-of-range double→int to INT_MIN (0x80000000). The GPU then used the wrong seed → wrong hash → wrong table entry → GPU-vs-oracle
divergence of 1.49 (a full feature magnitude). The NRC hash was the FIRST statement-tier kernel to use a u32 const > INT_MAX (the
B6 noise hash used the fragment/elementwise emitter, which was already correct via `app_int_const`). FIX: emit u32/i32 Const via
`app_int_const` (which uses `%lld` on `static_cast<long long>` — full 64-bit — + a `u`/`i` suffix), NOT `static_cast<int>`.
Applied to ALL 5 backends (ckir_glsl/hlsl/cuda/msl.hpp line ~633/213/169/199 → app_int_const; ckir_wgsl.hpp → app_ilit + `u`/`i`).
Golden byte-exact emissions HELD (values ≤ INT_MAX emit identically; only the previously-broken > INT_MAX case changed). **Lesson:
any statement-tier compute kernel using a large u32 constant (hashing, morton, bitmasks) must round-trip through app_int_const —
diagnose GPU-vs-oracle integer divergence by DUMPING the emitted GLSL and eyeballing the constant.**

<a id="memory-project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas"></a>
## project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas

---
name: project_nrc_moat_fused_mlp_crushes_cublas
description: "Fused MLP (tiny-cuda-nn/NRC technique) vs cuBLAS on RTX 4070 Ti SUPER — the GEMM/MLP+backprop campaign. DOUBLE CRUSH: forward 2.37×, backward 1.90× (both at cuBLAS's BEST split-K algo), full training step 1.98×. Standalone gold refs in bench/gpu-compute/. Next = port into CKIR."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**The NRC moat (2026-07-14).** After the sort campaign closed, resumed the journey per the user's "crush or parity"
directive on GEMM/MLP + backprop vs cuBLAS. Result: a genuine **double crush** of NVIDIA's vendor library.

**The thesis (fusion, same doctrine as [feedback_bit_exact_fft_crushes_only_when_dram_bound](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bit_exact_fft_crushes_only_when_dram_bound)):** cuBLAS is a
*per-call* library — every `cublasLtMatmul` reads its activation from DRAM and writes its output to DRAM. A 6-layer
64-wide MLP pays ~6× activation DRAM traffic on forward, plus a whole ReLU′-mask kernel per layer + every dz/da
intermediate round-tripping DRAM on backward. A **fully-fused** kernel (tensor cores / wmma, activations ping-pong
in shared through ALL layers, read input once / write output once) beats it structurally. This is exactly the
**tiny-cuda-nn / Neural Radiance Cache** fully-fused-MLP technique — NVIDIA's own NRC is built on tiny-cuda-nn for
precisely this reason. cuBLAS *cannot* express cross-GEMM fusion.

**Board (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, fp16 in / fp16 acc, batch 1M, 6×64):**
- **Forward 2.37×** — cuBLAS 2.68 ms → fused 1.13 ms (45.6 TF), bit-exact rel=0.
- **Backward 1.90×** — cuBLAS 9.60 ms (BEST split-K algo) → fused 5.06 ms (20.4 TF), rel=5e-5 vs fp32 CPU oracle.
- **Full training step 1.98×.**
Gold refs: `bench/gpu-compute/mlp_fused_bench.cu` + `mlp_backward_bench.cu`; board
`docs/bench/2026-07-14-fused-mlp-cublas-gold.md`. Build: nvcc `-O3 -std=c++17 -arch=sm_89 -allow-unsupported-compiler
-Xcompiler /Zc:preprocessor ... -lcublasLt -lcublas`.

**⚠⚠ THE FAIRNESS CORRECTION (the mandate [feedback_bench_all_peers_never_cherry_pick](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_all_peers_never_cherry_pick) in action):** the FIRST
backward run showed **8.14×** — a STRAWMAN. cuBLAS's *default* `cublasLtMatmul` heuristic ran the dW weight-gradient
GEMM (a pathological **huge-K=1 048 576 skinny 64×64 reduction**) at **37 ms / 1.4 TF** because the default does NOT
pick split-K. Adding a 256 MB workspace + `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` (which selects split-K) dropped dW
**37.29 → 2.64 ms (14×)**. Real crush = 1.90×. **LESSON: for any reduction-shaped cuBLAS GEMM (huge K, tiny MN =
weight gradients), the DEFAULT algo is a strawman — you MUST give it a workspace + heuristic algo selection or the
crush is fake.**

**Levers (serial measure→change→measure, the sort-campaign discipline):**
- Forward decisive lever = **register ILP**: 4 row-fragments × 4 col-fragments = 16 independent wmma accumulator
  chains per warp keeps the tensor pipe saturated (1 chain stalls on its own dependency). 2-warp/64-row stripe.
- Forward IN-PLACE activation store (drop ping-pong) was tried + REVERTED: wmma `store_matrix_sync`→`load_matrix_sync`
  of the same shared region scatters/gathers across lanes; a bare `__syncwarp()` does NOT make it correct (rel blew up).
  Ping-pong into the OTHER buffer is the correct fast form.
- Backward = 2 GEMMs/layer: dW = a^T·dz (reduced over batch → fp32 accumulate) + da = dz·W^T (→ on-chip g); ReLU′
  mask folded in-register. Correctness needed **per-warp** dW scratch (`sdw[WARPS][256]` — a block-shared scratch
  RACED the two warps → rel 0.54 bug, the classic per-warp-vs-block-shared trap).
- Backward atomic wall: dW is a global reduction = **200 M atomic adds** to a 64×64 fp32 target; a `NOATOMIC` probe
  measured the scatter at **1.89 ms (35 %)**. Split-K partial-accumulation (NGROUP copies + reduce) tried to relieve
  it: **NGROUP=256 (25 MB) was WORSE (5.88 ms)** — blew the atomic target out of the 48 MB L2 into DRAM latency; the
  cost is atomic *count*, not contention, and the small single target is L2-resident. NGROUP∈{1,8,32,64} all ~5.07 ms;
  NGROUP=8 marginal best. Further count reduction needs a persistent-block design holding all 6 layers' dW (98 KB fp32)
  in shared — does NOT fit Ada's 100 KB opt-in alongside activations. 1.90× is the honest floor for this design.

**Prior GEMM asset:** [project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct](project-history.md#memory-project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct) — single-GEMM FP32 ~88% cuBLAS, coopmat2 70.9 TF
tensor tier (Vulkan/GLSL). The fused MLP is a NEW capability (multi-GEMM, on-chip activations) not in CKIR's CUDA
emitter yet (which has `emit_contract_tiled_fused_cuda` = single GEMM + epilogue, FP32 FMA, no wmma path).

**✅ CKIR PORT increment 1 (2026-07-14): CUDA FORWARD authored in CKIR.** New `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_mlp.hpp` —
a MONOLITHIC per-backend recipe emitter (the SAME pattern as the coopmat2 GEMM tensor tier: cooperative-matrix ops do NOT
map to CKIR's per-invocation statement tier, so tensor kernels are whole-kernel templates keyed on a config, NOT
KStmt-built). One `MlpConfig` (width 64, layers 6, tile 128, warps 2) → `emit_fused_mlp_fwd_cuda` emits the wmma forward
kernel + `mlp_forward_ref` CPU oracle. Test `tests/kir/test_ckir_mlp.cpp` + `[.emit-cuda-mlp]` tool writes
`bench/gpu-compute/ckir_mlp_fwd_gen.cu`; driver `ckir_mlp_bench.cu` (nvcc, duels cuBLAS). **CKIR-authored kernel = 2.41×
crush**, `max_abs_diff=0` vs cuBLAS, **0/67M halves differ run-to-run = BIT-IDENTICAL** (the {1..16} determinism pillar
holds for the forward — fixed schedule, no atomics). crd-kir 706/125 green MSVC + clang-cl; tidy-clean.

**✅ CKIR PORT increment 2 (2026-07-14): Vulkan coopmat2 forward → PORTABLE across BOTH primary compute backends.**
`emit_fused_mlp_fwd_glsl` (ckir_mlp.hpp) emits a `VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2` workgroup-scoped kernel: one workgroup owns a
batch tile, activations ping in SHARED across all layers (the fusion — never touch global between layers), the fp32
accumulator round-trips a shared fp32 scratch for ReLU/linear + fp16 repack (avoids needing coopMatPerElementNV — more
portable). coopmat load/store from SHARED works. Test `tests/kir-vulkan/test_backend_vulkan.cpp` `[mlp]` (emit → shaderc →
dispatch via VulkanComputeContext → gate vs oracle): **rel = 0.0021 (fp16 tol), det_diff = 0/524288 (BIT-IDENTICAL
run-to-run)**. Same MlpConfig → CUDA wmma + Vulkan coopmat2, one oracle, both deterministic. Shared budget: 6·tile·W ≤ 48 KB
⇒ GLSL uses batch_tile=64 (24 KB) while CUDA uses 128 (perf); both match the tile-agnostic oracle. crd-kir 706/125 +
crd-kir-vulkan GPU 33027/32 green MSVC + clang-cl; tidy-clean. **⚠⚠ ORACLE WAS TRANSPOSED (latent Inc-15 bug):** the CPU
oracle read weights COLUMN-major `w[k + W·n]` — a transpose of what the kernels compute (ROW-major `w[k·W + n]`). The oracle
test only checked self-consistency, NOT that it matched the emitter. A host convention-probe (both layouts vs the LIVE CUDA
kernel output) proved row-major (col-major = 95× wrong, row-major = fp16 noise). LESSON: an oracle validated only against a
same-convention brute-force can be silently wrong vs the kernel — gate the oracle against the ACTUAL kernel output at least
once. Fixed; oracle is now the true shared reference.

**✅ CKIR PORT increment 3 (2026-07-14): forward on ALL backends via the FP32-PRECISE tier, bit-exact.** ⚠⚠ The named
tensor primitives are PHANTOM on this toolchain (I MEASURED, didn't assume): HLSL **WaveMatrix** REJECTED by DXC 1.8.2502
(`WaveMatrixLeft` undeclared — never shipped in mainline DXC; the DX12 backend also compiles cs_6_0); **WGSL subgroup-matrix**
is Dawn-experimental, absent from the `wgpu-native` this repo uses; **MSL simdgroup_matrix** mature on Apple but NO Metal
runtime on Windows. Emitting them = theater (forbidden). User chose (AskUserQuestion) **FP32-precise** = the STRONGER moat:
FP32 no-FMA ⇒ BIT-EXACT across ALL backends, which the fp16 tensor tier structurally cannot be. **KEY ARCHITECTURE INSIGHT:**
an FP32-fused MLP is plain compute (shared + barriers + loops) ⇒ it builds on the CKIR STATEMENT TIER (`build_mlp_fwd_fp32`,
ckir_mlp.hpp: 1 workgroup=1 sample, 1 thread=1 output feature, activations ping-pong in shared = the fusion; ascending
`acc=acc+a·w` fold, precise=no-FMA) and the GENERIC per-backend emitters lower it to ALL FIVE — no hand-written recipes.
Verified: CPU oracle bit-exact (512 `==`); **Vulkan RUN bit-exact; DX12 RUN bit-exact & IDENTICAL to Vulkan** (the {1..16}
cross-backend moat, on the MLP); CUDA nvcc-compiles; WGSL+MSL emit-validated (no imperative WebGPU ctx / no Metal here — the
kir-cuda/webgpu backends only do value-node run(), not statement-tier KEntry; Vulkan+DX12 have IComputeContext +
dispatch_kernel_1wg). Tensor tier (the CRUSH) stays CUDA wmma + Vulkan coopmat2; FP32-precise is the PORTABLE+BIT-EXACT
companion. crd-kir 1234/127 green; tidy-clean.

**✅ CKIR PORT increment 4 (2026-07-14): the BACKWARD pass with a DETERMINISTIC dW reduction — the full NRC moat is now in
CKIR.** Two statement-tier builders (ckir_mlp.hpp), NO atomics: `build_mlp_bwd_dz` (per-sample activation-gradient chain —
1 wg = 1 sample, dz[l] computed on-chip via the ReLU′ mask `select(a[l+1]>0, g, 0)`, da=dz·Wᵀ→next g, writes dz_all for
kernel B) + `build_mlp_bwd_dw` (the DETERMINISTIC weight-gradient reduction: dW[l][k][n] = Σ_r a[l][r][k]·dz[l][r][n] summed
in ASCENDING sample order = fixed order, no atomics; grid = L·W, wg=(l,k), thread=n). The standalone's fp32-`atomicAdd` dW
was NON-deterministic; this is bit-exact AND run-to-run BIT-IDENTICAL — the moat. Verified: CPU oracle `mlp_backward_ref`
bit-exact (28k `==`); **Vulkan dz+dW bit-exact (bad==0) + dW run-to-run BIT-IDENTICAL (det==0)**. Both on the statement tier
⇒ the generic emitters lower to all backends. crd-kir 28883/128 green MSVC + clang-cl; tidy-clean.

**✅ CKIR PORT increment 5 (2026-07-14): DX12 backward + CUDA TENSOR backward — THE FULL NRC MOAT IS NOW IN CKIR.** (a) FP32
statement-tier backward runs on DX12 too (bad_dz==0, bad_dw==0, BIT-IDENTICAL to Vulkan+oracle). (b) `emit_fused_mlp_bwd_cuda`
(ckir_mlp.hpp) = the CKIR tensor backward recipe (reduce_dw + fused wmma: dz mask + on-chip da wmma chain + dW=aᵀ·dz wmma
reduced over batch → fp32 atomic into NGROUP partials, dims baked, mirrors the forward tensor recipe); `ckir_mlp_bwd_gen.cu`
nvcc-compiles, `ckir_mlp_bwd_bench.cu` **reproduces the crush 1.94× vs cuBLAS** (best split-K), dW rel=5e-5. ⚠ fp32-atomic dW
= crush tier (per-backend, NOT bit-exact); the FP32 statement-tier backward is the deterministic/bit-exact companion. Vulkan
coopmat2 backward NOT built (coopmat2 batch-reduction dW disproportionately hard for marginal value; Vulkan has the
deterministic FP32 backward). crd-kir 28883/128 green MSVC + clang-cl; tidy-clean.

**⭐⭐ NRC-MOAT-IN-CKIR CAMPAIGN COMPLETE (increments 1–5):** forward = tensor CRUSH (CUDA wmma 2.41× + Vulkan coopmat2) +
FP32-precise PORTABLE/BIT-EXACT (Vulkan+DX12 run, CUDA nvcc, WGSL/MSL emit); backward = tensor CRUSH (CUDA wmma 1.94×) +
FP32-precise PORTABLE/BIT-EXACT + DETERMINISTIC dW (Vulkan+DX12 run). This is the B10 (neural / cooperative-vectors) compute
substrate for the D-007 detour, built ahead + doubling as the hesap-GPU ML substrate. Gold refs: mlp_fused_bench.cu +
mlp_backward_bench.cu. Optional future: Vulkan coopmat2 backward; formal B10/C6 coop-vector device path when the detour reaches it.
