<a id="memory-project_obj_torus_normals_unlit_ren3"></a>
## project_obj_torus_normals_unlit_ren3

---
name: project_obj_torus_normals_unlit_ren3
description: "RESOLVED (2026-07-27): torus unlit = CW winding -> inward normals; orient_outward_if_closed (signed volume, closedness by POSITION-welded edges) fixes it, gated for tetrahedron AND genus-1 torus. Shadows/albedo exclusivity resolved by the bindless material heap (REN-38)."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a3482f73-d858-400b-816d-942216e20052
  modified: 2026-07-28T23:57:52.041Z
---

Two OPEN defects found by the user inspecting the sandbox during REN-3.2-b (2026-07-25). Neither is a shadow bug.

**1. ⛔ The OBJ torus monument renders UNLIT — its generated normals are wrong.**
Symptom: the torus looks "in complete shadow, light does not affect it". **Confirmed by A/B**: it stays dark with
`crd-sandbox --no-shadows`, so it is not the shadow lookup.
Mechanism: the forward FS computes `lit = 0.25 + 0.75 * max(dot(N,L),0) * vis`. **A zero/inward normal (N·L ≤ 0)
and full occlusion (vis = 0) produce the SAME flat 0.25 ambient** — brightness alone cannot distinguish them,
which is why `--no-shadows` is the decisive test. Keep that flag.
Suspect: `crd::assetio::generate_normals` (`engine/asset-io/src/condition.cpp:170`) takes the face normal as
`cross(b-a, c-a)`, i.e. it ASSUMES CCW winding. An OBJ with CW winding yields inward normals everywhere.
⛔ **Gate gap**: `tests/asset-io/test_condition.cpp` covers smoothing/angle behaviour but never asserts normals
point OUTWARD against an independent metric. Same shape as the marching-cubes scar —
[feedback_marching_cubes_winding_needs_independent_metric](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_marching_cubes_winding_needs_independent_metric) — winding/orientation needs a metric that does not
come from the same assumption being tested (e.g. dot(normal, pos - centroid) > 0 on a closed convex-ish mesh, or
signed volume via the divergence theorem).

**2. ⛔ Shadows and albedo are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (a REN-3.2-b regression, user-visible).**
`draw_storage_shadowed_depth` and `draw_storage_textured_depth` both want descriptor slot 1, so
`record_one_group` nulls `base_color` when shadows are active — textured monuments lose their maps the moment
shadows turn on. The user noticed immediately ("I can see the textures" with shadows off).
Fix direction: bind the shadow atlas at its OWN slot (a 4th binding) so a group can be textured AND shadowed,
rather than choosing. The bindless material work in REN-3.3 subsumes this, but the regression is live NOW.

**3. Performance: ~45 fps with shadows (from ~116).** Every cascade draws ALL 10k instances regardless of
whether they fall in that cascade's volume — cascade 0 covers a few metres and still renders the whole field.
Per-cascade culling against the cascade sphere (already computed in `CsmCascades`) is the obvious first win.
A ~10 ms `present` phase is also unexplained; point the REN-8 per-pass timestamps at it before optimizing.

Related: [feedback_gates_run_configs_the_app_never_ships](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_gates_run_configs_the_app_never_ships), [feedback_fps_single_run_is_noise_median_of_five](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_fps_single_run_is_noise_median_of_five).

**RESOLUTION (2026-07-27):** `orient_outward_if_closed` (condition.cpp) decides orientation by SIGNED VOLUME
(divergence theorem — never consults the generated normals) and only on CLOSED meshes (edges identified by
POSITION, not index, because crease-splitting makes every corner unique). `assets/source/torus.obj` measured
6V = -18.35 (CW/inward) — exactly the class. Gated twice: the tetrahedron (centroid metric) and a genus-1 CW/CCW
torus (RING-DISTANCE metric — a torus is not star-shaped, so the centroid metric cannot test it). The
shadows/albedo slot conflict is closed by the bindless material heap + dedicated shadow-atlas binding.

**⛔ ADDENDUM (2026-07-29) — the fix was in, the gates were green, and the SANDBOX STILL SHOWED THE BLACK
TORUS for two more days.** Cause: the cooked MESH artifact was cached from BEFORE the orientation fix, and
`kWave1HandlerVersion` was never bumped — the cache key said "nothing changed". It re-cooked (and the torus lit
up) only when the REN-39 fox fix bumped v3→v4. **The rule: any behavioral change inside a cook handler MUST bump
its handler version in the same commit — a conditioning fix that leaves stale artifacts in every existing cache
looks exactly like the bug surviving the fix.** Related: [feedback_skinned_mesh_missing_normals_nan_black](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_skinned_mesh_missing_normals_nan_black).


<!-- end-memory:project_obj_torus_normals_unlit_ren3 -->

## project_ocean_visual_gaps_before_b16_close

---
name: project_ocean_visual_gaps_before_b16_close
description: Ocean/water render visual polish — status of the gold-standard gaps (user-flagged 2026-07-16)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9d587ba2-dba2-4939-baa4-c0515d41bdbe
---

The displaced-geometry ocean render (`crd::kir::water`, rendered by `[.ocean-frame]` in
`tests/gpu-context-vulkan/test_vulkan_context.cpp`). The user (2026-07-16) wants it to look like the reference
(`D:/Dev/cerid/build/ref_ocean_2.png`) and flagged a full visual-polish spec; addressed in a polish pass the same day.

**[✅ ADDRESSED 2026-07-16]:**
1. **Horizon seam** — fixed: the FS grazing-horizon veil now drives the OUTPUT ALPHA (transparency to the real sky in the
   composite), not a colour veil, so the far crests dissolve into the actual sky. Only a faint residual line remains.
2. **Temporal + textured foam** (the user's explicit model) — restored `build_ocean_foam_accumulate` in the bake: a 22-step
   warmup, foam=max(prev·decay, inject), decay 0.965 ⇒ whitecaps accumulate then fade EXPONENTIALLY, never instantly. The FS
   textures it with Worley bubbles + a fractal break-up (not a flat gray blob). ⚠ VERY sensitive: crest whitecaps + clean troughs
   needs assemble foam_bias≈0.70 + choppiness 1.3/1.5 on cascades 1/2 (choppiness sharpens only the baked Jacobian, NOT the gentle
   vertical geometry — so it adds foam without steepening the mesh) + FS ocr.foam_bias≈0.14. Too high ⇒ whitewater everywhere.
3. **Gentle waves + amplitude split** — low-freq cascade = tall geometry (geo_w[0]=1.0), high-freq = normal-map texture
   (geo_w→0.035); lower wind ⇒ gentle rollers.
4. **Anti-aliasing** — SSAA 3× (9 samples/px, box-downfilter).
5. **God rays** — crepuscular radial scatter (the `finish` lambda), tuned so shafts show but the sun doesn't white out
   (gain≈0.7, only lum>0.74 casts).
6. **Darker/defined clouds** — coverage 0.66 + a DENSITY-driven self-shadow (thick cores darker) ⇒ defined gray masses with the
   sun glowing through, extended toward the horizon (fragment sky `build_ocean_frame_fft_fs` in `ckir_raster_triangle.hpp`).

**[✅ CINEMATIC PASS — ALL GAPS CLOSED 2026-07-22]** the residual horizon line, the soft sun, and the clouds are DONE to a
cinematic bar (all 3 render paths consistent). The non-obvious lessons:

1. **The residual "faint horizon line" was the PROJECTED-GRID's dark SAWTOOTH top edge** (the last triangle row's world-space
   silhouette), NOT a shading bug — invisible at frame scale, obvious at 4× nearest-neighbour zoom (that's how you diagnose it).
   Killed by THREE cooperating changes, none alone enough: (a) `ocean_projected_vertex` far-crest displacement taper starts
   EARLIER (s=180 not 250) so the sawtooth amplitude shrinks before the horizon; (b) `build_ocean_water_geo_fs` coverage-**α**
   ramps to 0 over RANGE `dist∈[193,248]` (NOT a `v.y` grazing fade — grazing varies too slowly with distance, so pushing it
   hard enough to kill the seam also washes the mid-field) so the residual sawtooth is composited out; (c) `fogc = hazeh` (the
   sky-at-horizon tone) so the transition pixels match the sky behind them → invisible, not a grey band.
2. **ONE shared sky.** New `crd::kir::water::analytic_sky` (Rayleigh+Mie dome + puffy Worley×fbm cumulus) is THE atmosphere
   source, called by BOTH the sky pass (`build_ocean_frame_fft_fs`) and the water reflection (`build_ocean_water_geo_fs`,
   `with_clouds=true` ⇒ the sea mirrors the clouds). Before this the geo FS reflected the OLD sun — two sky defs had drifted.
3. **Blown-out sun = Mie/glow BREADTH, not the disk.** Tighten the `pow(mu,·)`/`exp` exponents (Mie 6→11, glow 32→60) before
   touching intensity.
4. **Puffy cumulus:** drive coverage with a broad fbm, use Worley billows to SCULPT (`fbm·(a+b·bill)`) — billows-alone = sparse
   dots. Full recipe (params→physics→assembly→traps): `docs/recipes/2026-07-22-cinematic-ocean-sky-and-seamless-horizon.md`.

DEFERRED still (prior user sequencing, explicit — not silently dropped): SSR/planar reflection/screen-space refraction/underwater
Beer-god-rays + B16-b caustics — only meaningful once scene objects / a deeper water volume exist; the open-horizon cinematic bar
is met without them. **Bake cost:** the 22-step temporal-foam warmup × 4 cascades × 3 frames makes `[.ocean-frame]` take a few
minutes — for fast iteration, temporarily render 1 frame (restore all 3 at close).

<a id="memory-project_ode_in_games_layering"></a>
## project_ode_in_games_layering

---
name: project_ode_in_games_layering
description: How ODEs map onto game dev + where ultra-fast implementations live — the 3-layer answer (brainstorm with user 2026-06-11; shapes v9-a/v9-g API + eylem integration)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a2c6b443-e9d7-415b-bcbd-33989fe1fde8
---

User brainstorm 2026-06-11 ("can we use ODEs in game dev... where should the ultra fast implementations
live?"). The agreed mental model — THREE kinds of ODE machinery in a game, never conflated:

1. **eylem core = fixed-step symplectic + NON-SMOOTH solvers (eylem-native, NOT hesap).** Contacts/friction/
   limits are complementarity problems; adaptive ODE solvers fight impacts. Stiffness handled by XPBD/TGS
   (springs-as-constraints, unconditionally stable), not implicit ODE integration. eylem consumes v9-g's
   FORMULAS + TEST CONTRACTS (energy drift, time-reversibility, determinism), not a driver — its integrator
   is fused into the SoA body sweep. eylem NEVER calls the general driver in the hot loop (virtual RHS per
   body per substep = the anti-pattern).
2. **The drivetrain crossover (differentiator):** car/tracked-vehicle drivetrains (engine→clutch→gearbox→
   wheels, 5–15 states) are GENUINELY stiff — industry substeps at 300–1000 Hz; the elite answer = one
   v9-f Rosenbrock step per physics tick (one small LU, unconditionally stable at low speed, deterministic).
   Horse carts/chariots = plain eylem multibody (joints + kinematic animal), no ODE solver.
3. **Gameplay/scripts/systemic = the GENERAL driver** (callbacks, adaptive, events): ballistics-with-drag
   (v9-c events = time-of-impact!), buoyancy, ecology/economy ticks (Lotka-Volterra for the living world —
   ties to [project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid](project-history.md#memory-project_endgame_story_games_on_cerid) agent-NPC worlds), Kerbal-class orbital gameplay
   (moat = deterministic-multiplayer feature). Budget via max_steps per tick. Animation: camera/UI springs
   = CLOSED-FORM critically-damped (tiny utility, no integrator); jiggle/secondary = fixed-step kernels or
   XPBD; Baraff-Witkin cloth = ONE CG solve ⇒ hesap-ITERATIVE consumer, not ode.

**Why/How to apply — the v9-a design consequence (load-bearing):** `crd-hesap-ode` ships TWO API layers —
(a) **stepper KERNEL HEADERS** (raw-span, allocation-free, inlineable: step_semi_implicit/verlet/yoshida...)
designed headers-first so eylem/animation/DAW use them without the driver; (b) the **general `integrate()`
driver** (OdeFunction callbacks, adaptive, events, dense output) for scripts/engineering/cinematic/CLI.
v9-f Rosenbrock needs a **preallocated-workspace variant** (audio-thread + physics-tick = no alloc).
Matches the ADR-0078 two-layer pattern. Related: [project_v9_ode_plan](project-history.md#memory-project_v9_ode_plan),
[project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism](project-history.md#memory-project_eylem_crush_physx_jolt_with_determinism).

<a id="memory-project_own_hdr_image_codec_no_third_party"></a>
## project_own_hdr_image_codec_no_third_party

---
name: project_own_hdr_image_codec_no_third_party
description: "HDR image import is OUR OWN codec (RGBE+EXR+PFM), zero 3rd-party even at import — a crd-resources slice B-hdr, built AFTER B13"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 40e3ad67-a505-447d-89df-272b48c237f6
---

User direction 2026-07-12 (emphatic): **"I don't want to use 3rd party library for just reading an
hdr image at all! We must do it ourselves."** So HDR image import is a first-class OWN codec — no
3rd-party lib even transiently at import (the user's "maybe use them just for importing" was
explicitly overridden for HDR: we own it end to end).

**STATUS 2026-07-13 — ✅ FULLY COMPLETE (4-config + tidy, `[hdr]`+`[deflate]` 23 cases / 197 assertions):**
`engine/resources/{include/crd/resources,src}/`: `hdr_image.{hpp,cpp}` (`HdrImage` = flat row-major channel-interleaved f32;
RGBE + PFM + `.crdr` round-trip type 'HDRI'), `hdr_exr.cpp` (the EXR container + our own IEEE half↔float + NONE + RLE + ZIP +
ZIPS + PIZ), `deflate.{hpp,cpp}` (our own RFC-1951 inflate ALL block types + fixed-Huffman/LZ77 deflate + RFC-1950 zlib +
Adler-32), `hdr_piz.{hpp,cpp}` (our own OpenEXR 2-D lifting wavelet + canonical-Huffman+RLE + bitmap/LUT). **⭐⭐ Validated
both readers against REAL OpenEXR files** (OpenCV-written ZIP-FLOAT + PIZ-HALF, decoded bit-exact) + a foreign CPython-zlib
dynamic-Huffman vector. Codec is span-in / Array-out (no filesystem — caller does file I/O). To get DEFLATE/wavelet/Huffman
byte-exact we referenced the published specs/algorithms (RFC 1951, the OpenEXR format); the code is ours. GPU float-texture
upload (env maps) is the renderer/rhi consumer leaf — needs a float `TextureFormat` (the enum is RGBA8/BC7 only today).
⛔ deflate scar: [feedback_array_push_back_self_reference_uaf](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_array_push_back_self_reference_uaf).

**Slice `B-hdr` (side RES) in the D-007 detour master table**, placed right after B13. Decided
timing (AskUserQuestion 2026-07-12): **finish B13 first, then build the codec.** Decided scope:
**RGBE + EXR + PFM** (the full set), all ours:
- **B-hdr-a Radiance RGBE** (`.hdr`/`.pic`) — text header + RLE'd RGBE scanlines; decode `f =
  mantissa · 2^(exp−128−8)`. ~150 lines, trivial. read+write.
- **B-hdr-b Portable FloatMap** (`.pfm`) — raw float raster, endian-tagged header. Trivial. read+write.
- **B-hdr-c OpenEXR** (`.exr`) — half/float, uncompressed + ZIP + PIZ scanline; needs our OWN
  DEFLATE/inflate + PIZ (wavelet + Huffman). The substantial one, still no 3rd-party.

**Architecture:** it lives in `crd-resources` (NOT crd-kir — it is an asset-import codec, not a CKIR
shader concern). Decodes to float pixels → wrapped as a versioned **`.crdr`** texture resource,
same path as B2 textures. The consumer is [project_b8_full_gold_standard_renderer_scope](project-history.md#memory-project_b8_full_gold_standard_renderer_scope) IBL
env maps (B8-e) and B15 sky/atmosphere. Round-trip bit-exact CPU tests + a real env map decoded and
sampled through the B2 texture path is the DoD.

Relates to [project_full_ckir_after_detour_legacy_path_deleted](project-history.md#memory-project_full_ckir_after_detour_legacy_path_deleted) and the no-3rd-party posture in
[feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor) / [feedback_no_std_containers_anywhere_incl_tests](build-and-verification.md#memory-feedback_no_std_containers_anywhere_incl_tests).


<!-- end-memory:project_own_hdr_image_codec_no_third_party -->

<a id="memory-project_phase_sequencing_pivot"></a>
## project_phase_sequencing_pivot

---
name: Phase sequencing pivot 2026-05-11 — geometry-before-eylem-v1c
description: ADR-0076 §12 amendment pivoted Phase 3.1.7 (crd-geometry) to execute BEFORE Phase 3.1 v1c instead of after Phase 3.1.6 hesap, eliminating deferred-refactor debt across eylem + sdf at the cost of ~5–7 months calendar delay before eylem v1c can resume.
type: project
originSessionId: 44374b19-0728-4302-88da-52db2ebbc4c4
---

**Decision date:** 2026-05-11
**ADR:** 0076 §12 amendment (alongside Status + §3 + §6 inline updates)

## What changed

Phase 3.1.7 `crd-geometry` (full 29-slice phase, ~5–7 months) now
executes **immediately after Phase 3.1 v1b cluster close** and
**BEFORE Phase 3.1 v1c (broadphase)**, instead of its original slot
after Phase 3.1.6 `crd-hesap`.

## New execution order

1. Phase 3.1 v0 ✅ + v1a ✅ + v1a-material ✅ + v1a-draw d0..d4 ✅ + v1b-a/b/c/d ✅ + v1b-e (sweep gates close)
2. **Phase 3.1.7 — full 29 slices, ~5–7 months calendar**
3. Phase 3.1 v1c (broadphase, **consumes `crd-geometry-bvh` from day 1**, no ships-own + refactor)
4. Phase 3.1 v1d (narrow phase, **consumes `crd-geometry-convex` GJK+EPA+SAT from day 1**)
5. Phase 3.1 v1d-mesh (**consumes `crd-geometry-mesh` from day 1**)
6. Phase 3.1 v1e–v1k as planned
7. Phase 3.1.5 `crd-sdf` interleaved between eylem v2 and v3; **v2 mesh-bake consumes `crd-geometry-mesh` directly** (ADR-0064 §4 deferred-refactor is OBSOLETED)
8. Phase 3.1 v3–v9 as planned
9. Phase 3.1.6 `crd-hesap` (unchanged: sequential successor to Phase 3.1; eylem v7 FEM still ships own PCG → `crd-hesap-iterative` refactor stays intact)

## Why

User invocation of `feedback_quality_bar.md` ("elite, no shortcuts,
single-path"). The original deferred-refactor pattern was a shortcut
by construction — it produced ~1500 LOC of throwaway BVH / GJK / EPA /
winding-number code across eylem + sdf that existed only until the
substrate landed. The user reviewed the calendar tradeoff (~5–7 months
delay before eylem v1c resumes) and explicitly chose to pay that cost
to avoid the shortcut.

Second-order argument supporting the pivot: the substrate-tier
sequencing rationale in the original ADR-0076 §6 ("physics → implicit
geometry → numerics → explicit geometry") actually strengthens under
the pivot. Eylem's broadphase + narrow-phase ARE explicit-geometry
consumers from day 1, so the more honest sequencing is **physics-
interface → explicit geometry → physics-runtime → implicit geometry →
numerics**: eylem v1a interface ✅, eylem v1b storage ✅, geometry,
eylem v1c+ runtime, sdf, hesap.

## What is OBSOLETED

- ADR-0076 §3 deferred-refactor table rows for eylem v1c/v1d/v1d-mesh + sdf v2 — now "consumes from day 1".
- ADR-0076 §6 deferred-refactor subsection — preserved as "Original decision (superseded)" so prior session logs remain auditable.
- ADR-0064 §4 sdf deferred-refactor — also OBSOLETE; sdf v2 ships consuming `crd-geometry-mesh` directly.

## What is NOT changed

- ADR-0076 §1–§5 architecture (module split, 11 sub-modules, API design, determinism, SIMD/containers commitments).
- ADR-0076 §7 slice list (same 29 slices, same LOC budget, same calendar).
- ADR-0076 §8–§10 (out of scope, risks, open research questions).
- ADR-0062 / ADR-0063 (eylem architecture + determinism) — eylem v1c+ implementation reaches the same final shape, just via a different path.
- eylem v7 FEM → hesap-iterative refactor reservation — that deferred-refactor remains intact (hesap is still after eylem).

## How to apply

- Whenever planning eylem v1c or later: assume `crd-geometry-{bvh,convex,mesh,primitives}` is available.
- Whenever planning sdf v2: same — `crd-geometry-mesh` is available.
- v1b-e closure is gated on full 14-config sweep PASS (per `feedback_full_sweep_required.md`).
- The moment v1b-e closes, the next slice is **Phase 3.1.7 v0a — `crd-geometry-primitives`** (types + closest-point + intersection tests + barycentric, ~3000 LOC, ~1 wk).
- Do NOT propose narrow-subset shortcuts of Phase 3.1.7 — full 29 slices ship.

## Cross-references

- ADR-0076 §12 amendment (canonical source)
- `docs/phases/phase-3.1-eylem.md` (pause-marker between v1b and v1c)
- `docs/phases/phase-3.1.7-geometry.md` (status: next-active)
- `docs/phases/phase-3.1.5-sdf.md` (note that ADR-0064 §4 deferred-refactor is obsolete)
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` (Phase 3.1 + 3.1.7 + 3.1.5 long-range outlook all updated)
- `context.md` (Active phase + Coming up next + Last shipped milestone all reflect the pivot)

<a id="memory-project_procedural_vertex_vocabulary_f7"></a>
## project_procedural_vertex_vocabulary_f7

---
name: procedural-vertex-vocabulary-f7
description: "REN-38-F7 vocabulary: .crdv `position = \"node:...\"` = procedural vertex (no pull) with [expand] + @corner/@instance/@category/field:/hdr: inputs + vertex-local view_proj op; ckir_draw.hpp DELETED — draw suite is .crdv+.crdm in draw_assets.hpp"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 31e31376-4d57-4a00-b30c-77365444ac88
  modified: 2026-07-27T02:45:56.786Z
---

The `.crdv` vocabulary (2026-07-27, REN-38-F7): root `position = "node:<name>"` makes a VERTEX stage
procedural — no vertex record, clip position IS the named vec4 node. `[expand]` declares
`verts_per_instance` (instance = vid/N, corner = vid−instance·N), `instance_words`/`instance_off`, and the
`@category` scheme (`category_field` + `category_mask_word` — the bit test is a SCHEME like skinning, not
authored bit math). Node input spellings: `@corner`, `@instance`, `@category`, `field:<k>` (f32 bits),
`fieldu:`, `fieldc:` (packed RGBA8→vec4), `hdr:`/`hdru:`/`hdrc:` (header words). `view_proj` is a
VERTEX-COOK-LOCAL op (header mat4 · (p,1) → clip; the material registry has no header concept). The material
registry gained `fwidth`. Varyings in procedural stages are `node:`/`clip.w` terms ONLY.

Consumers: the scene tess-corner + visbuffer-fullscreen VS (F6) and the whole debug-draw suite —
`engine/draw/include/crd/draw/draw_assets.hpp` embeds `vertex/draw_line|draw_tri|draw_grid.crdv` +
`material/draw_line|draw_tri|draw_grid.crdm` (shipped under `assets/`, drift-gated);
`engine/draw/include/crd/draw/ckir_draw.hpp` is DELETED. FS side: matcook materials read varyings BY LOCATION
via `geomcolor(i)`/`texcoord(i)`/`normal(i)`/`position(i)` and compose through the `unlit` technique with
CONSTANT SurfaceInputs. Related: [cook-only-gates-ship-device-impossible-programs](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_cook_only_gates_ship_device_impossible_programs),
[every-render-pass-through-our-own-frame-graph-machinery](rendering.md#memory-feedback_every_render_pass_through_our_own_frame_graph_machinery).


<!-- end-memory:project_procedural_vertex_vocabulary_f7 -->

## project_raf10_app_custom_renderer

---
name: project_raf10_app_custom_renderer
description: "RAF-10 (D-007) DONE — an application customises the Cerid renderer ten ways through public seams only, no engine-rendering edit, both backends"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: bf0ab64f-0cb7-4b04-970c-78c4f58c02b9
  modified: 2026-08-04T06:56:24.426Z
---

RAF-10 (D-007, closed 2026-08-04) proves the APPLICATION side of the RAF band: a small app package customises the
renderer in every intended way with NO engine-rendering-code edit and NO privileged engine-only path, on Vulkan AND
DX12. Session: `docs/sessions/2026-08-04-raf10-app-custom-renderer.md`. Follows [project_raf9_engine_default_assets_by_id](project-history.md#memory-project_raf9_engine_default_assets_by_id).

**The proof:** `tests/scene-render/test_raf10_app.cpp` (PUBLIC headers only — the Gate-10 boundary is compiler-enforced)
+ `tests/scene-render/app_assets/` — 61 assertions, 2 cases (Vulkan + DX12), all green. Does all ten: engine default
unchanged; include an engine graph as a subgraph; inject a custom pass at a declared anchor; app material; app
technique; app display transform; fully app-authored graph; custom C++ pass executor; explicit capability fallback;
both backends.

**The public engine seams added (`SceneRenderer`):**
- `set_app_asset_root(dir)` — mounts `app://` (uses RAF-9 `AssetResolver`).
- `set_scene_material(opaque_id, textured_id)` — overrides the hard-coded scene material; a new `resolve_asset_text`
  routes a `://`-schemed id through the mount table, a bare name through the engine mount (byte-identical default).
- `define_technique(const kir::technique::Technique&)` — the engine's OWN `TechniqueLibrary::define` mechanism, replayed
  after the builtins in `init_programs` so a same-named app technique shadows (find is last-match). NOT a weaker path.
- `register_post_asset(id, crdp_name)` — cooks an app `.crdp` via the generalised `ensure_post_program_named`.
- `register_pass_executor(id, fn)` — an app `PassRecordFn` joins the recorder's ONE `GraphExecutorTable`. Driven by the
  new `FramePassKind::Custom` + `FramePassDesc::executor` + `record_custom_via_executor` adapter in frame-cook. The id
  is the extension point — a new pass MECHANIC with no `FramePassKind` edit and no backend virtual.
- `capability(name)` — public query forwarding to the ONE predicate the `requires`/`fallback` step-down consults.

**Composition (`[[include]]` + `[[inject]]`) renders at runtime for the first time** — flatten is wired into
`set_frame_graph_toml` (RAF-9 seam B), the flat graph is re-validated, and 3 never-rendered-path bugs were fixed (see
[feedback_composition_and_app_registration_runtime_path_dropped_state](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_composition_and_app_registration_runtime_path_dropped_state)).

**Flagged, NOT RAF-10 scope:** `pbr_neutral`/`saturate` post ops fail CKIR→SPIR-V `create_program` (latent
material-cook/CKIR gap; app grade uses `agx`, which works). Fully `.crdt`-asset-driven techniques need a `.crdt`→CKIR
body serializer (out of scope per RAF9plan.md:162). The 2 pre-existing RAF-8-baseline GPU-gate failures (REN-39-C1,
REN-40-D) still await their own investigation.

**Next:** RAF-11 (hot reload) → RAF-12 (DELETE legacy draw verbs + the `FramePassKind` switch — deletion is the proof)
→ RAF-13 (docs + §22 DoD).

<a id="memory-project_raf9_engine_default_assets_by_id"></a>
## project_raf9_engine_default_assets_by_id

---
name: project_raf9_engine_default_assets_by_id
description: "RAF-9 DONE — engine default renderer loads by canonical engine:// id through a public AssetResolver + ProgramRegistry (no str_is chain, no relative-path caller); the two-layer pattern + the pre-existing RAF-8-baseline GPU-gate failures"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: bf0ab64f-0cb7-4b04-970c-78c4f58c02b9
  modified: 2026-08-03T22:25:19.095Z
---

**RAF-9 DONE (2026-08-04)** — the engine default renderer loads BY CANONICAL `engine://` ID through the SAME public
registry an app uses. Implemented the Ultraplan-refined plan (`docs/research/RAF9plan.md`) verbatim on branch
`raf-9-engine-default-assets`.

**Two thin layers over RAF-1's identity model** ([project_ren8a_flip_live_onto_render_graph](project-history.md#memory-project_ren8a_flip_live_onto_render_graph) is the sibling RAF-8):
1. **render-asset-core stays a PURE LEAF** — added only `asset_extension(folder)` + `on_disk_relative(AssetRef, out)`
   (I/O-free) to `identity.{hpp,cpp}`. ⛔ The folder→ext table is keyed on the FOLDER STRING, not `AssetType`:
   `infer_type` has no `post` case and maps `light` (not `lighting`). frame→.frame.toml · vertex→.crdv · material→.crdm
   · post→.crdp · lighting→.crdl · technique→.crdt · lod→.crdlod.
2. **scene-render gets the I/O `AssetResolver` + public `ProgramRegistry`** (new `engine/scene-render/src/asset_resolver.hpp`,
   header-only). Resolver: mount table (`engine://`=`asset_root`, so a resolved file is the EXACT pre-RAF-9 file →
   output unchanged by construction) + `read_relative` (the one disk-read path, lifted from `asset_text`) + `read_ref`
   (on_disk_relative + read_relative; a miss → the new `AssetNotFound` NAMED diagnostic). ProgramRegistry: AssetId →
   provider using the `FramePassFn` fn-ptr+`void*` idiom (NO std::function); engine registers captureless thunks over
   the `ensure_*` builders at `init_programs` (`register_default_programs`, idempotent).

**What changed in scene_renderer.cpp:** `asset_text`→delegates to `resolver.read_relative`; `resolve_frame_asset`→
`read_ref` (dropped the `crd://frame/` prefix-strip); `SceneHost::program()`/`kernel()`→parse the id to an AssetId and
look it up (the whole `str_is(id,"crd://scene/…")` chain is GONE — the bare-name resolvers for storage_buffer /
draw-list / "shadows" / instance_program STAY, they're graph resource names not asset identity); `ensure_post_program`
gained a `bool is_agx` discriminator. New public `set_frame_graph(engine:// id)` + `register_raster/kernel_program`.
Sandbox selects `engine://frame/…` via a small `install_frame` helper. The 16 `assets/frame/*.frame.toml` rewritten
`crd://`→`engine://` (pixel-neutral).

⛔⛔ **LOAD-BEARING:** `crd://` FOLDS to `engine://` in `AssetRef::parse` (identity.cpp:67 `parse_scheme`), so
`parse("crd://x").id() == parse("engine://x").id()`. Always look up by the PARSED AssetId (via `AssetRef::parse`),
NEVER raw `asset_id_of` on the unfolded string — that is what makes the registry match the still-`crd://` live frames
before the rewrite AND the rewrite pixel-neutral.

**Gate 9 PROVEN:** device-free `RAF-9: loads by canonical id` + `on_disk_relative` unit test (tests/render-asset-core)
+ `RAF-9 GATE` pixel-exact BOTH backends (id-selected == relative-selected, diffs==0, tests/scene-render) + sandbox
smoke byte-identical both backends (shadows ON, full scene, gpu-cull/gpu-skin kernels resolve). My changed library +
test code LLVM-20 tidy-clean.

⚠️ **PRE-EXISTING, NOT RAF-9 (stash-proven):** `test_scene_render_gpu.cpp` REN-39-C1 (pull/indexed bit-identity, 
diffs≈1923) + REN-40-D (EVSM/MSM moment shadows), 4 cases / ~14 assertions, fail IDENTICALLY with the RAF-9
scene-render changes stashed → they come from the prior RAF-8 WIP baseline, not RAF-9. A separate investigation (likely
the RAF-8a scene-flip or a REN-39/40 regression). ⛔ Method that nailed it: `git stash push <the RAF-9 scene-render
files>`, rebuild, re-run — identical failures = pre-existing. Also pre-existing tidy debt: geometry-mesh-processing

<a id="memory-project_ren38_bindless_multidraw_slices"></a>
## project_ren38_bindless_multidraw_slices

---
name: project_ren38_bindless_multidraw_slices
description: "⭐⭐ REN-38 renderer-weakness campaign COMPLETE (2026-07-27): shadows+albedo COMPOSE (atlas at bindings 4/5 · t4/s5); kBindlessMax 1024 PARTIALLY_BOUND; KBuiltin::DrawIndex (pc+gl_DrawIDARB / root const b7 — ARB spelling at #version 450!); draw_storage_multi_depth (ONE indirect cmd); AND the SCENE-BUFFER CONSOLIDATION: one buffer, draw table at word 120, regions from 384, Vx::loadu rebase — two mesh groups = ONE batch, gated."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 31e31376-4d57-4a00-b30c-77365444ac88
  modified: 2026-07-28T03:07:19.144Z
---

**What landed (all gated, green on win-debug + linux-gcc-release/llvmpipe, tidy-clean at LLVM 20.1.8):**

1. **Shadows/albedo exclusivity DEAD.** The shadow atlas moved off the material-map bindings to its OWN pair —
   Vulkan set 0 bindings 4 (depth-array image) + 5 (comparison sampler), DX12 t4/s5 (root params 4/5). The
   renderer cooks a COMBINED textured+shadowed variant (`program_textured_shadowed`), `record_one_group` keeps
   `base_color` under active shadows, the executor routes item-texture + pass-depth-read to the new
   `draw_storage_textured_shadowed_depth` verb. Gate: `REN-38 GATE: a TEXTURED receiver is ALSO SHADOWED in one
   frame` asserts the CONJUNCTION (texture visible + shadow lands + texture SURVIVES shadows-on).
2. **The material heap is real.** kBindlessMax 8 → 1024 on both backends; `descriptorBindingPartiallyBound`
   enabled at device creation when offered (`VulkanGpuContext::partially_bound()`); the bindless fill sites
   write ONLY the registered slots under the feature (duplicate-fill survives as the no-feature fallback).
3. **`KBuiltin::DrawIndex`** (enum END, cook-serialized): GLSL lowers to `(pc_draw.index + uint(gl_DrawID))`
   (push block + GL_ARB_shader_draw_parameters, declared only when reachable); HLSL to `pc_draw_index`
   (cbuffer b7 = root constant, param 6). VK raster-program layouts + shader objects carry the 4-byte VERTEX
   push range unconditionally (harmless when unused).
4. **`draw_storage_multi_depth`** (vtable END): N depth-tested storage draws in ONE device command. VK: a
   host-visible indirect-args RING (32 chunks × 256 commands) + one `vkCmdDrawIndirect`; push = batch's first
   DrawIndex. DX12: `{ROOT_CONSTANT(b7), DRAW}` command signature (⛔ created AGAINST the root signature it
   patches, cached per root) + upload ring, one `ExecuteIndirect`; stride 20B. `multi_batch_count()` counts
   batches monotonically. The frame executor coalesces CONSECUTIVE plain geometry items (same program, same
   storage, no textures, no pass read) into one batch. Gate: `REN-38 GATE: multi-draw batches N draws` asserts
   BIT-IDENTICAL pixels **and** batch-count delta == 1 — pixels alone cannot distinguish batched from looped.

**5. ⭐⭐ THE SCENE-BUFFER CONSOLIDATION — LANDED (same day, user-directed).** One renderer-owned scene buffer:
words [0..119] = THE frame header (the FS reads absolutely — no FS change, no flat varying needed: every
group's header carries the same frame fields, one canonical copy serves); [120..375] = the DRAW TABLE
(`kSceneDrawTableOff`); regions from 384 (`kSceneFirstRegion`), each an exact image of the group's private
layout so region-relative header offsets keep working. The scene VS is the SAME declaration + one top-level
`rebase_table = 120` line (single source of truth); `Vx::loadu` rebases every load when `desc.rebase_table`
is set. Consolidation activates for PLAIN groups on the single-viewport owner path with shadows OFF and no
explicit frame graph (⛔ the authored CULL graph computes visibility into the PRIVATE buffers — consolidating
under it splits the frame across two buffers; that guard was found by the CULL gate, not by inspection).
`SceneDraw.rebased` → `DrawItem.indexed` → the executor records indexed items through the multi verb EVEN
ALONE (a classic verb leaves the push stale ⇒ the draw reads another region). Gate: two DISTINCT mesh groups
→ `multi_batch_count()` delta == EXACTLY 1 + both halves' pixels present.

**⛔ Scars from landing it:** (a) `gl_DrawID` is the 4.60 spelling — under `#version 450` + the ARB extension
it MUST be `gl_DrawIDARB` (shaderc silently fails the program build otherwise, and the renderer falls back to
classic draws: pixels stay right, batches read 0 — the count gate caught what pixels could not); (b) the
`shaderDrawParameters` FEATURE must be enabled at device creation (Vulkan 1.1 core struct), not just used;
(c) consolidated regions pay a per-frame FULL instance upload (sync's dirty tracking covers only the private
buffers) — the recorded cost of one-batch drawing, in the same class as the header+visible writes.

Related: [feedback_every_render_pass_through_our_own_frame_graph_machinery](rendering.md#memory-feedback_every_render_pass_through_our_own_frame_graph_machinery),
[project_frame_graph_is_a_recording_mode_of_raster_context](project-history.md#memory-project_frame_graph_is_a_recording_mode_of_raster_context) (the 6.1×/38.8× board this cashes in),
[project_obj_torus_normals_unlit_ren3](project-history.md#memory-project_obj_torus_normals_unlit_ren3) (RESOLVED same day — genus-1 torus gate).

**38-G OPENED (2026-07-28): the POST CONTEXT (G1a).** The tonemap family (`agx`, `pbr_neutral`,
`srgb_encode`, `pq_encode`, `ev100`/`exposure_scale`, `gamut_compress`, `contrast_curve`) is in the ONE node
registry under a SECOND legality context: `parse_post_toml` + `cook_post_graph` (matcook) accept it;
`cook_material` refuses it BY NAME — ⛔ ADR-0102 two-sided (the display transform is a FRAME operation).
`texcoord` legal in post (screen coordinate); surface readers refused; output = the node NAMED "output".
⭐ The design finding: `is_lighting_op` already refused tonemap/exposure in materials — the architecture
itself dictated that post is a context, not a material extension. NEXT (G1b): host `crd://post/<name>`
resolution (fullscreen VS precedent: visbuffer_fullscreen.crdv + `cook_stage_named`), authored scene→tonemap

**38-G1 CLOSED (2026-07-28):** the device half landed — host resolves `crd://post/<name>`, the authored

**38-G1 ASSETS SHIPPED (2026-07-28):** `assets/post/tonemap_agx.crdp` + `srgb_only.crdp` +

**38-G1 FULLY CLOSED, BOTH BACKENDS (2026-07-28):** ⛔⛔ the DX12 scene-family blocker was the Slice-1
atlas range: t4 sat INSIDE t3[1024] (D3D12 refuses overlapping register ranges EVEN UNUSED; VK bindings are

209/209 linux wide. F6-DX12 (TESS/MESH/VISBUFFER·CULL·RT) green FIRST TIME on this rig.

**THE LIVE-APP CAMPAIGN (2026-07-28, sandbox-driven):** running the app found what no gate did:
1. ⛔⛔ `FrameRecorder` arena never reset — frame 33 failed EVERY record forever (the freeze). Fix:

2. ⛔⛔ The expansion-index host seam MUST discriminate: `plan[ii].index` is 0 for BOTH cascade-0 and

   scene). Recorder passes 0xFFFFFFFF for non-for_each passes.

7. ⭐⭐ PER-CASCADE CULLING: per-cascade visible lists after the camera's (stride = capacity, header word

<a id="memory-project_ren39_indexed_pull_vertex_reuse"></a>
## project_ren39_indexed_pull_vertex_reuse

---
name: project-ren39-indexed-pull-vertex-reuse
description: "NEXT PERF SLICE — the frame is measured vertex-bound (non-indexed pull, zero reuse); indexed pull via storage-buffer-as-index-buffer, expected 3-6x"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 31e31376-4d57-4a00-b30c-77365444ac88
  modified: 2026-07-28T03:07:01.446Z
---

After 38-G1 closed (2026-07-28, sandbox at 119 fps / 8.4 ms on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER), the GPU frame is **vertex-bound**: per-pass board shows csm cascade3 3.27 ms + forward 3.70 ms; halving the shadow map moved cascade3 only 3.27→3.08 (not fill). Cause: the vertex-pull idiom draws NON-INDEXED (`vertex_count = visible × index_count`) — every triangle corner re-pulls and re-transforms, zero post-transform reuse, ~38 M vertex invocations/frame.

**The slice — SLICED as D-007 row 142 (39-A1/A2 device verb · 39-B1/B2 cook contract · 39-C1/C2 renderer switch + measured close):**
- Bind the group's EXISTING storage buffer as the index buffer at `indices_off` (add INDEX_BUFFER usage at creation — zero data duplication; DX12 needs an IBV + resource-state handling on a UAV-heap buffer).
- `vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect` / DX12 indexed command signature; instanceCount = visible count (per-cascade counts already ride the host draw-list seam from 38-G1).
- Cooked VS gains an `indexed` mode: vertex = pull by `gl_VertexIndex` (which IS the index value — the per-vertex index load disappears), instance slot = `visible[cascade_base + gl_InstanceIndex]` (needs an InstanceIndex builtin through CKIR → both raster emitters — the [feedback-raster-emitters-lag-compute-wire-both-and-uint-suffix](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_raster_emitters_lag_compute_wire_both_and_uint_suffix) scar).
- Expected 3–6× vertex-work cut across shadow AND forward passes. Gates: bit-identical pixels vs the pull path (same shading, different draw verb) + the multi-draw count gates.

Also watch: DX12 RT ANY-HIT gate ("…can IGNORE every hit") flaked ONCE in a sweep (1 1 -1 -1) on 2026-07-28, then green 6×; nothing in that path had changed. If it recurs it is a race, not noise.

<a id="memory-project_ren8a_flip_live_onto_render_graph"></a>
## project_ren8a_flip_live_onto_render_graph

---
name: project_ren8a_flip_live_onto_render_graph
description: RAF-8 THE FLIP is COMPLETE — every FramePassKind (forward + amplification/RT/visbuffer/composite) records through a render-graph executor, both backends; the migration-adapter pattern + command-model extensions + the pre-existing VRS/cascade caveats
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: bf0ab64f-0cb7-4b04-970c-78c4f58c02b9
  modified: 2026-08-03T21:03:09.035Z
---

RAF-8a's flip of the LIVE renderer onto crd-render-graph (ADR-0106) is UNDERWAY, first kind proven (2026-08-03).

**The migration adapter** (`engine/frame-cook/src/frame_runtime.cpp`): `record_pass` is the gpu-context frame-graph
pass callback with the resolved target `t`, `p->sampled[]`, `p->program`, `p->draws`, etc. For a MIGRATED
`FramePassKind` it calls `record_<kind>_via_executor(p, ctx, r, t)`, which builds a render-graph
`ResourceTable`+`PassPayload` from the resolved `PassRec` and invokes the registered executor `PassRecordFn`
(`m_impl->records`, a `GraphExecutorTable` built once) through `r.create_command_encoder()` (a
`TranslatingCommandEncoder`). Returns false ⇒ the inline switch runs (both resolve during migration; RAF-12 deletes
both the switch and the adapters). `PassRec` carries `rec_alloc` (scratch for the per-pass table/diags) + `records`.

**Slot mapping** (fullscreen, the template): `color`→target · `input0..7`→`ctx.texture(sampled[i])` (resolve-or-abort)
· `constants`→`ctx.buffer(fs_constants)` · params `clear_color` (always, == the inline `ClearColor{d.clear_color}`),
`shading_rate`/`conservative`/`depth_as_float` when set. ResourceRef.resource_id must == the ResolvedResource.name_hash
(use the slot-name hash for both — one resource per slot).

**Status (2026-08-03): THE ENTIRE SANDBOX FRAME IS FLIPPED — all 7 pass kinds it uses record through the executors,
each PIXEL-EXACT on Vulkan AND DX12** — `fullscreen.raster` · `transfer.{clear,copy,blit,resolve}` · `RasterGeometry`
(forward+impostor) · `RasterMrt` (velocity prepass) · `RasterDepthOnly` (shadow cascades) · `compute.dispatch` (the
GPU-cull kernels — A/B executor-vs-inline on --gpu-cull = 0 changed both backends) · present. Adapters
`record_fullscreen_via_executor` / `record_transfer_via_executor` / `record_scene_via_executor` /
`record_compute_via_executor` in `record_pass`. The compute executor walks a per-pass `DrawList` (each item: storage +
args + `dispatch_groups`, added to `RenderDrawItem`) for the cull kernels, or a single dispatch. Fixes en route:
`record_scene_raster` hardcoded LessEqual → reads `depth_compare` (reverse-Z); `pass_texture_is_depth` guarded on a
non-null atlas.

**RAF-8b DONE** — scene-render has NO specialized backend draw path: `record_one_group` (the last synchronous draw
helper, the fallback for a backend without a frame graph) is DELETED; a no-frame-graph backend is a reported
unsupported config now. Pixel-exact both backends (dead code for VK/DX12). Scene-render answers only what a graph
cannot know + drives execution.

**RAF-8 TAIL DONE (2026-08-03) — every remaining pass kind flipped to an executor.** Mesh/Tess→mesh.raster/tess.raster
(amplify executor: per-item count+program from the draw list, or procedural amplify_count); MeshIndirect→mesh.indirect;
Visbuffer→visbuffer.raster (R32_UINT id, clear_id, first-clears-rest-loads); Composite→fullscreen.raster+load+blend
(WBOIT→draw_bindless_blend_load); RayTrace→raytrace.dispatch REPURPOSED to inline ray query (DispatchDesc.accel →
dispatch_kernel_rt); RayTracePipeline→raytrace.pipeline (TraceDesc SBT; PassPrograms grew any_hit/isect/callable);
ComputeIndirect→compute.dispatch + `args` slot → dispatch_kernel_indirect. Command-model additions (DATA not verbs):
RenderingDesc.{visbuffer,clear_id}, DispatchDesc.acceleration_structure; encoder arms: Meshlet/Patches-no-buffer →
draw_mesh/draw_tess(+_load), visbuffer, bindless_blend_load, dispatch_kernel_rt. 5 new executors + records ⇒ builtins
= 14. Load bridge fully closed (all 18 FramePassKinds map; compute-indirect routes the IndirectArgs read to `args`).
Gate: DX12 [frame-graph] 32/32 · Vulkan 50/51 (the 1 fail = REN-38-A13 VRS, PRE-EXISTING Vulkan-driver quirk —
draw_vrs unchanged from HEAD, DX12 A13 passes, backend-neutral change) · render-graph-gpu 303 · tidy-clean · smoke
both backends. **The earlier one-off DX12 anyhit-RT fail was a GPU-SUITE FLAKE (passes in isolation + on rerun).**
Inline switch = fallback until RAF-12. ✅ **REN-38-A13 VRS FIXED (2026-08-04)** — NOT a driver quirk: the flip read the
Enum params `shading_rate`+`conservative` via `u32_param` → tag mismatch → fell back to Rate1x1/Off → draw_vrs never
fired. Fix = an `enum_param` reader (+ the sibling `filter` for nearest-blit). Vulkan A13 coarse=2048>fine=1024; both
backends [frame-graph] green. See [feedback_executor_enum_params_read_with_enum_param_not_u32](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_executor_enum_params_read_with_enum_param_not_u32). geometry-mesh-processing
tidy debt still blocks win-tidy of scene-render's deps.

⛔ HARNESS GOTCHA (diagnosed 2026-08-03, NOT a bug): running `crd-sandbox.exe` DIRECTLY needs
`CRD_ASSETS_DIR=D:\Dev\cerid\assets` set, or `init_programs` fails early ("scene.crdv not found",
scene_renderer.cpp:2858) → overlay-only fallback → the DOWNSTREAM symptom "REN-3.2-b cascaded shadows: unavailable
(cascade shaders failed to build)". WITH the env var set: cascade shadows ON, 5384/5379 instances, both backends —
the shipped forward path (10k instances + 4-cascade PCSS) renders correctly through the flipped executors. The smoke
SCRIPT (sandbox-rebuild-smoke.bat) sets it; running the binary by hand does not. Diagnosed by instrumenting the 7
shadow-cook failure points — all TRUE once assets resolve; the fix was the env var, never a new asset or code change.

**⭐⭐ THE CASCADE SCAR (how I found it — the debugging method matters):** the cascade flip rendered instances BLACK
(forward read all-occluded). Isolation (block one kind at a time, pixel-diff each) narrowed it to `RasterDepthOnly`;
then a per-packet LOG in `record_scene_raster` vs the inline verb showed my executor emitted ONLY the untextured
casters (the TEXTURED ones went missing). Root cause: a DEPTH-ONLY pass binds NO colour textures, but a textured
shadow caster routed down the indexed-SAMPLED (colour) arm with a null atlas. Fix: `record_scene_raster` ignores
per-item maps + the pass atlas when there is no colour attachment. **Lesson: when a flipped kind mis-renders and the
verb ARGS match, log the PACKET STREAM (count + per-item routing) vs the inline — the divergence is which ITEMS take
which arm, not the verb.** The 4 executor/bridge gaps are closed+gated (depth_as_float · compute-reads-texture ·
raster-reads-buffers · MRT-depth-prepass + depth-only-multi encoder arms). ⏭ REMAINING for RAF-8: `compute.dispatch`
(cull kernels, per-item DrawList dispatch) · amplification/RT executors · retire inline switch cases · RAF-8b
(scene-render → pure orchestration).

**How to gate a flip (MANDATORY — smoke is pixel-blind, see
[feedback_gpu_frame_graph_requires_device_command_draw_path](rendering.md#memory-feedback_gpu_frame_graph_requires_device_command_draw_path)):** deterministic screenshot
(`--screenshot --screenshot-at 2.5 --fixed-dt 16.6 --seed 1`, + `--backend dx12`) → `ImageChops.difference` vs the
pre-flip baseline == 0 pixels, BOTH backends → confirm the adapter actually ran (temp log/counter, then remove). The
executor==verb identity (RAF-7 gates) is why the packet lowers to the SAME verb — that is the parity guarantee.

<a id="memory-project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir"></a>
## project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir

---
name: project_restir_gold_sampler_ckir
description: "D-007 B14-a: ReSTIR (Bitterli 2020) reservoir/RIS estimator in CKIR (ckir_restir.hpp) — build_restir_ris (WRS) + build_restir_temporal (two-reservoir merge). SCAR: temporal reuse only drops variance when the target p̂ CORRELATES with the integrand f; p̂=const ⇒ pure uniform reservoir sampling, NO reduction. CPU+Vulkan verified."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5
---

**D-007 B14-a — ReSTIR (Spatiotemporal Reservoir Resampling, Bitterli et al. 2020), in CKIR (2026-07-15).** The dominant
real-time many-light / GI sampler. Same pattern as [project_ddgi_gold_gi_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_ddgi_gold_gi_ckir)/[project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir): the
candidate GENERATION (which light, its shaded contribution f, the shadow-ray visibility) is the deferred **B9 RT leaf**; the
reservoir / RIS / reuse ESTIMATOR is built + verified now. `engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_restir.hpp` (namespace
`crd::kir::restir`), statement-tier COMPUTE. Tests `tests/kir/test_ckir_restir.cpp` + `tests/gpu-context-vulkan`.

A reservoir = 4 floats `[f(y), p̂(y), W, M]`. **`build_restir_ris`**: stream M candidates `(f_i, p̂_i, xi_i)` through Weighted
Reservoir Sampling — keep i w.p. `w_i/Σw` (`w_i=p̂_i`), then `W = Σw/(M·p̂(y))`; the single-sample estimate of the integral is
`f(y)·W`, and E[f(y)·W]=∫f (RIS is UNBIASED). **`build_restir_temporal`**: merge cur + reprojected-prev reservoir, each
contributing its own `Σw = p̂·W·M`, prev M CLAMPED to `m_cap·M_cur` (bounds temporal bias); pick one, `W = Σw/((M_c+M_p)·p̂)`.
**`build_restir_spatial`**: the OTHER half of spatiotemporal reuse — generalise the 2-reservoir merge to K+1 (center + K screen
neighbours; buffers 0=res N·4, 1=nbr N·K indices, 2=xi N·K randoms, 3=out), streaming WRS with one random per neighbour, merged
`W = Σ(all Σw)/(Σ all M · p̂(sel))`. Same variance-drop + unbiasedness as temporal (K=4 ⇒ 5 reservoirs' candidates). Ops:
add/mul/div/max/CmpLt/select + one F32→U32 index cast ⇒ FP32-precise **bit-exact**. **▶ B14-a ReSTIR COMPLETE = RIS + temporal +
spatial.** Vulkan RIS 1.11e-7 / temporal 1.19e-7 / spatial 1.29e-7. GPU perf (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): RIS M=32 0.527 ms/262 k px
([project_atmosphere_gold_sky_ckir](project-history.md#memory-project_atmosphere_gold_sky_ckir) shares the `docs/bench/2026-07-15-gi-atmosphere-vulkan.md` board). `RestirConfig{
num_candidates=32, m_cap=20, spatial_neighbors=4}`.

**⭐⭐ PERF RULE (2026-07-15 hand-written-GLSL head-to-head, `docs/bench/2026-07-15-ckir-vs-handwritten-glsl.md`) — a
statement-tier compute loop with MANY iterations must be a RUNTIME LOOP (`stmt_for_begin` + per-thread SHARED accumulators),
NOT a compile-time C++ unroll.** The unroll emits 32× straight-line blocks with all index temps hoisted → huge register
pressure → collapsed GPU occupancy: `build_restir_ris` was **1.56× SLOWER than hand-written** (0.486 vs 0.312 ms) despite
BIT-IDENTICAL output (the tell: same math, so the loss is pure code structure). Rewriting to a tight runtime loop with the
reservoir (Σw, cf, cph) in `shared[tid]` → **0.318 ms, PARITY with the hand register loop** (1.02×), still bit-exact (Vulkan
1.11e-7). Two hazards en route: (1) `Σw = sh[tid]+phi` re-evaluated after its own store DOUBLE-COUNTS phi → `stmt_materialize(Σw)`
freezes it; (2) a value first used INSIDE the loop but also AFTER it (the output index `p`) is scoped to the loop body ⇒
undefined at the store ⇒ compile error → `stmt_materialize(p)` hoists it. **BUT the rule is workload-specific**: for a
COMPUTE-bound march (atmosphere transmittance — heavy exp/sqrt, low register pressure) the unroll's register accumulators BEAT
the shared loop (shared-loop was 1.47× slower there) → keep the unroll; its residual 1.23× vs a hand REGISTER loop is the
compute-emitter's lack of register-carried loop values (`for_loop`/`LoopAcc` is fragment-emitter-only) — a scoped engine gap on
a negligible once-per-frame LUT. Heuristic: memory/occupancy-bound big loop → runtime shared loop; compute-bound → unroll.

**⛔ SCAR — ReSTIR temporal reuse reduces variance ONLY when the target p̂ CORRELATES with the integrand f.** My first
variance-drop test used a CONSTANT target `p̂=1` (the same one that correctly proves RIS unbiasedness) and it FAILED: with p̂
constant, RIS degenerates to uniform reservoir sampling — the reservoir holds exactly ONE uniformly-picked sample with W=1, and
merging two reservoirs just picks one of two single samples ⇒ `var` stays flat no matter how many frames accumulate. The fix is
the CANONICAL ReSTIR target `p̂=f` (in practice the unshadowed contribution): then the RIS estimate `f(y)·W = Σf/M` is the
candidate MEAN, and temporal merge accumulates the stream so the estimate is the running mean over M_eff samples ⇒ `var ~
Var(f)/M_eff` drops as M_eff grows. Lesson: a constant/useless target is the right stress for UNBIASEDNESS but the WRONG setup
for VARIANCE — the whole point of ReSTIR (importance-concentrating the kept sample) needs a target that tracks f.

Verified: CPU oracle — RIS unbiased (pixel-mean of f(y)·W == truth under imperfect p̂=1, var>0) + temporal reuse var ≥2× lower
(p̂=f, over 12 frames M_eff 32→416) while staying unbiased + M grew. **Vulkan RIS 1.11e-7, temporal 1.19e-7 == oracle.**
crd-kir 28959/142 + vulkan [restir] green MSVC + clang-cl; tidy-clean. Scope onward (all ride B9 RT): ReSTIR DI (direct) →
ReSTIR GI (Ouyang 2021, indirect) → ReSTIR PT / GRIS (Lin 2022, path reuse) + spatial neighbour reuse. **NEXT: B15 sky/atmosphere.**

<a id="memory-project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context"></a>
## project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context

---
name: project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context
description: "⛔ ADR-0105 (2026-07-23): crd-rhi + crd-renderer are FROZEN and being RETIRED (D-007 RET band rows 89-96) — never add features/consumers to them; gpu-context IS the graphics layer. (Historical: rhi adopts gpu-context's VkDevice, D-008 C2-f.)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9b330af5-88bb-499e-a92a-1752e160e0ba
---

**⛔ ADR-0105 (2026-07-23) — RETIREMENT DECIDED, user-directed ("squeaky clean, ASAP").** `crd-rhi` + `crd-rhi-vulkan`
+ `crd-renderer` are **FROZEN**: never add a feature or a new consumer to them (the GEO-3-2b sRGB double-wiring was the
last straw). The **D-007 RET band (rows 89-96)** absorbs every remaining capability into gpu-context (present/swapchain
· cooked-mip+sRGB texture seam · ADR-0085 allocator parity · ImGui · crd-draw port · bvh-gpu Morton compute · shader/
meshgen sweep), PORTS the ~5k device-level test asserts (parity = deletion PREcondition), then **DELETES all three
modules + their test dirs**. CPU-side resource types (TextureResource/MeshResource) re-home GPU-free in crd-resources.
Sequencing: GEO-3 close → RET complete → GEO-4..7 integrate once on the clean stack. Everything below is the
historical adopted-device record (still accurate until RET-8 deletes the modules).

**D-008 CONVERGENCE CLOSED (2026-07-11).** There is ONE `VkInstance`/`VkPhysicalDevice`/`VkDevice` — the
`VulkanGpuContext` owns it. `rhi-vulkan` **adopts** it and never creates its own: `crd::rhi::create_vulkan_device_adopting(crd::gpu::IGpuContext&)`
returns a `VulkanDevice` with `owns_device=false`. **`Instance::create_device` and `VulkanInstance`'s ~150-line
VkDevice-creation path were DELETED** — do NOT re-add them. `crd::rhi::Instance` now enumerates adapters only.

**How to apply:**
- Need a device (prod or test)? `create_vulkan_gpu_context({headless, enable_validation})` then
  `create_vulkan_device_adopting(*ctx)`. The context MUST outlive the device (it's borrowed). In tests, use the
  `AdoptedGpu` holder (ctx declared before device). Windowed = `headless=false` (swapchain surface still comes from the
  window handle at `create_swapchain` time, as the sandbox does).
- To attach to the adopted device's VkInstance (ValidationCapture, ImGui): go through the DEVICE, not an rhi Instance —
  `ValidationCapture(Device&)` / `crd::rhi::vulkan_instance(Device&)`. There is no rhi Instance on the adopted path.
- The gpu-context detects a dedicated compute family (`COMPUTE && !GRAPHICS`) exactly like rhi's old path, so
  `has_dedicated_compute_queue()` / `compute_queue()` identity semantics are preserved. `AsyncComputePolicy::RequireDedicated`
  is NOT expressible on the adopted path (no `DeviceDesc`) — no consumer needed it.

Both ADR-0103 invariants are closed: I1 (no shading language outside a backend) + I2 (no bytecode in a public header).
See [project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program](project-history.md#memory-project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program), [project_compute_rendering_separation](project-history.md#memory-project_compute_rendering_separation),
[feedback_reflect_needs_unoptimized_spirv_and_compiler_injection](build-and-verification.md#memory-feedback_reflect_needs_unoptimized_spirv_and_compiler_injection). Frontier device contexts still ahead: D-008 C3
(`IRayTracingContext`), C4 (DX12 raster), C5 (work graphs).


<!-- end-memory:project_rhi_device_is_adopted_from_gpu_context -->

<a id="memory-project_serial_iterative_qr_loses_to_dc_reduction_is_bottleneck"></a>
## project_serial_iterative_qr_loses_to_dc_reduction_is_bottleneck

---
name: project_serial_iterative_qr_loses_to_dc_reduction_is_bottleneck
description: "For dense eig/SVD, a faithful SERIAL iterative-QR (steqr/dbdsqr/MRRR-vectors) loses to BLAS-3 D&C at scale; and the visible gap to LAPACK is usually the UNBLOCKED reduction (dsytrd/dgebrd), not the QR sweep"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1b01fdee-d8a1-4b9c-8107-e8701a5237ce
---

When porting a dense eigen/SVD path, TWO measured patterns now repeat — design the
next leaf around them instead of expecting the serial QR to win:

1. **Serial implicit-QR (O(n³), big scalar constant) loses to BLAS-3 D&C at scale.**
   - MRRR vectors: serial lost 0.21× `dstedc`; even LAPACK's own `dstemr` loses to its
     `dstedc` for all-vectors. Crush came only from PARALLELISM (independent eigenvectors
     × cores). ([project_mrrr_perf_win_is_vectors_not_values](project-history.md#memory-project_mrrr_perf_win_is_vectors_not_values))
   - dbdsqr (v3b-1b SVD): beats Eigen JacobiSVD 3–15×, but C/BDC 0.14, C/dgesdd 0.13 @
     N=512. D&C (`dbdsdc`/BDCSVD) is ~7× faster than serial dbdsqr at N=512.

2. **The visible gap to LAPACK at scale is the UNBLOCKED reduction, not the QR sweep.**
   Smoking gun (v3b-1b): `svdvals` @ N=512 = **156 ms vs `dgesvd`-N 46 ms**, yet `dlasq2`
   (the values engine) is O(n²) and proven ~free (it tied `dstemr` in v3a-3.1). So the
   156 ms is the **unblocked `dgebd2` bidiagonalization (BLAS-2)** vs LAPACK's blocked
   `dgebrd` (BLAS-3). Confirmed in reverse by v3a-1: blocked `dsytrd` is what made
   `eig_sym` BEAT LAPACK; the QR sweep itself is comparable.

**Why:** D&C replaces O(n³) scalar recurrence with O(n³) BLAS-3 (tiny constant) or O(n²)
+ merges. Blocked reduction replaces BLAS-2 rank-1/rank-2 updates with one trailing
BLAS-3 `gemm` per panel. Both are the standard LAPACK levers.

**How to apply:** (a) ship the faithful serial QR as the proven baseline + a 4-column
bench (Eigen easy+D&C AND LAPACK direct+D&C) that MEASURES the gap — never architect the
D&C/parallel leaf on a guess (predictions were wrong both ways in v3a). (b) Prioritise the
**blocked reduction** (dlabrd/dgebrd for SVD; already done for dsytrd) — it's often the
LARGER lever than parallelising the QR sweep, and it helps the values-only path too.
(c) The crush leaf = D&C (Gu-Eisenstat) and/or parallelism, measured vs the serial
baseline. Applies to the next iterative-QR slices: QR-shift general eig, real Schur.
([feedback_always_bench_both_eigen_and_lapack](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_always_bench_both_eigen_and_lapack), [feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_reference_implementations_are_the_floor))


<!-- end-memory:project_serial_iterative_qr_loses_to_dc_reduction_is_bottleneck -->

<a id="memory-project_shader_entry_point_normalize_to_main"></a>
## project_shader_entry_point_normalize_to_main

---
name: project_shader_entry_point_normalize_to_main
description: Compute entry-point convention splits GLSL=main vs HLSL/WGSL/DX12=cs_main; normalize the Vulkan SPIR-V entry to main at the compiler
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9b330af5-88bb-499e-a92a-1752e160e0ba
---

Cerid's shader emitters use TWO compute entry-point names: the GLSL emitter emits `void main()`, but the
HLSL/WGSL emitters and the DX12/kir-dx12 backends use `cs_main` (`-E cs_main`) — the established cross-backend
convention (~35 sites in `ckir_hlsl.hpp`/`ckir_wgsl.hpp` + the dx12 backends). Do NOT try to unify all of them
on `main`; that perturbs DX12/WGSL and is out of scope for any Vulkan-side work.

**The seam rule (D-008 C2-d4, 2026-07-11):** every OPAQUE `IGpuProgram` a consumer holds must entry-point at a
CANONICAL name so pipelines need no source function name. Achieve this on the **Vulkan** side by passing DXC
`-fspv-entrypoint-name=main` in `vulkan_hlsl_compile.cpp` — it renames the SPIR-V `OpEntryPoint` to `main`
regardless of the HLSL function name (`cs_main`). GLSL already yields `main`. So every Vulkan program we mint
entry-points at `main`, and `rhi-vulkan`'s compute/graphics pipelines hardcode `pName = "main"`.

**Why:** the old `ShaderModule` carried an entry-point string; retiring it (I2 closure) dropped that channel.
Normalizing at the compiler is cleaner than threading an entry name through `create_program`. **How to apply:**
if a future backend (Metal/HIP) grows a Vulkan-style cooked path, normalize its entry to `main` at the vendor
compiler too — don't add an entry-name parameter to the program seam. See [project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program](project-history.md#memory-project_gpu_context_owns_every_gpu_program),
[project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor](project-history.md#memory-project_central_shader_ir_and_node_editor), [feedback_glsl_writeonly_buffer_readback_portability](device-programs.md#memory-feedback_glsl_writeonly_buffer_readback_portability).


<!-- end-memory:project_shader_entry_point_normalize_to_main -->

**Phase 3.1.7 v7h Taubin smoothing (Taubin 1995) ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-17** — `engine/geometry-mesh-processing/`'s 8th and FINAL algorithm slice (v7-close = wrap only). New `taubin_smooth(const HalfEdgeMesh<T>&, opts) -> HalfEdgeMesh<T>` — input untouched. **Algorithm**: volume-preserving 2-pass Laplacian. Per iteration pair: Pass 1 shrink `v ← v + λ·L(v)` with `L(v) = mean(neighbours) - v` (uniform-weight umbrella operator, D71); Pass 2 un-shrink `v ← v + μ·L(v)` with μ < 0. Frequency-domain LOW-PASS: high frequencies (noise) damped, low frequencies (shape) preserved. Default (λ=0.5, μ=-0.53) targets Taubin's wide-pass-band filter (k_PB ≈ 0.113); narrow-band alternative (λ=0.6307, μ=-0.6732) ships via opts. **Boundary handling** (D70): `keep_boundary_fixed = true` default clamps boundary vertices; false smooths them using ONLY boundary 1-ring neighbours (matches v7c cubic-B-spline-mask intent with Taubin λ/μ alternation). **Boundary flag cached ONCE** at entry (D68 — Taubin doesn't change topology). **Jacobi-style atomic update per pass** (D69): compute new positions against OLD into scratch array, apply atomically via `set_vertex_position` (added in v7d). Clone-and-mutate pattern (D67) — same as v7d/e/g. **InvalidParameters** check (D72): reject `λ ≤ 0` (must be positive shrink) and `μ ≥ 0` (must be negative un-shrink); does NOT enforce `|μ| > λ` (caller may want high-pass/experimental filters). ---

**Phase 3.1.7 v7g self-intersection removal ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-17** — `engine/geometry-mesh-processing/`'s 7th algorithm. New `remove_self_intersections(const HalfEdgeMesh<T>&, opts) -> HalfEdgeMesh<T>` — input untouched. **Algorithm 3 phases**: (1) **Broadphase** = brute-force O(n²) AABB-overlap + share-vertex filter (D60 — phase-doc-mentioned BVH broadphase deferred to v7g-followon optimization since static BvhTree doesn't expose `find_overlapping_pairs`, only DynamicBvh does). (2) **Narrowphase** = Möller 1997 triangle-triangle intersection test gated by exact-sign `crd::geometry::primitives::orient3d` (Shewchuk adaptive, FP-roundoff-immune; D61); **touch-only cases explicitly rejected** — ≥ 1 orient3d sign zero + the rest same non-zero sign → vertex-on-plane (single point, not transversal cut); ≥ 2 sign zeros → edge-on-plane (coplanar edge case); both defer to v7f manifoldness repair. (3) **Per-triangle CDT retriangulation**: drop-largest-normal-axis 2D projection + flip-winding-if-normal-negative (D63 — maximally orthogonal projection, CCW preservation matches CDT input expectation); epsilon-dedup at `opts.dedup_epsilon` default 1e-6 for 3+ triangle-common-edge case (D64); build CDT input (T boundary edges + intersection segments as constraints); call `crd::geometry::polygon::constrained_delaunay`; centroid-inside-T sanity filter on output sub-triangles (D66 — strips CDT super-triangle artifacts via barycentric in/out test); lift back to 3D via plane equation. **Cross-triangle vertex stitching** (D62): each intersection event creates 2 endpoint vertices ONCE (append to global pool), stores same indices in BOTH T_i and T_j's segment lists → independent CDT calls reference same global vertices → output 2-manifold along cut. **Graceful CDT-failure degradation** (D65): on `ConstraintsCrossing` (or other non-Ok), keep T's original tessellation and increment `triangles_skipped_cdt_failure` — better than emitting garbage. **Phase 3.1.7 v7f manifoldness repair ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-17** — `engine/geometry-mesh-processing/`'s 6th algorithm. New `repair_manifoldness(const HalfEdgeMesh<T>&, opts) -> HalfEdgeMesh<T>` — input untouched. **Phase A — non-manifold edge repair (D52-D54)**: detect at INDEX LEVEL via `crd::containers::HashMap<u64, Array<u32>>` keyed on packed `(min(u,v), max(u,v))` u64; for each edge with > 2 incident HEs, pair by orientation (forwards: origin < dest; backwards: origin > dest); first pair keeps original endpoints; subsequent pairs share a single duplicated `min(u,v)` vertex (both triangles in the pair share the new manifold edge); singletons (orientation imbalance — odd extras) get individual duplicated endpoints (become boundary edges in output). `replace_vertex_in_triangle` scans the 3 corners of the target triangle and updates the matching one. **Phase B — bowtie vertex repair (D55-D57)**: build a TEMP HalfEdgeMesh from the (possibly Phase-A-repaired) indices; for each alive vertex, run v7a CW fan-walk to get walk_count, scan all alive HEs for slot_count; if walk_count != slot_count → bowtie. Collect all triangles incident to `v` via linear index scan; build triangle-share-edge-through-v adjacency (two triangles adjacent at v iff they share another vertex); union-find / BFS gives fans; lowest-min-triangle-id fan keeps `v`, each other fan gets duplicated vertex. **Phase A → Phase B sequence** (D58 — Phase B requires manifold-edge precondition). **Two phases CAN CASCADE**: Phase A's vertex duplication for a non-manifold edge can DISCONNECT the previously-connected fan at the OTHER shared endpoint → Phase B then detects that bowtie and adds another duplicate (tests explicitly verify this with phase-A-only vs full-A+B counts on 3-tri and 4-tri non-manifold-edge cases). Reports `Ok` / `EmptyMesh` / `AlreadyManifold` (D59 — set when neither phase detected anything) + telemetry (`non_manifold_edges_detected`, `non_manifold_edges_repaired`, `bowtie_vertices_detected`, `bowtie_vertices_repaired`, `duplicated_vertices_added`, `output_vertices`, `output_faces`). Two-layer typing per ADR-0078 §5 D34: raw `<MathScalar T>` body; explicit `f32` + `f64` instantiations. **9 Catch2 cases**: empty / closed-cube-AlreadyManifold / 3-tri-shared-edge (verified Phase-A-only count = 1 + full A+B cascade count = 2 + output is_manifold + verify rebuild) / 4-tri-shared-edge-paired (same cascade pattern) / 2-disjoint-tetra-fans-bowtie (1 duplicate, output is_manifold) / phase-A-toggle-off / phase-B-toggle-off / determinism / f64. Mesh-processing suite total **67 cases / 1065 assertions**. **4-config DoD PASS first try** (`scripts/per-slice-check.ps1`, elapsed 03:45). **Test expectation bug found mid-pass**: initial assertions expected only Phase-A counts but full repair triggers Phase B cascade (Phase A's vertex duplication breaks a previously-connected fan structure at the OTHER edge endpoint); updated tests to verify both phases explicitly. **HashMap iteration nuance**: `crd::containers::HashMap` iterator yields const `value()` only — to mutate during iteration, collect keys first via const-iter, then re-look-up via non-const `find` for mutation. Used this pattern in both Phase A's edge-group processing and considered for Phase B fan grouping (which uses parallel Arrays instead). **Phase 3.1.7 v7e Liepa hole filling (Liepa 2003) — initial v7e SHIPPED 2026-05-17** (then re-opened same-session as v7e-refine — see top of file for full pipeline ship details) — `engine/geometry-mesh-processing/`'s 5th algorithm (after v7a substrate + v7b QEM + v7c Loop + v7d remesh). New `fill_holes(const HalfEdgeMesh<T>&, opts) -> HalfEdgeMesh<T>` — input untouched. **Algorithm**: (1) **boundary loop detection** walks all alive boundary HEs in slot order, groups via `.next` traversal until start HE re-occurs; visited bitmap prevents double-processing (D39); loops with < 3 vertices skipped. (2) **Per-loop outside-mesh face normal precomputation** (D40): for each loop edge `(b_i, b_{i+1})`, find the boundary HE going `b_i → b_{i+1}` via walking `b_i`'s outgoings, take its twin's face, compute the triangle normal CCW. (3) **Liepa O(N³) DP min-weight triangulation** (D41) with `ω(T) = area(T) + λ · sum_of_dihedral_penalties_over_T's_edges`; recurrence `W[i, k] = min_m { W[i, m] + W[m, k] + ω(T_{i, m, k}) }`; for each candidate triangle T's known edges, dihedral resolved either against precomputed outside-mesh normal (if loop boundary edge `m == i+1` or `k == m+1`) or against the PHANTOM-EDGE TRIANGLE of the relevant sub-DP `T_{i, O[i, m], m}` (if interior patch edge — needs O[i, m] for lookup); the phantom-edge dihedral on edge `(b_i, b_k)` is DEFERRED at sub-DP — resolved at parent merge or against closing-edge outside normal at top-level `W[0, N-1]` (D42); every patch edge contributes exactly once to final weight. (4) **Recursive triangulation reconstruction** from optimal-split table O[i, k]. (5) **Patch attachment via to_indexed → append patch indices → build_from** single rebuild (D45) — avoids needing per-loop atomic edits on HalfEdgeMesh. **Patch triangle vertex order** `(b_i, b_m, b_k)` with `i < m < k` is CCW from OUTSIDE the surrounding mesh (D44) — outward normals consistent with rest of mesh (verified via **signed-volume divergence-theorem check** on filled cubes: `Σ (1/6) v0 · (v1 × v2) > 0` ⇒ correct outward orientation). **Determinism** via lex-tiebreak on smaller split index `m` (D43) — byte-identical optimal split across compilers given byte-identical input. Reports `Ok` / `EmptyMesh` / `NonManifoldInput` / `NoHolesToFill` + telemetry (`holes_detected`, `holes_filled`, `holes_skipped_too_large` for loops > `max_hole_size` [default 256 = comfortable on every realistic hole], `triangles_added`, `output_vertices`, `output_faces`). Two-layer typing per ADR-0078 §5 D34: raw `<MathScalar T>` body; explicit instantiations for `f32` + `f64`. **9 Catch2 cases**: empty mesh / no-holes (closed cube) / 3-vertex-hole (cube-minus-1-triangle, 1 patch tri, closed, positive volume) / 4-vertex-hole (cube-minus-1-face, 2 patch tris) / 2-separate-holes (cube-minus-2-opposite-faces) / `max_hole_size = 3` guard (skips 4-vertex hole) / determinism / f64 (cube-minus-right-face) / signed-volume orientation. Mesh-processing suite total **55 cases / 990 assertions**. **One MSVC `C4267 (size_t → u32)` build error fixed mid-pass** with explicit `crd::u32` cast on `report.triangles_added += patch_idx.size() / 3U`. **Liepa §4 Steiner-point REFINEMENT + §5 high-order FAIRING DEFERRED** (D46) — `fairing_iterations` option API surface reserved (no-op in v7e — without Steiner points, no patch-INTERIOR vertices exist to fair); ships in v7-close or follow-on. Pure DP triangulation is the minimal correct closure for the scanner-data cleanup consumer path; this matches the phase doc scope. **4-config DoD PASS first try** (`scripts/per-slice-check.ps1`, elapsed 03:41): win-debug + win-asan + win-shipping + win-tidy. Pinned design decisions D39-D46 carried for ADR-0076 §22 amendment at v7-close. Session log `docs/sessions/2026-05-17-geometry-v7e-fill-holes.md`. **🎯 Next = v7f manifoldness repair** (detect + fix (a) non-manifold edges with >2 incident faces — split edge into one copy per face pair, reconnect twins, isolate component; (b) non-manifold "bowtie" vertices — two surface fans meeting at one vertex — detect via one-ring walk that fails to close, duplicate the vertex per fan; consumes v7a's `BuildStatus::NonManifoldEdge` partial-build flag).

**Phase 3.1.7 v7d Isotropic remeshing (Botsch-Kobbelt 2004) ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-17** — `engine/geometry-mesh-processing/`'s 4th algorithm (after v7a substrate + v7b QEM + v7c Loop). New `isotropic_remesh(const HalfEdgeMesh<T>&, opts) -> HalfEdgeMesh<T>` — input untouched. **4-pass-per-iteration loop**: (1) **split** edges > `(4/3)·L` at midpoint via v7a's `split_edge`; (2) **collapse** edges < `(4/5)·L` gated by link condition (HalfEdgeMesh internal) + **post-collapse safety pre-check** (no resulting edge to merged-vertex neighbours may exceed `(4/3)·L`, prevents oscillation); (3) **flip** interior edges toward target valence (6 interior / 4 boundary), gated by **(a)** total-deviation reduction AND **(b)** `vertices_connected(c, d)` duplicate-edge pre-check — v7a's `flip_edge` doesn't gate on c-d-already-connected (would create non-manifold); (4) **tangential smoothing** (Botsch-Kobbelt §4 actual spec, not naïve "move-to-centroid"): displacement decomposed via area-weighted vertex normal `n`, only tangential component `d_t = d - (d·n)·n` applied, then projected back to ORIGINAL input surface via f32 BVH `mesh_closest_point` query (precision-cast at boundary for f64). **Inversion-rejection safeguard** (Hoppe-style): if move would flip any incident face's `dot(n_old, n_new) ≤ 0`, keep v fixed. **Per-pass canonical-HE snapshot** discipline (Botsch-Kobbelt iteration order: new HEs created within pass NOT re-processed). Jacobi-style smoothing (all positions computed against OLD, applied atomically) via new `HalfEdgeMesh::set_vertex_position` setter (added in this slice). Multi-iteration via `n_iterations` option; `n_iterations = 0` returns clone-of-input. **Module deps EXTENDED**: `crd-geometry-mesh-processing` now PUBLIC-links `crd-geometry-bvh` + `crd-geometry-mesh` for `TriangleMeshBvh` + `mesh_closest_point`. Reports `Ok` / `EmptyMesh` / `NonManifoldInput` / `InvalidTargetLength` + telemetry (`splits_applied`, `collapses_applied`, `flips_applied`, `vertices_smoothed`, `output_vertices`, `output_faces`). Two-layer typing per ADR-0078 §5 D34: raw `<MathScalar T>` body; explicit instantiations for `f32` + `f64`. **9 Catch2 cases**: empty mesh, invalid target length, n_iterations=0 clone, subdivided cube refines (target < mean), subdivided cube coarsens (target > mean), open quad boundary held fixed (corner positions + boundary loop preserved), determinism (same input → byte-identical stats), surface projection keeps cube vertices in `[0,1]^3`, f64 precision. Mesh-processing suite total **47 cases / 925 assertions**. **2 mid-slice bugs found by bisection** (manifold-fail at iter 3 of cube-refines): (a) v7a's `flip_edge` doesn't gate on duplicate-edge case → added D36; (b) naïve Laplacian smoothing + BVH projection accumulates degeneracy across iterations → upgraded to true tangential smoothing (D37) + inversion-rejection (D38). Bisection path: disable projection PASSES → disable smoothing PASSES → root-cause both. **First DoD attempt failed at win-tidy** with transient `bugprone-reserved-identifier` clang-tidy access violation (upstream LLVM bug, same class as MSVC LTCG ICE per `feedback_transient_msvc_ltcg_ice_accept.md`); **new `feedback_transient_clang_tidy_crash.md` policy filed**; retry PASS elapsed 03:13. **Phase 3.1.7 v7c Loop subdivision (Loop 1987) ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-17** — `engine/geometry-mesh-processing/`'s 3rd algorithm (after v7a substrate + v7b QEM). New `loop_subdivide(const HalfEdgeMesh<T>&, opts) -> HalfEdgeMesh<T>` — input untouched; returns fresh subdivided mesh on requested allocator. **Indexed-form pipeline** per level (`to_indexed → tmp build_from → emit new positions+indices → repeat`; final `build_from` creates output) avoids HalfEdgeMesh move-semantics questions. **Interior edge midpoint mask** = `3/8·A + 3/8·B + 1/8·C + 1/8·D` (Loop 1987 §2.2; C, D = apex of incident faces via `he_prev(h).origin` and `he_prev(twin).origin`). **Boundary edge midpoint mask** = `(A + B)/2` (cubic-B-spline limit). **Interior vertex update mask** = `(1 - n·β)·V + β·Σ neighbours` with `β = (1/n)·(5/8 - (3/8 + 1/4·cos(2π/n))²)` — uses **`crd::math::deterministic::cos`** (Cephes-style polynomial: bit-identical FP across MSVC/clang-cl/GCC/x64/ARM64 per ADR-0063). **Boundary vertex update mask** = `3/4·V + 1/8·u_left + 1/8·u_right` (cubic-B-spline boundary curve refinement). **Sub-triangle CCW emission** (4 per face): corner@v₀ (v₀, m₀₁, m₂₀), corner@v₁ (v₁, m₁₂, m₀₁), corner@v₂ (v₂, m₂₀, m₁₂), central (m₀₁, m₁₂, m₂₀) — orientation propagates. **Vertex numbering** = [n_old old vertices in slot order with UPDATED positions] ++ [n_edges new midpoint vertices in canonical-HE-id order]. Canonical HE = min(h, h.twin) per undirected edge. **Boundary-neighbour detection** = v7a's CW fan walk: for each outgoing HE at v, edge `(v, dest)` is boundary iff `he_is_boundary(ho) OR he_is_boundary(twin(ho))` — guarantees exactly 2 hits for 2-manifold boundary vertex. **Multi-level** via `n_levels` option; `n_levels = 0` returns fresh clone-of-input (via `to_indexed → build_from` on requested allocator). Reports `Ok` / `EmptyMesh` / `NonManifoldInput` + telemetry (`levels_applied`, `output_vertices`, `output_faces`). Two-layer typing per ADR-0078 §5 D34: raw `<MathScalar T>` body; explicit instantiations for `f32` + `f64`. **9 Catch2 cases**: cube L=1 (V=26, F=48, E=72, χ=2 sphere-preserved + closed-manifold), cube L=2 (V=98, F=192, E=288, χ=2), open quad L=1 (V=9, F=8, E=16, χ=1 disk, **boundary-loop-count=1 preserved** — each old boundary edge splits 1→2, loop topology preserved), boundary midpoint = geometric-midpoint invariant, determinism (byte-identical positions across two runs), cube-corner-inward smoothing assert (corner pulled toward centroid but not past), f64 precision tier, `EmptyMesh` diagnostic, `n_levels=0` no-op.
