**Phase 3.1.7 Geometry v4-validate ✅ shipped 2026-05-16** — `validate_triangle_mesh(view, alloc, opts) -> MeshValidationReport{defects, triangle_count, vertex_count, non_manifold/boundary/manifold edge counts, well_formed, watertight}`. Six defect kinds covered by `MeshDefectKind` enum: OutOfBoundsIndex (a=tri, b=bad vertex), DegenerateTriangle (a=tri), ZeroAreaTriangle (a=tri), NonManifoldEdge (a=v_lo, b=v_hi), BoundaryEdge (a=v_lo, b=v_hi), InconsistentOrientation (a=tri, b=tri). Three-pass deterministic algorithm: pass 1 = triangle-level walk (bounds + degenerate + area-zero via `|e1×e2|² vs (2·ε)²` squared-comparison drops sqrt); pass 2 = build sorted edge table with canonical `(min(v_lo,v_hi), max(...))` keys + original `dir` preserved (0=lo→hi, 1=hi→lo); pass 3 = run-length classify by count (1=boundary, 2=manifold with `dir` comparison flagging InconsistentOrientation when both same direction, ≥3=non-manifold). `well_formed` excludes critical defects (OutOfBounds/Degenerate/NonManifold/InconsistentOrientation); zero-area + boundary are authoring smells not critical. `watertight = well_formed && boundary_edge_count == 0 && triangle_count > 0` (empty mesh is well-formed but not watertight — not a closed surface). **`MeshValidationOptions::area_epsilon: Area32` at the options surface; raw `f32` inside the algorithm per ADR-0078 §5 D34 — typed boundary, raw inner loop.** Sorted-edge classification chosen over hashmap for cross-compiler determinism (hashmap bucket order non-portable). `MeshValidationOptions` toggles `check_edges` (skip O(E log E) pass 2/3) + `check_orientation` + `report_boundary_edges` for cooker / debug-runtime cases. Use cases: cooker pipeline gate (reject ill-formed meshes from cooked artifacts), editor mesh-import diagnostics, optional runtime gate before TriangleMeshCollider construction. 10 cases / 46 assertions in `tests/geometry-mesh/test_mesh_validate.cpp` (one case per defect kind + toggle-cases + determinism roundtrip); 5-config DoD green (win-debug 1952/1952, win-asan 1952/1952, win-shipping 1865/1865, win-shipping-profile 1947/1947, win-tidy clean); full project ctest 1942 → 1952. Session log `docs/sessions/2026-05-16-geometry-v4-validate.md`.

**Phase 3.1.7 Geometry v4d ✅ shipped 2026-05-16** — `mesh_raycast_simd(view, bvh, ray, tmax, cull_back)` AVX2 8-wide Möller-Trumbore at BVH leaves, alongside v4b Woop as the watertight reference. Same BVH traversal (Williams/Ize precomputed slab + ordered nearer-first descent + best_t pruning), differs only at the leaf inner loop: chunk leaf's triangles into groups of ≤8 + gather AoS Vec3f vertex positions + transpose into 9 × Vec8f SoA registers (v0x/y/z, v1x/y/z, v2x/y/z) + SIMD MT pipeline (edge1, edge2, pvec=rd×e2, det=e1·p, inv_det, tvec=ro-v0, u=(tv·p)·inv_det, qvec=tv×e1, v=(rd·q)·inv_det, t=(e2·q)·inv_det) → 4 Vec8f result (det, u, v, t) + scalar lane scan applies masking decisions (cull_back / |det|>ε=1e-7 / 0≤u≤1 / 0≤v / u+v≤1 / 0≤t≤best_t) with lowest-tri-index tiebreak. **Lesson learned mid-implementation**: first-draft SIMD-mask AND via `min(mask_gt, mask_lt)` is implementation-defined for NaN-encoded `_CMP_*` result registers — silently lost the cull bit; switched to scalar lane scan after SIMD ALU (8 cheap branches vs the SIMD ALU work). MT-vs-Woop precision divergence on tessellated curved-surface near-edge rays: bounded cross-validation against v4b on 36-ray sphere corpus tolerates ≤6 divergent triangle-picks. Pad-replicate last valid tri for partial chunks (lane scan ignores via lane<valid_count; deterministic; no NaN-poisoning). 7 cases / 15 assertions in `tests/geometry-mesh/test_mesh_raycast_simd.cpp`; 5-config DoD green (win-debug 1942/1942, win-asan 1942/1942, win-shipping 1855/1855, win-shipping-profile 1937/1937, win-tidy clean); full project ctest 1935 → 1942. v4d-fast follow-on (per-leaf SoA repack at BVH build time, saves gather/transpose cost) deferred until benchmarks justify. Session log `docs/sessions/2026-05-16-geometry-v4d-mesh-raycast-simd.md`.

**Phase 3.1.7 Geometry v4c ✅ shipped 2026-05-16** — generalised winding number for robust inside/outside on non-watertight meshes via Jacobson, Kavan, Sorkine-Hornung 2013 + Van Oosterom-Strackee 1983 per-triangle solid angle. `mesh_winding_number(view, query) -> f32` direct O(N) summation `Σ 2·atan2(a·(b×c), |a||b||c| + (a·b)|c| + (b·c)|a| + (c·a)|b|) / 4π` + convenience `mesh_is_inside(view, query, threshold=0.5)`. Degenerate handling: p-coincident-with-vertex short-circuits that triangle's contribution to 0 (surrounding faces accumulate the local solid angle); zero-area triangle contributes 0. **Jacobson robustness verified** via "+X face removed" 10-triangle open cube test: interior point still returns w≈5/6≈0.833 (lost +X face's 4π/6 sr contribution), above 0.5 threshold → still classified inside. Typed wrapper signature `mesh_winding_number(TriangleMeshViewT<D, T>, ConstSpan<Vec3<T>> raw_verts, Vec3<Quantity<D, T>> query) -> f32` (return dimensionless — winding is rotations/4π, no Quantity wrap on return). 8 cases / **281 assertions** in `tests/geometry-mesh/test_mesh_winding_number.cpp` including translation-invariance + 125-point interior cube spray + Jacobson robustness verification; 5-config DoD green (win-debug 1935/1935, win-asan 1935/1935, win-shipping 1848/1848, win-shipping-profile 1930/1930, win-tidy clean); full project ctest 1927 → 1935. Determinism caveat documented: atan2/sqrt libm drift 1-2 ULP per contribution; 0.5 threshold absorbs it. **v4c-fast (Jacobson §4 hierarchical treecode with per-BVH-node dipole moments)** deferred until a real consumer (eylem volumetric inside-checks at scale; editor "fill" tool over millions of triangles). Session log `docs/sessions/2026-05-16-geometry-v4c-mesh-winding-number.md`.

**Phase 3.1.7 Geometry v4b ✅ shipped 2026-05-16** — `mesh_raycast(view, bvh, ray, tmax, cull_back) -> MeshRayHit{t, MeshHitPayload{tri, bary}}` via Woop 2013 watertight ray-tri (`crd-geometry-primitives::intersect_ray_triangle_watertight` with `precompute_ray_tri` shear) at BVH leaves + Williams/Ize `intersect_ray_aabb_robust` slab traversal at interior nodes + ordered nearer-first descent (far-pushed-first so near-popped-first tightens best_t before far subtree) + lowest-triangle-index tiebreak on equal t per ADR-0076 §4 pin #11. **Switched from planned Möller-Trumbore to Woop** after probing v0f corpus — watertight contract eliminates edge-leak failure mode, exact-zero edge predicates promote to double, bit-exact across f32/f64 rays. Typed `Ray3T<D,T>` + `MeshRayHitT<D,T>` wrappers in `mesh_queries_typed.hpp` (origin = `Vec3<Quantity<D, T>>`, direction = dimensionless `Vec3<T>`, t = `Quantity<D, T>`). 8 cases / 16 assertions in `tests/geometry-mesh/test_mesh_raycast.cpp`; 5-config DoD green (win-debug 1927/1927, win-asan 1927/1927, win-shipping 1840/1840, win-shipping-profile 1922/1922, win-tidy clean); full project ctest 1919 → 1927. Session log `docs/sessions/2026-05-16-geometry-v4b-mesh-raycast.md`.

## project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir

---
name: project_svgf_gold_denoiser_ckir
description: "D-007 B14-c: the GOLD-STANDARD SVGF-2017 denoiser built in CKIR (ckir_svgf.hpp) — gold à-trous (depth-gradient + variance pre-blur) + temporal integration (reproject/disocclusion/EMA/moments→variance) + 5-iteration pipeline (≥10× noise crush). Vulkan+DX12 verified. NEXT: B14-c-4 A-SVGF adaptive-α."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1487a581-3392-44fb-bc9e-ebeaffd19da5

**D-007 B14-c — the SVGF/A-SVGF spatiotemporal denoiser, GOLD-STANDARD, in CKIR (2026-07-15).** The first slice of the
resumed visual frontier (row #20 B14 GI; B14-c chosen because ReSTIR (B14-a) needs ray tracing, which is later). User mandate
"full crush and gold standard system and full quality CKIR" ⇒ built the FAITHFUL Schied 2017 formula, not a proxy. All in
`engine/kir/include/crd/kir/ckir_svgf.hpp` as statement-tier COMPUTE passes (gather their own stencil from storage buffers,
unlike the B13 resolve passes that defer the gather); tests `tests/kir/test_ckir_svgf.cpp` + `tests/gpu-context-{vulkan,dx12}`.

**[✅ B14-c-1 GOLD] `build_svgf_atrous`** — one edge-stopping à-trous iteration:
- `w_z = exp(−|z_p−z_q| / (σ_z·|∇z_p·(p−q)| + ε))` — the DEPTH-GRADIENT weight (∇z from unit-stride neighbours). This is the
  whole point vs a flat `|Δz|`: edges hold under OBLIQUE surfaces (a steep-but-continuous plane still blurs), and a genuine
  silhouette is caught by the normal weight, not depth. A flat-|Δz| proxy over-stops slopes.
- `w_n = max(0, n·n')^σ_n`; `w_l = exp(−|Δl| / (σ_l·√(g₃ₓ₃(Var)) + ε))` — luminance guided by a 3×3-GAUSSIAN-blurred variance
  (single-pixel variance is itself noisy ⇒ lets fireflies survive; the pre-blur fixes it).
- variance filtered as `Σ(h·w)²·Var_q / (Σ h·w)²` (variance of the weighted mean, Schied §4.2 — already correct because the
  code's `w` includes `h`).

**[✅ B14-c-2] `build_svgf_temporal`** — exponential-history integration + variance-from-moments (8 buffers; ≤ the
`dispatch_kernel_1wg` max-8 cap): reproject along the motion vector (nearest tap, `cast` float↔uint — CAST is in all 5
compute emitters), DISOCCLUSION reject on depth-jump / normal-flip / off-screen by forcing **α=1** (⇒ `lerp(prev,cur,1)=cur`,
the reprojected sample discarded, no ghost — so NO per-output validity `select` is needed, only for `hist`), else blend
`α=max(1/hist, α_min)`. Accumulate `m1=E[l]`, `m2=E[l²]` ⇒ `Var=max(m2−m1²,0)`. Mix is NOT in the compute emitter ⇒ manual
`lerp = a + t·(b−a)`. Bit-exact (no transcendentals): Vulkan max_abs **0.0**.

**[✅ B14-c-3] PIPELINE** — temporal → à-trous ×5 (steps 1,2,4,8,16, ping-pong color+var). Verified end-to-end: temporal
alone cuts error, the à-trous cleans the residual ≥2× more (on a smooth GI signal), the FULL pipeline crushes noise **≥10×**
vs the raw frame. ⚠ LESSON: the à-trous helps most on SHORT-history / SMOOTH signals (residual noise); on an ALREADY-converged
high-frequency image it slightly over-blurs (correct SVGF behavior — test with a short history + smooth GI-like gradient, not
a busy pattern + 24 frames).

crd-kir 28894/133 + gpu-context vulkan/dx12 [svgf] green MSVC + clang-cl; tidy-clean. Config `SvgfConfig{width,height,step,
sigma_z=1,sigma_n=128,sigma_l=4, alpha_min=0.05,depth_reject=0.1,normal_reject=0.9}`. See also
[feedback_compute_kernel_emitter_lacked_exp_pow](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_compute_kernel_emitter_lacked_exp_pow) (the Exp/Pow emitter gap this slice first hit).

**[✅ B14-c-4] A-SVGF adaptive-α** (config `asvgf`, in `build_svgf_temporal`) — variance-aware, self-contained (reuses the
moments the temporal pass tracks, NO separate gradient/stratification buffer): `λ = clamp((|Δl|/σ_hist − lo)/(hi − lo), 0, 1)`,
`α = lerp(base_α, 1, λ)` with σ_hist=√Var_hist, lo=2, hi=8. Where the incoming sample is a real OUTLIER from the history mean
(|Δl| ≫ σ, a lighting/motion change) → α→1 → RESET → no lag/ghosting; where within noise (|Δl| < lo·σ) → α=base → keep
accumulating. Verified: fixed AND adaptive both keep a long history through a noisy stable phase (noise doesn't reset), but on
a step change adaptive tracks the new value **>5× closer**; Vulkan bit-exact (2.98e-8, sqrt-ULP; sqrt is IEEE-exact so the
whole temporal+asvgf pass stays bit-exact on GPU). **⭐ B14-c (the spatiotemporal DENOISER) is COMPLETE: gold à-trous +
temporal + 5-iteration pipeline + A-SVGF, all CKIR statement-tier, CPU+Vulkan+DX12, MSVC+clang-cl.**

**REMAINING in B14 (GI):** [B14-b] world-space radiance cache — DDGI irradiance probes (Majercik 2019, the no-RT-HW GI
fallback) — and [B14-a] ReSTIR (needs ray tracing B9/C3, later). Optional B14-c polish: ReBLUR/ReLAX/SIGMA diffuse+specular+
shadow separation + firefly clamp.

<a id="memory-project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap"></a>
## project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap

---
name: project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap
description: "v5a-4 breakthrough — the CHOLMOD factor gap was the SERIAL SYMBOLIC, not the numeric; Cerid's numeric already wins hood/ldoor"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f039483d-cb60-446b-af8b-a75467157c25
---

2026-05-29, Phase 3.1.6 v5a-4. The supernodal-Cholesky gap vs CHOLMOD (hood/ldoor) was **not** the numeric factor or parallel scaling — it was the **serial symbolic factorization**. Measured (8T, WSL bench vs system CHOLMOD on OpenBLAS):

- **Cerid's NUMERIC factor already beats CHOLMOD's** on hood (224 vs 305ms) and ldoor (~1520 vs 1845ms). The whole loss was setup.
- The gap was the symbolic running ~4.4× CHOLMOD's `analyze` (hood 281 vs 64ms), split into two co-dominant costs: **build_adjacency** (per-vertex introsort, O(nnz·log deg)) AND the **full simplicial L pattern `out.li`** (O(nnz(L)) — 152M entries for ldoor — that the supernodal factor never needs).

**Lever found via the advisor's measurement discipline** (don't guess the target): a per-level scale profiler (dispatcher-thread, race-free at >1 worker) showed the level loop only accounted for 42-73% of FACTOR; the rest was serial symbolic. A symbolic sub-phase profiler then split it adj vs li.

**Fix 1 SHIPPED (banked, byte-identical, suite exit 0):** `build_adjacency` rewritten to counting-sort transpose + per-vertex sorted merge-dedup, O(nnz) no introsort, assumption-free (still correct for non-symmetric AMD callers). hood adj 143→31ms. **Flipped hood 0.85→1.11× WIN and ldoor 0.82→1.01× WIN at 8T.**

**Fix 2 SHIPPED + VERIFIED (the decisive crush):** `symbolic_factorize(…, supernodal_patterns=true)` builds per-fundamental-supernode LEADING-column patterns (`SymbolicFactor::slead_ptr/slead_idx`) via assembly-tree union R(g)={fc}∪adj(fc)[>fc]∪(∪ child fund supernode h: R(h)[>fc]) — correct because interior columns of a fundamental supernode have ≤1 etree child ⇒ every external child connects at the leading column. `build_supernodal_symbolic` reads `slead` via `lead_pat` else `li`; full-`li` path kept for the API (tests/bench read `sf.li`). Pattern-build hood 95→6.4ms, ldoor 630→30ms. **8T: hood 1.33× · ldoor 1.28× WIN; bmwcra 0.68; bcsstk25 1.41×.** Verified bit-identical (hesap-direct 68692 asserts + moat {1,2,4,8} + hesap-ordering 40 cases + gcc -Werror, all exit 0). `acc.size()==colcount(fc)` guards the tree.

**bmwcra stays a loss (~0.68×)** — its numeric (2070 vs 1179) is the OpenBLAS-asm dense-supernode wall (ADR-0082 intrinsics cap). Two decisive wins (hood/ldoor), not three.

**SOLVE batched-diag SHIPPED 2026-05-30 (improved, NOT crushed):** measure-first (advisor) — solve phase-split profiler showed the multi-RHS diagonal block solve was per-RHS BLAS-2 (re-reading L_diag nrhs×), 31-48% of the x16 solve. Fixed: BATCHED diag for nc≥48 fronts (c-contiguous scratch, L_diag once, vectorized; DIVIDE-not-reciprocal ⇒ bit-identical), per-RHS below the threshold (bmwcra's ~12k tiny fronts). Diag ~halved; 1T x16 SOLVE bmwcra 0.70/hood 0.84/ldoor 0.67. Verified 70046 asserts + new wide-front test + gcc clean. **Honest: NOT a crush** — solve is now gemm-bound (ADR-0082 ceiling, like bmwcra) + SERIAL (loses to CHOLMOD OpenBLAS-parallel at 8T). x1 (0.59-0.86, common case) UNCHANGED + uncharacterized. **Next fresh-session lever: PARALLELIZE the solve** (level-parallel fwd/back, the tree-parallel advantage that crushed the factor; moat-bound). Don't start parallel-solve at a session tail.

**SOLVE parallel BACKWARD SHIPPED 2026-05-30 (measure-first probe paid off):** advisor warned "CHOLMOD's solve barely scales might mean the solve doesn't parallelize for ANYONE (memory-bound)" — so probe the backward (race-free left-looking already: each supernode writes its own columns, reads done ancestors) before building the hard forward. Stored etree levels (m_lvl_ptr/m_lvl_list) + level-parallel backward (descending, per-worker tmp/dscr scratch, cnt≥2 gate). VERIFIED 340678 asserts + the existing moat. RESULT: backward scales ~2.5× → 8T SOLVE x16 hood 0.87→**1.20× WIN**, ldoor 0.77→~1.06× (≈tied, within noise), bmwcra 293→233ms (1.26× faster, ratio 0.58→0.73 — improved, still loses, CHOLMOD's big-dense home turf). **x1 single-RHS UNCHANGED + still loses (8T hood 0.74/ldoor 0.76/bmwcra 0.53)** — parallel backward is multi-RHS-only.

**CORRECTION (advisor-caught) on the determinism claim above:** the existing moat's `xmp==xm1` runs BOTH solves at the fixed pool size (`solve()` reads `jobs::num_workers()`, fixed per test run) ⇒ it tested FACTOR determinism (identical L → identical solve), NOT the SOLVE path across thread counts. The parallel-backward (and now forward) solve determinism was proven by-CONSTRUCTION (race-free left-looking + fixed accumulation order), not empirically — until the FORWARD slice's new `solve_with_workers` test below.

**SOLVE parallel FORWARD SHIPPED 2026-05-30 (the full multi-RHS solve crush — measure-first paid off again):** the forward is right-looking (scatters into shared ancestor rows → same-level race). Reformulated LEFT-looking: each s GATHERS Σ_{k∈upd_list[s]} L_{s,k}·Y_k from descendants (L_{s,k} = k's panel rows in s's column range, binary-searched — the cmod gather mirror), writes only its own columns. k-ascending == the right-looking accumulation order ⇒ bit-identical. Stored m_upd_ptr/m_upd_list. RESULT (8T x16, vs prior parallel-backward-only): hood 87→**61ms (1.69–1.81× WIN)**, ldoor 553→**277ms (1.84–1.98× WIN, ~doubled the lead)**, bmwcra 233→**200ms (0.84–0.85×, improved, still loses — ADR-0082 gemm ceiling)**. But the advisor's tiny-gemm caution was RIGHT: the left-looking SERIAL forward (many tiny per-descendant gemms) REGRESSED 1T x16 (hood +19%, ldoor +11%) vs the right-looking's few big gemms ⇒ **TWO-PATH** (`solve_with_workers`: nw≤1 RIGHT-looking serial, nw>1 LEFT-looking parallel; 1T back to ≈prior — no regression). DETERMINISM now proven EMPIRICALLY: new `solve_with_workers(nw)` test compares nw=1 [right serial] vs nw∈{2,3,pool} [left parallel] on ONE factor — BIT-IDENTICAL at every count (548751 asserts/21 cases). Advisor-caught footgun fixed: the hook's tmp/dscr scratch is POOL-sized (`worker_index()` is pool-global regardless of the parallel_for chunking factor per [jobs-worker-index-aliasing](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_jobs_worker_index_aliasing) — sizing by nw heap-overflows for 1<nw<pool). Verified MSVC + gcc -Werror + clang-cl + ctest-guards + clang-format + win-asan (gather OOB-clean) + clang-tidy (lib+tests); running the proper close gate FIXED 3 latent cluster failures the prior binary-direct verify missed: a non-ASCII `ᴴ` TEST_CASE name, a clang-cl unused-lambda-capture, 7 pre-existing factor tidy issues (avR/bvR/ttR→lower_case + a lowercase u-literal). **STILL OPEN: x1 single-RHS solve (serial, loses); bmwcra x16 (0.85×, gemm ceiling).** The solve is "multi-RHS wins hood/ldoor," NOT "solve crushed."

Commit-prep DONE: symbolic.cpp profiler fully removed; `CRD_HESAP_CHOL_SCALE_PROFILE` disabled (#ifdef-off like pre-existing `CRD_HESAP_CHOL_PROFILE`); CHOLMOD-SPLIT removed. PERMANENT: build_adjacency O(nnz) rewrite + the slead supernodal-symbolic + the batched-diag + the level-parallel backward. See [project_cholmod_factor_gap](project-history.md#memory-project_cholmod_factor_gap) (superseded — the gap was symbolic, not per-thread BLAS-3), [reference_cholmod_oracle_and_wsl_build](build-and-verification.md#memory-reference_cholmod_oracle_and_wsl_build).


<!-- end-memory:project_symbolic_is_the_cholmod_gap -->

## S8f single-pass V0 (radix-2) CORRECT but 0.156× — confirms the four-step IS the efficient 256K structure (2026-06-20, Part 47cc)

**Gate `CRD_FFT_256K_SINGLEPASS_POC`: dispatched 256K f32 forward to `execute_reference` (the radix-2 DIT oracle — bit-reversal + log2(N)=18 folded-twiddle butterfly stages, NO four-step inter-stage pass).** ⭐ **RESULT: CORRECT 2.6e-7 but CRD 2.643ms / 0.156× MKL — 5.7× SLOWER than S6 (0.46).** The naive single-pass (which DOES avoid the inter-stage twiddle pass) is far slower because radix-2 = 18 scalar passes through 2MB (memory-bound) + bit-reversal random access; no batching ⇒ no SIMD width (the four-step gets its SIMD from batching the column sub-FFTs). The production Stockham (baseline) = 1.659ms is also single-pass and also slower than S6. ⭐⭐ **DECISIVE CONCLUSION (now proven 4 ways — S7 spills, S8b table-mem, S8f-radix2 2.6ms, baseline-Stockham 1.66ms): the BLOCK FOUR-STEP with hier codelets IS the efficient structure for a single 256K transform; its ONLY weakness vs MKL is the inter-stage twiddle PASS (~0.05ms = the 15% gap). MKL is faster because it folds that twiddle into a vectorized cache-blocked kernel — which for CERID = the M18-class fully-fused tiled hier (fold the inter-stage twiddle into a memory-TILE producer, NOT registers=S7-spills, NOT a 2MB table=S8b). That is the ONE remaining lever and it's a multi-session codegen effort, not a V1 tweak.** **256K BEST stays S6 = 0.46-0.47ms / 0.82-0.87× MKL (3.6× over Stockham, gap 5.0×→1.18×).** S8f V1 = the M18-tile fused hier (reuse emit_p2_fused rect + M16-B producer for 1024×256). All gated; default byte-unchanged. NO COMMITS.

## S8b table-twiddle REJECTED + DIAGNOSTIC PROVES the inter-stage twiddle is the irreducible four-step gap (2026-06-20, Part 47bb)

**Gate `CRD_FFT_256K_INTILE_POC`.** ⭐ **DIAGNOSTIC (decisive): skipping the twiddle multiply+recurrence (output intentionally wrong, timing-only) drops 256K 0.498→0.434ms — and 0.434 < MKL 0.446. So the inter-stage twiddle (~0.03-0.06ms) IS the entire gap to MKL; without it CRD BEATS MKL.** Implemented S8b = replace the per-k1 serial RECURRENCE with a precomputed full inter-stage twiddle TABLE load (members m_s8b_tr/ti, ctor precompute, gated): tried [k1][col] layout (strided, 0.521) AND access-order [col_group][k1][8] contiguous layout (0.534) — **BOTH SLOWER than S6's recurrence (0.461)**, correct 2.3e-7. ROOT: the recurrence uses NO memory; any table is a 2MB L3 read that costs more than the 2-mults/k1 recurrence. ⇒ **the twiddle is at its compute floor (recurrence optimal); it can't be cheapened.** Combined with S7 (fusing it into the producer = register spills) the verdict is rigorous: **the four-step inter-stage twiddle is an IRREDUCIBLE structural pass (~0.05ms = exactly the MKL gap); it can't be cheapened (recurrence optimal), fused (S7 spills), or table-loaded (S8b memory). MKL avoids it via a single-pass radix kernel that folds the twiddle in — a fundamentally different algorithm.** **256K BEST stays S6 = 0.461-0.467ms / 0.85-0.87× MKL (3.6× over Stockham).** Only S8f (single-pass cache-resident small-FFT) can close the last ~15% — a different algorithm, not a four-step tweak. All gated; engine default byte-unchanged. NO COMMITS.

## S7 twiddle-fusion REJECTED (measured) — scratch ENABLES the efficient per-k1 twiddle; best 256K stays S6 0.841× (2026-06-20, Part 47aa)

**S7 fully implemented + correct + benchmarked + REJECTED (a complete attempt, not a skip).** Gate `CRD_FFT_256K_TWIDDLE_FUSED_POC`: generator `emit_batched_twiddle(32,1024,128)` → `codelet32_batched_twiddle1024` (stage-2 DAG + inter-stage W_N^{col·k1} by recurrence over output m, step W^{col·32}, base/step from factored table, scatter-store to tbuf[col·n1+k1]); wired in the P1 m13 branch (n2==256) + `s7_fused` flag skips the twiddle pass via `continue`. ⚠ **RESULT: CRD 0.652ms vs S6 0.464ms = 40% SLOWER (×MKL 0.545), correct 7.5e-7 (recurrence drift, no reseed).** ROOT CAUSE (fundamental, not a bug): the fused producer must HOLD all 32 stage-2 outputs in registers for the m-ordered twiddle recurrence → **register spills**; the separate scratch buffer is precisely what ENABLES the efficient existing SIMD twiddle (reads scratch ONE k1 at a time, recurrence over k1, reseed/8 — no holding). **Eliminating scratch is counterproductive.** ⇒ the inter-stage twiddle is NOT cheaply fusable; further twiddle-fusion (S8a) hits the same wall. **256K BEST stays S6 = 0.464ms / 0.841× MKL.** The only remaining parity lever = M18-style FULL P1+P2 in-tile fusion (keep the whole intermediate L2-resident, no tbuf round-trip) = S8b, a major M18-class undertaking. S7 left gated (documented rejected variant). Engine default UNCHANGED. NO COMMITS.

Seeds build/gen_cmp{128,256}.cpp (composition, slow — measured-dead).** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **Part 47 — FOUR-STEP CRACKS N=256: 0.80→0.92, BEATS FFTW (0.80)! `build/four256.cpp` (N=256=16×16, gate 9.83e-16): Stage A = 8 col-pair over-2 sr16 (crushing size-16, FITS no-spill) + per-lane W256 twiddle → A[r*16+c]; Stage B = 8 row-pair sr16 with STRIDED gather across 2 rows (=the transpose) → out X[c'*16+r]. gcc **0.915/0.924/0.916 = ~0.92×** (clang 0.85). ⇒ the FOUR-STEP (register-fitting crushing sub-FFTs + inline transpose) is the LARGE-N lever — lifted N=256 from single-lane-split 0.80 to 0.92, and BEATS the genfft gold-standard FFTW (0.80) by 12pts. The transpose was NOT the killer feared (historical aos_fft1024 0.26× was a DIFFERENT naive transpose; L1-resident + crushing subs carry it). ⭐ FULL SCOREBOARD (all gated): N=8 2.32 · N=16 1.36 · N=32 1.16 CRUSH · N=64 parity · N=128 0.98 · **N=256 0.92** — near-parity through 256, BEATS FFTW EVERYWHERE. ⇒ four-step is THE technique for N≥256 (and the engine's large-N curve). NEXT: optimize the transpose (SIMD permute2f128 16×16 like crush64w3 vs the strided gather) to push 0.92→parity; apply four-step to N=512/1024 (the engine curve); wire into FftPlan. Seeds build/four256.cpp.** ⭐⭐ **Part 48 — FOUR-STEP N=512 = 0.75 (below FFTW 0.85): the SIZE-32 SPILL wall. `build/four512.cpp` (N=512=32×16, gate 9.92e-16): Stage A = 8 col-pair over-2 sr32 (size-32 MONOLITHIC over-2 = 32 ymm SPILLS) + W512 twiddle; Stage B = 16 row-pair sr16 (gather). gcc 0.68 / clang 0.75. ⇒ non-square N=512 forces a size-32 stage; the over-2 size-32 codelet spills (vs N=256's clean 16×16 register-fitting size-16). So four-step BEATS FFTW through 256 (256=0.92) but N=512 size-32-spill = 0.75 (below FFTW 0.85, ~engine's best 0.75). ⭐ FIX for N≥512 (no-spill): either (a) 3-LEVEL 8×8×8 all-size-8 crushing codelets (fit easily, 2 transposes) OR (b) Stage-32 via sr32w lane-split with strided gather (per-row, no spill) OR (c) the recursion. SCOREBOARD: N=8 2.32 / 16 1.36 / 32 1.16 CRUSH · 64 parity · 128 0.98 · 256 0.92 (ALL beat FFTW) · **512 0.75 (size-32 spill, below FFTW — the new frontier)**. four-step VALIDATED as large-N lever (beats FFTW ≤256); N≥512 needs no-spill size-32 (3-level or strided-lane-split). Seeds build/four512.cpp.** ⭐⭐ **Part 49 — N=512 NO-SPILL ATTEMPT = SAME (0.72), the gather offsets the spill-fix. `build/four512b.cpp` (gate 9.92e-16): Stage A per-column lane-split size-32 (sub-16 over-2 in lanes FITS, inline strided gather, W512 twiddle folded into merge, split-store) = gcc 0.725 / clang 0.674 — ≈ the spill version (0.75). ⇒ the no-spill removed the 32-ymm spill but the per-column STRIDED GATHER (16/col) + split-store overhead exactly offset it. BOTH N=512 four-step variants ~0.72-0.75, BELOW FFTW 0.85. ⭐ HONEST LARGE-N TRUTH: our four-step BEATS FFTW at SMALL-SQUARE (N=256=16×16 size-16 subs → 0.92 > FFTW 0.80) but is BELOW FFTW at LARGE/NON-SQUARE (N=512 0.75 < FFTW 0.85). FFTW's large-N four-step is better-tuned (blocking/prefetch/transpose refined over years) than our 2 structures. To match/beat FFTW@512 = FFTW-LEVEL large-N tuning (deep, years of refinement) — NOT a quick structural fix (tried spill-over-2 AND no-spill-per-column, both ~0.73). FINAL SCOREBOARD: N=8 2.32 / 16 1.36 / 32 1.16 CRUSH MKL · 64 parity · 128 0.98 · 256 0.92 ALL BEAT FFTW · 512 0.75 BELOW FFTW (the deep large-N tuning frontier). ⇒ we OWN the FFTW-beating frontier through N=256; N≥512 = FFTW's better-tuned large-N (deep optimization tier, not a structural quick-win). Seeds build/four512b.cpp.** ⭐⭐ **Part 50 — N=512 PROFILED (the honest root): `build/four512b.cpp` -DONLYA/-DONLYB stage isolation: Stage A (size-32 cols + transpose-gather + W512 twiddle + split-store) alone = 1.06× MKL-WHOLE (≈0.94 of MKL's entire-transform time BY ITSELF!); Stage B (size-16 + gather) alone = 2.09× (≈0.48 of MKL whole). ⇒ the 2-stage four-step inherently does ~1.4× MKL's work (0.94+0.48) because of the SEPARATE transpose + twiddle pass. MKL's N=512 = INTEGRATED transpose-free large-N (radix STAGES, never materialize a transpose, refined over years) ⇒ avoids the pass overhead. ⇒ N=512 gap is STRUCTURAL (2-pass-four-step vs MKL's integrated transpose-free) + deep-tuned, NOT a codelet swap (tried spill-over-2 0.75 + no-spill-per-column 0.72, both Stage-A-transpose-dominated). HONEST FRONTIER: our codegen+four-step BEATS FFTW through N=256 (the open-source gold standard), CRUSHES MKL ≤32; N≥512 = MKL's integrated transpose-free large-N (the deep tier, even FFTW only 0.85). To match MKL@512 = build the integrated transpose-free large-N (radix-stages across the array kept L1, single-reorder), a SUSTAINED profiling/blocking campaign (FFTW/MKL spent years), NOT a session quick-win. The grind through N=256 is WON; N=512 = the deep transpose-free large-N campaign. Seeds build/four512b.cpp (-DONLYA/B profile).**

## v11 DSP — PLANNED 2026-06-20 (detailed plan in `docs/phases/phase-3.1.6-hesap.md` § "v11 — DSP … DETAILED PLAN"; ADR-0093 at v11-a)

**MAXIMAL scope (user direction): "every functionality of the DSP subject" — full Signal-Processing-Toolbox surface
+ Adaptive + Wavelets + Comms/SDR.** ~36 slices · ~12,000 LOC · ~425 tests · multi-session (the LARGEST hesap
cluster — don't marathon). Delivered as **3 ISOLATED modules** (module-isolation cornerstone — a DAW links dsp not
comms) + a `crd-units` add:
- **`crd-hesap-dsp`** (core + adaptive) — the bulk, slices v11-a…t
- **`crd-hesap-wavelet`** (→ crd-hesap-fft) — v11w-a…e
- **`crd-hesap-comms`** (→ crd-hesap-dsp) — v11c-a…g
- **`crd-units`** add: `Decibel` (LOGARITHMIC-scale type, NOT a linear Quantity<D,T> — design question) + `NormalizedFrequency`

**Edges (acyclic):** dsp → crd-hesap-fft (spectral/conv/Hilbert/CZT) + crd-hesap-eigen (DPSS multitaper, MUSIC/ESPRIT,
AR) + math(simd) + units + core/containers/memory. wavelet → fft. comms → dsp. **NO edge to crd-hesap-opt** (keep
acyclic; firls/remez use own exchange/LS).

## ⭐⭐ THE HONEST GATE (load-bearing — the v10 scar [feedback_source_must_match_honest_scoreboard](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_source_must_match_honest_scoreboard), advisor-flagged)
- **Filter DESIGN** (ellip/cheby2/remez/firls = transcendental + iterative numerics) → gate = **SPEC-COMPLIANCE**
  (passband ripple ≤ Rp · stopband ≥ Rs · equiripple alternation count · monotonicity) **+ coeffs-to-N-digits** vs
  scipy/MATLAB. **NOT bit-match** (won't hold cross-compiler = fake scoreboard).
- **Filter APPLICATION** (lfilter/sosfilt/biquad/conv) → gate = **BIT-EXACT vs scipy + {1..16} determinism MOAT.**
- **The determinism moat scopes to APPLICATION + STREAMING ONLY** (DAW replay/certification). Design is one-time
  setup — do NOT reflex-claim "deterministic ellip()" on every design slice.

## Two-layer (ADR-0078) + streaming (user: EVERY filter)
Upper typed batch (scipy-style whole-array, Frequency<T> Hz + Decibel + NormalizedFreq) + Lower raw **allocation-free
STATEFUL block-streaming kernels** (Direct-II-transposed biquads, FIR delay-line, polyphase) = the DAW/SDR real-time
hot loop, fixed per-element FP order. Every filter ships BOTH.

## ⭐ TWO gold standards — CORRECTNESS ≠ PERFORMANCE (user-flagged 2026-06-20: "scipy isn't perf gold standard")
**Correctness** = scipy.signal + MATLAB (what v11-a/b gate on). **Performance** = SIMD-tuned kernel libs (Intel IPP `ippsIIR`/`ippsFIR` = x86 ceiling · ARM CMSIS-DSP · liquid-dsp). ONLY HOT-PATH slices get perf benchmarks (the `bench_*_vs_<gold>` pattern like bench_hesap_cholesky_vs_cholmod / bench_fft_vs_refs-vs-MKL): **v11-i filtering · j fast-conv · k multirate · m/n spectral(FFT-bound, inherits v10-MKL) · t adaptive/comms(liquid-dsp).** DESIGN slices (c-g elliptic/remez · o AR · p subspace) + reps/windows are ONE-TIME ⇒ NO perf benchmark (faking one = dishonest; nobody benchmarks ellip()). ⭐ v11-i CRUSH GATE (parallel to FFT-vs-MKL): portable-C++ streaming kernels match/beat IPP's hand-tuned SIMD AND keep bit-determinism + {1..16} = the moat IPP/CMSIS/liquid lack. ⚠ USER PREREQUISITE for v11-i: install Intel IPP (oneAPI) + liquid-dsp (source) + CMSIS-DSP (none installed yet) — until then v11-i ships correctness-gated, perf rows land when libs present. v11-a/b correctly have NO perf benchmark (not hot-path).

## Gold standards (availability CONFIRMED 2026-06-20)
- **MATLAB R2026a — ALL toolboxes installed** ([reference_matlab_gold_standard](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-reference_matlab_gold_standard); signal/dsp/comm/wavelet/ident).
  The industry spec-compliance authority + native wavelet/comms refs. ⚠ matlab -batch ~44.5s startup ⇒ batch ALL
  slice refs into ONE call → coeff file (the ODE SUNDIALS-tableau pattern). scipy.signal = free primary. Intel IPP =
  kernel-perf crush (needs oneAPI). liquid-dsp + CMSIS-DSP = comms/embedded peers. PyWavelets = wavelet cross-check.

## Sub-slice spine (full table in the phase doc)
**dsp:** a substrate(reps tf/zpk/**SOS**/ss/lattice + conversions + **freqz/group_delay** + units add) · b windows(+DPSS→eigen)
· c FIR-windowed · d FIR-Remez/firls/SavGol/RRC · e IIR-Butter/Cheb/Bessel · f **ELLIPTIC**(own slice — AGM/Landen/degree-eqn)
· g IIR-digital+order-est+notch/comb · h **RBJ-biquad-EQ**(DAW) · i **filtering+STREAMING**(lfilter/filtfilt/sosfilt+kernels)
· j fast-conv(over fft) · k multirate(resample_poly/upfirdn/Farrow/CIC) · l Hilbert · m spectral(welch/STFT/csd) · n **multitaper**(→eigen)
· o AR(Yule-Walker/Burg+AIC/MDL) · p **subspace MUSIC/ESPRIT**(→eigen) · q cepstrum/Goertzel/Walsh/CZT/Z · r waveforms · s peaks+measurements(SNR/THD/SINAD/SFDR) · t **adaptive**(LMS/NLMS/RLS/AP).
**wavelet:** a families/filterbanks · b DWT/IDWT+modes+multilevel · c SWT/WPT · d CWT · e 2-D+denoising/MODWT.
**comms:** a PSK/QAM/PAM/FSK · b pulse-shaping RRC · c timing-sync · d carrier-recovery · e equalizers(LMS/CMA/DFE/MLSE) · f AGC/framing/channels · g OFDM.
**z close:** CLI hesap.{dsp,wavelet,comms}.* + full scoreboard + 3 system docs + ADR-0093.

## v12-pull decision
Multitaper/AR spectral CIs need χ²/F inverse-CDF (v12 Statistics, AFTER v11). DECISION: ship estimators in v11
WITHOUT parametric CIs; CI layer = thin v12-followup (or 2-quantile-fn v12-pull à la v9-i Philox if needed sooner).
AIC/MDL order-selection ships in v11 (log-likelihood only).

## v11-a IN PROGRESS (2026-06-20). ⭐ dB UNITS DESIGN SETTLED + SHIPPED:
**KEY FINDING — crd-units ALREADY had a pinned dB framework** (`units_nonlinear.hpp`, Phase 3.1.7.5): dB is an
I/O LENS, NOT a type — no type-level arithmetic (`dB+dB≠2·dB`), convert dB→linear at the boundary, compute in the
linear domain, convert back. A naive linear `Decibel` Quantity would be WRONG (dB is logarithmic). ⇒ I EXTENDED it,
did NOT invent a new type (the user's "add Decibel" intent honored more rigorously). Shipped in `units_nonlinear.hpp`:
- **`DecibelRatio`** (amplitude/field, dimension=Dimensionless): lin=10^(dB/20), dB=20·log10(lin) — magnitude responses, "Rs dB down".
- **`DecibelPower`** (power, Dimensionless): lin=10^(dB/10), dB=10·log10(lin) — the 10^(0.1·Rp) form scipy/MATLAB *ord routines use on |H|².
- Both conventions EXPLICIT in the type name ⇒ kills the amplitude-vs-power footgun. DSP design code converts the dB spec to the linear ratio at the boundary, all arithmetic on the linear ratio (matches the pin).
- Literals `_dB_amp`/`_dB_pow` in `crd::units::literals` — ⚠ POSITIVE-only (UDL `-60.0_dB_amp` parses as -(60.0_dB_amp), sign escapes the log ⇒ negates the LINEAR ratio = WRONG; negative/attenuation dB MUST use `quantity_from_nonlinear<DecibelRatio>(-60.0)`. Documented in literals.hpp).
- **`NormalizedFrequency<T>`** (`normalized_frequency.hpp`, new): strong type killing the rad/sample-vs-Nyquist-fraction-vs-cycles/sample footgun. Canonical=cycles/sample (ν=f/fs). Named ctors `from_{cycles_per_sample,rad_per_sample,nyquist_fraction,hz}` + accessors `{cycles_per_sample,rad_per_sample,nyquist_fraction,hz}()`. NOT a Quantity (a normalization, not an SI dim). scipy/MATLAB Wn = nyquist_fraction ∈[0,1].

## project_v16_reverse_ad_plan

---
name: project_v16_reverse_ad_plan
description: "v16 reverse-mode AD + differentiable solvers — kicked off 2026-07-06; the moat, the a–z slices, and the NEW 2025-26 parts"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d095b72d-cb68-40b1-aaa2-1147516ea4fd
---

**v16 = reverse-mode AD + differentiable solvers**, same module `crd-hesap-autodiff` (`::reverse`), sibling to the shipped v15 forward cluster. Kicked off 2026-07-06 with deep research. **DO NOT re-plan the shape — read `docs/phases/phase-3.1.6-v16.md` (spec) + `docs/research/2026-07-06-v16-reverse-ad-crush.md` (per-slice crush levers) before any slice.** 12 tasks queued (a–k+z).

**★ THE MOAT (the whole cluster's differentiator):** bit-identical **`{1..16}`-worker AND batch-invariant** gradients ⇒ **deterministic training** — a world-first for a C++ engine. torch/JAX can't: their reverse pass scatters adjoints through non-associative atomic adds (run-to-run drift O(1e-4)). The 2025 research sharpened the diagnosis: non-determinism is dominated by the **batch-size dependence of reduction kernels** (Thinking Machines "Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference", 2025-09) — so the tape must be fixed-order, no-atomics, AND **batch-invariant** (gate perturbs batch layout, not just worker-count). The verifiable-training literature is asking for exactly this.

**NEW 2025-26 parts folded into the slices at kickoff:**
- v16-a: **batch-invariant adjoint reductions** + **local-adjoint preaccumulation** (CoDiPack arXiv:2405.07819, shrinks the tape).
- v16-c: **bicoloring** (arXiv:2505.07308, joint row+col fewer evals than v15-e unidirectional) + **sparse reverse-mode LA** (torch/TF LACK sparse-matrix autodiff — a capability crush, arXiv:2212.05159).
- v16-f: **discretize-then-optimize (exact, revolve-checkpointed, DEFAULT) vs continuous-adjoint (O(1)-mem but can be INCONSISTENT with the forward discretisation, arXiv:2306.02192)** — ship both, honesty caveat loud; symplectic/MALI when reversible.
- v16-g: **Alt-Diff** (arXiv:2210.01802) alongside direct KKT-implicit; jaxopt is DEAD ⇒ own the C++ implicit-diff lane (peers cvxpylayers/CuClarabel/Theseus/OptNet).
- v16-k: **Efficient-KAN** B-spline-linearity restructuring (do NOT ship naive per-edge eval) + **KAN-ODE**; KAN is ICLR 2025, built on the v13 splines.

**Key correctness principles:** a VJP is the TRANSPOSE of the JVP — reuse the v15-b/f rule slopes (one library, two modes) ([feedback_bench_gate_all_peers_agree](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_bench_gate_all_peers_agree)); matrix VJPs are self-contained (take the stored factor, factor-reuse, never AD-through-LU); Enzyme named OUT (LLVM-plugin/MSVC loss). **DoD note (user 2026-07-06):** the full 6-config sweep runs as a **2-config pass AFTER v16 finishes** (batched with the v15 sweep), NOT per-slice. Supersedes the plan-shape parts of [project_v14_v18_planning](project-history.md#memory-project_v14_v18_planning) for v16. Tape/step-control scars: [feedback_taylor_ode_step_control_and_tape](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_taylor_ode_step_control_and_tape). Crush playbook: `docs/hints/crush-playbook.md`.

## project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope

---
name: project_v17_gpu_compiler_maximal_scope
description: "v17 is a GPU compute COMPILER (CKIR), not a Vulkan port — 4 locked user decisions, read before any v17 work"
metadata:

---

**v17 = the Cerid GPU compute COMPILER (`crd-kir` + `crd-hesap-gpu`), maximal frontier scope.** User locked the
architecture on 2026-07-07 ("do everything, API-agnostic to its core, bit-identical AND fastest, for physics/rendering/
all-compute/research/ML"). It is a tensor/kernel compiler (Triton/TVM/XLA-class), the substrate every Cerid project
stands on — NOT "mirror the suite onto Vulkan."

**The 4 locked decisions (do NOT relitigate):**
1. **A Cerid kernel DSL/IR** — module `crd-kir` (a NEW foundational module, peer of crd-math/crd-rhi, *below* hesap-gpu
   so rendering/physics/geometry author kernels on it too). TWO-LEVEL: **CKIR-Graph** (typed tensor op-graph, *extends
   the v16-h `graph_ad` IR* ⇒ every kernel differentiable by construction) → **CKIR-Tile** (tile/loop/schedule IR,
   coop-matrix/tensor-core, fixed-tree reductions) → codegen. A **CPU reference lowering** = the single oracle.
2. **SIX backends shipped** (not seamed): Vulkan/SPIR-V · CUDA/PTX-NVRTC · WebGPU/WGSL (browser+WASM) · DirectX12/DXIL ·
   Metal/MSL · ROCm/HIP. Each = one Tile codegen + one runtime driver; the op library is untouched.
3. **Beat the VENDOR kernels** (cuBLAS/cuFFT/cuDNN/cuSPARSE/cuSOLVER/rocBLAS) at matched precision — via a scheduler +
   **autotuner** (checked-in tuning DB, deterministic replay) + coop-matrix/tensor-core intrinsics. Honest per-op gap.
4. **Certified bit-exact core + reproducible elsewhere** — T1 run-to-run · T2 cross-arch reproducible (binned/RFA) · T3
   cross-VENDOR bit-exact IEEE-only (NoContraction + `float_controls` audit) + **crd::math transcendentals AS CKIR ops**
   (cross-vendor deterministic transcendentals) + **computation certificates** (hash-chained transcripts).

**Standing rule:** NO float atomics anywhere — fixed reduction trees, IR-enforced (a float-atomic kernel is a compile
error). `crd-hesap-gpu` = the op library authored in CKIR (GEMM/FFT/reduce/tensor/sparse/LA/NN/autodiff — multi-backend
+ differentiable + deterministic for free; autodiff-on-GPU nearly free since CKIR-Graph IS the autodiff graph).

**Kickoff (2026-07-07):** RTX 4070 Ti SUPER + Vulkan 1.4.341 + glslc; **CUDA 13.3 + cuDNN + Slang 2025.18.1 INSTALLED**
(nvcc/cublas/cufft verified). Substrate proven via `geometry-bvh-gpu`. Honest size **~66 KLOC / ~1480 tests / ~19–27
wk** (a–o + z, incl. Part C).

**Hardware coverage (user-decided 2026-07-07):** develop everything on the local RTX 4070 Ti + Windows — **4/6 backends
fully local** (Vulkan/CUDA/DX12/**WebGPU incl. real browser**) + **HIP-on-NVIDIA** exercises the ROCm codegen path

## project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct

---
name: project_v17g_gemm_cublas_parity_89pct
description: "v17-g CUDA FP32 SGEMM honest board (bench_vendor.cu, clock-locked, full 3-entry vendor bar, min-of-5, correctness-gated): ⭐ GENUINE VERIFIED CRUSH at N=512 = 105.7% (reproduced 3x, two-stage shared-mem double-buffer gemm_wt_db2 @ 64x64); N=1024 89%, N=2048 83%, N=4096 78% (below parity — 1 block/SM cancels db2 at large N). Path to large-N parity = occupancy-preserving db2 (opt-in shared)/warptile-depth/tensor. cuBLAS JIT'd. Queue #1-12; #1/2/12 done + N=512 crush. ⭐ TENSOR (#5, gemm_wmma2 tensor_lab.cu): cp.async double-buffer + vectorized loads = 61-63 TF = 77-79% of cuBLAS-tensor = 2.1x cuBLAS-fp32 (fp16 acc) at N=2048/4096 — the large-N win FP32 couldn't get. Full cuBLAS-tensor crush needs mma.sync+ldmatrix (last ~22%). UPDATE: built raw mma.sync.m16n8k16+ldmatrix+cp.async-db (gemm_mma, tensor_lab.cu) — CORRECT (maxrel 4.5e-5, layouts verified — hardest kernel done right) but ~72% of cuBLAS-tensor, does NOT beat wmma2 (~74%) or crush the tensor peak; needs register-level fragment PREFETCH + multi-stage pipeline (CUTLASS tensor mainloop depth). Measurements now thermally noisy (cuBLAS-tensor 69-82 TF, long bench session). Both tensor kernels = ~2x cuBLAS-fp32 (large-N win holds). ⭐⭐ BREAKTHROUGH: the ~72-79% 'plateau' was NOT a ceiling — it was a TOO-SMALL WARP TILE. Fix = 64x64 warp tile (2x2 warps not 8-warp 64x32) + BK=16 (2 blocks/SM). gemm_wmma2<128,128,16,2,2> = 92-99.6% of cuBLAS-tensor (peak 99.6 = PARITY with NVIDIA CUTLASS, hand-written!) = ~2.4x cuBLAS-fp32 @ fp16. LESSON: I invoked a plateau without a full geometry sweep — that was a flinch; the warp tile was the lever. This is the tensor kernel to port (#9). ⭐⭐ PORTED (2026-07-08, #6+#7 DONE): winning GEMM schedule (64x64 block, 4x4 microtile, TRANSPOSED-A shared, FMA) now emitted as the T2 DetTier::Fast GEMM across ALL backends. Added `tier` param to KGraph::contract() (ckir.hpp); wrote emit_contract_fast_{glsl,hlsl,wgsl,msl} (transposed-A shared/groupshared/var<workgroup>/threadgroup + fma/mad); routed in backend_{vulkan,dx12,webgpu,metal} when tier==Fast && 64x64x8-tileable && single-batch, grid=(M/64)*(N/64), else naive precise T1 stays default. VALIDATED ON REAL GPUs: Vulkan (25332 assns), DX12 (25427), WebGPU (25427) all PASS — correct within FMA tolerance (maxrel<1e-4 vs the precise oracle) + run-to-run bit-identical (T2 determinism) + 0 validation errors. Metal emitter-validated on Windows (22 assns, can't run Metal here). Tests: test_backend_{vulkan,dx12,webgpu}.cpp v17-h cases + test_ckir_msl.cpp fast-matmul section. NEXT: #8 fusion port, #9 tensor tier (coopmat), #10 Strassen, #11 split-K small-N. ⛔⛔ PERF-BENCH FINDING (2026-07-08, DISPROVED the perf crush — correctness/determinism shipped, PERFORMANCE did NOT): per-backend fast-vs-naive bench (test_backend_vulkan.cpp v17-h PERF, [.bench], kernel-only via elementwise-add transfer subtraction) shows the ported T2 tiled GLSL GEMM is 10-20x SLOWER than the naive precise kernel: [Vulkan] N=512 fast 47 vs naive 1066 GFLOP/s (0.04x); N=1024 92 vs 2307 (0.04x); N=2048 192 vs 1900 (0.10x). Non-transposed-As fix (reverting my 8-way-conflict write) did NOT help => bank conflict was NOT the dominant cost. ROOT CAUSE = (a) OCCUPANCY STARVATION: 64x64 tile => only (N/64)^2 workgroups (256 at N=1024) vs naive's M*N/256 (4096) => 16x less parallelism for latency hiding (fast GFLOP/s RISES with N as workgroups grow: 47->92->192); (b) LOW ARITHMETIC INTENSITY: 4x4 scalar microtile = 8 shared-reads : 16 FMA (1:2) => shared-bound; naive wins because at N<=2048 the 12-48MB working set is L2-RESIDENT (48MB L2 on 4070 Ti Super) so the naive's B-column reads hit L2 at ~2TF and tiling overhead isn't worth it. FIX = a real GLSL GEMM campaign (same levers as CUDA): vec4 vectorized shared loads + 8x8 register microtile (raise intensity) + enough workgroups + conflict-free shared. The T2 fast tier should NOT be routed as-is (it regresses perf) until optimized. HONEST: 'ported to all backends' = correct+deterministic ONLY; the perf CRUSH is unproven/negative and is the open work. ITERATIONS TRIED (all ~same slow ⇒ inner loop is NOT the bottleneck): (1) transposed-As scalar, (2) non-transposed-As scalar coalesced-write, (3) vec4 `shared vec4` transposed + vec4 outer-product FMA (2 vec4-reads:16 FMA, high intensity) — ALL land 49/97/183 GFLOP/s. So the cause is STRUCTURAL, two parts: (A) EXPECTED — at N<=2048 the working set (<=48MB) is L2-RESIDENT on the 4070 Ti Super, so the naive one-thread-per-output kernel gets full L2-bandwidth reuse (~2TF) and shared-tiling's whole premise (cut global traffic) is MOOT; tiling only wins when working set >> L2 (huge N, DRAM-bound, untested — needs N>=8192 = 768MB buffers). (B) REAL INEFFICIENCY — the tiled kernel is 20x slower not just 'no faster': 64x64 tile => 256 workgroups at N=1024 vs naive's 4096 (16x less occupancy for latency hiding) + K/8 barrier loop. NEXT campaign (needs Nsight-Vulkan/RenderDoc profiling — could NOT diagnose by code-reading, 3 blind iterations failed): profile the actual SPIR-V; test N>=8192 (DRAM regime where tiling should win); fix occupancy (more workgroups: smaller tiles or split-K). ⚠ The T2 Fast tier currently REGRESSES perf at L2-resident sizes — it is opt-in (default=Exact/T1 naive, still fast) so no silent default regression, but Fast should NOT be recommended until the perf campaign lands. The naive precise kernel is genuinely good here. ⭐⭐ RESOLVED (N=4096 DRAM-regime test): the tiled kernel is NOT broken — at N=4096 (192MB working set >> 48MB L2) the naive CRATERS to 150 GFLOP/s (DRAM-bound, no L2 reuse) and the fast tiled kernel hits 333 GFLOP/s = **2.22× CRUSH of naive**. So the full picture: naive wins at N<=2048 (L2-RESIDENT, free reuse, ~2TF) BUT the fast tiled kernel wins 2.22x at N>=4096 (DRAM-bound, where shared-reuse is the whole point). The kernel does exactly what tiling is for. Vulkan board: N=1024 fast/naive 0.05x, N=2048 0.11x, N=4096 2.22x. TWO open items remain: (1) absolute perf at N=4096 is only 333 GFLOP/s — far below CUDA's ~25TF & a good Vulkan GEMM's multi-TF; the occupancy/efficiency campaign (Nsight-Vulkan profiling, more workgroups, deeper pipeline) would push it up. (2) Routing is currently Fast=>tiled always (non-adaptive) => Fast regresses at L2-resident sizes; the right final design is size-adaptive selection (tile when working-set > L2) — documented future improvement. Bench is test_backend_vulkan.cpp 'v17-h PERF' [.bench], N sweep 1024/2048/4096. ⭐ PROFILING INFRA + DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-08, user mandate 'reach CUDA parity, profile till the end'): (1) built KirBackendVulkan::bench_contract(g,out,inputs,n,reps,&ms) — compile pipeline + upload ONCE then GPU-time `reps` WAW-serialized dispatches ⇒ TRUE kernel-only time (excludes SPIR-V compile / driver pipeline JIT / alloc / transfer, all of which run() pays every call). Confirms fast kernel genuinely ~95/175/320 GFLOP/s (NOT a compile artifact — compile hypothesis was wrong). (2) nsys GPU-metrics profiling WORKS headless: `nsys profile --gpu-metrics-devices=0 --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none -o out exe '*PROF*'` (NO --trace=vulkan — that needs admin registry write; GPU metrics don't); export sqlite + query GPU_METRICS join TARGET_INFO_GPU_METRICS. CLEAN fast-kernel-only metrics (N=2048, [.prof] test = bench_contract fast reps=200): SM Issue 1.4% (warps stalled 98.6%!), DRAM R/W 1.2%/1.0% (IDLE — not memory-bound), Compute Warps in Flight 58% (occupancy OK), Tensor 0. DIAGNOSIS: warps resident but not issuing DESPITE 58% occupancy ⇒ they stall TOGETHER at barriers — the 4x4 microtile (32 vec4-FMA between barriers) is too little compute to hide shared-load latency; every warp races to the barrier and waits. FIXES TRIED: single-barrier double-buffer + prefetch-to-register + all-256-threads-load ⇒ NO change (driver doesn't auto-overlap the global load w/ the short compute). NEXT (principled): 8x8 register microtile / 128x128 block (4x FMA per shared read = classic high-perf GEMM), then BK tuning + multi-stage. This is the live campaign — do NOT bank until Vulkan reaches CUDA-backend parity. ITER LOG: (a) 4x4->8x8 register microtile (128x128 block, 256 vec4 shared, double-buffered) => +38% (N=1024/2048/4096 = 127/243/441 GFLOP/s, N=4096 now 3.37x naive), correct. Re-profile (8x8): SM Issue still 1.5%, but Compute Warps in Flight DROPPED 58%->24% + Unallocated Warps 61% => now REGISTER-LIMITED (64 acc/thread kills occupancy). So the tension is explicit: bigger microtile = more compute/barrier (good) but more registers = less occupancy (bad); net +38%. Bottleneck is STILL barrier-stall (issue 1.5%) now compounded by low occupancy. DRAM still idle (1.3%). NEXT LEVERS (profiler-directed): reduce barrier count (bigger BK=16/32 => fewer tiles), register-prefetch the NEXT kk's shared reads inside the inner loop (hide shared latency), find the microtile/occupancy sweet spot (autotune 8x8 vs 8x4 vs 6x6), multi-stage (3-deep) prefetch. Progress is real (320->441 GFLOP/s N=4096) but still ~56x from CUDA's 25TF FP32 — a multi-iteration campaign, now fully instrumented (bench_contract + nsys). Each iter = ~2min build+profile. ⭐⭐ DEEP DIAGNOSIS (nsys ad10x-gfxt set = graphics-throughput metrics, richer than 'General'; + probe experiments): RULED OUT via direct probes — (1) SPIR-V opt level (added shaderc_optimization_level_performance to compile.cpp — NO change; NVIDIA driver re-optimizes SPIR-V regardless; kept the fix, correct + helps other drivers), (2) BARRIERS (stripped both barrier() — NO change, ~3%), (3) UNCOALESCED-A load (made A load contiguous — only +7%), (4) DRAM (VRAM throughput 1.5% idle), (5) OCCUPANCY alone (4x4=58% occ AND 8x8=24% occ both give SM-issue ~1.5%). ROOT CAUSE (ad10x-gfxt): EVERY unit is IDLE — SM 1.5%, FMA-heavy 1.4%, L1 2.1%, L2 2.6%, Shared 1.1%, VRAM 1.5%. Nothing pegged. => PURE LATENCY-BOUND with nothing to hide it: the driver does NOT software-pipeline the tile loads (double-buffer had zero effect => confirmed the compiler won't overlap load w/ compute), so memory/cache latency (L2-hit-from-L1 90% but L2-hit only 46.7% => VRAM-miss latency ~600cyc) is fully exposed, and register-limited occupancy (CS Register Alloc 63.5%, 60% unallocated warps) can't cover it. Core GLSL has NO cp.async/async-copy => can't force the pipelining that CUDA/nvcc does. ⚠ At L2-resident sizes the NAIVE kernel (1x1 microtile, max occupancy, no shared/barriers) is 8x FASTER than the tiled (1021 vs 246 GFLOP/s N=2048) — tiling only wins DRAM-bound (N=4096, 3.34x). FRONTIER: pure-FP32-GLSL CUDA parity is blocked by (a) no async-copy in GLSL + driver not auto-pipelining, (b) register-limited occupancy — an architectural gap vs nvcc. PATH TO PARITY: VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix (tensor path, bypasses this entirely = task #9) OR reproduce a public fast Vulkan GEMM to confirm the ceiling (Order 3). NOT yet crossed; NOT a tile-param problem (all tile levers tried). ⭐⭐ COOPMAT PIVOT (2026-07-08, #9, user 'pivot the parity push to coopmat'): FOUND prior working reference external/coopmat_gemm.comp + coopmat_bench.cpp (Vulkan VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix, fp16-in/fp32-acc, device-local VRAM, driver-scheduled tensor cores; device feature chain = CooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR + VulkanMemoryModel + ShaderFloat16 + 16BitStorage; needs GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix ext + Vulkan 1.3). Iterate loop: edit .comp -> glslc --target-env=vulkan1.3 -> build/coopmat_gemm.spv -> coopmat_bench.exe. RESULT: 10.6 TF fp16 (correct 4.6e-8) = 37x my FP32 tiled kernel (0.28TF), 10x naive, BYPASSES the FP32-latency wall entirely. BUT PLATEAUS at ~10.6 TF across EVERY lever tried (all measured): tile WMxWN {2x4,4x4,2x8,4x2}, block {128,256}, BK {16,32,64}, shared-staging (declared As/Bs were unused=direct-global first cut; added staging = +0.2TF), double-buffer ping-pong (+0), remove inter-dispatch barrier/overlap (+0.3). So 10.6 TF is the genuine single-GEMM throughput = only 15% of CUDA-tensor's 72-79 TF (my wmma2). Profiling (diluted by bench copies): L2 max 99% / VRAM 81% during GEMM => likely mem-bound but reuse opts didn't help => probably the driver's coopMatMulAdd throughput ceiling for the gl_ScopeSubgroup 16x16x16 config. NEXT for parity: VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 (newer ext, larger tiles/less overhead, may close the 7x) OR reproduce a public fast Vulkan coopmat GEMM (Order 3). HONEST OVERALL: full CUDA-backend parity via Vulkan NOT reached — FP32 architecturally blocked (no async-copy), coopmat plateaus 10.6TF (15% of CUDA-tensor). Coopmat 10.6TF is the RIGHT path + a 37x win; the residual 7x is deeper driver-level work. DELIVERABLE: port the 10.6TF coopmat into CKIR as the tensor tier. ⭐⭐⭐ PARITY REACHED via VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 (2026-07-08)! The 10.6TF 'plateau' was a KHR-coopmat (subgroup-scoped, HAND-scheduled) limitation — NOT the hardware. THE FIX: WORKGROUP-SCOPED cooperative matrices (coopmat2). external/coopmat2_gemm.comp declares ONE coopmat<float, gl_ScopeWorkgroup, 128, 128, Accumulator> per workgroup + coopmat<f16,Workgroup,128,16,A>/<16,128,B>, loops K/16 coopMatMulAdd, coopMatStore — the DRIVER owns the ENTIRE 128x128 tile schedule (register blocking, tensor dual-issue, load pipelining) = the cuBLAS-class SASS we could NOT hand-write. RESULT: **67-71 TF @ N=2048, 70 TF @ N=4096, correct 3.8e-8** = 89% of cuBLAS-tensor (79TF) = **PARITY with our CUDA wmma2 (72-79TF)**. 6.7x over KHR coopmat, PORTABLE (Vulkan, NO CUDA). Device: RTX 4070 Ti Super HAS VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 (cm2_query.cpp lists it + the KHR configs). Bench: external/coopmat2_{gemm.comp,bench.cpp}; device needs VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 ext + VkPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrix2FeaturesNV{cooperativeMatrixWorkgroupScope=T, cooperativeMatrixFlexibleDimensions=T} in the feature chain, on top of the KHR-coopmat chain. glslc --target-env=vulkan1.3. LESSON: for portable tensor GEMM, use coopmat2 WORKGROUP scope + let the driver schedule — don't hand-tile subgroup coopmat. NEXT: port coopmat2 workgroup GEMM into CKIR kir-vulkan as the tensor tier (enable the ext/feature in rhi-vulkan device creation); fan out to the analogous ext on DX12(WaveMatrix)/Metal(simdgroup_matrix)/WebGPU(subgroups-f16). ⭐ PORTED INTO CKIR (2026-07-08, #9 Vulkan done): (1) rhi-vulkan device creation (vulkan_backend.cpp ~L3762) now enables VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix + VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 + 16BitStorage/ShaderFloat16/VulkanMemoryModel + CooperativeMatrix2FeaturesNV{workgroupScope,flexibleDimensions}, GUARDED by dev_has() (absent adapter => tensor tier just unavailable). find_package(Vulkan) => SDK 1.4.341 headers HAVE coopmat2. (2) emit_contract_coopmat2_glsl (ckir_glsl.hpp) — the workgroup-scoped shader, push-constant M/K/N, 2D dispatch. (3) KirBackendVulkan::bench_tensor(g,out,inputs,n,reps,out,&ms) — fp32->fp16 f2h upload to DEVICE-LOCAL VRAM (+ staging; host-visible was 380x slower/BAR-starved) => coopmat2 dispatch => copy C back. shaderc compiles coopmat2 fine. VALIDATED: test_backend_vulkan.cpp 'v17-h TENSOR coopmat2' => 32 TF through CKIR @ N=2048, maxrel 1.09e-3 (fp16), full suite 32928 assns green (no regress). 32 TF = 30x naive / 110x FP32-tiled, but ~2.3x BELOW the 70 TF standalone — NOT barrier/spirv-opt/dispatch-shape (all ruled out); residual is an RHI-device-path overhead (likely the ValidationCapture validation layer the KIR device attaches, which the raw-Vulkan standalone lacks) => follow-up. ⭐⭐⭐ 2.3x CLOSED => FULL PARITY THROUGH CKIR (2026-07-08): the 32-vs-70 TF gap was NOT the RHI/validation/barrier/dispatch-shape — it was PUSH-CONSTANT vs SPECIALIZATION dims. The standalone bakes M/N/K as spec constants (constant_id) => driver specializes the coopmat loop (known trip count K, known strides N, unrolled). My CKIR emitter used push_constant K/N (runtime) => generic un-specialized coopmat code => 2.3x slower. FIX: emit_contract_coopmat2_glsl now BAKES kdim/ndim as GLSL literals (per-shape shader) + removed the push constant entirely (pipeline layout has 0 push ranges). RESULT: 70856 GFLOP/s = 70.9 TF THROUGH CKIR @ N=2048, maxrel 1.09e-3 = EXACT parity with the standalone (68-71) = ~90% cuBLAS-tensor = CUDA wmma2 parity, PORTABLE. LESSON: for coopmat/tensor kernels, dims MUST be compile-time (spec-const or baked literal), never push-constant — worth 2.3x. ⚠ DESIGN DEBT (user flagged): KirBackendVulkan::bench_contract/bench_tensor carry reps+out_ms TIMING in the production backend — that is measurement scaffolding (needed because run() recompiles the pipeline every call, so fair kernel timing needs compile-once/dispatch-many). CLEAN design = pipeline CACHE in run() (compile once, reuse) + route the tensor tier through run() + move perf timing to a test/tooling harness. NEXT: that cleanup, then fan out tensor tier to DX12(WaveMatrix)/Metal(simdgroup_matrix)/WebGPU."

**v17-g CUDA FP32 SGEMM vs cuBLAS (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, N=2048, clock-locked 2610).** Full journey +
every kernel: `docs/bench/2026-07-08-v17g-gemm-nsight-loop.md` (Steps 0–17), lab = `external/gemm_lab.cu` (modes 0–15:
mode 10 = cuBLAS baseline, 13 = mainloop, 15 = 256×128 dyn-shared).

**Result: ~24.9 TF avg = ~88% of cuBLAS (range 82-89% across runs; cuBLAS ~28.2 avg), bit-exact vs our own naive FMA
kernel (NOT vs a true fp oracle).** NOT the phantom 40 TF I chased — cuBLAS FP32 SGEMM only hits ~65% of the 44 TF FMA
peak (bandwidth-bound). **⚠ POST-AUDIT CORRECTIONS (do not repeat the old overstatements):** (a) it's ~88% not a flat 89%,
quote the RANGE; (b) **we BEAT siboehm's published kernel ON THIS GPU** — ran his exact k10 config (mode 6), ~23 TF vs our
~25; his 93-96% is an A6000 number, cross-GPU, never applied here — so "below the public best / Order-3-not-satisfied" is
RETRACTED, we're above it on this card; (c) **cuBLAS's kernel is runtime-JIT-compiled** — searched cublasLt(463MB)+cublas64
(52MB), sm_80+sm_89: the fp32 simt_sgemm_256x128 is NOT a static symbol, so `cuobjdump`-on-DLL can't reach it (verified, not
assumed); (d) "cuBLAS denser" = its FMA-pipe 78% vs our 64% (ncu, both measured on the LIVE kernel) — I only disassembled
OURS (71% FFMA); never had cuBLAS's instruction mix. (e) **"clock-locked 2610" was NOT a real lock** (needs admin -lgc; I
only read it) → N=2048 baseline moves ±10-15%. (f) I compared only ONE of THREE vendor entry points (cublasSgemm PEDANTIC/
DEFAULT/cublasLtMatmul — honest bar = min of all 3). (g) **⛔ PRIOR WORK `docs/hints/v17-kir-gpu-gotchas.md` (v17-e/g,
2026-07-07) already did this MORE rigorously — I re-derived it without reading it (process failure).** It found REPRODUCIBLE
CRUSHES at **N=1024 (RAW 1.06×, SiLU 1.13×, ReLU 1.20×, all 6 runs)** + N=512 fused-ReLU 1.06×; N=2048 too clock-variable to
claim; tensor crush needs raw `mma.sync`+`ldmatrix` PTX (wmma caps ~0.6-0.7×); fused-SiLU epilogue = structural crush lever
(SiLU is OFF cublasLt's menu, every LLM MLP). **HONEST COMPOSITE: ~88% at clock-unreliable N=2048, but we ALREADY CRUSH
cuBLAS at N=1024. READ v17-kir-gpu-gotchas.md BEFORE any GEMM work.** The [feedback_never_invoke_a_wall_a_peer_already_beat](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_never_invoke_a_wall_a_peer_already_beat) mandate
(`docs/KERNEL-CRUSH-MANDATE.md`) WORKED: **Order 1 (pin the target) instantly debunked the phantom** — I'd falsely claimed
"58% is the ceiling / SASS wall" and was flogging against a number that doesn't exist. Retracted.

**What got built + PROVEN (each by ncu counters):** warptiling (short_scoreboard 0.90→0.11) · cp.async (long_scoreboard
0.46→0.02) · float4-fragment XOR-swizzled A-read (bank conflicts 235M→9K) · multi-stage pipeline · register-lean 256×128
(fits 255-reg cap via WMITER=1) · batched-B pure-FMA · full unroll. The 256×128 config **structurally MATCHES cuBLAS**:
219 vs 202 regs, 16.6% occupancy, all stalls <0.2.

**The residual (89%→100%) — Order-3 TESTED by `cuobjdump -sass`:** our inner loop is **71% FFMA** (14,109 FFMA / 19,752
instr); the ~29% overhead = XOR-swizzle bit-ops (798 SHF/LOP/PRMT) + register MOVs/addressing that ptxas emits and
cuBLAS's hand-tuned SASS does not. FMA pipe 63.9% vs cuBLAS ~78%. **This is SASS instruction-density — measured, not
assumed.** We're a few pts below siboehm's public ~93–96%, so NO absolute wall claimed; the last few % is matching
cuBLAS's exact register-alloc/schedule (hand-tuned-SASS frontier CUDA-C reaches ~90% of).

**The crush we DO hold (cuBLAS can't):** bit-exact determinism + portability across 6 backends.

**v17-h — CHANGE-THE-GAME experiments (2026-07-08, `docs/bench/2026-07-08-v17h-research-crush.md`) — NONE is a clean crush,
each a NARROW regime win with caveats (be honest):** (1) **error-corrected tensor GEMM** (Ozaki fp16-limb split, rides
cuBLAS's OWN tensor kernel as primitive): tensor = 2.7× fp32 this card. Ozaki-2 = 38.5 TF @ 2.5e-5 = 1.32× cuBLAS-fp32 BUT
25× less accurate, and cuBLAS-tensor (79 TF) is 2× faster than it — a NICHE Pareto point, not a crush; "3-5× datacenter"
is UNMEASURED extrapolation. `external/tensor_lab.cu`. (2) **Strassen** 1-level: 1.12× ONLY @ N=16384 (loses <8192, ~20×
worse accuracy, single-run, rides cuBLAS base case). `external/strassen_lab.cu`. (3) **fusion**: 2.50× but fused-vs-unfused
of OUR OWN elementwise chain — NOT vs cuBLAS (it can't express it). `external/fused_lab.cu`. Real capabilities worth having;
not headline cuBLAS crushes.
**Mission-optimal next:** port the 89% base GEMM + these 3 techniques into CKIR GLSL/HLSL/WGSL/Metal emitters as portable
capabilities (coopmat tensor path, algorithmic Strassen, op-graph fusion). Do NOT re-chase FP32 SGEMM SASS — documented.

**hesap v5c Multifrontal QR (SPQR/Algorithm-915-class) — core LANDED 2026-06-01, correctness-first + verified; the perf crush vs SPQR remains.** New `engine/hesap-direct/.../multifrontal_qr.{hpp,cpp}` (`MultifrontalQR<T>:IFactorization`, f32/f64). Dossier `docs/research/cerid-hesap-v5c-multifrontal-qr.md`.

**Key design (advisor-validated):**
- **QR fronts ARE chol(AᵀA) supernodes** ⇒ REUSE the proven v5a `symbolic_factorize`+`build_supernodal_symbolic` on an explicitly-formed AᵀA pattern (correctness-first; the AᵀA-free implicit leftmost-merge is the perf follow-on).
- **QR is NOT the v5a `extend_add`** — contribution-block COLUMNS map ⊆ parent (verified by the symbolic test) but ROWS are APPENDED ⇒ QR uses a COLUMN-MAJOR front + scatter-PLACE/row-append assembly. `extend_add` stays correct for v5d LDLᵀ (symmetric, rows match by id). [project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm](project-history.md#memory-project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm) is the sibling LU.
- `struct(R)⊆struct(chol(AᵀA))`, equality only strong-Hall ⇒ tests assert `⊆` not `==`; the `Σ colcount`+etree match vs `column_counts_ata`/`column_elimination_tree` is a two-PATH cross-check, NOT a tightness claim.
- **Solve = implicit Qᵀ re-walk of the assembly tree in the SAME canonical row order** (own rows then children in front-tree order) carrying a per-front row workspace — NO HPinv array needed, provenance is in the symbolic; then back-sub the CSR R. Determinism moat = the fixed row-stacking order.
- Gotcha fixed: taking `&array[off]` when `off==size()` (empty trailing region, e.g. a root front's empty contribution) trips the bounds-checked `operator[]` — use `array.data()+off`.

**SURPRISE (the honest scoreboard): the multifrontal+no-pivot QR CRUSHES Eigen `SparseQR` even UNBLOCKED/serial** — bcsstk13 FACTOR 9.07×/SOLVE 2.65× (R fill 0.46×), bcsstk24 48.1×/12.9× (fill 0.17×), both more accurate. Eigen `SparseQR` is left-looking column-by-column with **numerical column pivoting that WRECKS the fill-reducing order** (R 2–6× denser) — a weak header peer (like the v5a Eigen-SimplicialLLT was). **The real gold standard = SuiteSparseQR/SPQR** (multifrontal + blocked-WY + MT + LAPACK); beating it needs the perf levers.

**BLOCKED-WY LANDED 2026-06-01 (v5c-1d, the 1st perf lever) — size-gated compact-WY front factor:** large fronts (≥64 rows) panel the npiv pivots into nb=48 sub-panels + ONE BLAS-3 larfb `C:=(I−V·Tᵀ·Vᵀ)·C` (W=VᵀC; W=TᵀW; C=C−VW) via the COLUMN-MAJOR `dense::gemm` (Trans) + `build_block_t_from_vtv` (dlarft); small fronts keep the unblocked path (no gemm-call overhead ⇒ no regression). Reused the column-major front (assembly+solve unchanged) instead of relaying out for the row-major `apply_q_block`. **IMPROVED the crush, zero regression: bcsstk13 9.07→13.3×, bcsstk24 48.1→70.6× factor; verified win-debug 14 cases/5353 asserts (+dense-150×100 one-front-3-sub-panel RᵀR + LS test) + clang-cl clean.** Gotcha: V is extracted unit-lower-trapezoidal per sub-panel (the front column's upper part holds R, not 0); VᵀV symmetric so layout moot.

**bcsstk25 (15k) is NOT a bug/hang (user asked) — QR-fill-bound: measured 208 CPU-s + 1.5 GB.** nnz(chol(AᵀA))≫nnz(chol(A)) (AᵀA squares the fill) ⇒ GB factor storage; bcsstk25 is SQUARE SPD = the WRONG tool for QR (use Cholesky). Amplified ×3 by best-of-3 + explicit-AᵀA-per-rep + all-fronts-resident (no stack). Dropped from default bench corpus.

**RECTANGULAR-LS BENCH (QR's real domain) — PREMISE-CHECK that REFUTED the levers (advisor+user "measure first" before building 600 lines):** added the HB LS set (well/illc 1033/1850), generalized the bench to m×n least_squares. **Eigen CRUSHED on its home turf: well1033 6.81× · illc1033 7.13× · well1850 36.6× · illc1850 36.8× FACTOR (solve 3–6×), Cerid R fill 0.07–0.24× of Eigen, resid 2e-15…3e-13.** These factor in 0.4–1.3 ms with TINY fill (2.7–8.3K Rnnz) ⇒ **the AᵀA-free-symbolic + front-stack levers are NOT the bottleneck on the real target** — the bcsstk25 1.5 GB was 100% the wrong-tool square-SPD artifact. LEVERS DEFERRED (premise-check vindicated, ~600 core-touching lines saved). LESSON: when an optimization is motivated by ONE matrix you've flagged as unrepresentative, MEASURE the real target before building (`feedback_benchmarks_mandatory_at_slice_close`).

**Eigen SparseQR = CRUSHED on BOTH domains (rectangular LS 7–37× + square 13–71×).**
