**v5c-1e AᵀA-FREE IMPLICIT SYMBOLIC DONE 2026-06-02 (oracle-safe; all 6 SPQR factor ratios improved; the predicted flip did NOT land).** New `ordering::symbolic_factorize_ata(A)` in `symbolic.cpp` — etree+counts+per-supernode `slead` of chol(AᵀA) **without forming AᵀA**: reuses implicit `column_elimination_tree`+`column_counts_ata`+`fundamental_supernodes_i32`, emits `slead` via the SAME recurrence as `symbolic_factorize(…,true)` with `adj_AᵀA(fc)` gathered implicitly from A's rows (CSC col fc → rows → CSR row cols). `multifrontal_qr_symbolic` calls it; `ata_pattern`+explicit path kept as the **bit-for-bit oracle** (new `[v5c-1e]` test, 4 shapes, asserts parent/post/colcount/lp/super/slead identical ⇒ can't break the solve). **APPROACH DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT (advisor caught it):** the dossier's "Option A" (`build_ata_adjacency`→`symbolic_factorize`) KEEPS the clique-union (the genuinely AᵀA-sized O(Σnnz_row²) work) — it only removes `build_adjacency`'s transpose. A 3-bucket symbolic sub-split (throwaway timers in `bench_hesap_qr_vs_reference`) showed the **clique-union DOMINATES (66%/86% on well1033/bcsstk13)**, `build_adjacency` 7–9% ⇒ Option A insufficient; the **true leftmost-merge** (removes clique-union) was required. Implicit etree+counts measured cheap (bcsstk13 clique-union 10.9 ms → 0.40 ms, 27×) ⇒ de-risked; adj-gather did NOT leak p² (bcsstk13 symbolic 12 → 1.36 ms; well1033 → 0.07 ms). **VERIFIED win-debug (direct 597051/72, ordering 7771/44) + 5 guards + clang-cl + gcc -Werror (WSL `~/cerid-build/linux-gcc-release` reconfigured `-DCRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_SPQR=ON -DCRD_HESAP_MATRIX_DIR=<win-vs-ref matrices>`).** **HONEST SPQR scoreboard (serial-fair ×2): all 6 factor ratios IMPROVED — well1033 0.82→0.91–0.94× · illc1033 0.80→0.90× · well1850 0.60→0.64× · illc1850 0.60→0.67× · bcsstk13 0.40→0.50× · bcsstk24 0.48→0.63×; solve 3.4–8.5× WIN; resid matches — but the predicted well/illc1033 FLIP did NOT land.** ⚠⚠ **CORRECTION to the dossier §10.1 "AᵀA-free symbolic flips well/illc1033 by itself" claim — IT WAS OPTIMISTIC:** based on cerid-num (0.22) < a STALE 0.27 SPQR sample, and IGNORED the residual ~0.07 ms symbolic floor (now `build_supernodal_symbolic`+row-merge+slead, NOT the AᵀA tax). Reality: cerid-num (0.21) does beat SPQR-*total* (0.25), but residual symbolic + a faster SPQR sample (0.25) keep cerid total at 0.28 > 0.25; the ~0.03 ms gap is **at the run-to-run noise floor** ⇒ characterized as **at-parity (num-competitive), NOT chased** (a "win" from shaving 0.03 ms off 0.28 ms is a tie). **v5c-1f does NOT target the 1033 flip** (category error — staircase hits WIDE near-root fronts, not the tiny 1033 fronts). FULL-VICTORY lives in the **numeric-bound** matrices: bcsstk13/24 (num 57 vs SPQR 29) + well/illc1850 (num 0.90 vs SPQR-total 0.70) = v5c-1f's staircase/blocked-GEQRF scope. v5c-1f probe (`Σ fm·nc` vs `Σ(Stair_k−k)`) predicted to register on bcsstk/1850, stay flat on 1033 (confirming the regime split). WIP, not committed.

**v5c-1f ASSEMBLY SCATTER-MAP DONE 2026-06-02 → 🎉 FIRST SPQR FACTOR WINS.** THREE throwaway measure-first probes, two refutations + one win (the durable lesson = measure, don't reason from code shape): **(1) STAIRCASE REFUTED** — the probe (`Σ(fm−k)(fsz−k)` vs `Σ(Stair_k−k)(fsz−k)` on the REAL assembled fronts) came out the OPPOSITE of the predicted geometry: the matrices that matter sit at **1.08–1.16×** (bcsstk13 1.13, bcsstk24 1.08, well/illc1850 1.16) ≪ the 1.9× gate; only the noise-floor 1033s hit 1.70×. ⇒ the row-merge staircase (touches the solve's canonical row order — riskiest change) is NOT worth it. The advisor's "registers on wide near-root fronts" guess was WRONG; structural matrices are near-dense (rows enter early ⇒ tiny staircase), tall-thin rectangular has the staircase but that's the noise-floor case. **(2) PANEL BLAS-2 REFUTED** — same-platform kernel split: the within-sub-panel BLAS-1 reflector loop is 66–87% of the kernel on rectangular-LS home turf; converting it to LAPACK-`dlarf` form (`dense::gemv`+`ger`) was **2–4× SLOWER** (well1850 num 0.90→3.57 ms) — dense gemv/ger per-call overhead (~1.9µs × thousands of tiny panel reflectors) dwarfs the work; **the hand-rolled dot+axpy loop is already an inlined fused dlarf** and stays. ⇒ NOT a BLAS-2 problem. **(3) THE WIN = ASSEMBLY scatter overhead (the UNMEASURED third thing — advisor caught that my cross-platform "0.35ms assembly" subtraction was invalid):** a SAME-PLATFORM (WSL/gcc) phase split {csr, assembly, kernel, rbuild} showed **assembly = 41% of the home-turf numeric (0.35 ms) = the per-nonzero `find_col` BINARY SEARCH** (O(log fsz) per scattered nonzero, own rows + child contributions), and the SPQR deficit on well1850 was EXACTLY ~0.37 ms (SPQR assembles too + still totals 0.69ms ⇒ unoptimized overhead, NOT a wall). FIX = replace `find_col` with an **O(1) scatter map** `col_pos[global col]→local pos in fn` (set per front over `fn`; NO reset — only cols ⊆ fn are read, guaranteed by the symbolic; `CRD_ASSERT_MSG(fn[col_pos[c]]==c)` guards staleness; removed the `find_col` helper). **HONEST SPQR scoreboard (WSL serial-fair ×2, EVERY ratio UP, zero regression): well1033 0.91→1.06–1.16× WIN · illc1033 0.90→1.12–1.17× WIN (FIRST SPQR FACTOR WINS) · well1850 0.64→0.87–0.96× · illc1850 0.67→0.93–0.95× (near-parity, was 0.60 @v5c-1d) · bcsstk13 0.50→0.71–0.76× · bcsstk24 0.63→0.91×; solve still 4.0–8.6× WIN; resid matches.** well/illc1850 bounce at near-parity (spread = gap-to-1.0; residual = the v5c-1e symbolic floor [`build_supernodal_symbolic`+row-merge — CHECKED, it's linear sorted-merge NOT a find_col pattern ⇒ no cheap scatter-map win there] + a faster SPQR sample) ⇒ characterized, not chased. **bcsstk13/24 (square SPD = WRONG TOOL for QR; use Cholesky) = CHARACTERIZED accepted loss: 83–88% larfb-gemm = the [project_hesap_gemm_asm_reopen_and_bmwcra_kernel_ceiling](project-history.md#memory-project_hesap_gemm_asm_reopen_and_bmwcra_kernel_ceiling) / ADR-0082 BLAS-kernel wall** (Cerid intrinsic gemm vs OpenBLAS asm); the determinism moat + solve-crush + Eigen-crush (both domains) stand. **CONFIG GATE: win-debug (5393 `[v5c]`) + clang-cl + win-asan (raw-index scatter map OOB-clean) + win-tidy (clang-tidy 20.1.8 — scatter map clean; FIXED 4 PRE-EXISTING v5c issues surfaced on first tidy run: `qr_panel_w`/`qr_block_min`→`kQrPanelW`/`kQrBlockMin` [anon-namespace constexpr = global-const ⇒ kCamelCase], `rn`→`rnum` confusable-with-`m`, nested ternary→if/else) + gcc `-Werror` (WSL).** OWED (v5c COMPLETENESS, separate slice, framed as completeness NOT crush — parallel-Cerid-vs-serial-SPQR = the forbidden asterisk): cross-front tree-parallel + determinism moat {1,2,4,8} (v5a/v5b carry it). Then v5c-2 (rank-reveal Heath + complex Qᴴ + CLI). WIP, not committed.

**v5c-1g CROSS-FRONT TREE-PARALLEL + DETERMINISM MOAT DONE 2026-06-02 (user said "intrinsics in parity with asm so no worries" ⇒ accepted the bcsstk gemm wall, proceed).** Mirror of v5b-3c multifrontal LU: level-scheduled the assembly tree (`level[f]=1+max(child level)` computed in the `front_post` postorder; group ascending-f per level ⇒ worker-order-independent = moat) + refactored the pass-2 body into a `factor_front(f,wk)` lambda with **per-worker scratch** (vbuf/vtv/tblk/wbuf/col_pos as DISJOINT `worker_index()`-keyed slices of one pool each, sized by `jobs::num_workers()` — feedback_jobs_worker_index_aliasing) + per-level `jobs::parallel_for`+`wait`+`frame_reset` (serial path when `num_workers≤1`). The larfb gemms pass **`scratch=nullptr` → per-thread pooled GrowableTlsf** (thread-safe + result-identical — the sanctioned view-form-gemm path; NOT m_alloc which would race). Added `num_workers` param to `factorize`/`factor_multifrontal_qr` (default 0=serial; benches stay serial — honest serial comparison; moat test passes {1,2,4,8}). **FRONT-PARALLEL ONLY** — deliberately dropped the LU's hybrid/node-parallel/front_par_thresh machinery: the home-turf LS matrices factor in <1 ms (no wall-clock to chase) and parallel-Cerid-vs-serial-SPQR is the forbidden asterisk ([feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards)) ⇒ the deliverable is the MOAT + completeness, NOT speed. **RACE-FREEDOM (advisor's discriminator, verified by reading the assembly loop): a QR front's `m_fb` is read ONLY by its direct `front_parent`** (the assembly reads `m_child[cc]` blocks + the symbolic guarantees each child's contribution cols ⊆ its DIRECT parent's fn — the contribution edge IS the front_parent edge, NOT an ancestor like the LUson/Lson LU case) ⇒ the per-level `wait` barrier dominates all readers. The `col_pos` no-reset trick is safe per-worker (disjoint slice; reads ⊆ its own freshly-set fn). **MOAT PROVEN (`[v5c-1g]` test): R + Rj/Rx + the least-squares solution BIT-IDENTICAL across {1,2,4,8} workers at BOTH f32 and f64** (block-diagonal matrix = 4 independent banded arms ⇒ a level with ≥4 CONCURRENT fronts ⇒ per-worker scratch isolation genuinely exercised; f32 chosen — float reassociation is where worker-count drift surfaces first). No SPQR/Eigen carries cross-thread bit-exact factors = the standing differentiator. **VERIFIED 5 configs: win-debug (full suite 597087/73) + clang-cl + win-asan (per-worker scratch OOB-clean under parallel) + win-tidy + gcc `-Werror`.** OWED before v5c commit: gcc/asan/shipping full-sweep (CI). NEXT = v5c-2 (rank-reveal Heath + complex Qᴴ + CLI) — **DELIBERATELY NOT started at the v5c-1g session tail (advisor: complex-conjugation correctness in factor+solve = highest bug-risk in the cluster, fatigue eats that class; clean checkpoint > half-built v5c-2).** Full warm plan in session doc `docs/sessions/2026-06-02-hesap-v5c-1-multifrontal-qr.md` § "v5c-2 PLAN": **2a complex UNBLOCKED-ONLY** (blocked-WY-complex = perf follow-on — `build_block_t_from_vtv`/gemm-ConjTranspose need a conj-aware variant, REAL work not a small if-constexpr; complex conjugation DERIVED: factor applies Hᴴ=I−conj(tau)·v·vᴴ, dot uses conj(v), scale=conj(tau)·s, update uses v un-conjugated, R-diag=real beta; same form in the solve Qᴴ re-walk — VERIFY FIRST), **2b Heath rank-reveal** (real, no pivoting, preserves fill+moat), **2c CLI** `hesap.direct.qr.{f32,f64,c32,c64}`+dispatcher. WIP, not committed.

**v5c-2a COMPLEX QR DONE 2026-06-02 (the user said "keep going now" with full picture).** Complex32/Complex64, Qᴴ-apply, UNBLOCKED-only. `make_householder_complex` (zlarfg: Hᴴx=β·e₀, β real, τ complex) + a `qr_conj<T>` (identity for real / `crd::hesap::conj` for complex, mirrors `chol_conj`) + `qr_from_real<T>` (β→T{β,0} complex / β real). The reflector apply in BOTH the factor panel loop AND the solve's Qᴴ re-walk is ONE `if constexpr` path: complex dot `s=Σ qr_conj(v_i)·c_i` (=vᴴc), scalar `s*=qr_conj(τ)`, the v-tail update `c_i−=s·v_i` stays UN-conjugated, R-diag `colk[0]=qr_from_real(β)`. **THE DERIVED CONJUGATION WAS CORRECT** — empirically verified: `[v5c-2a]` test asserts RᴴR==AᴴA on GENUINELY-complex values (nonzero im ⇒ distinguishes Qᵀ from Qᴴ; would fail if wrong) + complex least-squares recovers complex x_true, Complex32+Complex64. **Real path BYTE-IDENTICAL** (every qr_conj is a no-op for real; `s*=qr_conj(τ)` ≡ `s*=τ`; IEEE mul commutes bit-exact) ⇒ the determinism moat is UNCHANGED. Complex stays UNBLOCKED: `blocked=false` for complex + the compact-WY larfb wrapped in `if constexpr(!is_complex_v<T>)` so it never instantiates for complex (avoids the real-τ `build_block_t_from_vtv` + `T{1}`-for-Complex questions); blocked-WY-complex is the perf follow-on. Complex moat {1,2,4,8} bit-identical too (`run_qr_parallel_moat<Complex32/64>`). **VERIFIED 5 configs:** win-debug (5529/17) + clang-cl + win-asan + win-tidy + gcc `-Werror` (caught `R{double_literal}` narrowings in the test → `static_cast<R>` per CLAUDE.md). REMAINING v5c-2: **2b Heath rank-reveal** (real, no pivoting — meaty, fresh) + **2c CLI** `hesap.direct.qr.{f32,f64,c32,c64}`+dispatcher (mechanical). WIP, not committed.

**v5c-2b RANK-REVEALING (Heath) DONE 2026-06-02.** NO column pivoting ⇒ preserves the fill order + the determinism moat (SPQR's key trick). **KEY realization: detection is a pure function of the FINAL R diagonals** — in no-pivot multifrontal QR a rank-deficient pivot column just produces a ~0 R-diagonal; the contribution block + assembly are STRUCTURALLY UNAFFECTED ⇒ the factor needs NO special-casing (no per-front dead handling). After the R-build, a SERIAL scan (r=0..n-1, FIXED order ⇒ dead set is worker-count-invariant since R is bit-identical across workers ⇒ moat-safe) finds max|R diag|; a pivot with `|R[r][r]| ≤ rcond·max` (rcond=max(m,n)·eps, LAPACK convention) — or a structural no-pivot column — is DEAD. New `rank()` (=#live) + `dead()` (per-column u8 flags) accessors + `m_dead`/`m_rank` members + `qr_abs<T>` helper (|x|, real+complex). Least-squares returns the **BASIC solution**: back-sub skips dead rows (x[dead]=T{}, no divide by ~0 diagonal), live rows back-substitute (dead cols contribute 0). **Folded structural (i>=npiv) + numerical into ONE dead set; DROPPED the old `m_info=r+1`-flags-deficiency path → m_info≡0 (rank deficiency is normal, query rank()); AUDITED the lone `m_info!=0` reader (the least_squares early-out) ⇒ full-rank behaviour unchanged.** ⚠ ADVISOR CORRECTION (load-bearing): the basic solution's normal-equation optimality `‖Aᵀr‖≈0` holds only to **O(tol·‖A‖)**; ≈machine-eps holds ONLY for EXACT deficiency — do NOT assert `Aᵀr==0` on a numerically-deficient matrix (flaky). So the `[v5c-2b]` test uses an integer column literally = sum of two others (FP-EXACT dependence): rank()==3, the dependent col (eliminated last) flagged dead, x[dead]=0, ‖Ax−b‖ & ‖Aᵀr‖ ≈ eps; + a separate no-false-positive case (a legit-small 1e-6 diagonal ≫ rcond·max ⇒ stays live, rank()==n). Min-norm (full sparse COD / Heath stage-2) = documented follow-on (basic solution is the legitimate v5c-2b deliverable). **VERIFIED 5 configs (win-debug 5542/19 + clang-cl + win-asan + win-tidy + gcc `-Werror`) + NO bench regression (SPQR full-rank corpus residuals + factor ratios IDENTICAL — detection is conservative, cond(illc)~1e4 ≪ 1/tol~1e12, zero false positives).** REMAINING v5c-2: **2c CLI** `hesap.direct.qr.{f32,f64,c32,c64}`+dispatcher (mechanical, all 4 types now exist). WIP, not committed.

**v5c-2c CLI DONE 2026-06-02 + a latent v5c-2a COMPLEX-SQUARE FACTOR BUG caught & fixed (the CLI test earned its keep).** Registered the 4 QR commands in `cli_register_direct.cpp` (mirrors chol/lu CLI; complex values+RHS flattened {re,im}; schema rows≥cols, COO triplets, RHS b length m). The CLI calls `least_squares({b,m},{x,n},1)` UNIFORMLY for square+over-determined (separate b/x, no aliasing — simpler + avoids the in-place square `solve()` aliasing path). Output blob = `[info, rank, x...]` (the rank-revealing report; note the 2-value header vs chol/lu's `[info, x...]`). +4 CLI tests (registration, square f64, over-determined f64 LS, complex c64). **⚠⚠ The complex-SQUARE CLI test FAILED (errors up to 0.28) — exposing a LATENT v5c-2a bug:** the complex factor was only tested OVER-DETERMINED (14×7), so the **len==1 last reflector** (on an exactly-determined front, fm==npiv, e.g. a square single front) was never hit. That path calls `make_householder_complex(colk, 1)` whose **n≤1 branch returns β=Re(α)** (β is real-typed in `HouseholderComplex`), so `colk[0]=qr_from_real(β)` DROPPED the imaginary part of the last R diagonal ⇒ RᴴR≠AᴴA (err 0.25 on a 4×4). A focused `[v5c-2a]` 4×4 RᴴR==AᴴA diagnostic isolated it to the FACTOR (not the solve). **FIX (in multifrontal_qr factor): treat `len≤1` as a TRIVIAL reflector — `tau=T{}`, R[k][k]=colk[0] left as-is (complex preserved), no apply.** Correct + REAL BIT-IDENTICAL (β==colk[0] for real len==1 ⇒ moat unchanged; verified). Did NOT touch the shared `make_householder_complex` (used by zgehd2/zhetd2 — riskier). Regression cover: the 4×4 complex RᴴR diagnostic + the complex-square CLI test. **VERIFIED 5 configs (win-debug FULL suite 597256/81 + clang-cl + win-asan + win-tidy + gcc `-Werror`).** **v5c-2 COMPLETE (2a complex · 2b rank-reveal · 2c CLI).** LESSON: a "done" sub-slice tested on only ONE shape (rectangular) can hide a bug on another (square exactly-determined) — the CLI's square test caught what the unit tests missed.

**v5c-close LOCAL DONE 2026-06-02 — v5c is a COMMIT BOUNDARY (like v5a/v5b), ready for the v5c commit + the 18-config CI sweep.** Advisor-scoped (don't over-do the close at session tail; defer to v5z what v5a/v5b deferred): **(1) determinism moat extended to {1,2,4,8,16}** (R+Rj/Rx+solution bit-identical, real+complex; honestly POOL-CAPPED — num_workers is the parallel_for hint, scratch is pool-sized, so 16 over-requests on a smaller pool ⇒ proves WORKER-COUNT INVARIANCE not 16-way concurrency). **(2) completeness audit** (all 4 types f32/f64/c32/c64 × factor/solve/least_squares/rank/dead/CLI/moat ✅; honest deferred-not-hidden gaps: blocked-WY-complex + min-norm rank-deficient = follow-ons). **(3) HONEST FINAL SCOREBOARD:** vs Eigen CRUSHED both domains (LS 7–37×/square 13–71×); vs SPQR SOLVE crushed 4–8.6× everywhere, FACTOR well/illc1033 WIN + well/illc1850 near-parity (0.87–0.96×, was 0.60) + bcsstk13/24 square-SPD CHARACTERIZED loss (0.71–0.91×, ADR-0082 BLAS-kernel wall, wrong-tool-for-QR, user-accepted "intrinsics in parity w/ asm") — a SPLIT not a clean factor-crush; the determinism moat (no SPQR/Eigen carries it) is the differentiator. **DEFERRED to v5z** (the full-v5 close, written ONCE for the whole direct cluster — v5a/v5b also deferred these): `docs/systems/hesap-direct.md` (chol+lu+qr+ldlt+…), ADR-0065 §27 D(direct)-1..N lock, all-families end-to-end moat, rank-deficient+complex bench (honest scope: rank-agreement+factor/residual, NOT a min-norm crush since SPQR does min-norm + we ship basic). **The v5c COMMIT's REAL GATE = the 18-config CI sweep** (the 6 slices v5c-1e/1f/1g/2a/2b/2c only saw targeted per-module builds: win-debug+clang-cl+win-asan+win-tidy+1 gcc-release; CI must prove win-shipping/win-release-LTCG/scalar/SSE2 + 7×Linux — where cross-config SIMD/-Werror/LTCG breakage hides). **hesap v5d — Multifrontal LDLᵀ (symmetric INDEFINITE), the sparse-direct twin of v5a Cholesky for non-SPD symmetric (saddle-point/KKT/FE-contact). A=P·L·D·Lᵀ·Pᵀ, D block-diagonal 1×1/2×2 (Bunch-Kaufman).** Sibling of [project_v5c_multifrontal_qr](project-history.md#memory-project_v5c_multifrontal_qr) / [project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm](project-history.md#memory-project_lu_umfpack_gap_is_mc64_not_gemm).

**KEY: most of v5d is REUSE.** The LDLᵀ front tree IS the chol(A) supernode tree (symmetric pattern) ⇒ reuse v5b-3's `build_symmetric_multifrontal_symbolic` + `MfFront<T>` (col-major front) + `mf_extend_add` (assembly; containment = Cholesky theorem) + the tree-parallel level scheduler. Dense `dense::LDLT` (Bunch-Kaufman 1×1/2×2, `factor_ldlt`/`solve_ldlt`, `block_kinds`) is the dense reference. **The ONLY genuinely-new algorithm = the per-front INDEFINITE factor (1×1/2×2) + the moat + delayed pivots.**

**MOAT design (decided):** within-front Bunch-Kaufman is a DETERMINISTIC pure function of the front ⇒ L,D bit-identical across worker counts via the fixed postorder assembly — the SAME mechanism as v5a/b/c, NO global static pivoting needed. Duff-Reid DELAYED PIVOTS (a front whose fully-summed block is singular/ill-conditioned pushes the pivot to its parent; MA57-class, grows the parent front) = a robustness FOLLOW-ON (first cut: within-front BK + assert/fallback on a degenerate front).

DESIGN: a front's fully-summed block = {columns DELAYED up from children} PREPENDED to its symbolic pivots; the BK kernel eliminates r≤attempt of them, the rest relay to the PARENT (added to its fully-summed set). Front sizes are DYNAMIC (symbolic = lower bound; +ndel delayed-in slack). KEY INVARIANTS that make it work + keep the moat: (1) every delayed id < c0 (descendant pivot, postorder) < every symbolic row id ⇒ the sorted delayed block LEADS an ascending front row_index ⇒ the extend-add precondition holds; (2) factor POSITIONS are dynamic (a delayed pivot lands at an ancestor) ⇒ ALL of perm/D/block_kinds/L are assigned by a SERIAL postorder pass (running counter gp; gp==pivot_first[f] in the no-delay case ⇒ BYTE-IDENTICAL to the old static scheme ⇒ the refactor is a no-op on every prior test); (3) after the BK [0,r) swap-replay on row_index, the delayed region [r,attempt) is SORTED ascending via `ldlt_swap_sym` (symmetric data swap + row_index) so the child's trailing [r,fnr) is ascending for the parent's extend-add; (4) gp≠n at the end ⇒ genuinely singular ⇒ info≠0. NEW per-front records `fdelay[f]`/`fbk[f]` MUST use `front_alloc` (the thread-safe ts in parallel — they're written by worker threads with allocation; a TLSF concurrency assert caught this — same class as [feedback_container_allocator_must_outlive](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_container_allocator_must_outlive)). `delayed_count()` = lower-bound delay indicator (moat test asserts >0 + worker-invariant). 4 new `[v5d-h]` tests: a delayed pivot reconstructs (the old refuse matrix) · big indef-3D (k=3,4) factors w/ resid<1e-9 + delayed_count>0 · **the MANDATORY delay-TRIGGERING moat: indef-3D n=64 bit-identical {1,2,4,8} (the SPD/complex moat cases never delay ⇒ said nothing about determinism-under-delay)** · the v5d-d "invalid" test moved to a genuinely-SINGULAR matrix (var0 structurally null). gcc -Werror=shadow caught `const u32 a` shadowing the matrix param (→`sp`). VERIFIED 5 configs on the NEW code (win-debug 372/34 + clang-cl 372/34 + gcc-debug RUN 372/34 + win-asan parallel-delay 65/4 + win-tidy clean + ctest 33/33 + non-ascii guard). **BENCH CORRECTNESS WIN: big indefinite 3D (n=4k–32k) now `Cerid OK` resid 5e-13→1.5e-11 (was FAIL/−1.0); Eigen SimplicialLDLT is FAST but WRONG (resid 4.1e+01→4.1e+03, pivot-free garbage) ⇒ Cerid is the ONLY correct solver besides MUMPS.**

**⚠ NEXT GRIND (the user's "FULLY CRUSH"): indefinite PERF. Cerid LOSES 16.8×→123×→350× to MUMPS on big indef-3D (n=4k→32k; 93s vs 0.27s at n=32k).** TWO causes (advisor-predicted): (1) indefinite fronts BAIL the blocked-BLAS-3 path → the UNBLOCKED BLAS-2 rank-1/2 kernel runs on big fronts; (2) likely delay-driven FRONT BLOWUP (the shifted Laplacian is very indefinite ⇒ high delay rate ⇒ near-root fronts grow O(n)-wide ⇒ unblocked BLAS-2 on a 5000²-ish front ≈ tens of seconds). The CRUSH needs a BLOCKED INDEFINITE front kernel (xSYTRF/xLASYF — BLAS-3 with 2×2 pivots IN the panel, the hard part deferred at v5d-b) AND probably a delay-rate-limiting pivot threshold (MUMPS limits blowup). DIAGNOSE FIRST (delayed_count + max-front-size on indef-3D): is it pathological delay-rate or pure kernel? Don't interleave with correctness (now locked).

**v5d COMPLETE (a–h): correct on the ENTIRE symmetric-indefinite domain + cross-thread determinism moat (incl. under delays) + complete family (f32/f64/c32/c64, sym+Herm) + CLI + honest bench + blocked-BLAS-3 SPD front.**

**⚡ v5d-h-PERF 2026-06-03 (the indefinite crush grind — advisor-measured, NOT a full crush but a MASSIVE close + accuracy WIN): 375× → 1.6–6.9× vs MUMPS, with BETTER-than-MUMPS accuracy.** Built (1) a BLOCKED-BK indefinite front kernel (`factor_front_ldlt_blocked` rewritten = full Bunch-Kaufman 1×1/2×2 + swaps + flush-on-pivot-beyond-panel; subsumes the SPD-only path; returns r≤attempt for delays) — but it ALONE did NOT help (92s→96s): the blocked kernel was fed BLOWN-UP fronts. **DISCRIMINATING MEASURE (advisor): MUMPS `INFOG(13)`=0 delays on EVERY case (SPD+indef) while Cerid delayed 30% (del 10480, maxf blew 2051→12160 at n=32k) ⇒ the gap was DELAY-DRIVEN FRONT BLOWUP from Cerid's textbook BK threshold α=0.64, NOT the kernel.** LEVER = relaxed pivot threshold (MA57/MUMPS standard ≈0.01; `set_pivot_threshold` + default now 0.01). SWEEP (time+del+resid together, advisor-mandated): α 0.64→0.01 cut n=13824 5158→96ms (del 4241→1443, maxf 4847→1446=SPD-size), n=4096 101→8.7ms (del 1193→20). **IR SAFETY NET (required — the relaxed α trades element growth): `solve` now stores A's lower tri + runs iterative refinement (symv residual, Hermitian-aware mirror `cj(v)`) with a backward-error ACCEPT guard (rnorm≤1e-6·bnorm else return false = accurate-or-flagged, never silent garbage; deterministic ⇒ moat holds). IR cost ~5% of solve.** **THE LEVER THAT SOLVED THE SCALING (advisor wanted amalgamation = accuracy-safe; MEASURED that a LOWER α + IR works + is far lower-risk — NO shared-symbolic change): sweep α at n=13824/32768 ⇒ at α≈0.0003–0.001 + IR, delays COLLAPSE to ~0 (like MUMPS), maxf → SPD separator size, IR converges + recovers accuracy. Set default α=0.001.** **🎉 FINAL @ α=0.001 + IR vs MUMPS (the indefinite CRUSH): n=4096 1.48× · n=13824 1.92× · n=32768 2.01× (was 19/137/375× at α=0.64; 1.6/2.7/6.9× at α=0.01) — STABLE ~1.5–2.0× FLAT across n (the scaling blowup is GONE), IDENTICAL to the SPD gap (1.53–1.73×). Cerid resid 1.8e-15/2.2e-15/3.0e-13 — BETTER than MUMPS (5.6e-12/4.5e-11/6.3e-11) at every size.** **HONEST framing (the user's own bar — beat speed-class AND keep determinism, the moat is the differentiator): Cerid indefinite is now at MUMPS's SPEED-CLASS (~1.5–2× serial = the SAME kernel-rate gap SPD/v5a-Chol/v5b-LU/v5c-QR all hit vs OpenBLAS+amalgamation, NOT v5d-specific), BEATS MUMPS on accuracy, is the ONLY correct solver besides MUMPS (Eigen SimplicialLDLT fast-but-WRONG resid 4e1–4e3), faster than Eigen, + the cross-thread determinism moat MUMPS lacks.** The residual ~2× is the cross-cluster kernel-rate/amalgamation wall (shared w/ v5a/b/c — ADR-0082 asm + relaxed-front amalgamation are the future cross-cluster levers; amalgamation would also let α rise back toward textbook = IR-lighter). Tests: delay-machinery tests force α=0.64 (`set_pivot_threshold`) since the relaxed default AVOIDS delays; default path covered by dense-indef + bench + SPD. VERIFIED 5 configs on ALL the new code (win-debug 383/36 + clang-cl 383/36 + gcc-debug RUN 383/36 (incl. @0.001) + win-asan 383/36 + win-tidy clean). **⭐ AMALGAMATION — the user's diagnosis CONFIRMED (it's NOT asm; the intrinsics are at par — the gap is FRONT STRUCTURE). The tell: Cerid emits ~n TINY fundamental-supernode fronts (22129 for n=32768 ≈ 1.5 pivots/front, mostly SINGLETONS → BLAS-2 + per-front assembly overhead) where MUMPS amalgamates into FAT BLAS-3 fronts — the SAME ~1.5× shows on SPD where del=0, proving it's structure not delays/kernel.** **AMALGAMATION DONE RIGHT (CHOLMOD `cholmod_super_symbolic` port — read the actual source `~/suitesparse/CHOLMOD/Supernodal/cholmod_super_symbolic.c`).** First attempt = naive SUBTREE-COLLAPSE → EXPLODED FILL/OOM on big 3D at every criterion (collapsing a sparse region into a DENSE front). The CORRECT algorithm (`amalgamate_fronts`): merge ADJACENT fronts s,s+1 ONLY when s+1 is s's CURRENT parent (a CHAIN, union-find path-compressed) AND the new explicit zeros `nscol0·(snz[s+1]+nscol0−snz[s])` pass the graduated nrelax/zrelax test (CHOLMOD defaults nrelax={4,16,48}, zrelax={0.8,0.1,0.05}). FILL-AWARE ⇒ merges nested separator chains into fat BLAS-3 fronts, NEVER collapses sparse siblings (the OOM). Merged rows = chain pivots ++ chain-TOP's CB (etree fill-propagation). `m_amalg_relax`=nrelax0 (default 4 ON). **WORKS: no OOM, reconstruction-correct, moat-safe.** **RESULT (relax=4 + α=0.001 + IR vs MUMPS): SPD 1.56→1.27× (n=13824), 1.73→1.46× (n=64000); indef 1.92→1.63× (n=13824), 2.01→1.74× (n=32768).** ⚠ nf only dropped ~6% (22129→20788) — on this AMD-ordered 3D-FEM the leaf singletons are mostly SIBLINGS not CHAINS, so neither CHOLMOD nor Cerid merges them (chain-only is the safe limit; sibling-merge = the OOM). So amalgamation closed the FRONT-OVERHEAD part; **the residual ~1.3× is the BLOCKED-BK KERNEL-PANEL rate (the discriminating measure: Cerid-blocked 42 GF/s vs LAPACK dsytrf 56 — the panel structure flush-restart + within-panel BLAS-2, NOT the gemm which is at-par; a proper xLASYF W-workspace panel is the next kernel lever).** VERIFIED 5 configs (win-debug 354/37 + clang-cl + gcc-debug RUN + win-asan + win-tidy).

**🎉 v5d-h indefinite COMPLETE (shipped: α=0.001 + IR): 375×→~2× = MUMPS SPEED-PARITY-CLASS (stable across n — NOT a speed crush of MUMPS; ~2× is the same kernel-rate/front-overhead gap as SPD/v5a/v5b/v5c) + a DECISIVE win on accuracy + determinism + correctness (only-correct-besides-MUMPS, faster-and-correct vs Eigen). The path to an actual speed crush = amalgamation-done-right (CHOLMOD zrelax) — the confirmed lever, OOMs in the naive form.** ⚠ Wording (advisor): say "parity-class + accuracy/determinism/correctness win"; do NOT write "crushes MUMPS" (crushes Eigen IS fair). ⚠⚠ The α=0.001 default is TUNED on well-conditioned 3D-FEM (`make_indefinite_laplacian_3d`); 10× below the MA57/MUMPS field standard (0.01). Ill-conditioned KKT/contact may need 0.01 (the IR accept-guard returns false loudly if 0.001 fails) — exposed via `set_pivot_threshold`. ✅ BLIND-SPOT CHECK PASSED (advisor): at α=0.001 the bench's `kkt_saddle_point` (n=250–2250) + `zero_diag_2x2` solve at MACHINE PRECISION (resid 4.4e-16/0.0, del=0, maxf=3 tiny fronts) and Cerid is FASTER than MUMPS there (0.14–0.69× = a real small/saddle WIN). So the honest indefinite scoreboard is NUANCED: Cerid WINS small/saddle (faster + matched acc) AND is parity-class (~1.5–2×) on big-3D-FEM. (A genuine high-κ KKT isn't in the bench — the IR-guard is the safety.) OWED before commit: 18-config CI sweep (IR = new FP-sensitive code w/ hardcoded `accept_tol=1e-6` — win-release LTCG + Linux scalar/SSE2 are where FP-contract diffs surface) + confirm f32+IR converges at 0.001 (1e-6 ≈ 10× f32 eps). Owed at the v5c+v5d commit: the 18-config CI sweep. Next v5 = v5e (HSS+BLR rank-structured fronts) / v5f (mixed-precision IR). · v5d-c driver (postorder walk + extend_add; vs dense oracle) · v5d-d L·D·Lᵀ solve (block-aware fwd / 1×1+2×2 diag / bwd) · v5d-e tree-parallel + moat {1,2,4,8,16} · v5d-f complex-SYMMETRIC (LDLᵀ, no conj) AND Hermitian-indefinite (LDLᴴ, conj) — two `if constexpr` variants · v5d-g CLI `hesap.direct.ldlt.{f32,f64,c32,c64}` + bench vs Eigen `SimplicialLDLT` (fixed-pivot breadth gap; MA57-class floor). RESEARCH FIRST: MA57/Duff-Reid delayed pivots, Bunch-Kaufman vs Bunch-Parlett. Full warm plan: session `docs/sessions/2026-06-02-hesap-v5c-1-multifrontal-qr.md` § v5d.

## project_v5e3_blr_premise_and_plan

**⭐⭐ GATE VERDICT (2026-06-04, advisor check #2 — DECISIVE, BLR ABANDONED AS CRUSH VEHICLE):**
The `[.][mfblr-blrgate]` bench (serial, AMD-permuted 3D Laplacian, BLR `blr_min=512` ε=1e-6 vs
Cerid's OWN dense path `blr_min=∞`, both same jobs state, accuracy via check_solve):
- **k=48 n=110592: dense 7.91s (acc 3.4e-15) · BLR 20.16s (acc 5.5e-16) · BLR/dense=2.55× SLOWER · nnz 53.7M→53.7M UNCHANGED.**
- **k=56 n=175616: dense 23.48s (acc 3.7e-15) · BLR 53.50s (acc 8.3e-16) · BLR/dense=2.28× SLOWER · nnz 118.1M→118.1M UNCHANGED.**
- **STRUCTURAL ROOT (advisor):** the driver DENSIFIES the Schur at each extend-add ⇒ the low-rank
  structure is destroyed at every tree edge ⇒ pay compress/LUAR overhead, capture NEITHER the flop
  NOR the storage benefit (nnz unchanged = smoking gun). Not a tuning gap. BLR as written *WIDENS*
  the gap it was built to close (extrapolated ~5-6× behind MUMPS-BLR at n=262K).
- **WHY the premise didn't transfer:** MUMPS-BLR crosses over MUMPS-*FULL* at n≈110K because MUMPS-full
  is slow; Cerid-FULL is already elite (~50 GF/s kernels) ⇒ Cerid's OWN BLR crossover is at much larger
  N (~500K-1M, where 3D off-diag ranks finally stay bounded). At sim-target sizes (n≤~250K) BLR loses.
- **DISPOSITION:** keep the BLR substrate (3a/3b/3c/3d — CORRECT, tested, moat-safe, [blr] 34 + [mfblr]
  28 asserts green) as a capability for the out-of-core/very-large-N frontier; NOT the default, NOT the
  v5e-3 crush vehicle. **DO NOT sink more time into BLR kernels** (advisor: real cross-tree BLR + efficient
  compress + favorable ranks = a large build with uncertain payoff right at the sizes sim tops out).
- **CRUSH PATH FORWARD (the real gap, already known): Cerid-FULL dense multifrontal ~2.2× behind
  MUMPS-full SERIAL.** Vehicle = node-parallel (built + moat-proven this session: serial front loop +
  within-front `gemm_parallel_auto`, bit-identical {1,2,4,8}). ⚠ node-parallel UNPROVEN: 0.79× at k=40
  (overhead-bound) + a HEAP CORRUPTION (`corrupted size vs prev_size`) at k=48 parallel (NOT yet ASan-localized;
  ruled out concurrent-alloc + worker-index-overflow by inspection). Serial path is clean.

**⭐⭐⭐ SERIAL-GAP LOCALIZATION (2026-06-04, user chose "profile serial gap first"; env-gated `CRD_MFBLR_PROFILE`
phase split + achieved-GF/s + AMD-vs-ND flop ratio — all in `[.][mfblr-prof]`):**
- **PHASE SPLIT (serial dense, AMD): factor DOMINATES 67-72%** (k=48: sym 4% / asm 12% / **factor 68%** /
  extract 16%, sum 7.34s; k=56: 3/10/**71**/15, sum 22.7s). REFUTES the advisor's symbolic/assembly hypothesis
  (v5a/v5b history did NOT repeat). The factor phase ALONE (4.95/16.2s) already EXCEEDS MUMPS-full's TOTAL (3.36/10.3s).
- **ACHIEVED FACTOR GF/s (flop=Σ col_nnz², = n³/3 for a dense front = the single-front bench convention, CALIBRATION-
  CONSISTENT): AMD 30 GF/s** (both sizes). Single-front peak is 50; the drop is the multifrontal mix (small leaf
  fronts at low eff + full-gemm-Schur 2× + tall-skinny panels). 30 is the advisor's AMBIGUOUS band ⇒ flop-bound
  (fill OR syrk), NOT a microkernel verdict.
- **⭐ ND IS A RED HERRING — THE GAP IS PURE MACHINERY ON IDENTICAL AMD FILL.** The MUMPS bench
  (`bench_hesap_ldlt_vs_reference.cpp:550-583`) feeds MUMPS the SAME AMD-permuted matrix + **ICNTL(7)=1 PERM_IN=identity
  ⇒ MUMPS uses CERID'S AMD ORDER, no re-reorder ⇒ IDENTICAL fill (53.7M nnz, 1.483e11 flop) BY CONSTRUCTION.** So:
  **MUMPS = 1.483e11/3.36s = ~44 GF/s all-in; Cerid = 30 GF/s factor + 33% non-factor overhead = ~20 GF/s all-in = the 2.2×.**
  ND/amalgamation is NOT needed for the MUMPS-full comparison (it would only matter if MUMPS used ND, which it does NOT here).
- **AMD-vs-ND probe (for the record): ND has 2.1-2.8× FEWER flops (k=48 2.12×, k=56 2.76×) + 18-34% less nnz, BUT
  is 3× SLOWER in our driver** (factor 6.5 GF/s, assembly EXPLODES 7×) because `build_symmetric_multifrontal_symbolic`
  builds FUNDAMENTAL supernodes (NO relaxed amalgamation, multifrontal_lu.cpp:158) ⇒ ND's small/skinny separator
  fronts factor at single-digit GF/s. ND would need relaxed amalgamation to pay — a multi-slice build, NOT needed
  for MUMPS-full parity (MUMPS uses AMD here).
- **NO-REGRET LEVERS (advisor-blessed, in-scope, NO ordering/amalgamation build): (1) BLOCKED SYRK for the Schur
  update** A22−=L21·L21ᵀ — current code does the FULL ms×ms `gemm_parallel_auto` then copies lower = 2× the needed
  flops; the public `syrk` (blas3.cpp:501) is NAIVE scalar (~2-5 GF/s, the v5e-2 trsm trap) so a BLOCKED lower-tri
  syrk-via-gemm is needed (mirror `blocked_trsm_lower`). **(2) PREALLOCATE the per-worker triplet arrays to nnz(L)**
  (the 16% extract is push_back reallocation). (3) tighten extend-add (asm 12%). Then within-front parallel for the
  parallel crush. Target: factor 30→~45 GF/s (syrk) + overhead 33%→~10% ⇒ close to MUMPS-full serial parity.

**⭐ SYRK LEVER LANDED (2026-06-04, `syrk_lower_sub` in blr.cpp + triplet reserve in driver; [mfblr] 28 asserts /
5 cases STILL GREEN, correctness held):**
- **AMD serial: factor 30→48-51 GF/s · k=48 sum 7.34→5.66s (vs MUMPS 3.36 ⇒ 2.18×→1.68×) · k=56 22.71→15.76s
  (vs MUMPS 10.3 ⇒ 2.20×→1.53×).** `syrk_lower_sub` (blocked lower-tri syrk: gemm only the lower block-tiles
  straight into the front, alpha=−1 beta=1, no scratch/copy; diagonal tiles write unused upper, harmless).
- **⭐ Cerid FACTOR now EXCEEDS MUMPS's ~44 GF/s all-in rate (48-51 vs 44) — the factor KERNEL is no longer the gap.**
- **PREALLOCATION was a NO-OP** (extract 1.20→1.26s unchanged) — the realloc was NOT the cost; the extract cost is
  the DATA COPY (strided `front.at(t,k)` column reads out of a ROW-MAJOR front [MUMPS stores fronts col-major ⇒
  contiguous L columns] + 53.7M triplet writes). Kept the reserve (correct, cheap) but it doesn't move the needle.
- **REMAINING SERIAL GAP = non-factor OVERHEAD (asm 18% + extract 22% = ~40%)** that MUMPS amortizes. Next serial
  levers: (a) extract — col-major front storage OR direct-indexed write (kill push_back) to fix the strided column
  read; (b) tighten extend-add. With MUMPS-minimal overhead Cerid's 3.1s factor ≈ MUMPS 3.36s = SERIAL PARITY.
  Then the PARALLEL crush (within-front node-parallel — needs the heap-corruption fix first) + the determinism MOAT.
- ND path also improved (factor 6.5→20 GF/s via syrk) but STILL 3× slower (assembly explodes) — ND stays a red herring.

**⭐ LEG A — DIRECT-CSC L ASSEMBLY LANDED (2026-06-04, user chose "Leg A: serial parity"; [mfblr] 28 asserts /
5 cases incl. MOAT STILL GREEN):** Replaced the triplet-buffer + counting-sort L extraction with **m_lp/m_li
PRECOMPUTED from the symbolic + factor writes m_lx STRAIGHT into the CSC slot** (MUMPS-style direct assembly;
diagonal at m_lp[c] first, ascending rows ⇒ valid CSC + solve_llt "diagonal first" intact; each global col is a
pivot of ONE front ⇒ disjoint slots ⇒ MOAT-CLEAN, worker-count-independent — CLEANER than the old worker-order
concat). Killed the triplet push_backs AND the untimed strided counting-sort scatter.
- **WALL (true end-to-end, AMD serial): k=48 5.24s (vs MUMPS 3.36 ⇒ 1.56×) · k=56 14.79s (vs MUMPS 10.3 ⇒ 1.44×).**
  extract phase 1.26→0.725s (k=48) / 2.85→1.82s (k=56). **SESSION ARC: 2.2-2.35× → 1.44-1.56× behind MUMPS-full serial.**
- **Cerid FACTOR 49-53 GF/s STILL BEATS MUMPS's ~44 GF/s all-in rate.** The residual gap is NON-FACTOR OVERHEAD:
  assembly (extend-add) 16-19% + extract 13-15% + symbolic 6% ≈ 35-40%. With MUMPS-minimal overhead Cerid's ~3.0s
  factor ≈ MUMPS 3.36s = PARITY. ⚠ verify direct-CSC under ASan before slice close (computed-index m_lx/m_li writes).
- **REMAINING Leg-A sub-levers (diminishing): (1) extend-add scatter (now the biggest overhead, cache-hostile
  loc[]-mapped element scatter — relative-indexing/sorted assembly like UMFPACK v5b L2); (2) COL-MAJOR front storage
  ⇒ contiguous extract column read (the literal "leg A" — factor kernels need ColMajor instantiation, bigger). Then
  LEG B = the parallel crush (node-parallel corruption fix + scaling + matched-thread bench + determinism MOAT).

**Leg-A extend-add GATHER HOIST = NO-OP (2026-06-04, measured):** precomputing the child→parent row map once
(per-worker `eamap` scratch) + contiguous Schur-row read changed NOTHING (k=48 asm 0.946→0.900s, wall 5.24→5.13s;
k=56 unchanged). ⇒ the assembly cost is NOT the gather (cache-resident, cheap) but the **SCATTERED WRITE into the
large front** (front.at(li,lj) at arbitrary positions = cache misses) — INHERENT to multifrontal extend-add. Kept
the hoist (clean, parallel-ready, neutral). **⇒ the cheap serial levers are SPENT. Further serial gains need
INVASIVE restructuring: COL-MAJOR fronts (contiguous extract) and/or relative-indexed assembly (MUMPS's mature
scatter). Diminishing returns.** STATE: serial 1.44-1.53× behind MUMPS-full, factor kernel BEATS MUMPS (50-52 vs 44
GF/s). The bigger crush is LEG B (parallel + the determinism MOAT MUMPS lacks).

**✅ VERIFY+BANK DONE (2026-06-04, user chose it): cross-config GREEN — gcc-release ([mfblr] 28 asserts incl moat) +
win-tidy (MSVC+clang-tidy 20.1.8 clean) + clang-cl (-Werror clean) + win-asan (dense-path+direct-CSC ASan-clean, no
OOB/UAF). Fixed MSVC `getenv` C4996 ⇒ converted CRD_MFBLR_PROFILE env-gate→COMPILE-gate (#if defined). Phase doc v5e-3
row updated.** ⚠ win-asan FULL [mfblr] (incl BLR-path moat at n=4096) is pathologically SLOW under ASan (unchanged
factor_front_cholesky_blr LR-arith) — validated the dense-path subset, deferred the BLR-path ASan to CI. Node-parallel
heap corruption still UNFIXED (Leg B). Files: blr.cpp (syrk_lower_sub),
multifrontal_cholesky_blr.cpp (direct-CSC + eamap hoist + compile-gated profiling), test_multifrontal_cholesky_blr.cpp
(mfblr-prof/blrgate/bench). The header still carries a now-ignored `num_workers` factorize param (harmless legacy).

**✅✅ v5e-3 CLOSED — LEG B INVESTIGATED → SERIAL SHIPPED (2026-06-04, user: "stop parallel grind, 1.44 serial is
enough, close the slice"):**
- **The "heap corruption" was the gemm FrameArena leak (NOT an OOB).** ASan-localized: `gemm_parallel` `frame_alloc`s
  its JobDecls but NEVER resets ⇒ a big front's hundreds of within-front gemm calls EXHAUST the per-thread arena ⇒
  win-asan `frame_arena.hpp:60` assert; linux-RELEASE compiles the assert out ⇒ pointer past the arena ⇒ glibc
  `corrupted size vs prev_size`. SAME defect, two configs. **The advisor was RIGHT: the corruption I "remembered" was
  pre-Leg-A code; reproduce-under-ASan, don't debug from memory.** Filed debt `gemm-parallel-frame-arena-leak` (proper
  fix = a scoped per-thread frame marker in jobs + use in gemm_parallel; blast radius = every gemm caller ⇒ separate
  verified change). Localized `reclaim_frame_arena()` (guarded `num_workers()>0`, valid frame boundary: serial main-
  thread dispatch + gemm waits before return). ASan-clean k=40 AND k=48 (resid 2.5e-15/3.4e-15) — exhaustion was the
  WHOLE bug, no second OOB.
- **Node-parallel within-front scaling = SUB-1×, structural.** First try (per-tile gemm_parallel_auto) 0.20× (hundreds
  of tiny parallel dispatches). B2a panel-syrk (one gemm per block-COLUMN over the lower trapezoid, ~ms/nb big gemms
  not ~ms²/nb² tiny) → 0.37/0.51/0.67× at k=40/48/56 (growing but still <1×): most fronts too small to amortize
  parallel-gemm dispatch; only the few huge near-root fronts benefit + serial assembly/extract cap it.
- **DECISION (user + advisor): SHIP SERIAL.** syrk_lower_sub + blocked_trsm_lower route through SERIAL `gemm` (not
  gemm_parallel_auto). Factor never regresses with threads: jobs-up 0.81/0.87/0.93× (the residual = factor_cholesky's
  minor internal parallelism only — left as-is, moat-safe). The reclaim+jobs-include stay ONLY for factor_cholesky.
  **WHY (the honest ceiling, advisor ×N): serial is 1.44-1.53× behind MUMPS-full + MUMPS scales well ⇒ parallel CANNOT
  beat MUMPS on raw speed (parity-class at best); the {1,2,4,8} determinism MOAT — the real differentiator — is ALREADY
  proven. So parallelizing buys nothing toward the crush.** The level-scheduled HYBRID (tree-parallel small fronts +
  node-parallel big + per-worker allocators, v5b-3c-class) = future PRODUCT-PERF work, NOT a MUMPS-crush enabler.
- **v5e-3 CLOSE DELIVERABLE:** BLR substrate (correct/moat-safe, deprecated-for-crush) + dense multifrontal Cholesky
  SERIAL-CRUSH (factor kernel 49-53 GF/s > MUMPS ~44; 1.44-1.53× behind MUMPS-full all-in via blocked-syrk + direct-CSC)
  + the FrameArena fix + the moat. [mfblr] 28 asserts/5 cases (incl moat) + [mfblr-par] ASan + [mfblr-prof]/[mfblr-blrgate]/
  [mfblr-bench] benches. VERIFIED win-tidy + clang-cl + win-asan + gcc-release-RUN. Phase doc v5e-3 row + main slice table
  marked ✅. **The honest WIN this session: serial crush (factor beats MUMPS rate) + the determinism moat + a real
  latent-corruption fix — NOT a parallel speed crush (unreachable + unnecessary).** Follow-ons: LDLᵀ/LU BLR + the hybrid.

---

**Phase 3.1.6 v5e-3 = BLR-embedded multifrontal (flat block-low-rank, Amestoy 2015 /
MUMPS-BLR) — the production-default complement to v5e-1/2's hierarchical HSS.** User
directive: "go for v5e-3 and go for full crush." Advisor-gated: premise-check FIRST.
**(SUPERSEDED by the GATE VERDICT above — the premise was MUMPS-BLR-vs-MUMPS-full, which
did NOT transfer to Cerid-BLR-vs-Cerid-full. History below kept for the audit trail.)**

**v5e-3a SUBSTRATE ✅ (2026-06-04):** `engine/hesap-direct/{include/crd/hesap/direct/blr.hpp,
src/blr.cpp}` — `BlrBlock<T>` (dense OR low-rank u·vᵀ) + symmetric `BlrMatrix<T>` (lower
block-triangle; diagonal dense, off-diag compressed) + `compress_blr_sym` (per-off-diag-block
`interp_decomp` column-ID, kept LR iff rank·(rows+cols)<rows·cols) + `blr_to_dense_sym`.
`tests/hesap-direct/test_blr.cpp` ([blr], 6 asserts): dense-fallback exact · LR path exercised
· monotone-in-tol · DETERMINISTIC (moat-free, no RNG — cleaner than HSS) · f32. The block
compression reuses v5e-1a's RRQR ID directly (u=cols, v=projᵀ).

**⭐ PREMISE CHECK (the decisive de-risking, advisor's #1) — MUMPS-BLR vs MUMPS-full, SYM=2,
3D Laplacian, OMP=1, via `CRD_MUMPS_BLR`/`CRD_MUMPS_BLR_EPS` env toggle added to
bench_hesap_ldlt_vs_reference.cpp (ICNTL(35)/CNTL(7)):**
- n=4096→32768: BLR 2.6×→1.45× SLOWER (overhead regime — fronts too small).
- n=64000 (k=40): ~PARITY.
- **n=110592 (k=48): BLR 1.28× FASTER · n=175616: 1.69× · n=262144 (k=64): 2.0× — and GROWING.**
- Accuracy: BLR ε=1e-8 ⇒ resid ~1e-6/1e-7 (vs full 1e-15) ⇒ **IR is MANDATORY** (recover accuracy).
- **CROSSOVER ≈ n=110K (k=48).** Below it BLR is pointless; build/bench ONLY at n≥110K.
- **BLR is NECESSARY, not optional:** at n=262144 MUMPS-BLR beats CERID-FULL 2.79× (Cerid-full
  is ~1.4× behind MUMPS-full per v5d-h × MUMPS-BLR's 2× over MUMPS-full). Without BLR, Cerid
  falls behind MUMPS at large 3D. This is the motivation.

**v5e-3b BLR-CHOLESKY FACTOR+SOLVE ✅ (2026-06-04):** `blr_cholesky_factor` (FSCU SIMPLE:
dense Cholesky → compress L's off-diag blocks into BLR; diagonal dense; the flop-saving LR×LR
update is 3c) + `blr_cholesky_solve` (single-RHS L·Lᵀ·x=b; off-diag LR blocks applied as
`u·(vᵀ·)` fwd / `v·(uᵀ·)` bwd = the BLR solve win; dense diag trsv). `[blr]` now 17 asserts /
10 cases: SPD smooth-kernel low-rank-L + solve within tol · generic full-rank SPD exact
(dense fallback) · non-SPD ⇒ false · deterministic factor+solve · f32. VERIFIED 4 configs
(win-debug + win-tidy + clang-cl + gcc-release RUN). NOTE: 3b factor is DENSE (compress-for-
memory only) — no factor flop savings yet; that is 3c.

**v5e-3c LR×LR UPDATE + RECOMPRESSION (the flop-saving factor) ✅ (2026-06-04):**
`detail::low_rank_recompress` (the LUAR core: uc·vcᵀ → u·vᵀ rank-r via QR(uc)/QR(vc) → SVD the
TINY rc×rc Ru·Rvᵀ → truncate → Qu·Uσ / Qv·V; dense-ID fallback when rc≥min(m,n); the SAME
QR-then-tiny-SVD pattern as v5e-2's compress fix) + `apply_schur_update` (builds L_ik·L_jkᵀ as
a low-rank ub·vbᵀ for all 4 dense/LR cases — both-LR: M=v_ikᵀv_jk, ub=u_ik·M, vb=u_jk; mixed;
both-dense — then subtracts: dense target densely, LR off-diag target via concatenate
[Ua,−Ub]·[Va,Vb]ᵀ + recompress) + `blr_cholesky_factor_lr` (compress front → per-panel:
chol diag, LR-preserving TRSM [apply L_kk⁻¹ to v columns], LR×LR trailing update in FIXED
k-ascending order). `[blr]` now 29 asserts / 14 cases: recompress redundant rank-4→true-rank-2
EXACT · LR-arith solve within tol AND matches the 3b dense ORACLE · deterministic factor+solve
(moat: fixed accumulation order) · f32. VERIFIED 4 configs (win-debug + win-tidy + clang-cl +
gcc-RUN). NOTE: factor is SERIAL (single-thread determinism tested; cross-thread {1,2,4,8} moat
+ the MEASURED flop-savings/crush vs MUMPS-BLR are v5e-3d). The mm helpers are naive (correctness
first; 3d swaps in fast gemm for the crush).

**v5e-3d PREP / GATE ✅ (2026-06-04, advisor's go/no-go before the driver):** (1) routed the
BLR arithmetic (`mm`/`mm_at`/`mm_bt`/`block_dense`/`dense_sub_lr`) through `gemm_parallel_auto`
(the fast kernel; fixed reduction order ⇒ moat-safe; [blr] 29 asserts still green). (2) SINGLE-
FRONT CROSSOVER bench (`[.][blr-bench]` hidden test, optimized linux-gcc-release, smooth Gaussian
front c=4/n²): **dense Cholesky (factor_cholesky) at 35.5/44.5/50.2 GF/s = OpenBLAS-class** (n=1024/
2048/4096) — the ADR-0082 wall does NOT bind SPD Cholesky's gemm; **BLR factor speedup 0.67×→1.30×
→2.33×** (crosses at n≈2048, GROWS, matching/exceeding MUMPS-BLR's 2×-over-full). **⇒ GREEN GATE:
kernels competitive + BLR shows a real within-front win ⇒ machinery is CRUSH-CAPABLE.** The
advisor's pessimistic ~1.4×-behind projection (kernel-wall) is REFUTED for Cholesky (kernel at
50 GF/s). Honest claim to be set by the real 3D bench (less compressible than Gaussian ⇒ <2.33×,
but crossover real): ≥ parity + the determinism MOAT (MUMPS-BLR lacks) + matched accuracy via IR;
plausibly a speed win. (maxrank 3-4 on the smooth Gaussian = very compressible; real 3D fronts
rank ~O(√separator) ⇒ less speedup.)

**v5e-3d PERF CYCLE 1 (2026-06-04) — DENSE FRONT FACTOR 5×→2.3× behind MUMPS-full serial.**
Bounded kernel fixes (advisor-sanctioned one cycle, all correctness-preserving, full suite
598043/160 green, 4 configs): (1) diagonal chol `chol_lower_dense`→`chol_lower_fast` (blocked
`factor_cholesky`, ~50 GF/s; only ~12% — NOT the bottleneck). (2) `factor_front_cholesky_dense`
(NEW, the fast dense path the driver dispatches to below `blr_min`): `factor_cholesky` +
`blocked_trsm_lower` + gemm — **skips the interp_decomp QRColPiv waste** the BLR path ran on
big dense blocks just to decide "keep dense" (a real lever). (3) **`blocked_trsm_lower` (THE
lever): cast the panel TRSM as gemm** (hesap-dense `trsm` is UNBLOCKED ~5 GF/s — the v5e-2 HSS
finding; blocked trailing-panel update via gemm ≈ gemm rate). **RESULT (AMD 3D Laplacian, serial):
dense k=48 14.5→7.74s, k=56 86→23.3s — ~2.3× behind MUMPS-full (3.36/10.3s), was ~5×.** ⚠ The BLR
path (factor_front_cholesky_blr) is STILL slow (23-62s) on the 3D Laplacian — compress/recompress
overhead > savings (3D fronts compress to high rank); the DENSE path WINS here ⇒ raise driver
default `blr_min` (use dense) until BLR overhead is fixed. **REMAINING crush levers (FRESH-session
perf track — advisor: don't rush tree-parallel into a determinism-critical factor at a marathon's
tail): syrk (½ the Schur-update flops, ~25%) + TREE-PARALLEL (THE crush lever, the v5a pattern that
beats CHOLMOD — level-sched the front tree + per-worker scratch + per-worker triplet buffers + the
moat) + matched-thread bench (run BOTH @8t; premise was OMP=1). v5a Cholesky CRUSHES CHOLMOD via
tree-parallel ⇒ same path here.**

**v5e-3d DRIVER COMPLETE + HONEST BENCH (2026-06-04) — CORRECT, NOT YET A SPEED CRUSH.**
`MultifrontalCholeskyBlr<T>` (`multifrontal_cholesky_blr.{hpp,cpp}`): full BLR multifrontal
Cholesky — reuses `build_symmetric_multifrontal_symbolic` + own row-major assembly/extend-add/
postorder/L-extract (CSC) + `factor_front_cholesky_blr` (BLR large fronts, dense small via
`blr_min`) + solve (CSC fwd/bwd) + IR with backward-error-accept guard (v5d-h discipline). `[mfblr]`
14 asserts/4 cases (2D dense + 2D BLR-path + 3D BLR-path + DETERMINISM moat), 4 configs green.
**⚠ HONEST CRUSH BENCH (AMD-permuted 3D Laplacian, serial, `[.][mfblr-bench]`): Cerid-BLR
23.4s/63.8s (k=48/56, n=110K/175K) vs MUMPS-BLR 2.6s/6.1s ⇒ ~9× SLOWER. NOT a speed crush.**
ROOT CAUSE (advisor-confirmed): the front factor uses NAIVE `chol_lower_dense`/`trsv` for the
DIAGONAL Cholesky + TRSM (I routed only the UPDATES through gemm) ⇒ on big fronts (npiv~3000) the
naive O(npiv³) chol at 2 GF/s is catastrophic (factor_cholesky does it at 50 GF/s = 25×); + serial
(no tree-parallel) + compress/recompress overhead + the real 3D Schur fronts compress to MUCH higher
rank than the Gaussian gate (maxrank 3-4 was a false-positive). nnz(L) dense==blr (first pass stores
dense L, no memory win). **HONEST CEILING (advisor, 3× consults, confirmed): BLR scales BOTH sides ⇒
the achievable honest win is PARITY-class speed + the determinism MOAT (MUMPS-BLR lacks) + matched
accuracy via IR — NOT sub-1× speed.** PERF TRACK (fresh session, NOT an end-of-marathon grind):
(1) diagonal chol → `factor_cholesky` (the 25× lever; v5a CRUSHES CHOLMOD-full ⇒ Cerid CAN do fast
Cholesky, this driver just hasn't inherited the tuning), (2) panel TRSM → the v5e-2 HSS blocked-gemm
cast, (3) tree-parallel (reuse v5a/v5d level-scheduling) + the {1,2,4,8} moat, (4) overhead tuning,
then bench vs MUMPS-BLR matched-ε. The CORRECT driver + moat is bankable now.

**v5e-3d DRIVER — CORE KERNEL ✅ (2026-06-04): `factor_front_cholesky_blr`** (the partial-front
BLR Cholesky, the driver's heart). In-place on a dense m×m front + `npiv`: factor the leading
npiv fully-summed pivots in BLR arithmetic (npiv-aligned grid, compress + LR-preserving TRSM +
LR×LR updates incl. the Schur rows) → L (cols[0,npiv): L11+L21) + DENSE Schur S=A22−L21·L21ᵀ
written back to the front (decompress-to-dense ⇒ driver extend-add + L-extract unchanged). `[blr]`
34 asserts/16 cases: full front npiv=m⇒L·Lᵀ=A · partial⇒L+Schur COMPLETE to A. 4 configs green.
**REMAINING (the v5d-scaffolding-reuse wiring — the BULK):** multifrontal loop (reuse
`build_symmetric_multifrontal_symbolic` + MfFront + `mf_extend_add_trailing_sym` + postorder +
tree-parallel + L-extract from multifrontal_ldlt.cpp; Cholesky is SIMPLER — no pivot/delay/D/swap)
calling `factor_front_cholesky_blr` for large fronts (dense small) + solve + IR + backward-error
(reuse v5d-h) + bench vs MUMPS-BLR matched-ε at n≥110K + {1,2,4,8} moat. v5d factor call site =
multifrontal_ldlt.cpp:482.

**PLAN (advisor-blessed, Cholesky-first — cleanest: no pivoting ⇒ static block grid):**
- v5e-3d: integrate into the multifrontal Cholesky driver (compress fronts above a size
  threshold — n≥110K regime) + IR + backward-error-accept guard (reuse v5d-h verbatim) +

<a id="memory-project_v5e_hss_crush"></a>
## project_v5e_hss_crush

---
name: project-v5e-hss-crush
description: "v5e HSS/ULV crush vs STRUMPACK — factor CRUSHED (algorithmic fix, not intrinsics); compress needs v5e-2 global-sample construction; solve needs BLAS-3 trsm. The per-phase diagnosis + the real levers."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9f96b548-5cee-464d-a0aa-59f3b7b19839
---

**Phase 3.1.6 v5e rank-structured fronts (HSS+ULV). Built v5e-1a (ID `interp_decomp`,
hesap-dense) → v5e-1b (`randomized_range`/`rsvd_op`/`rsyev_op` over `LinearOp`,
counter-RNG, hesap-dense) → v5e-1c (`HssMatrix` symmetric HSS: `build_cluster_tree`,
`hss_matvec`, INDEPENDENT `hss_to_dense`, `build_hss_from_dense` telescoping SVD) →
v5e-1d (`HssUlv:IFactorization` + `factor_hss_ulv`, ULV factor+solve). All verified
4 configs (win-debug/clang-cl/win-tidy/gcc-RUN). STRUMPACK oracle wired:
`scripts/setup-strumpack-ref.sh` + `bench_hesap_hss_vs_strumpack.cpp` (CRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_STRUMPACK,
WSL, ~/strumpack/install) + `bench_hesap_hss_vs_reference.cpp` (Eigen). Reset flags OFF after.**

**SCOREBOARD vs STRUMPACK (serial, identical rank=4, machine-eps both), SPD low-rank kernel, N up to 4096:**
- **factor: CRUSH 2.7–3.8×** (was 0.16× LOSS). ALGORITHMIC fix, NOT intrinsics (user was
  right): the ULV factor MATERIALIZED the dense m×m Q + two O(m³) `Qᵀ D Q` matmuls per node
  when rank r≪m. Fix = apply the r Householder reflectors IMPLICITLY via `apply_q_block`
  (dlarfb, O(m²r)); store QR reflectors in `UlvNodeFactor.qr`, never form Q. 6× loss → ~3× win.
- **compress: CRUSH at ALL N — 3.41×/1.83×/1.71×/1.39× (N=512/1024/2048/4096), machine-eps**
  (was 24.9s→0.26s via global-sample, THEN 0.81→1.39× via the QR-SVD fix below). Construction
  = GLOBAL-SAMPLE feeding the EXISTING explicit-basis telescoping: sample `Y = A·Ω` ONCE
  (counter-RNG Ω, blocked gemm, O(N²ℓ)); each node off-diag `S_k = Y(I_k,:) − A(I_k,I_k)·Ω(I_k,:)`;
  `U_k = leading left-sing-vecs of S_k`. **THE big-N fix (profile-found, NOT adaptive-ℓ):**
  `compress_samples` did a FULL `svd(sk)` of the TALL sk (n_k×ℓ, n_k up to 2048) — the scalar
  bdsqr Givens-accumulation into U over the tall dim was 67% of compress (210ms→pa_svd, 0.3 GF/s).
  Replaced with **QR sk = Q·R (BLAS-3) → SVD the tiny ℓ×ℓ R → q_out = Q·U_R[:,:r] via implicit
  apply_q** (same singular values, deterministic ⇒ moat-safe). pa_svd 210→40ms ⇒ compress 0.81→1.39×.
  Branch on `n_k > ℓ` (tall=QR path; small/wide=direct svd, QR would be rank-deficient).
  Phases now balanced (aomega 41 / pa_gemm 37 / pa_svd 40 / passb 26 ms). Profiler split was
  decisive — the advisor's adaptive-ℓ hypothesis was REFUTED (A·Ω only 13%, SVD was 67%).
- **solve: 0.14× → PARITY/WIN 1.04×/1.06×/0.99×/0.99× (N=512/1024/2048/4096), machine-eps.**
  The 0.14× was NEVER "intrinsics slow" — it was a STACK of real problems found by MEASURING
  (env/#ifdef phase profiler in HssUlv::solve), each fixed:
  1. **4→2 triangular solves (the big one, advisor-found).** The solve did `z=D22⁻¹b` (2 solves)
     forward AND `D22⁻¹D21·xt` (2 solves) backward = 4/leaf. The standard ULV carries
     `W=L⁻¹·D21` (factor ALREADY computes it for the Schur `D11−WᵀW`, then threw it away).
     Store `fc.w`: forward `u=L⁻¹b` (1 solve) + `bhat=b_top−Wᵀu`; backward `x_bot=L⁻ᵀ(u−W·xt)`
     (1 solve). Exact (Wᵀu=D12·D22⁻¹b). 0.50→0.75×. (Also DROPPED dead `d12` field — W carries it.)
  2. **Vectorized `gemm_blk`/`gemm_at_blk`** (were scalar triple-loops) → AXPY-over-contiguous-nrhs
     (outer-product form, row-wise A). 0.75→0.85×.
  3. **Register-blocked trsv** (`tri_solve_vec`/`_t`): left-looking, the nrhs result block held
     in a `T acc[16]` register accumulator across the k-loop → 1:1 mem:FMA (was 3:1 reload/restore
     each k). 0.85→0.92×.
  4. **Alloc-free reflector apply** (`apply_reflectors_left`): the leaf Qᵀ/Q apply used
     `apply_q_block` (blocked-WY) which allocates **5 Arrays PER CALL** — thousands of calls ⇒
     63.6ms of pure TLSF churn for r=4 work (0.03 GFLOP/s = the tell). Per-reflector rank-1 updates
     (tiny k) = zero alloc. 36.7ms. 0.92→0.99-1.06×. (apply_q_block STILL used in FACTOR — keep it.)
  Profiler verdict (cumulative): chol/trsv 64% (now ~OpenBLAS-dtrsm parity), scatter 12%
  (strided col-major RHS write — the residual large-N gap), applyq 8%, gather 4%. Lesson: when
  N tweaks of ONE kernel don't move the bench, that kernel ISN'T the bottleneck — PROFILE.

**KEY reference finding (read ~/strumpack/src/HSS/HSSMatrix.factor.hpp):** STRUMPACK's ULV
uses ID bases (U = P·[I;E]) → elimination is a permutation + tiny (m-r)×r gemm + one LQ.
Advisor RECONCILED (was wrong that ULV REQUIRES orthonormal): ID is valid but NOT required
— orthonormal + implicit reflectors bottoms out at the SAME O(p³) fully-summed-block
elimination floor, and is MORE accurate (ID's E unbounded under plain col-piv QR). Do NOT
rewrite to ID; if v5e-2 needs cheap row-extract, decide ID there with measurements.

**MOAT PROVEN (v5e-2 done):** `tests/hesap-direct/test_hss_ulv.cpp` "[moat]" test — compress
(parallel A·Ω at n=512) + factor + solve are BIT-IDENTICAL across jobs::init {1,2,4,8} workers
(serialize all node D/U/R/B + the solution, exact `==`). 18 asserts; green on gcc-release (real
threading) + win-asan (clean under the init/shutdown loop). gemm_parallel_auto's fixed k-order
reduction + counter-RNG Ω = thread-count-independent. The differentiator STRUMPACK lacks.

**ALSO fixed en route:** a pre-existing crd-jobs landmine — `WorkerPool::shutdown()` left
`num_workers()` stale ⇒ gemm_parallel_auto dispatched onto a dead scheduler ⇒ full-gcc-release-
suite SIGSEGV (in compress's dense_gemm). 1-line root fix + guard. See
[feedback_jobs_shutdown_must_reset_num_workers](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_jobs_shutdown_must_reset_num_workers).

**v5e-2 SCOREBOARD COMPLETE vs STRUMPACK (serial, rank=4, machine-eps): compress CRUSH
3.41/1.83/1.71/1.39× · factor CRUSH 2.7-4.1× · solve PARITY/WIN 1.04/1.06/0.99/0.99× · MOAT
proven.** All 6 configs green (gcc-release full 597995 asserts/140 cases, win-debug/clang-cl/
shipping/tidy/asan). NEXT (optional polish): adaptive-ℓ would cut aomega+pa_gemm further (phases
now balanced ~26-41ms each); tree-parallel Pass-A loop (currently serial-over-nodes, gemm-parallel
within). See
[feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_crush_persist_research_dont_retreat), [feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards).
Mandate: don't blame intrinsics — find the real (usually algorithmic) problem and crush.

<a id="memory-project_v5f_mixed_precision"></a>
## project_v5f_mixed_precision

---
name: project_v5f_mixed_precision
description: "v5f mixed-precision IR (factor-f32 + f64-IR) — a-d, honest smumps+IR scoreboard, the symmetric-lever finding"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 440829ac-85ee-4df7-aa74-16c24285879e
---

v5f = mixed-precision iterative refinement (HPL-AI / Carson-Higham): factor in f32, refine in f64 to f64
accuracy when κ(A)·u_f ≲ 1 (κ ≲ 1e7). Converges via a fixed-point IR loop (residual via spmv, raw-f32
factor apply each step). Substrate: `engine/hesap-direct/include/crd/hesap/direct/mixed_refine.hpp`
(`IterativeRefinedSolve<TWork,TLow,LowFactor> : IFactorization<TWork>`, `factor_mixed_{lu,cholesky,ldlt}`;
refine_tol=64·eps, accept_tol=√eps stall+accept guard, max_iters=20).

**v5f-a/b/c DONE 2026-06-05** (verified win-debug/clang-cl/asan/tidy + guard; tests `[mixed]` 67 asserts +
`[v5f][cli]`). Key audit-found lock: `IFactorization` got a NEW `apply_inverse(Span,nrhs)` virtual appended
AT END (D135 vtable-safe), default→solve for raw families (Cholesky), overridden in LU (`static_lu_apply`,
no inner IR) + LDLᵀ (`ldlt_apply_once`, refactored from the solve lambda → byte-identical). WHY: MF-LU/LDLT
`solve` run their OWN internal IR whose accept-gate returns false on f32-stall ⇒ a naïve `low->solve()` would
spuriously fail the OUTER IR on exactly the ill-conditioned systems mixed-precision targets.

**⭐ THE HONEST FINDING (advisor-confirmed, do NOT re-litigate): mixed precision is a SYMMETRIC lever.**
It cannot crush a peer the f64 path wasn't already crushing — the peer does the same f32-factor trick and
gets the same lift. Internal bench (`bench_hesap_mixed_internal`, 3D Laplacian, matched post-IR accuracy):

memory + the cross-thread determinism MOAT** (factor+solve bit-identical {1,2,4,8}; the iteration count is
worker-independent because r/x are bit-identical each step).

- This IS the advisor's prediction: **parity-class + moat, the v5b story at f64 accuracy** — not a new crush.

**⭐ v5f-c2 GMRES-IR DONE 2026-06-05 (fixes the static-pivot DIVERGENCE — garon2).** Root cause of
garon2/raefsky3 `[INACCURATE]`: the MC64+static-pivot LU (no row interchanges = the moat design) is a POOR
approximation on saddle-point/indefinite unsym systems ⇒ tiny pivots GESP-perturbed ⇒ factor drifts from A ⇒
FIXED-POINT IR DIVERGES. This is the FACTORIZATION not mixed precision (f64-FULL also fails: garon2 resid

pivots for the common case) — DEFERRED to next session (touches the determinism-critical kernel; advisor:

## project_v6_eigen

---
name: project_v6_eigen
description: "Phase 3.1.6 v6 sparse eigenvalue — plan, hesap-eigen module, v6-a symmetric Lanczos DONE"

  node_type: memory

v6 = SPARSE EIGENVALUE (matrix-free over `LinearOp<T>`), the cluster after v5 (sparse direct, shipped
`f0ae6db`). New module **`hesap-eigen`** (acyclic edges → hesap-dense [Rayleigh-Ritz via `eig_sym`/`eig_nonsym`],
hesap-sparse [SparseLinearOp]; later hesap-direct [shift-invert], hesap-preconditioners + hesap-iterative
[LOBPCG/JD]). Detailed plan in `docs/phases/phase-3.1.6-hesap.md` (v6 row + v6-a..z sub-rows).

**⭐ TWO load-bearing truths (advisor-locked):**
1. **The crush axis is ALGORITHMIC, not kernel.** Plain Lanczos/Arnoldi = parity + matvec-count + MOAT
   (ARPACK/Spectra share the BLAS/LAPACK ceilings; shift-invert IS our v5 = parity+moat). The genuine crush =
   converging in FEWER matvecs via the PRECONDITIONED methods (v6-d shift-invert / v6-e LOBPCG / v6-f
   Jacobi-Davidson using a v5 factor or AMG as preconditioner can beat ARPACK on hard problems). Spend the
   crush energy there; report plain Krylov honestly as correctness+moat (the v5f discipline).
2. **The eigensolver moat has hazards the linear-solver moat lacks:** clustered/multiple eigenvalues ⇒
   non-unique eigenvectors (moat tests use WELL-SEPARATED spectra; block methods test SUBSPACE identity);
   pin a SIGN/ORDER convention (largest-|component| positive); the dense Rayleigh-Ritz is the inner kernel ⇒
   must be bit-deterministic. ⚠ **Restart-method SUBSTITUTION:** deliver the MODERN equivalents — Krylov-Schur
   ≡ IRAM (v6-c), thick-restart Lanczos ≡ IRLM (v6-b) — because IRAM/IRLM's implicit shifted-QR bulge-chasing
   is ordering-sensitive + NOT deterministic; Krylov-Schur/thick-restart are equivalent, stabler, AND moat-safe.

**Gold standards:** ARPACK (scipy eigsh/eigs, primary) + PRIMME (state-of-art symmetric, the real crush target
on hard problems) + FEAST lib + Spectra (C++ same-class). SLEPc = parallel ref (asterisk caution). The
cross-thread determinism MOAT is the differentiator none carry. Drop order if long: FEAST(g)+JD(f); core =
a/b/c/d/e/h+z. Commit boundaries: sym(a-b) · nonsym+SI(c-d) · precond(e-f) · FEAST/IRLBA(g-h).

**⭐ v6-a DONE 2026-06-06** (`hesap-eigen` module stood up + builds). `eigen_problem.hpp` (the SPEC: `Which`,
`EigenOptions<T>` [nev/ncv/which/tol/seed], `EigenResult<T>` [complex values + vectors + residuals + nconv];
generalized `A x = λ B x` reserved as a first-class spec dim). `lanczos.hpp` `eigs_sym<T>` (REAL symmetric,
full-reorthog NO-restart Lanczos): SplitMix64 deterministic start + MGS-twice fixed-order reorthog + sign
convention + Rayleigh-Ritz via dense `eig_sym(tridiagonal)` + Ritz-vector recovery X=V·S + true residuals.
Tests `[eigen]` 29 asserts/3 cases: 1D-Laplacian largest/smallest vs ANALYTIC λ_k=2−2cos(kπ/(n+1)) (full
Lanczos at n=16 ⇒ exact) · run-twice bit-identical · {1,2,4,8} MOAT bit-identical eigenvalues AND eigenvectors
(ParallelSparseLinearOp forced-parallel spmv, well-separated spectrum). VERIFIED win-debug + win-tidy (gcc/
asan/release → CI/next). ⚠ KEY LEARNING: a NO-restart Lanczos with bounded m converges only WELL-SEPARATED
extremes — the Laplacian's LARGEST are CLUSTERED near 4 (eigenvalue density bunches there) ⇒ didn't converge
at m=20 (the SMALLEST, relatively well-separated, did) ⇒ default tol = √eps (the achievable no-restart
target; machine-precision needs the v6-b thick-restart). Moat tests don't need convergence (only bit-identity).

**⭐ v6-b DONE 2026-06-06** (`thick_restart.hpp` `eigs_sym_tr`): thick-restart Lanczos (Wu-Simon). Keep
k=nev+buffer Ritz vectors + the residual at restart; the restarted projected matrix is the ARROWHEAD (diag θ +
couplings s_i=β_m·Y[m-1][i] | continued tridiag) — but FULL reorthog handles the recurrence (the kept-component
removal), so s_i appear ONLY in the Rayleigh-Ritz matrix (the simplification); cheap convergence via the Ritz
residual |β_m·Y[m-1][idx]|; deterministic re-seed on lucky breakdown. Chosen over implicit shifted-QR (IRLM) =
DETERMINISTIC (moat-safe). Tests: **converges the CLUSTERED largest Laplacian eigenvalues at bounded ncv=20≪
n=64 — the EXACT v6-a no-restart FAILURE, restart fixes it** + {1,2,4,8} MOAT bit-identical THROUGH the restart
cycles (n=240 multi-restart, well-separated end). VERIFIED win-debug + win-tidy.

**⭐ v6-c ARNOLDI DONE (PARTIAL) 2026-06-06** (`arnoldi.hpp` `eigs_nonsym`): nonsymmetric. Full-GS Arnoldi →
upper Hessenberg H → Rayleigh-Ritz via dense `eig(H)` (`EigNonsym` = complex values + complex Ritz vectors,
already has a sign convention) → wanted COMPLEX eigenvalues + cheap Arnoldi residual estimate β_m·|s[m-1]|;
`detail::more_wanted_c` complex `which`. Tests: 2×2 rotation blocks [[a,b],[−b,a]] ⇒ KNOWN eigenvalues a±b·i,
full Arnoldi at m=n recovers them + {1,2,4,8} MOAT bit-identical complex Ritz values. VERIFIED win-debug+tidy.
**⭐ v6-c COMPLEX EIGENVECTORS DONE 2026-06-06:** added `vectors_im` to `EigenResult` (Re→`vectors`, Im→
`vectors_im`; empty for real/symmetric). `eigs_nonsym` now recovers X=V·S (Re=Σ Re(S_j)v_j, Im=Σ Im(S_j)v_j),
unit complex-norm, a pinned PHASE convention (rotate e^{−iφ} so the largest-|component| is real-positive ⇒
deterministic ⇒ moat-safe), + the TRUE complex residual ‖A·x−λx‖ (A·X=A·Re(X)+i·A·Im(X)). Moat extended to
the eigenvectors (Re+Im bit-identical {1,2,4,8}). VERIFIED win-debug+tidy+gcc.
**⭐ v6-c KRYLOV-SCHUR RESTART DONE 2026-06-06 — v6-c COMPLETE.** `krylov_schur.hpp` `eigs_nonsym_ks` (bounded-
memory nonsym at ncv≪n). One cycle: extend Arnoldi to m ⇒ real Schur H=Z·T·Zᵀ ⇒ A·(V·Z)=(V·Z)·T+β_m·v_{m+1}·
(last row Z)ᵀ; `reorder_schur` the wanted to the lead (selection sort, recompute-each-step, 2×2-block-aware),
truncate to k (block boundary), restart with B=[[T_k, new-cols],[β_m·b_kᵀ, Hessenberg]]. Deterministic (serial
Schur/reorder/eig; only spmv parallel+bit-exact) ⇒ moat. **⚠⚠ KEY BUG (cost the debugging session): the
restarted H is NON-Hessenberg (kept Schur block T_k + the arrowhead residual row), but `real_schur` ASSUMES
upper-Hessenberg input — so calling it directly on the restarted H silently dropped the sub-Hessenberg entries
⇒ cycle-2+ Z wrong ⇒ Ritz values FROZEN at the 1st-cycle approximation + FALSE convergence (cheap estimate
β_m·|s[m-1]|≈0 but true ‖A·x−λx‖=2.4).** Diagnosed by instrumenting the relation A·V_k=V_k·T_k+β_m·v_{m+1}·b_kᵀ
(held at cycle 1 relerr~1e-13, so construction was fine ⇒ the bug was the Schur of the non-Hess H). FIX =
`general_real_schur` helper: Hessenberg-reduce h=Q·Hess·Qᵀ (`hessenberg`+`form_hessenberg_q`), `real_schur` the
Hess, compose Z=Q·Z_s. (`eig` itself was fine — it runs the full balance→Hess→schur pipeline; only the direct
`real_schur` call was wrong.) Then converges (matvecs 116, residual 5e-8). Tests: KS converges top LargestReal
at ncv=20≪n=200 with restarts ENGAGED (REQUIRE matvecs>ncv); conjugate pairs ⇒ Re=100,100,99,99 (each block
a±b·i shares Re — test-expectation gotcha); KS nconv≥no-restart nconv==nev; {1,2,4,8} MOAT values+eigenvectors
bit-identical THROUGH restarts. VERIFIED win-debug+tidy+gcc, non-ASCII guard PASS, 113 asserts/12 cases.
**LESSON: `real_schur`/`schur_aed` REQUIRE Hessenberg input; for a general/structured matrix use the
Hessenberg-first pipeline (or `eig`).**

**⭐ v6-d SHIFT-INVERT DONE 2026-06-06** (`shift_invert.hpp`, standard `(A−σI)`): the FIRST algorithmic crush
lever + the v5↔v6 bridge. `ShiftInvertOp` (LinearOp = `(A−σI)⁻¹·x` via a v5 factor's `apply_inverse`) +
`eigs_sym_shift_invert` — build (A−σI) [one diag/row, robust] → factor with v5f-e PARTIAL-PIVOT multifrontal
LU (accurate on the indefinite shift) → thick-restart Lanczos for LargestMagnitude μ (⇔ λ closest to σ) →
λ=σ+1/μ + TRUE residual on A. NEW edge hesap-eigen→hesap-direct. Test: finds the INTERIOR Laplacian
eigenvalues nearest σ=2 (v6-a/b CANNOT target the interior) exact <1e-7, residual <1e-8 + {1,2,4,8} MOAT
bit-identical. VERIFIED win-debug+tidy. ⚠ KEY: the LU-based SI op is symmetric only to ROUNDING ⇒ achievable
residual ~1e-8 (NOT machine); the inner SI eigensolve must converge TIGHTER than the final tol (sio.tol =
opts.tol·0.01) for the transformed A-residual to land below; tighter floor ⇒ LDLT factor / IR. Generalized
`(A−σB)⁻¹B` = follow-on.

**⭐ v6-e-a LOBPCG CORE DONE 2026-06-06** (`lobpcg.hpp` `eigs_sym_lobpcg`): block symmetric, the `nev` extreme
eigenpairs at once. Each iter works in S=[X, W=T·(A·X−X·Θ), P] kept ORTHONORMAL by block MGS (drop rank-
deficient cols) ⇒ Rayleigh-Ritz = plain `eig_sym(SᵀAS)` (NO generalized Gram/Cholesky solve — the simplifier).
AX carried through the q×k combination ⇒ only new matvecs/iter = A·W + A·P. **`precond` = `const LinearOp<T>*`
(T≈A⁻¹, nullptr ⇒ identity) — the algorithmic-crush hook, wired + exercised (Jacobi diagonal `SparseLinearOp`),

Laplacian vs analytic λ_k (unpreconditioned + preconditioned) + {1,2,4,8} MOAT values+vectors bit-identical
(deterministic: SplitMix start + fixed-order MGS + eig_sym + combinations; only spmv parallel). VERIFIED win-

`.values.data()[i]`, NOT `[i]`); `Array` has NO member `swap` (use `std::swap`, Array is movable). block=nev
(no soft-locking). ⚠ v6-e-b = generalized A·x=λ·B·x + the PRECONDITIONED CRUSH (v5 factor or AMG as T, the FEM
modal/buckling target — fewer matvecs than ARPACK is the win).
**⭐ v6-e-b PRECONDITIONED LOBPCG DONE 2026-06-06 — the algorithmic-crush MECHANISM.** NO new engine code: the
existing `eigs_sym_lobpcg` `precond` param consumes the existing `crd::hesap::preconditioners::Ic0Preconditioner`
(SPD by construction) + `crd::hesap::amg::SaAmg` (V-cycle, fwd-pre+bwd-post GS ⇒ SPD) — both `LinearOp`s,
TEST-ONLY link (no new module edge; eigen stays clean of preconditioners). Tests on the 2D Laplacian
(rectangular ⇒ non-degenerate): IC0 finds smallest-4 vs analytic; MECHANISM = a real SPD precond cuts iters-to-
tol ~4–5× (unprec 159 → IC0 40 → AMG 32); {1,2,4,8} MOAT bit-identical WITH IC0 in the loop. VERIFIED win-
debug+tidy+gcc+ASAN, guard PASS. **⭐⭐ HONEST CRUSH FRAMING (ADVISOR-LOCKED — read before the v6-close bench):
(1) iteration count is NOT a cross-library metric (a V-cycle ≠ an A-apply) ⇒ "fewer iters" is a MECHANISM proof,
NOT a crush — the fair metric is WALL-CLOCK + memory at MATCHED ACCURACY (count AMG setup like ARPACK's
factorization). (2) PEER trap: nobody runs plain/SM ARPACK for SMALLEST SPD (glacial) — scipy `eigsh` uses
shift-invert (`sigma=`); the REAL peers = SHIFT-INVERT ARPACK + scipy `lobpcg` (same class ⇒ expect parity+MOAT,
the honest floor). (3) the crush is REGIME-DEPENDENT: AMG-LOBPCG wins where direct-factor FILL-IN is the killer
= LARGE 3D / FEM; on small 2D shift-invert-direct usually wins (don't misread your own bench). (4) LOBPCG needs
an SPD precond (IC0 ✓; ILU0-on-SPD NOT guaranteed SPD ⇒ can misbehave).** ⚠ the ACTUAL crush (vs shift-invert
ARPACK/Spectra, large-3D/FEM, wall-clock) = a v6-CLOSE bench slice, built FRESH (needs an oracle install like
CHOLMOD/MUMPS).
**⭐ STANDING USER MANDATE (2026-06-06): "we need crushing for ALL slices, make sure about it AT THE END."** ⇒ v6
does NOT close until a fair benchmark PROVES the crush (or honestly reports parity+MOAT where parity is the
ceiling) vs the right peers (shift-invert ARPACK + scipy lobpcg + Spectra/PRIMME), per [feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_full_victory_beat_all_gold_standards).
**⭐⭐ v6 CRUSH BENCH DONE 2026-06-06 — SYMMETRIC, HONEST CRUSH PROVEN.** `runtime/examples/bench_hesap_eigen_lobpcg.cpp`
(Cerid AMG-LOBPCG) + `scripts/eigen_ref_scipy.py` (oracle, scipy 1.17 in `~/eigref-venv`; PEP668 ⇒ venv, NOT
system pip). 3D RECTANGULAR Poisson (s,s+3,s+7 ⇒ NON-degenerate ⇒ identical distinct eigenvalues; cubic grid's
triply-degenerate λ made eigsh@1e-7 return a WRONG 4th — rectangular fixed it). Both SINGLE-THREADED, matched
tol=1e-7, eigenvalues IDENTICAL. RESULT @ n=43680: **wall-clock 11.7× (0.64s vs 7.40s, GROWING 2.7→11.7×) ·
memory 40× (AMG 31 nnz/row vs SuperLU factor 1241/row, GROWING 24→40×).** scipy is splu-DOMINATED (75%) ⇒ tol-
robust; the factor fill grows ~O(n^4ᐟ3) in 3D while AMG stays O(n). **⚠⚠ EXACT CLAIM (advisor-locked, every
qualifier load-bearing): "AMG-LOBPCG (iterative+multigrid) CRUSHES DIRECT shift-invert ARPACK on 3D model-
POISSON (memory + wall-clock, matched accuracy) and carries the determinism MOAT." NOT same-class head-to-head
(diff algorithms; iterative-beats-direct in the fill-in regime). 3 WORDING GUARDS: (a) memory = AMG
`operator_complexity()` = level-operator nnz only (a STANDARD AMG metric; EXCLUDES P/R+smoother ⇒ understates;

(reuses `iterative::fgmres`; NEW acyclic edge **hesap-eigen→hesap-iterative**, same direction as v5f-c2) with the

deflation for nev pairs. TWO helper LinearOps `detail::JdProjectedOp`/`JdProjectedPrecond` (project→A/K⁻¹→project;
serial-used by fgmres, only A's spmv parallel). `result.iterations` repurposed = TOTAL matvecs (Σ inner fgmres
iters + per-expansion A·t) = the mechanism metric. **SCOPE (advisor-gated, explicit in phase doc): EXTREME
(Smallest/Largest) + CLUSTERED (deflation handles multiplicity) + preconditioned correction; INTERIOR via
harmonic-Ritz DEFERRED (v6-d shift-invert covers it; standard-Ritz interior = spurious values).** Inner solve =
loose tol (rel 0.1) + hard cap (≤25, bounds the clustered case). **RESULTS:** extreme smallest+largest 1D-Lap vs
analytic (largest CLUSTERED near 4 — JD converges where v6-a stalled); EXACTLY-degenerate λ resolved (square 2D
λ_{1,2}=λ_{2,1}, both copies locked — assert VALUES, degenerate vectors non-unique); **MECHANISM `unprec 985 →
IC0 897 → AMG 742` matvecs, BIT-IDENTICAL across MSVC/clang-cl/gcc** (margin drift-proof, NOT a fragile compare —
the count is a deterministic reproducible function); {1,2,4,8} moat bit-identical UNPRECONDITIONED **+ IC0-in-loop**
(the advisor's load-bearing ask — the projected-precond path must not be dead-under-moat). **VERIFIED win-debug
ctest (5 cases + all 5 guards) + win-tidy + win-clang-cl + win-asan (projected-op raw indexing clean) + gcc-release
(moat under real threading).** ⚠ KEY DESIGN TRUTH (advisor-confirmed): the projected op is well-posed even as θ→λ
because the near-null direction ≈u lives in Ũ and gets projected out — so unpreconditioned inner solves don't blow
up. HONEST: matvec-reduction = the v6-f crush; cross-library wall-clock vs ARPACK/PRIMME = v6-z. ⚠ JD's matvec
mechanism is WEAKER than LOBPCG's (985→897 IC0 = only 9%, vs LOBPCG 159→40): JD's count is dominated by the
CAPPED inner GMRES, so a preconditioner's effect on the total is indirect/smaller — AMG (742, 25%) shows it
clearly, IC0 modestly. Minor follow-on noted: MINRES (the natural symmetric-indefinite inner solver) instead of
FGMRES = a perf optimization, NOT a v6-f decision (FGMRES is correct + flexible-precond + moat-proven).
