**⭐ v6-g FEAST (contour integration, Polizzi 2009) DONE 2026-06-06.** `feast.hpp` `eigs_sym_feast<T>(a, lo, hi,
m0, opts, alloc, num_workers)` — ALL eigenvalues in `[lo,hi]` (the INTERVAL/INTERIOR specialist; takes the
MATRIX not a LinearOp — it must factor). Spectral projector `ρ=(1/2πi)∮(zI−A)⁻¹dz` ≈ **8-pt Gauss-Legendre on the
half-contour** (real-sym ⇒ conjugate-pair fold ⇒ `Q≈Σ_k Re[ω_k·(z_kI−A)⁻¹Y]`, `ω_k=(γ_k·r/2)·e^{iθ_k}`,
`θ_k=(π/2)(x_k+1)` — advisor-verified derivation); each `(z_kI−A)⁻¹` = a COMPLEX shifted solve factored ONCE by
the **v5 complex `factor_multifrontal_lu<Complex<T>>`** (z_k off the real axis ⇒ well-conditioned ⇒ static OK; the
"quadrature→shift-invert(v5)" of the plan; REUSES the v6-d hesap-direct edge — NO new edge); subspace iteration →
block MGS → RR `eig_sym(QᵀAQ)` → select `[lo,hi]`. **⚠⚠ KEY CORRECTNESS (advisor #2 — I FIRST got the framing
WRONG, then EMPIRICALLY corrected it): the in/out SELECTION = TWO filters: (1) INTERVAL `λ∈[lo,hi]` (just-outside
Ritz land outside) + (2) RESIDUAL GATE `‖A·x−λ·x‖≤tol` (excludes a spurious in-interval Ritz — the safety net,
added). The MGS rank-drop (`norm<16·eps`) is DEFENSIVE ONLY: an 8-pt quadrature does NOT null the surplus columns
to machine zero (~1e-3 ≫ 16·eps) ⇒ `q==m0` ALWAYS (VERIFIED by temp-instrumenting q vs m0 — never dropped). My
phase-doc/memory first headlined the drop as load-bearing; it isn't — the residual gate is. LESSON: when a
defensive branch is claimed load-bearing, INSTRUMENT it (like the v6-f reseeds / v6-e-d DROP).** Contract
m0≥count+headroom; no-headroom (q==m0 && all inside) ⇒ `converged=false` (saturation flag). **⚠ TEST DESIGN
(advisor #3): Q orthonormalized before RR ⇒ Ritz VALUES invariant to ω_k's scale ⇒ a value-vs-analytic check would
NOT catch a wrong contour filter — the in/out SEPARATION is what the contour+residual govern. The discriminating
test puts eigenvalues JUST OUTSIDE both endpoints and asserts EXCLUSION.** RESULTS: smallest 1D-Lap band vs
analytic; interior band k=28..30 with λ_27/λ_31 EXCLUDED; count robust to m0 (3 at m0=6 and 10). **⚠ MOAT
NON-VACUITY (advisor #2b): a 1D-chain factor runs SERIAL regardless of num_workers ⇒ a 1D moat is VACUOUS. FIX:
the moat uses a 2D grid (parallel elimination tree) + the driver runs a FORCED-parallel SELL spmv when
num_workers>1 (ParallelSparseLinearOp min_stored_bytes=0; jobs-safe to construct, parallel apply only when
workers>1, serial SparseLinearOp otherwise so non-moat tests need no jobs) ⇒ genuine parallel reductions,
bit-identical {1,2,4,8} under real gcc threading.** Factor-once (`Array<MultifrontalLU<Complex<T>>>` via
reserve+push_back; MultifrontalLU move-constructible). **VERIFIED win-debug ctest (4 cases + all 5 guards) +
win-tidy + win-clang-cl + win-asan (complex factor/solve + parallel spmv + projector indexing clean) + gcc-release
(non-vacuous moat under real threading).** HONEST: interval/
interior + the moat are the deliverable; wall-clock crush vs FEAST-lib/ARPACK = v6-z. nq=8 hardcoded (param ⇒
general GL nodes, follow-on). ⚠ win-asan run needs the ASan DLL on PATH (vcvars + MSVC Hostx64\x64 dir; a fresh
shell without it gives 0xC0000135 STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND — NOT an ASan error; see CLAUDE.md).

**⭐ v6-h IRLBA (sparse SVD via GKL bidiagonalization + thick restart) DONE 2026-06-07.** `svds.hpp`
`SvdResult<T>` (σ desc + U m×k + V n×k + two-sided residual — distinct lengths ⇒ NOT EigenResult) +
`svds<T>(a, opts, alloc)` (a = `LinearOp` with `apply`=A·v, `apply_adjoint`=Aᵀ·u; `SparseLinearOp` /
`ParallelSpmvLeastSquaresOp` provide both). Golub-Kahan-Lanczos → tiny upper-bidiagonal B → dense `svd(B)` → σ=Σ,
u=U_k·U_B, v=V_k·V_B. **⚠⚠ TWO advisor-flagged correctness points (both folded in BEFORE writing): (1) FULL
reorthog is BOTH-SIDED (new u vs U AND new v vs V, MGS-twice — one-sided leaks orthogonality ⇒ GHOST singular
values); (2) SVD sign is COUPLED (σ≥0 links u,v) — take u,v STRAIGHT from the dense svd's already-pinned U_B/V_B,
do NOT independently re-sign-pin (the established eigenvector habit would BREAK A·v=σu here).** Thick restart
(Baglama-Reichel augmented = the deterministic implicit-restart equiv, like v6-b): keep j=2·nev largest
(A·Ṽ=Ũ·diag(σ), kept block DIAGONAL) + spike ρ_i=β_last·P[last][i], continue GKL from residual v_res; restarted
B = diag(Σ)+spike-column+trailing-bidiag ⇒ converges at bounded ncv≪min(m,n). **SCOPE: LARGEST only; SMALLEST
DEFERRED** (GKL bottom glacial — needs shift-invert-on-normal-eqns / harmonic; explicit defer like v6-f). **⚠
DEV LESSON: my first core test used a CLOSELY-SPACED spectrum (gaps ~0.02 relative) ⇒ no-restart didn't converge
the top 4 at ncv=24 — diagnosis showed A·v=σu machine-exact but Aᵀu=σv residual grew for smaller σ = the textbook
GKL convergence measure (NOT a bug; values matched the oracle); fixed the CORE test with a SPIKED (geometric 2×)
spectrum, and reused the closely-spaced one for the RESTART test (converges in 3 cycles where no-restart fails).**
RESULTS: core largest-4 of a tall A vs dense `svd` oracle to machine precision + coupled-sign check + unit norms;
restart converges closely-spaced at ncv=20 (`iterations≥2`); {1,2,4,8} moat bit-identical σ/U/V (both spmv dirs
forced parallel, min_stored_bytes=0 — the only parallel reductions, no factor). **VERIFIED win-debug ctest
(4 cases incl. an f32 case + all 5 guards) + win-tidy + win-clang-cl + win-asan (bidiag/restart/svd clean) +
gcc-release (moat under real threads).** HONEST: parity + the moat; no crush bench.

v7 = **the WHOLE optimization domain** (`crd-hesap-opt`), planned 2026-06-07 (advisor-vetted). User direction:
**v7 ABSORBS the old v8 constrained cluster** — optimization is ONE domain (unconstrained + bound-constrained +
constrained). Full plan in `docs/phases/phase-3.1.6-hesap.md` (v7 header + v7-a..r + v7-z rows). ADR-0065 D14.

**Consumer story (why it's foundational):** the universal "find the best X" — eylem (constrained dynamics/IK/
trajectory/powered-ragdoll motors), estimation+control 3.1.11 (MPC=QP/NLP·LQR·Kalman=LS·SLAM/bundle-adjustment=
sparse nonlinear-LS), FEA/CFD (topology/shape/design opt·parameter ID), CAD (sketch constraint solving), ML
(training=stochastic opt·differentiable sim), rendering (calibration/BRDF-fit/photogrammetry-BA), games (AI/RL/
CSP/balancing), robotics (inverse dynamics/motion planning/calibration), DAW (filter design). Backed by hesap
dense/sparse/direct/iterative/eig (Newton step=linear solve; exact-TR=eig subproblem) + autodiff (gradients).

**Subslices (consumer-pull sequenced):** a substrate (Objective/providers/OptResult/LineSearch + ADR edges +
autodiff contract) · b derivatives (FD/forward-AD/complex-step/gradient-check) · c line searches (Armijo/Wolfe/
strong-Wolfe/More-Thuente) · **d⭐ quasi-Newton (BFGS/L-BFGS/L-BFGS-B/SR1)** · **e⭐ nonlinear-LS (GN/LM/TRF/robust
losses; PROBE CERES here)** · f first-order (steepest/nonlinear-CG/momentum) · g Newton family (full/Newton-CG/
modified) · h trust-region (Cauchy/dogleg/Steihaug/trust-Krylov/exact-Moré-Sorensen-via-eig) · i stochastic/ML
(SGD/Adam/AdamW/Nadam/RAdam/RMSprop/Lion/LAMB + schedules) · j constrained substrate (KKT/Lagrangian/multipliers)
· **k⭐ QP (Goldfarb-Idnani/Mehrotra/OSQP-ADMM)** · l LP (revised simplex/Mehrotra IPM) · m conic (SCS) · **n⭐ NLP

## project_v7e2_lattice_cholmod_perf

---
name: project_v7e2_lattice_cholmod_perf
description: "v7-e-2 sparse-LM perf arc — lattice-3D JᵀJ vs CHOLMOD; what's shipped, the scoreboard, and the pinned residual wall"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3571170c-1886-4c83-b787-c787213d0125
---

v7-e-2 = sparse-Jacobian LM (the "crush vehicle"). Benched JᵀJ-from-NLS (3D elastic lattice, `dump_nls_lattice_jtj`,
genuinely SPD/deformation-class) vs **CHOLMOD** (= exactly what Ceres-sparse uses), same AMD order, matched accuracy.
Full story: `docs/sessions/2026-06-07-v7e2-gate-and-nls-cholmod-bench.md`.

**Shipped (all moat-safe, bit-identical {1..16}, zero FEA regression):**
- **The gate:** `SupernodalCholesky::factorize(..., reuse_symbolic)` + `refactorize()` — symbolic (AMD+etree+
  amalgamation) paid ONCE, numeric per λ-trial. Wired into the sparse-LM driver (Ceres caches symbolic the same way).
- **SYRK levers:** symmetric Schur/trailing as lower-triangle-only (`syrk_lower_minus` + cmod `col_limit` + (C)
  two-pass). Removed the 1.39× flop excess ⇒ **Cerid min-flops == CHOLMOD cc.fl**, with ~22% LESS fill.
- **Balanced-triangular primitive** (`hesap-dense/.../detail/parallel_triangular.hpp`, `triangular_bound=round(n·√(k/w))`)
  + fork **size-gate** (don't fork tiny late-panel triangles).
- **Uninit-scratch** (`ubuf.resize_uninitialized`) — surfaced+fixed a real **gemm beta=0 bug** (see
  [feedback_gemm_beta0_must_store_zero_and_umr_validation](numerics-and-performance.md#memory-feedback_gemm_beta0_must_store_zero_and_umr_validation)). ~180ms/13% off lat32, re-paid every refactorize.

**8T scoreboard (FACTOR, CHOLMOD/Cerid; >1 = Cerid wins):** hood **1.53×** · ldoor **1.69×** · bmwcra_1 **1.09×**
(was ADR-0082 wall) · lat20 **0.95×** · **lat24 0.99× = PARITY** · lat28 0.87× · lat32 **0.83×** (0.66× at session
start). SOLVE still loses on lattices (~0.5×) — a later lever.

**⭐ The residual lat32 gap is PINNED and MEASURED:** it is the **serial per-thread GEMM kernel** (W=1 ratio 0.73×),
NOT parallel scaling (Cerid scales **3.16× vs CHOLMOD 2.76×** at 8T — Cerid scales BETTER) and NOT Amdahl
(cdivA serial-chain = 1.5% of the node front). = the ADR-0082 intrinsic-vs-OpenBLAS wall; user has confirmed
hand-tuned asm does NOT move it (don't re-try asm). Cerid's better scaling crosses to a win at higher core counts.
So: parity reached through lat24; lat28/32 are serial-kernel-bound; the determinism moat is the standing
differentiator CHOLMOD lacks. **Don't chase lat32 8T parity via more parallelism/alloc — the wall is single-thread.**

⭐⭐ **2026-06-11 — THE "SERIAL KERNEL WALL" WAS ⅓ WALL, ⅔ FIXABLE** (the lattice kernel dig, session
2026-06-11-lattice-kernel-crush.md — the second time a wall-attribution fell to a profile): (1) **the syrk-pack
pathology** — syrk_lower_minus packed its full operand ELEMENTWISE via MatrixView::at() (one TLB miss/element on
big-ld panels); rebuilt as a Goto-blocked triangular gemm sharing pack_a/pack_b + the microkernel + the EXACT gemm
Kc-grouping ⇒ also HEALS a latent serial-syrk-vs-parallel-gemm value divergence at knc>256 (worker count picked the
path!); lat32 serial 4283→3705ms alone. (2) **ColMajor merge stride fix** in gemm_packed_inner (j-inner strided every
write by ld; i-inner now; bit-identical, lifts every ColMajor gemm). (3) below-outer TRSM in **bit-identical in-place
wide-N RowMajor form** (transpose-VIEWS of the panel; B1 = one beta=1 in-place gemm, no Tᵀ-scratch). RESULT: **lat32
serial 0.73→0.85-class · lat24 8T 0.99 PARITY · hood 1.57× / bcsstk25 1.85× WIN (improved) · residuals unchanged**;
dense 359508 + direct 598861 asserts green (WSL + win-debug/shipping/asan/tidy). ⭐ THE ONE NAMED REMAINING LEVER for
lat28/32 (~0.85): a **dedicated packed-TRSM driver** — B1's M=64-skinny shape re-streams packed B per 6-row a-panel
(bandwidth-bound ~50 GF/s any orientation; M=256 fused needs an inverse build that tail blocks can't amortize) —
OpenBLAS-style fused solve kernel, C-level, NOT asm. ⚠ PROBE LESSON: ad-hoc bench TUs MUST carry
-DCRD_SIMD_TARGET=2 (+CRD_DETERMINISTIC_FP) or header templates instantiate the SCALAR microkernel (a 20× phantom);
rebuild the .a before probing headers (COMDAT can pick the stale lib copy).

⭐⭐ **2026-06-11 LATER — THE SOLVE CRUSH (the full-scoreboard correction):** the user caught FACTOR-only
victory reporting (solve lost 2-3×, regressing with threads) — see feedback_full_scoreboard_no_partial_victory.
Fixes: single-RHS parallel solve was NET-NEGATIVE → always-serial gate; backward = scalar FP-add chain → shared
SIMD kernels (solve_axpy_* bit-identical maps + solve_dot_conj→simd_dot deterministic tree) in serial+parallel →
lat32 serial solve 70→51ms; multi-RHS 16T collapse (lat12 x16 0.08×) → work gate lnz·nrhs≥160M + 8-lane cap.
RESULT: solve flat at all worker counts; WINS small lattices (→2.67×) + bcsstk25 (→3.82×), hood parity +
x16 WINS 1.66-1.82×; big lattices 0.69-0.83. Ceiling MEASURED 26 GB/s (both buffers; us 80%, CHOLMOD ~100% on
fewer bytes — perf-counter dig NAMED). The packed-TRSM driver landed bit-identical (resident-panel walk) but the
old "B1=1060ms" finding was built on a MISLABELED TIMER (cdiv_outertrail wraps the (C) TRAILING, not B — B was
~165-400ms all along); (C) now merges in-place via the syrk col_indexed_out mode. ubuf 16T OOM root-fixed
(per-worker Array slices vs the TLSF ~4GB structural chunk cap) → 16T factor: lat24 1.02 WIN · lat28 1.00 ·
lat32 0.96 parity. Session: 2026-06-11-solve-crush-full-scoreboard.md (the FULL board table).
⭐⭐⭐ **2026-06-11 FINAL — THE MULTI-STREAM DIG FLIPPED THE SOLVE TO A WIN** (session
2026-06-11-multistream-solve-win.md; "deep research, 100% confidence" directive): READ the CHOLMOD source
(SuiteSparse cloned to ~/cerid-deps/suitesparse; solve = dtrsv+dgemv, same structure) → pinned BYTES (true
trapezoids IDENTICAL 67.87M both — "22% less fill" was our-trapezoid-vs-their-RECTANGLES, claim corrected;
bench now prints both + CHOLMOD L/Lt per-pass split permanently) → pinned RATE (theirs 29 GB/s > the 26
"ceiling") → MECHANISM measured: **1 stream 22.7 / 2 streams 29.7 / 4 streams 36.9 GB/s** (DRAM page-level
parallelism; OpenBLAS dgemv = 4 columns = 4 streams) → **4-COLUMN-FUSED solve kernels** (solve_fwd_diag/
below_acc/apply_minus + solve_back_below/diag + solve_dot4_f64; forward fusion BIT-IDENTICAL ascending-k
per element; backward = new fixed deterministic order; serial≡parallel SHARE the helpers by construction).
**SOLVE WINS EVERY MATRIX AT 1T (1.06–1.47), most at 8/16T (to 3.74×); lat32 0.50→1.14; hood all-metric
all-thread WIN.** NAMED remaining (measured): x16 mid-lattices 8/16T 0.51-0.80 (their threaded multi-RHS
dgemm; lever = fused multi-RHS kernels) · lat28/32 1-RHS @8T 0.90-1.03 (their threaded gemv on big fronts;
lever = within-supernode parallel solve) · FACTOR serial 0.77-0.94 (our gemm 75 vs OpenBLAS-asm 84 GF/s ≈
90%; lever candidate = multi-stream PACKING reads — same DRAM mechanism) · tiny-matrix 16T factor forks.
⚠ pure-load 1-stream probes UNDERESTIMATE achievable DRAM bandwidth — always probe multi-stream too.

⭐⭐ **2026-06-11 FINAL ROUND — x16 + FACTOR (session 2026-06-11-x16-factor-crush.md):** the multi-stream
mechanism applied to pack_a/pack_b (4-way p-interleave, bit-identical) ⇒ every cold gemm operand 1→4
streams ⇒ lat32 serial factor 3770→3516ms, factor 8/16T parity-to-WIN lat20/24/28 (1.02-1.04). The x16
split MEASURED (42% in diag solves = quadratic dscr re-streaming; below = per-supernode gemm calls) ⇒
fused mRHS kernels (solve_mrhs_{fwd,back}_{below,diag}: alloc/pack-free, 4-8-fused streams, r-blocked so
panel streams ONCE + scratch stays cached, fma-latency unrolls; per-element gemm-exact k-ascending chains;
serial≡parallel via shared helpers) ⇒ **x16 lat24 1.28/1.21 WIN @8/16T · lat32 1.29 WIN @16T · hood
1.67/1.52 WIN · serial x16 lat28 123→87ms**. ⚠ TWO measured kernel lessons: (a) loop order that re-streams
a scratch block per column = quadratic cache traffic — r-block so the reduction scratch stays resident;
(b) ONE fma chain per accumulator = ~22 GF/s latency wall — need ≥2 independent chains (8-col fusion).
Remaining named: lat12/20 x16 0.60-0.77 (sub-25ms problems) · lat28/32 1-RHS @8T 0.83-0.90 (their threaded
gemv; within-front lever) · lat28/32 factor serial 0.81-0.84 (last ~10% to OpenBLAS asm) · lat12@16T factor
(worker guidance). Host noise ±8-10% — CHOLMOD's own numbers swing that much run-to-run.

WIP, awaiting user commit (agents never commit).

<a id="memory-project_world_normal_varying_reads_zero"></a>
## project_world_normal_varying_reads_zero

---
name: project_world_normal_varying_reads_zero
description: "⛔⛔⛔ RETRACTED + the lesson: I read a PIXEL COUNT as a colour channel and built 5 theories on it. The world normal was NEVER broken. Real open issue: the cooked Forward BRDF renders black. ALWAYS read the assertion's definition before interpreting its number"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

⛔⛔⛔ **RETRACTED — the premise of this entry was a MEASUREMENT ERROR, and the error is the lesson.**

**What happened (2026-07-25).** Chasing a black cooked-Forward render in `crd-scene-render`, I repeatedly read the
GEO-7 gate's `lit` value as a normalized colour channel. It is not. It is a **COUNT of non-black pixels** out of
256 samples:

```cpp
u32 lit = 0;
for (sy...) for (sx...) if ((target->read_pixel(sx, sy) & 0x00FFFFFFU) != 0U) { ++lit; }
CHECK(lit > 40U);          // 256 samples
```

So "`lit` = 24" meant **24 of 256 pixels were non-black**, NOT "the channel is 24/255 ~= 0.09". Every reading in
that investigation — 0, 14, 17, 24, 27 — was a pixel count. **The world normal was never actually measured.**

**⛔ THE COST.** On that misreading I built and reported FIVE successive theories, each falsified by a further
(also misread) measurement: emitter assigns locations by declaration order · the VS matrix arithmetic is wrong ·
varyings do not transport under `VK_EXT_shader_object` · the vertex-pull draw path drops varyings · the world
normal is zero and "the 0.25 ambient floor masked it, and that explains the unlit torus". **All of it was
downstream of reading one number wrong.** A direct probe — bypass the BRDF, write the raw varying out as colour —
**passes**, i.e. the normal arrives correctly.

**⭐ THE RULE, and it generalises far beyond this bug:**
> **Before interpreting any number a gate prints, READ THE ASSERTION THAT PRODUCED IT.**
> Is it a channel value, a pixel COUNT, a percentage, a delta, a mean? A plausible-looking integer in `0..255`
> is not evidence of anything until you know what it counts.

Corollaries that would each have caught this in one step:
- When a metric's meaning matters, **print its units in the log line** (`lit_pixels=24/256`, not `24`).
- A probe that CHANGES the shader must be validated against a control whose expected value you can state in
  advance — e.g. "writing the raw varying out must light >40 pixels" (it did; the normal was fine all along).
- ⛔ Also observed and separately real: one probe run silently used a **STALE BINARY** after a warning-as-error
  build failure and still printed "All tests passed". **Verify the build actually recompiled** (check for
  `error`, and that the binary timestamp changed) before trusting a probe.

**What remains genuinely open (NOT a normal bug):** the cooked Forward variant
(`build_fs_for_pass` at `PassType::Forward` -> `shade_forward` -> `brdf_direct`) renders **0 non-black pixels**,
while the same FS with a *constant* `(0,1,0)` normal renders 27. Since the varying is proven good, look at
`shade_forward`'s inputs: **`view_dir` is still a placeholder constant `(0,1,0)`** and `brdf_direct` derives
`NoV`, the Smith visibility term, `env_brdf_approx` and `energy_compensation` from it — a degenerate view vector
plausibly zeroes the whole chain. Fix the view direction first (it needs the camera position, a frame-frequency
uniform, REN-37.3) and re-measure with a control.

**What IS proven correct** (do not re-investigate): emitter location assignment (`ckir_glsl.hpp:1257` emits the
explicit `nd.iidx`) · the VS normal arithmetic (traced in the emitted GLSL: `nwy = m[1]*nx + m[5]*ny + m[9]*nz`,
matrix words 1/5/9, normal words 3/4/5) · varying transport under BOTH `draw` and `draw_storage_depth` · that
unmatched extra VS outputs do not break linkage — the last two are pinned by the permanent `[ren37]` gates in
`tests/gpu-context-vulkan/test_vulkan_frame_graph.cpp`.

Related: [project_material_technique_composition_ren37](project-history.md#memory-project_material_technique_composition_ren37), [feedback_fps_single_run_is_noise_median_of_five](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_fps_single_run_is_noise_median_of_five)
(the same failure mode — trusting a number without verifying what produced it),
[feedback_gates_run_configs_the_app_never_ships](workflow-and-correctness.md#memory-feedback_gates_run_configs_the_app_never_ships).
